articles.title: Randomized Caches in HW: Overheads And Limitations (RUB, Max Planck, Georgia Tech)
articles.text:
Home
                        TECHNICAL PAPERS
		
								November 3rd, 2026 - 
								By: Technical Paper Link
								
							
Researchers at Ruhr University Bochum, the Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy, and Georgia Tech published “Randomized Caches in Hardware: Challenges and Trade-offs.”
Abstract Excerpt:
“Randomized caches protect against side-channel attacks by obfuscating the mapping of memory addresses to cache locations. Existing proposals typically describe architectural behavior, leaving practical hardware implementation challenges largely unexplored. We implement four prominent designs, CEASER-S, ScatterCache, SassCache, and MIRAGE, and integrate them as the last-level cache (LLC) of a multi-core out-of-order RISC-V system-on-chip (SoC). We identify common and design-specific implementation challenges and develop practical solutions. We evaluate complete FPGA implementations by running SPEC CPU 2017 rate and GAPBS workloads to completion, providing, to our knowledge, the first comparative evaluation of these designs on a common full-system hardware platform.”
Find the technical paper here. October 2026
Wang, Xinrui, Pascal Kosak, Christof Paar, Daniel Genkin, Yuval Yarom, and Anirban Chakraborty. “Randomized Caches in Hardware: Challenges and Trade-offs.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2611.00282 (2026). CC BY 4.0 license.

articles.title: AI Image Enhancement Improves Detection Of Flip-Chip Interconnect Defects (MCL, PVA TePla, ASE)
articles.text: Researchers at Materials Center Leoben, PVA TePla , and Advanced Semiconductor Engineering ( ASE) published “AI-Based Image Enhancement Improves Detection of Interconnect Defects in Microelectronic Packaging.” Abstract Excerpt : “Traditional failure-analysis (FA) methods face growing challenges due to the increasing miniaturization and complexity of modern semiconductor devices. In particular, the detection of cracks in the extreme low K layers of flip-chips, utilized in advanced packaging architectures at the back end of line (BEOL), is challenging. To improve detectability of these so-called “white bumps”, we propose an AI-based image-enhancement workflow, specifically tailored to improve scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM) images.” Find the technical paper here . October 2026 Wilhelmer, R., Djuric-Rissner, T., Czurratis, P. et al. AI-Based Image Enhancement Improves Detection of Interconnect Defects in Microelectronic Packaging. J Fail. Anal. and Preven. (2026). https://doi.org/10.1007/s11668-026-02537-z. Open access . articles.title: Fast, Sub-Volt HZO Ferroelectric Capacitors For DRAM-Like Memory (SNU)
articles.text:
Seoul National University-led researchers published “Resolving the Kay–Dunn limit and the speed–endurance dilemma in ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 for DRAM-class sub-volt capacitors.”
Abstract
“Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide can increase charge density in scaled capacitors, but its high coercive field limits the low-voltage, high endurance switching required for dynamic random-access memory and embedded ferroelectric memories. Here we show that plasma-engineered (111)-textured TiN electrodes with N-rich, oxidation-resistant surfaces suppress interfacial oxidation and enable robust switching in 5 nm Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 capacitors. The devices exhibit saturated hysteresis at 0.6 V, with 2Pr = 31.5 μC cm−2 and Ec = 0.62 MV cm−1, and no hard electrical breakdown through 1012 bipolar cycles. Their nucleation-limited switching kinetics extrapolate to sub-nanosecond polarisation reversal at DRAM-relevant capacitor areas. At 1.1 V, circuit simulations of a common plate 1T–1 C cell yield short- and long-term stand-by sensing margins of 482 and 201 mV under a 20 fF bit line load. Electrode texture and interface engineering therefore enable low-voltage, high speed switching without compromising endurance, mitigating the practical Kay–Dunn scaling penalty and the speed–endurance dilemma.”
Find the technical paper here. October 2026
Park, G.H., Jo, S., Park, S. et al. Resolving the Kay–Dunn limit and the speed–endurance dilemma in ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 for DRAM-class sub-volt capacitors. Nat Commun (2026). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78705-4

articles.title: Quantum Interconnects Link Two 120-Qubit Processors (IBM Research)
articles.text: Researchers at IBM Research published “Meter-scale quantum interconnects between large quantum processors.” Abstract Excerpt : “Modular quantum architecture requires long-distance quantum interconnects to stitch together individual processor modules. Such interconnects, long-distance couplers or L-couplers, must support coherent quantum operation over meter-scale distances and scale to multiple connections between any two modules. Here we demonstrate four L-couplers operating between two 120-qubit IBM Nighthawk R1 superconducting qubit processors. “ Find the technical paper here . October 2026. IBM’s related blog post is here . Sundaresan, Neereja M., et al. “Meter-scale quantum interconnects between large quantum processors.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2610.29986 (2026). The post Quantum Interconnects Link Two 120-Qubit Processors (IBM Research) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering .

articles.title: How to watch Stick season 2 online — Watch the sitcom from anywhere
articles.text:
How to watch Stick season 2 online — Watch the Owen Wilson golf sitcom from anywhere in the world
Pryce and Santi are ready to tee off once more in this hilarious golf comedy
While much of season 1 focused on Santi Wheeler's attempts to break into the professional golf game, it's his coach, Pryce (Wilson), who is picking up the clubs again and ending his retirement in the second season. There's a lot of hard work on the horizon, though, especially seen as his former coach, Butch, is suffering with Alzheimer's; but Pryce hires Butch's daughter instead (played by the brilliant Rhea Seehorn). articles.title: Could the GTA 6 launch break the Australian internet? We asked NBN Co to find out
articles.text:
Could the GTA 6 launch break the Australian internet? We asked NBN Co to find out
Australia's broadband network is bracing for one of gaming's biggest launches, but NBN Co says it's ready for the challenge
- NBN Co says Australia's broadband network is ready for the expected surge in traffic when GTA VI launches
- A previous major game release pushed NBN traffic to a record 32.91Tbps, around 30% above normal levels
- GTA VI's week-long preload period should help prevent a massive spike in network traffic on launch day
- NBN Co believes GTA VI could set a new record for total download volume across its 7–8-day launch period
Grand Theft Auto VI is shaping up to be one of the biggest video game launches in history, and with millions of gamers expected to download Rockstar's long-awaited sequel, it's fair to wonder whether Australia's internet infrastructure can cope with the demand.
After all, GTA VI is confirmed to require a hefty 212GB download, meaning even a single copy will consume a considerable amount of bandwidth. Multiply that by potentially hundreds of thousands of Australian gamers all wanting to get their hands on the game at once, and it's easy to imagine the strain it could place on the country's broadband network.
But could GTA VI actually break the internet?
We put that question to NBN Co, and its response was reassuring. Not only does the company believe its network is ready for the game's arrival, but it also suggested GTA VI could potentially set a new record for the amount of data downloaded over a single game launch period.
NBN Co says it's ready for GTA VI
Despite the enormous anticipation surrounding GTA VI, NBN Co doesn't appear particularly concerned about the network being overwhelmed when the game launches.
"We've planned for major download events like this, and we're confident the NBN network is ready for the increased demand," an NBN Co spokesperson told us.
The company explained that it works closely with content distributors to model the potential impact of major game releases, allowing it to prepare for periods of particularly heavy demand.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Part of that preparation involves working with distributors to spread downloads over a longer period, rather than allowing everyone to begin downloading at the same time.
This has already changed the way major game launches affect the network. According to NBN Co, traffic now begins building earlier in the day, rather than suddenly surging when gamers return home from work.
Game launches have already pushed NBN traffic to record highs
There's good reason for NBN Co to take major game releases seriously — the company revealed that gaming downloads have been responsible for some of the biggest traffic peaks ever recorded on its network.
In fact, NBN Co told us that “a game download release last year” coincided with a record traffic peak of 32.91 terabits per second (Tbps).
“This was approximately 30% higher than baseline traffic, with almost 8Tbps of additional demand during the busiest hour.”
And while NBN Co didn't identify which game was responsible for that particular peak, it demonstrates just how significantly a major release can affect Australia's internet traffic. With GTA VI arguably being one of the most anticipated games of all time, it's reasonable to expect another substantial increase in demand.
Why preloading could prevent a massive traffic spike
Fortunately, there's one factor working in NBN Co's favour: preloading.
GTA VI preloading is scheduled to begin on November 10 for anyone who has preordered the game from a digital store. For anyone looking to buy the code-in-box variant, preloading is confirmed for November 12, giving players the opportunity to download the game ahead of its official release.
Rather than having millions of players attempting to download more than 200GB of data simultaneously, the preload window allows that demand to be distributed over several days.
"Preloading is good news for gamers and good news for the network," NBN Co told us.
The company explained that the impact of major game launches has become less significant over time, largely because distributors now spread downloads and updates across longer periods. In GTA VI's case, NBN Co expects the week-long preload period to help avoid particularly sharp spikes in network traffic.
However, that doesn't necessarily mean the game won't break any records.
GTA VI could still set a new Australian download record
While NBN Co doesn't necessarily expect GTA VI to produce the biggest single-hour traffic spike in its history, it believes the game's launch could achieve something arguably more impressive.
"While the preloading approach will likely prevent a record-breaking traffic spike during a specific hour or day, we expect to see increased traffic across the preload and release period, which could result in a record-breaking download volume across that 7 – 8-day period," the company said.
In other words, GTA VI might not generate the highest instantaneous demand ever seen on the NBN, but the total amount of data downloaded over its launch period could still be unprecedented.
Indeed, with a 212GB download potentially being repeated across a huge number of Australian households, it's not difficult to see why NBN Co is anticipating a particularly busy week.
How to prepare your internet connection for GTA VI
While NBN Co is confident its network can handle the increased demand, individual households could still encounter slower-than-expected downloads if their home internet setup isn't up to scratch.
The company recommends checking your router's location, ideally positioning it somewhere elevated and central, away from obstacles and sources of interference.
It also suggests checking the age of your router, since older models may struggle to deliver the full speeds available on faster NBN plans. Of course, this isn’t advice aimed solely at prospective GTA players; it’s advice we recommend ourselves, particularly if you have one of the fastest NBN plans.
For larger or multi-storey homes, the best mesh Wi-Fi systems in Australia can help improve wireless coverage, while households still using older copper-based NBN connections may want to check whether they're eligible for a free fibre upgrade.
Finally, NBN Co recommends reviewing your current internet plan to determine whether it still meets your household's needs.
Of course, even the fastest NBN connection won't guarantee maximum download speeds if the game distribution servers are struggling to keep up with demand.
But with GTA VI's launch fast approaching, the message from NBN Co is clear — Australia's broadband network is ready, even if the country's gamers are about to put it through one of its biggest tests yet.

articles.title: I’ve never played World of Warcraft, but a few weeks with its Dungeons & Dragons’ expansion has me convinced it’s the perfect first Universes Beyond tie-in for the popular TTRPG
articles.text:
Dungeons & Dragons’ World of Warcraft Gameplay Expansion isn’t just perfect for WoW fans, every D&D player and DM should pick it up
For the Horde!
Universes Beyond has finally leapt from Magic: The Gathering and into Wizards of the Coast’s other hugely popular game, Dungeons & Dragons, with the release of its World of Warcraft Gameplay Expansion — a 256-page book detailing precisely how the planet of Azeroth should be adapted into the most popular tabletop RPG.
I’ve spent the last couple of weeks devouring this new book, and while I’ll admit to already being a fan of Universes Beyond — I think it has done an amazing job of introducing my favorite trading card game to complete newcomers, and I have hopes it’ll do the same for D&D — whether you’re in my camp, or you’re someone who would rather keep your game worlds isolated, I think you’ll struggle to find complaints with this module.
Of course the book heavily focuses on the WoW-ness of the additions it makes to the TTRPG, yet so many of the new races, subclasses, monsters, and other rules could easily slot into any campaign setting. And if you need a little extra nudge, this book includes the long-awaited refresh of some fan-favorite subclasses which had yet to receive their post-2024 update (like the Swashbuckler Rogue and Way of the Drunken Master Monk, renamed to Warrior of Mystic Brews).
Though perhaps best of all, none of this excellent new content will destroy your bank balance. The Gameplay Expansion costs $59.99 / £49.99 / AU$84.99, which, while at the higher end of what D&D books sell for, feels like a reasonable price considering the amount here for players and Dungeon Masters. Plus, third-party retailers are sure to sell you this expansion for less than MSRP, especially during sales periods when D&D books are known to get a price cut.
My only disappointment is that I feel it’s not the most newcomer-friendly if you’re looking to be the Dungeon Master — the person who has to run the games. Just a quick one-shot adventure would do the trick to get the ball rolling, but as is, I’d suggest the DM is someone with D&D experience. Which is a shame considering Universes Beyond’s new-player appeal.
That said, I think this expansion is excellent no matter your affinity for WoW, but if you’re still unsure whether you should grab the World of Warcraft Gameplay Expansion for Dungeons & Dragons, let me explain a little more why I love it.
A feast of flavour, and heroes
Let’s begin where this book does: Chapter 1: Character Classes. Every class in Dungeons & Dragons features in this World of Warcraft expansion to give players a guide for how the TTRPG can be adapted to fit the champions Azeroth locals will be familiar with. Admittedly, some get more attention than others, but what I loved to read was that every class gets at least something new — rather than some being ignored entirely like with other recent expansions.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
For those on the shorter end of the stick — Druids, Wizards, Fighters, Warlocks, and Rangers (though they’re a special case I’ll get back to later) — this means just some new spells, Battle Master maneuvers, or Eldritch Invocations. Though I’m not complaining after reading through their new tools.
Conjuration-focused Warlocks will love the Expendable Minions invocation, which turns downed minions into healing for you or an ally, while the new version of Mass Polymorph feels like a hilariously perfect way for a more chaotic Wizard to dispatch a surrounding army — transforming any number of terrifying foes into harmless goats.
You’ll also notice these classes, and all others, have simple guides to follow for what spells and feature choices to make so that the D&D class feels most like the World of Warcraft specializations. Some class names have changed too. Wizard is Mage, Fighter is Warrior, and Rangers are Hunters (I’ll highlight other class name variations as we go).
One step above are Monks, Paladins, Clerics (Priests), Rogues, and Barbarians (Shamans), who all get a new subclass or two, or at least a revised version of a subclass, yet to be updated since the 2024 rules update.
In that latter camp are the Swashbuckler Rogue and Drunken Master Monk, which has been renamed Warrior of Mystic Brews. As with other post-2024 rules update refreshes, these subclasses feel very familiar, though there are some mechanical tweaks here and there to better balance the player option against the other choices you could make — or, in the case of Warrior of Mystic Brews, make the subclass feel like a more distinct option in your repertoire.
The brand-new subclasses steal the show to some extent because of their freshness, and I’m desperate to play an Oath of the Holy Paladin in my next campaign. This version of the knight is far more focused on healing than fighting — fulfilling a more supportive tank role; however, I still wouldn’t want to get struck by its Divine Smite.
Finally, circling back on the Ranger’s ‘special case,’ you’ll find three so-called Hero Classes — the Death Knight, Demon Hunter, and Evoker. This never-before-seen flavor of character option is a sort of subclass, but rather than building on the existing class’s base, they tear down and rebuild some core aspects (something subclasses don’t tend to do).
For example, the Oath of the Ebon Blade Death Knight takes away the Paladin’s healing Lay on Hands and turns it into a damaging Death Coil, and transforms the heavenly Divine Smite into a demonic Runic Smite.
Calling them ‘Hero Classes’ does perhaps suggest a level of superiority; however, I haven’t necessarily felt that from the options present. These don’t feel like the new best way to play a class, merely an alternative way. The Hero Class designation just denotes that there’s a layer of complexity because the core class is altered — though I found the World of Warcraft Gameplay Expansion’s guide very easy to follow, and I expect newcomers won’t struggle to build one of these three options if they follow it.
Azeroth professionals
Characters are more than their class, however.
Unfortunately, the World of Warcraft expansion doesn’t provide us with any new Backgrounds — pre-adventure origins which determine the starting skills of the player’s character — but there is a wide selection of fantastical races to select from, and various WoW factions for their party members to develop an affiliation with.
Much like classes, if there is an existing Dungeons & Dragons native — such as Dwarves or Elves — you’re asked to lift the rules from the Player’s Handbook, but races or variants of races that exist only in WoW are given bespoke traits. The monastic Pandaren can use their Inner Peace to recover more health when resting, and leave foes quaking after an attack, while Dracthyr can use their wings to glide — taking no falling damage if the drop is under 100ft, and being able to travel horizontally as they plummet.
Of course, there are also a few pages spared for mounts and creature companions — iconic World of Warcraft pets that you can ride into battle, or which offer some small buff if your friendship with them is high enough.
Factions are lifted wholesale. The Alliance and the Horde (and their respective subfactions) take center stage, but there are other groups a party may prefer to build a relationship with. There are some mechanical advantages to building renown with various factions, but they’re generally a narrative device — Dungeon Masters have a reliable quest giver in the form of friendly faction leaders; they could lock greater quest progression behind first gaining the trust of a new faction, or force players into a strained truce with rival factions to work together to achieve some greater goal (requiring careful role-playing scenarios to ensure the two sides don’t resume their hostilities).
I’ll get back to the toys and tools this Gameplay Expansion affords DMs, but finishing things off on the players' side, we need to talk about Professions.
Professions expand the basic crafting rules from the 2024 Player’s Handbook and Dungeon Master’s Guide by providing players specific guidance on how to develop their character’s foraging and item-making skills — and how to take advantage of these abilities.
For parties who spend a lot of time among civilisation, these skills aren’t going to change their games very much, I expect, but if you’re planning a campaign which ventures deep into the wilderness (which I now am after being inspired by these rules), they’ll provide a vital way for the group to replenish and upgrade their gear.
The basic idea is that crafted items and foraged resources are given specific values based on their rarity and where they were found. Collect enough resources, and you can create an item that’s worth as much as the combined value of the resources you’re using — provided they’re of the appropriate type, i.e., foraged plants and animal viscera are perfect for potions, while mined ores and animal skins are used for weapons and armour.
The rulebook stays away from generating specific recipes outside one or two examples, but it encourages DMs to bring the crafting system to life within their game world. This could involve requiring specific quantities of specific resources rather than merely generic value — i.e., a potion of waterbreathing needing five pieces of common stranglekelp, and two vials of oil extracted from the rare blackmouth fish rather than merely 100GP of parts — or turning getting a specific rare resource into a side quest — such as a Staff of Fire requiring a ruby plundered from an adult dragon’s horde, or tracking down an expert blacksmith if crafting a magic sword for the first time.
Though the rulebook encourages DMs and players to not turn their D&D adventure into a grinding slog. Repetitive actions are boring, and constantly diverting attention away from the main quest might derail the campaign into one about crafting gear with no real purpose behind the item making. Even if collecting enough of a resource might take a character a week to do in-game, this could be handled with just a couple of die rolls and only take a few minutes of real-world time — with that week either using up the character’s downtime allotment or impacting the ongoing quest if there are time-sensitive elements.
The world of Warcraft
The second half of the book is dedicated to describing the world of Azeroth. It takes you through the planet’s mythology, a brief history, and its geography — providing a quick description of key locations — before delving into a selection of iconic dungeons you could explore on your adventures, and a bestiary of foes you could face off against.
It’s very much a section dedicated to the Dungeon Master, the ‘player’ who runs the whole game for the party. Providing them with many of the tools they’ll need to manage an engaging campaign, or one-shot for the group.
Much like the rest of the book, it strikes a balance between in-depth information and leaving room for the DM’s creativity. And while it’s not the most relevant to players, I think it’s a smart idea that it’s included in this singular expansion rather than being a standalone product — making this WoW 5e release feel very approachable because you don’t need to decipher which selection of books you need; it’s just this one and the three core rulebooks (Player’s Handbook, Dungeon Master’s Guide, Monster Manual).
As a more experienced DM, I love the more light-touch approach — it provides more freedom for me to adapt the Azeroth elements for my own campaigns on or off its world — however, I do think newer Dungeon Masters will struggle with the resources here.
I understand that Dungeons & Dragons modules tend to lay things out alphabetically, but I think it would have been smarter to order the pre-made dungeons in challenge rating order so that it’s easier to find the noob-friendly expeditions. I also wish there was a more fleshed-out starter adventure that takes pre-made characters from level one to levels three or four, with guidance on how to manage running puzzles, combat encounters, and social interactions.
Coming from Magic: The Gathering, I’ve seen how Universes Beyond excels as an onboarding tool for newer players, and for the most part this World of Warcraft expansion hits the mark. However, on the actual adventure-running side, without a proper, even just a quick one-shot to guide newer Dungeon Masters through the motions of running a game, I can see it being a struggle for complete newcomers to jump into their first TTRPG game.
This one-shot would also simplify the resources you need out of the gate, because the premade character sheets and adventure could include any relevant details you’d find in the core rulebooks, like race traits and stat blocks. This reduces the barrier to entry to just this one World of Warcraft book to get into your first adventure, without removing the need to pick up the core rulebooks if you’re keen to play a full-on campaign.
As it stands, I think the World of Warcraft Gameplay Expansion for Dungeons & Dragons is mostly excellent. As someone with little affinity for this Universes Beyond IP, I’ve been pleasantly surprised by how much I have been inspired by its contents, and how excited I am to use its new player options and rules in future games.
For D&D newcomers, this expansion is superb for players — the guides under each class for how to best build its WoW counterpart are a superb detail that should help remove the initial decision paralysis that can afflict newer players who aren’t 100% sure what they should choose — but I wish it offered more support to new DMs. Folks with some experience will adore the light-touch approach, but budding Dungeon Masters (especially any drawn to the game because of this Universes Beyond tie-in) would have been well served by a dedicated one-shot guide that eases them into running a game before setting them loose.
If you’re looking for an excellent gift for the D&D fan in your life as we head into the holiday season, you’ll be hard-pressed to find a better expansion pick than this. This holds true for the World of Warcraft enjoyer in your life, but consider also offering to run their first game in Azeroth for them.

articles.title: De la multitarea a los emuladores: lo que no sabías que tu iPhone Duo puede hacer
articles.text:
El iPhone Duo ya es una realidad, y con su llegada Apple se suma de forma oficial a la categoría de los teléfonos con pantalla plegable. Más allá del panel flexible y de las funciones multitarea que acaparan los titulares, el terminal esconde una serie de herramientas poco conocidas que inciden directamente en la productividad, la privacidad y el entretenimiento del usuario.
De la posibilidad de abrir aplicaciones en pareja con un solo gesto hasta la opción de convertir el dispositivo en una consola portátil para emuladores, el recorrido por estas funciones demuestra que el plegable de Apple ofrece mucho más de lo que aparenta a simple vista.
Multitarea avanzada y gestión de aplicaciones en el iPhone Duo
La pantalla dividida es, sin duda, una de las bazas más comentadas del iPhone Duo. Sin embargo, existe una capa adicional que suele pasar desapercibida: el sistema permite crear parejas de aplicaciones para abrirlas juntas con un único gesto, en combinaciones como Safari y Notas o Mensajes y Fotos.
A esto se suma la posibilidad de reorganizar la posición de las ventanas de forma rápida mediante gestos, lo que agiliza el flujo de trabajo cuando se manejan varias tareas a la vez.
El terminal también ofrece soluciones para las aplicaciones que todavía no están optimizadas para pantallas plegables. Aunque cada vez más desarrolladores adaptan sus apps a este formato, algunas siguen mostrando franjas negras o distribuciones que no aprovechan el espacio disponible.
Para corregir esto, el iPhone Duo incluye ajustes de visualización que permiten que muchas aplicaciones saquen mejor partido a la pantalla, incluso sin que exista una optimización específica por parte de quienes las desarrollan.
La escritura en el dispositivo también se adapta al contexto de uso. El usuario puede elegir entre un teclado dividido, pensado para escribir con ambos pulgares, o uno a pantalla completa que recuerda a la experiencia de un portátil. La distribución dividida resulta más práctica para mensajes rápidos, mientras que la versión ampliada ofrece mayor superficie para correos electrónicos o textos largos.
Privacidad y accesibilidad: los ajustes menos visibles del plegable de Apple
En materia de privacidad, Apple ha incorporado un sistema que, con el terminal cerrado, limita de forma automática la visibilidad de la información que aparece en pantalla. Esta función resulta de utilidad en situaciones cotidianas como el uso del móvil en el transporte público, en cafeterías o en cualquier lugar donde otras personas puedan ver información sensible.
A esto se suma una opción pensada para facilitar el acceso con una sola mano. En lugar de deslizar desde la esquina superior derecha, el iPhone Duo permite abrir el Centro de Control pulsando directamente el grupo de iconos de batería, wifi y cobertura móvil situado en la barra de estado.
Esta alternativa simplifica el manejo del dispositivo, en especial cuando está plegado y la anchura dificulta alcanzar determinadas zonas de la pantalla.
Fotografía y videollamadas con el diseño plegable del iPhone Duo
El formato plegable del iPhone Duo también influye en el terreno fotográfico. El Modo de vista previa dual permite mostrar, de forma simultánea, la imagen captada por las cámaras delanteras y traseras, de manera que todas las personas que aparecen en la fotografía pueden comprobar el encuadre antes de disparar. El dispositivo, además, incluye animaciones pensadas para captar la atención de los niños durante este proceso.
El diseño con bisagra no se limita a ofrecer una pantalla de mayor tamaño. Cuando el terminal permanece parcialmente abierto, puede funcionar como reloj de mesilla, como soporte para videollamadas o como pantalla multimedia cuando se usa en modo manos libres.
Estas funciones aprovechan tanto la inclusión de la bisagra como la flexibilidad de uso que ofrece el dispositivo, y son, precisamente, las que diferencian al iPhone Duo del resto de la gama de iPhone.
Emuladores y videojuegos retro en el iPhone Duo
Para los aficionados a los videojuegos, el iPhone Duo ofrece una compatibilidad notable con emuladores. Su pantalla interna, de mayor tamaño, permite distribuir los controles virtuales en una mitad del panel y reservar la otra mitad para el juego, lo que se traduce en una experiencia cercana a la de las consolas portátiles clásicas.
Esta característica resulta especialmente atractiva para quienes disfrutan de títulos retro, ya que el plegable de Apple da un paso adicional frente a otros smartphones a la hora de emular consolas antiguas.

articles.title: Le CNRS tourne le dos à Microsoft et bascule 50 000 boîtes mail vers le logiciel libre français
articles.text:
Le CNRS abandonne Microsoft Exchange pour PARTAGE, la messagerie collaborative française de RENATER. La migration concerne 35 000 agents, mise sur le logiciel libre et la souveraineté numérique, avec à la clé de grosses économies.
Le Centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS) a annoncé mardi 3 novembre 2026 avoir souscrit à PARTAGE, le service de messagerie en mode SaaS opéré par RENATER, en lieu et place de Microsoft Exchange. L’organisme inscrit ce choix dans sa stratégie de sortie des GAFAM et dans un plan d’optimisation de ses coûts informatiques, puisqu'il devrait économiser plusieurs millions d'euros chaque année. Il rejoint par là même une plateforme hébergée en France, qui équipe déjà plus de 90 établissements de l’enseignement supérieur et de la recherche.
Le CNRS migre sa messagerie de Microsoft Exchange vers PARTAGE de RENATER
La bascule de Microsoft vers PARTAGE touche l'ensemble des personnels du CNRS. Chacun des quelque 35 000 agents du CNRS a reçu ou va recevoir automatiquement une adresse @cnrs.fr, désormais hébergée sur PARTAGE. S'y ajoutent les boîtes partagées, consultées par plusieurs collègues, et les boîtes de service, rattachées à une équipe ou à un service plutôt qu'à une personne, soit environ 50 000 boîtes mail au total.
Côté technique, Exchange, le logiciel de messagerie de Microsoft, que le CNRS faisait jusqu'ici héberger à l'extérieur, cède la place à Zimbra. Cette solution issue du monde du logiciel libre, dont le code est ouvert et consultable par tous, est désormais opérée par RENATER sur ses propres infrastructures.
Ce changement respecte la logique de sevrage des GAFAM engagé par le CNRS (et plus largement d'autres entités administratives françaises), avec Microsoft en ligne de mire. En plus, animé par la volonté ferme de réduire ses coûts informatiques, l'organisme table sur environ 3,5 millions d'euros d'économies par an, une manne financière considérable. François Pouget, son directeur général délégué aux ressources, estime donc que cette bascule apporte plus de souveraineté et de sécurité, pour moins cher, grâce à la mutualisation.
Une messagerie 100 % française pour la recherche
RENATER, pour « Réseau National de télécommunications pour la Technologie, l'Enseignement et la Recherche », est le réseau national qui relie entre eux les universités, écoles et laboratoires français. Ce groupement d'intérêt public, structure qui réunit plusieurs partenaires publics, leur fournit aussi des services numériques, dont PARTAGE, la fameuse messagerie pensée sur mesure pour le monde de l'éducation et de la recherche.
Les données y sont hébergées à 100 % en France, dans des centres de données et sur des réseaux qui appartiennent à RENATER. Et seuls les utilisateurs identifiés peuvent s'y connecter. C'est un vrai atout quand les e-mails véhiculent des échanges scientifiques sensibles. La plateforme compte déjà plus de 930 000 utilisateurs, qui envoient quelque 30 millions de messages par an.
Le CNRS compte parmi les membres fondateurs du GIP RENATER. Pour son directeur général, Boris Dintrans, la messagerie reste le « premier canal d'échanges » des communautés de recherche. S'appuyer sur un logiciel libre et sur ses propres datacenters et réseaux permet, selon lui, de sécuriser leurs données scientifiques. Son objectif est d'atteindre 1,5 million d'utilisateurs d'ici fin 2027. Pour y parvenir, RENATER mise notamment sur un nouveau stockage objet, une architecture capable d'absorber d'énormes volumes de données sans sacrifier leur souveraineté.

articles.title: Samsung’s official early Black Friday deals include up to AU$7,000 off TVs
articles.text:
Samsung’s official early Black Friday deals include up to AU$7,000 off TVs
Plus a range of savings on soundbars, gaming monitors and more
We’re still a month out from the official weekend of Black Friday sales in Australia, but that hasn’t stopped a number of Australian brands from dropping some respectable early deals.
Samsung is the latest to get in on the action, with a range of savings across mobiles, tablets, gaming monitors and home appliances. The standout deals, in my opinion, have to be the savings available on a range of TVs and soundbars.
For a limited time, there are discounts on Mini-LED and Micro RGB TVs, with the biggest saving being given to the brand's huge 115-inch MR95F. This monster of a screen is down from AU$41,999 to AU$34,777, a saving of AU$7,222. You can even get up to a further AU$1,100 knocked off when you trade in a TV.
Additionally, Samsung is offering a 20% saving on selected TV and soundbar bundles. For example, you can pick the 55-inch S95H OLED TV (AU$3,999) and pair it with the HW-Q800H soundbar (AU$1,999), for a total AU$4,078.40 — a saving of AU$1,019.60.
Obviously, as Samsung's flagship OLED, the S95H might not suit everyone, but fortunately, Samsung has a selection of other discounted TVs that are more accessible.
Samsung The Frame Pro | save up to AU$1,500
The latest update to the popular Frame TV series now benefits from Neo QLED mini-led technology, and it gets the wireless One Connect box too. The ushering in of Neo QLED dramatically improves picture quality, including brightness, contrast and black levels. This screen is available in 55, 65, 75 and 85-inch variants, with up to AU$1,500 knocked off depending on the price. Plus, you can save up to AU$725 extra when you trade in an old TV.
Samsung R85H Micro RGB TV | save up to AU$3,500
The R85H is the slightly lower-spec model in Samsung’s two-strong Micro RGB lineup (the other being the R95H). We haven’t had a chance to review it just yet, but Samsung regularly impresses us with its screens, so we have high hopes for this one. The biggest saving applies to the 100-inch model (now AU$9,499). Plus get up to AU$1,100 extra discount with trade in.
There are plenty more early Samsung Black Friday deals to get stuck into, and I’ve listed out the most appealing below:
Samsung is gunning for Sonos’ crown with the Music Studio 7. This 3.1.1-channel speaker can serve up "spatial sound" from a single unit, or you can pair two together for an authentic stereo presentation. They can be used with music or movies, complete with Hi-Res audio support, and the ability to be used as rear surrounds with a Q-series soundbar. Now better-than-half-price, you can concievably get a pair for less than the price of one — use code BFHOME to get the full discount.
The smaller member of the Music Studio family, the Studio 5 is a 2.1-channel affair that adopts a similarly minimalistic aesthetic. Given there’s no HDMI port, this model is best suited for music playback, but as with the 7, you can pair two together for stereo sound — use code BFHOME to save a further 5%.
This enormous 57-inch gaming monitor combines Dual UHD resolution, Mini-LED backlighting and a 240Hz refresh rate for incredibly immersive gaming. Use code BFHOME for the biggest discount.
I expect plenty more Samsung Black Friday deals to continue to pop up as we approach the official Black Friday and Cyber Monday weekend, so make sure to regularly check back to this page for all the latest highlights.

Max is a senior staff writer for TechRadar who covers home entertainment and audio first, NBN second and virtually anything else that falls under the consumer electronics umbrella third. He's also a bit of an ecommerce fiend, particularly when it comes to finding the latest coupon codes for a variety of publications. He has written for TechRadar's sister publication What Hi-Fi? as well as Pocket-lint, and he's also the editor of Australian Hi-Fi and Audio Esoterica magazines. Max also dabbled in the men's lifestyle publication space, but is now firmly rooted in his first passion of technology.

articles.title: Apple lanza las primeras versiones beta de iOS 27.3 y watchOS 27.3 con IA siempre activa
articles.text:
Apple lanzó las primeras versiones beta para desarrolladores de iOS 27.3 y watchOS 27.3, con las que comenzó a probar a gran escala un conjunto de funciones que incluye herramientas de inteligencia artificial siempre activas, una plataforma de IA y una aplicación de Salud rediseñada.
El avance forma parte de la actualización que la compañía adelantó hace más de un mes, durante un evento de lanzamiento de productos celebrado en septiembre. En aquella ocasión, la empresa presentó sus funciones de inteligencia de audio, hoy en fase de prueba, junto con cambios que afectan tanto a los iPhone como a los relojes inteligentes de la marca.
Qué son Siri Recap y Live Rewind, las funciones de audio con IA del Apple Watch
Las nuevas herramientas de audio son compatibles con los relojes inteligentes Series 12 y Ultra 4, y utilizan la inteligencia artificial junto con el micrófono del dispositivo para rastrear y analizar conversaciones cercanas. Se trata de una de las aristas más comentadas de esta actualización.
Entre ellas se encuentra Siri Recap, que convierte los puntos clave de una conversación en listas, de forma similar a lo que ya ofrecen aplicaciones como Granola y Otter. A esta se suma Live Rewind, que genera transcripciones de texto de lo dicho durante los últimos 15 segundos de un diálogo.
Apple ejemplificó su uso con un escenario cotidiano: la posibilidad de reproducir parte de una conversación con una camarera en un restaurante, sin necesidad de pedirle que repita lo que dijo.
Por el momento, estas funciones solo están disponibles en inglés y permanecen en etapa de pruebas. Según se informó, la tecnología está llamada a poner a prueba las leyes sobre escuchas ilegales vigentes en algunos estados, en particular aquellas que exigen el consentimiento de todas las partes para ser grabadas.
Privacidad y escuchas: los resguardos que promete Apple frente a la IA siempre activa
El lanzamiento de estas herramientas también amenaza con avivar preocupaciones más amplias sobre la privacidad. Con este paso, Apple se suma a Meta Platforms Inc. y a otras compañías tecnológicas en el desarrollo de dispositivos basados en IA que buscan tener un papel más activo en la vida diaria de los usuarios, desde el seguimiento de actividades físicas hasta la grabación de videos y conversaciones.
La inteligencia artificial siempre activa en el Apple Watch es una función que usa el micrófono del dispositivo para escuchar y analizar conversaciones en tiempo real, con el fin de generar resúmenes o transcripciones breves, sin que el usuario deba grabar manualmente el audio.
Cuando la compañía presentó estas funciones en septiembre, destacó varias medidas de protección. Entre ellas, una alerta sonora que se activa cada vez que un usuario solicita un resumen en directo, pensada para advertir a las personas presentes.
Apple también señaló que el procesamiento del audio ocurre en el propio dispositivo y no a través de internet, y aseguró que el audio subyacente no se graba ni se almacena. La compañía afirmó, además, que las herramientas no atribuyen los comentarios a personas específicas.
Según lo informado por la empresa, los resúmenes generados pueden omitir información considerada sensible, como datos financieros, identificadores personales o datos de autenticación, como parte de los resguardos incorporados al sistema.
La nueva app de Salud con pestañas de Información, Longevidad y Edad de Salud
Otro de los cambios centrales de iOS 27.3 es el rediseño de la aplicación Salud. La actualización incorpora una pestaña de Información, orientada a monitorizar la frecuencia cardíaca, las constantes vitales y métricas de actividad física como los pasos dados.
A esta se suma una pestaña de Longevidad, que ofrece datos más detallados sobre el corazón, la audición, el movimiento, el metabolismo y la salud mental del usuario. También se incorpora una función llamada Edad de Salud, que estima la edad de una persona a partir de su estado de salud general.
Muchas de estas opciones ya existían en plataformas de la competencia, como Whoop y Oura, que desde hace tiempo ofrecen métricas similares orientadas al seguimiento del bienestar físico y mental de sus usuarios.
Cuándo estará disponible la actualización completa de iOS 27.3
Las versiones beta de iOS 27.3 y watchOS 27.3 están disponibles, en esta primera instancia, exclusivamente para desarrolladores. Apple suele complementar este tipo de lanzamientos con una versión beta pública destinada a los consumidores en las semanas siguientes.
El lanzamiento completo y definitivo de estas actualizaciones está previsto para diciembre, cuando se espera que las nuevas funciones de inteligencia artificial, la aplicación de Salud rediseñada y el resto de las herramientas lleguen de forma general a los usuarios de iPhone y Apple Watch.

articles.title: Avant le Black Friday, le Dyson V8 Cyclone tombe à 248,99 € chez Amazon
articles.text:
Plus de trois semaines avant le Black Friday, Amazon lance une offre à durée limitée sur un aspirateur balai Dyson largement relayé ce week-end. Le V8 Cyclone y passe à 248,99 €, 61,19 € sous sa moyenne de marché des trois derniers mois, mais ses 60 minutes d’autonomie restent un maximum : les tests mesurent environ 8 minutes en puissance maximale.
Le Dyson V8 Cyclone remet à jour le V8 avec un moteur revu, 150 AW d’aspiration annoncée et une batterie à sept cellules. Amazon le vend 248,99 € jusqu’au 29 novembre, contre 310,18 € en moyenne sur le marché ces 90 derniers jours selon Affilizz, qui n’a jamais relevé de prix plus bas pour ce modèle.
Vendu et expédié par Amazon, il devance d’un centime Boulanger et Cdiscount, à 249 €, quand la Fnac et Darty l’affichaient à 279 € fin octobre. L’offre vise d’abord les foyers qui veulent un Dyson sans fil pour l’entretien courant, sans monter au prix d’un V15.
Le Dyson V8 Cyclone, balai sans fil de 150 AW à batterie amovible, est affiché à 248,99 € chez Amazon, contre 310,18 € en moyenne sur le marché ces trois derniers mois.
Pourquoi choisir le Dyson V8 Cyclone ?
- Une brosse pensée pour les poils : La brosse Motorbar utilise des lamelles en polycarbonate pour démêler les poils et les envoyer dans le collecteur. En test, seuls des cheveux d’une vingtaine de centimètres s’y sont enroulés, sans bloquer la brosse.
- Une batterie qui se change : La batterie à sept cellules se clipse et se retire sans outil. Avec une seconde batterie, vendue à part, la séance de ménage se prolonge dans un grand logement.
- Plus de gâchette à tenir : Un bouton lance l’appareil et fait défiler les trois modes, Eco, Medium et Boost. Sur une longue séance, votre index n’a plus à rester crispé.
Tapis, poils et recoins : ce que change ce V8 remis à jour
Sur les tapis, le test publié par Meilleure Innovation relève de bons résultats, avec 97 % des grains récupérés en une minute sur une moquette épaisse. Les 150 AW annoncés apportent environ 30 % de puissance de plus que le V8 d’origine, et le suceur long atteint 18 cm de profondeur dans une fente de 1,3 cm, entre un meuble et un radiateur par exemple. En alternant les modes Eco et Medium, ce même test a tenu 49 minutes, de quoi couvrir un appartement en une charge.
Le profil type est un foyer avec un animal ou des tapis, dans un logement de taille moyenne. Le mode Boost est en revanche à garder pour les saletés tenaces : il vide la batterie en 8 minutes environ, selon les mesures de Which? et de Meilleure Innovation. Le petit collecteur oblige à vider souvent, et aucune jauge n’indique la batterie restante. Les personnes sensibles au bruit noteront aussi des mesures de 78 à 83 dB avec la brosse principale, pour un poids de 2,6 à 2,7 kg selon les tests.
Face au V15 Detect et aux balais à moins de 350 €
Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs aspirateurs balais, mis à jour le 27 octobre, le Dyson V15 Detect Absolute coûte 799 € pour 240 AW et un collecteur de 0,76 l, avec une gâchette jugée fatigante à la longue. Le V8 Cyclone renonce à cette puissance et à ce volume, mais coûte plus de trois fois moins cher ce mois-ci. Le Dreame V20 Pro, à 349 €, annonce 210 AW et a tenu 72 minutes en mode automatique dans le même guide. Le V8 Cyclone se défend donc par sa brosse anti-poils et sa batterie amovible, plus que par sa fiche technique.
✅ Les points forts
- Brosse Motorbar qui démêle les poils
- Batterie à sept cellules amovible
- Démarrage par bouton, sans gâchette à maintenir
- Suceur long pour les fentes de 1,3 cm
- Plus bas prix relevé par Affilizz pour ce modèle
❌ Les limites
- Environ 8 minutes d’autonomie en mode Boost
- Petit collecteur à vider souvent
- Aucune jauge de batterie restante
- Bruyant : 78 à 83 dB avec la brosse principale
Amazon, vendeur direct, maintient cette offre à durée limitée sur le Dyson V8 Cyclone jusqu’au 29 novembre à 23 h 59, au prix de 248,99 €.
À 248,99 €, le Dyson V8 Cyclone s’aligne à un centime près sur Boulanger et Cdiscount, et passe une trentaine d’euros sous le prix relevé fin octobre à la Fnac et chez Darty. La baisse face à sa moyenne de marché reste mesurée, 61,19 €, mais elle le place sous le Dreame V20 Pro de notre comparatif sans renoncer à la brosse anti-poils de Dyson. Pour un appartement avec un chat, un chien ou quelques tapis, l’achat est cohérent.
Si vous vivez dans une grande maison ou poussez souvent la puissance au maximum, l’autonomie réelle risque de vous frustrer, sauf à prévoir une seconde batterie. Le V15 Detect garde l’avantage en puissance et en contenance, pour qui accepte un budget de 799 €. Avant de commander, demandez-vous combien de pièces vous voulez couvrir en une charge : c’est ce chiffre, plus que les 150 AW, qui décidera de votre satisfaction.

articles.title: La crisis de RAM en computadoras personales enfrenta a Elon Musk y Sam Altman: “La usan solo el 5% del tiempo”
articles.text:
Un comentario sobre la memoria de las computadoras domésticas desató un nuevo cruce público entre Elon Musk y Sam Altman.
El consejero delegado de OpenAI sostuvo que resulta ineficiente que millones de usuarios mantengan memoria DRAM en sus equipos personales cuando, según sus propias estimaciones, ese componente se utiliza apenas el 5% del tiempo.
El dueño de X y SpaceX respondió con un meme que se viralizó en horas y reavivó la rivalidad entre ambos empresarios, en medio de una escasez mundial de memoria que ya impacta en los precios de computadoras, celulares y otros dispositivos electrónicos.
El origen del comentario de Altman
Las declaraciones de Altman se produjeron el 29 de octubre durante una entrevista en el pódcast Cheeky Pint, conducido por John Collison, cofundador de Stripe. La conversación giraba en torno a si los modelos de inteligencia artificial de código abierto, ejecutados de forma local en computadoras personales, podrían reducir la dependencia de los grandes centros de datos.
El directivo de OpenAI cuestionó esa premisa y defendió que la DRAM debería priorizarse en infraestructura centralizada antes que en equipos domésticos, dado el contexto de escasez global del componente. No ofreció datos adicionales que respaldaran el porcentaje que citó durante la charla.
La respuesta de Musk con un meme
Dos días después, el 1 de noviembre, Musk publicó en X un meme basado en la escena inicial de la película Malditos bastardos, en la que un oficial nazi interpretado por Christoph Waltz interroga a una familia que esconde personas. En la versión que circuló, el personaje pregunta: “¿Le estás negando DRAM a la nube?”. Junto a la imagen, el empresario escribió: “¡La gente también merece tener su RAM!”.
La publicación generó una cadena de respuestas de usuarios que compartieron sus propios memes. Uno de los más comentados decía: “Díganle a Sam Altman que uso 64 GB de RAM para jugar RollerCoaster Tycoon. Quiero que sepa que fui yo”. Musk respondió con un emoji de risa.
Intereses comerciales detrás del debate
OpenAI mantiene algunos modelos de código abierto, pero su negocio principal se sostiene sobre sistemas de código cerrado que operan en infraestructura propia, lo que vincula la postura de Altman con los intereses de la compañía que dirige: cuantos menos usuarios ejecuten inteligencia artificial de forma local, mayor es la dependencia de los servicios en la nube que factura OpenAI.
Musk, por su parte, tampoco es ajeno a la disputa por el suministro de chips. El empresario opera los centros de cómputo Colossus, de su empresa xAI, que según declaró en septiembre ya utilizan 550.000 procesadores Nvidia GB200 y GB300, con planes de seguir ampliando esa capacidad. En meses previos, también había calificado de “extorsivos” los precios futuros anunciados por algunos proveedores de memoria.
Una escasez con proyección hasta 2027
El cruce se da en un escenario de encarecimiento sostenido de los componentes de cómputo. La firma de investigación TrendForce proyectó que los precios de contrato de la DRAM convencional subirán entre el 10% y el 15% en el cuarto trimestre de 2026, y advirtió que el giro de los fabricantes hacia la producción para servidores podría restringir aún más el suministro destinado a computadoras personales en 2027.
Ejecutivos de otras compañías del sector coincidieron en ese diagnóstico. El consejero delegado de Intel, Lip-Bu Tan, afirmó que el hardware de inteligencia artificial “se mantendrá en escasez durante los próximos dos a tres años” por restricciones persistentes en la cadena de suministro. En la misma línea, el consejero delegado de Dell, Michael Dell, anticipó que la escasez de memoria se agravará hasta 2027.
El rol de los fabricantes surcoreanos
Los principales fabricantes mundiales de DRAM, Samsung y SK hynix, también advirtieron que la escasez impulsada por la demanda de inteligencia artificial se extenderá hasta 2027 o después, con inventarios que, según trascendió, podrían reducirse a menos de diez días de suministro.
OpenAI anunció en octubre de 2025 acuerdos con ambas compañías, en el marco de su proyecto Stargate, orientados a elevar la producción de memoria avanzada hasta 900.000 arranques de oblea de DRAM por mes.
En ese contexto, Altman se reunió recientemente con cerca de 50 ejecutivos sénior de Samsung en Corea del Sur, en una gestión destinada a asegurar mayor provisión de hardware para ampliar la capacidad de cómputo de OpenAI.

articles.title: El mito de la moneda sobre el router: qué dicen los especialistas sobre este truco casero
articles.text:
Poner una moneda sobre el router de WiFi es uno de los trucos caseros que más circula en redes sociales como supuesto método para mejorar la señal de internet en casa. La teoría sostiene que el metal redirige las ondas inalámbricas y amplía la cobertura, pero especialistas en telecomunicaciones y fabricantes como Cisco coinciden en que no existe evidencia científica que respalde esta práctica.
Por el contrario, advierten que los objetos metálicos cerca del equipo pueden generar interferencias y afectar su funcionamiento, ya que la calidad de la conexión depende de factores como la ubicación del router, los materiales de la vivienda y la cantidad de dispositivos conectados.
El origen del mito de la moneda sobre el router
La idea de colocar una moneda sobre el router parte de la creencia de que el metal podría modificar la dirección de las ondas de radio, concentrando la señal hacia determinadas zonas de la vivienda.
Quienes promueven este método sostienen que el objeto metálico actuaría como un reflector capaz de aumentar el alcance del WiFi y reducir las pérdidas de señal en los rincones más alejados del hogar.
Sin embargo, esta hipótesis carece de respaldo técnico. Los routers domésticos cuentan con antenas y sistemas de transmisión calibrados para distribuir la señal de una manera específica, por lo que una moneda no tiene capacidad real de alterar ni mejorar ese rendimiento.
Poner una moneda sobre el router no mejora la señal de WiFi. Se trata de un mito sin sustento técnico: los especialistas explican que los metales no amplifican ni redirigen las ondas de forma beneficiosa, sino que pueden bloquearlas o reflejarlas de manera negativa, reduciendo el alcance efectivo de la red.
En muchos casos, cuando alguien percibe una mejora después de probar este truco, la explicación real suele estar en un cambio de ubicación del dispositivo o en variaciones normales del tráfico de la red, y no en la presencia del objeto metálico sobre el equipo.
Qué opinan los especialistas sobre esta práctica
Los especialistas en redes inalámbricas desaconsejan de manera uniforme colocar cualquier tipo de objeto metálico sobre el router.
La Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones de Estados Unidos (FCC) explica que numerosos materiales, entre ellos los metales, pueden bloquear, reflejar o debilitar las señales inalámbricas, lo que termina reduciendo el alcance efectivo de la red WiFi en lugar de ampliarlo.
En la misma línea, el fabricante de equipos de red Cisco señala que los objetos metálicos de gran tamaño y otras superficies reflectantes interfieren con la propagación de las ondas de radio. Por esa razón, la compañía recomienda instalar el router en espacios abiertos y alejados de este tipo de elementos.
A las posibles interferencias se suma otro riesgo: cubrir parcialmente el equipo puede dificultar la disipación del calor. Aunque una moneda por sí sola difícilmente provoque un sobrecalentamiento, acumular objetos sobre el router nunca resulta recomendable, dado que estos dispositivos necesitan ventilación adecuada para funcionar de manera estable.
Consejos reales para mejorar la señal del WiFi en casa
En lugar de recurrir a trucos virales sin sustento, los especialistas recomiendan aplicar medidas que sí influyen en el rendimiento de la red doméstica.
Uno de los aspectos más importantes es la ubicación del router. Instalarlo en un punto central de la vivienda y, de ser posible, en una posición elevada permite que la señal se distribuya de manera más uniforme hacia las distintas habitaciones.
También se aconseja mantener el equipo alejado de paredes gruesas, columnas de concreto, muebles grandes y electrodomésticos como hornos microondas, refrigeradores o teléfonos inalámbricos, ya que todos estos elementos pueden interferir en la propagación de las ondas.
Reiniciar el router de forma ocasional ayuda a resolver problemas temporales de rendimiento, en especial después de largos periodos de funcionamiento continuo. A esto se suma la importancia de mantener actualizado el firmware del equipo, una medida que permite corregir errores de seguridad y mejorar la estabilidad de la conexión.
Cuándo instalar un repetidor o sistema de malla WiFi
Cuando la vivienda es grande o tiene varios pisos, las soluciones caseras como la moneda sobre el router resultan todavía más insuficientes para resolver los problemas de cobertura.
En esos casos, la alternativa más eficiente es instalar un repetidor WiFi, un sistema de malla (Mesh) o un punto de acceso adicional. Estos dispositivos amplían la cobertura de la red de forma mucho más efectiva que cualquier truco casero y permiten mantener velocidades estables incluso en las habitaciones más alejadas del router principal.
Otra opción que representa una mejora significativa, tanto en alcance como en velocidad, es reemplazar un router antiguo por un modelo compatible con estándares modernos como WiFi 6 o WiFi 7.

articles.title: Major PC makers are shifting production back to China as costs rise — HP, Asus among firms moving work in efficiency push
articles.text:
Major PC makers are shifting production back to China as costs rise — HP, Asus among firms moving work in efficiency push
HP and Asus reportedly head to China to claw back savings
- HP and Asus are moving some PC production from Thailand and Vietnam back to China as AI-driven component costs climb
- The work is going to Chinese assemblers like Luxshare and Huaqin rather than Taiwan's server-focused ODMs, partly for access to Chinese memory
- TrendForce expects the share of notebooks built outside China to slip from 24% to 21% this year, with no sign yet of cheaper PCs as a result of said move back to the country
HP and Asus have started moving some of their PC manufacturing out of Thailand and Vietnam and back into China, as AI-driven price increases for memory, storage, and other components eat into already-thin hardware margins.
The shift was reported by Nikkei Asia, whose reporters Lauly Li and Cheng Ting-fang cited unnamed industry sources.
Acer is also among the brands rebalancing output, while Dell, the world's third-largest PC maker, is reportedly evaluating a similar move as manufacturers chase efficiency amid ballooning bills of materials.
Reversing the China+1 strategy as memory silicon costs hit home
The move partly reverses the "China+1" strategy the industry has pursued since the first round of US-China trade tensions.
Nikkei reported in 2023 that HP planned to move a large share of its laptop production out of China, and some PC makers even explored building plants in Saudi Arabia to sidestep tariffs on Chinese-made goods. Asus told investors in August 2025 that it had already shifted more than 90% of its US-bound motherboard and PC production to Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia.
"The move is really driven by cost pressures," a chip industry executive whose company supplies all major PC makers told Nikkei. The executive added that prices have climbed sharply for far more than just memory, leaving PC makers struggling to absorb the increases, and that Chinese contract manufacturers are winning work largely because they can undercut on price.
The scale of the squeeze shows up in the bill of materials (BOM). According to TrendForce, processors, DRAM and SSDs accounted for roughly 68% of a mainstream notebook's BOM in the third quarter of 2026, up from about 45% in the first quarter of 2025.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Omdia arrives at a similar picture from a different angle, with memory and storage rising from around 15% of a PC's total price to roughly 40%, according to figures reported previously by TechRadar Pro.
The move is a bit interesting considering that relocating assembly does not make DRAM cheaper; It implies that roughly a third of the bill, plus assembly, logistics and engineering costs, is the only place a factory move can save money, unless the new factory also comes with cheaper memory.
That is, however, precisely the pitch from Chinese contract manufacturers: a supply chain manager told Nikkei that these firms are marketing better access to Chinese-made memory chips to prospective clients, and TrendForce reports that they are waiving engineering and tooling fees to win orders. China also keeps an edge in peripheral and structural parts that other countries still struggle to match, Counterpoint analyst Ivan Lam told Nikkei.
The memory angle is not theoretical by any measure: HP, Asus and Acer qualified DRAM from China's CXMT around mid-2026 and have begun shipping it in small volumes, in a handful of notebooks sold outside the United States.
A lack of leverage meets new players vying for orders
More interestingly, the brands are not going back to their traditional partners; Quanta, Compal, Inventec and Foxconn, which have long dominated PC contract manufacturing, are pouring capacity into higher-margin AI servers.
That leaves room for Chinese assemblers such as Luxshare, Huaqin Technology and Longcheer Technology to win PC orders, and one supplier executive told Nikkei these firms are actively sending representatives to court the big brands with lower prices.
Who builds the machines may matter as much as where they are built. Servers made up more than 80% of Quanta's revenue in the second quarter of 2026, per TrendForce, and the balance of power has shifted with it. In September, Quanta reportedly halted HP notebook production for about a week after price talks stalled, resuming only once senior HP executives agreed to a cost adjustment. Neither company has confirmed the account, and Quanta has said it does not comment on individual customers.
This indicates that brands are not simply courting cheaper labor; an ODM that earns most of its money from AI racks can afford to walk away from a laptop contract, and a pool of hungry Chinese assemblers is the obvious counterweight that has sprung into action in what one can only describe as a 'needs must' situation.
The cost of the reversal lands on the suppliers that followed the brands south. One manager at a PC component supplier told Nikkei that the firm built two new production lines in Thailand for PC customers, only to watch substantial orders move back to China. "Those two lines have not yet turned profitable," the manager said, according to Tom's Hardware, adding that the firm has no idea when those orders will come back.
TrendForce estimates that the share of global notebook production outside China will fall from about 24% in 2025 to 21% in 2026, and could slip below 20% in 2027. Flipped around, that means China's share climbs from roughly 76% to 79%. In hindsight, China+1 never really dislodged China; what is being relocated back is a few points of share that the industry paid heavily to move in the first place.
The reports do not say where the China-built machines are headed, and that part is crucial because the original exodus was about US tariffs: Asus's 90% figure quoted above referred specifically to US-bound production, and the CXMT-equipped notebooks were limited to non-US markets.
One could read this as brands splitting output by destination, keeping US-bound lines in Southeast Asia while pulling the rest back to China, but nothing confirms this so far, directly or indirectly. What we do have, however, is a market backdrop that explains the urgency in play: Global PC shipments fell 20.1% year over year to 62.7 million units in Q3 2026, according to IDC, with HP suffering the steepest decline among the top five vendors at 30.9%. Asus, by contrast, slipped just 8.6%.
The memory makers see no quick fix either; SK hynix said alongside record quarterly results last week that it expects demand to outstrip supply through 2030, and Intel finance chief David Zinsner told investors, "Make no mistake, we are not optimistic about next year in terms of memory."
Acer chairman and CEO Jason Chen expects average PC prices to rise by between 5% and 20% in the fourth quarter, so any efficiency gains look set to protect margins rather than cut sticker prices in a market doomed to short-term volume decline. Chen remains an interesting outlier, however, insisting that, "It's impossible for the shortage to last until 2030!" and predicting prices will start to ease from mid-2027.
Until that happens, cost continues to matter more than diversification to avoid hemorrhaging global market share for many PC makers, and the cheapest place to build a laptop is once again the country the industry spent years trying to leave.

Rahim Amir is a UAE-based tech writer who enjoys building PCs as much as he enjoys writing about them. He has been professionally writing about PC hardware since 2023, focusing on buyer’s guides, hardware reviews, and sponsored content and features related to tech.
Having built hundreds of gaming PCs and being an avid gamer in his spare time, Rahim tends to have stronger opinions about hardware than most. This is particularly on display when he gets his way with powerful, but minimalistic RGB builds even as Small Form Factor (SFF) PCs come a close second.
