articles.text:
Dell's 15.6-inch touchscreen laptop is ideal for hybrid workers, and it's a massive $350 off for Black Friday
Dell's everyday productivity laptop will set you back under $650
Dell makes some of our favorite laptops, and the company's 15.6-inch touchscreen model offers a useful combination of performance, screen space, and connectivity.
For Black Friday, it's on sale for $650 (was $1000) at Best Buy. That's a 35% saving on a laptop with a 2K resolution touchscreen and Core i7 processor. And we'd definitely recommend it.
• Best for: Remote and hybrid workers who need a dependable Windows laptop for spreadsheets, video meetings, browser-based applications, and everyday office tasks.
• What we like: Dell's business laptop range has also proved reliable in our tests - for general work, it's well-specced. However, the real highlight is the lifted hinge that angles the keyboard slightly when opened. It's a small design detail, but one that could improve typing. The enlarged keyboard gives you more room to tap away, and the separate numeric keypad will be handy for anyone who regularly enters figures into spreadsheets or accounting software.
This Dell laptop features a 15.6-inch Full HD IPS touchscreen, 13th-generation Intel Core i7-1355U processor, 16GB DDR5 RAM, 512GB SSD, Intel UHD graphics, Wi-Fi 6, HDMI, USB-C, and Windows 11 Home.
Why we recommend it
There's a lot we like about this business-oriented laptop. Under the hood, Intel's 10-core Core i7-1355U processor offers enough performance for everyday use. The processor can boost to 5GHz when additional performance is needed. Dell's ComfortView software helps reduce blue light emissions, which will make working long hours more comfortable.
Price context & historical value
The $350 reduction represents a massive 35% discount and at $649.99, you're getting a touchscreen Windows laptop with a capable processor and a reasonable amount of memory and storage for everyday business use. This is the cheapest we've seen this particular model on sale, and coming from Dell it's a great deal.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy Dell's 15.6-inch touchscreen laptop if...
You want a well-equipped Dell laptop for home office duties, general productivity, and occasional travel. The combination of a large display and physical number pad makes it particularly suitable for administrative work.
❌ Skip Dell's 15.6-inch touchscreen laptop if...
You need a lightweight machine for frequent commuting, a brighter display for working outdoors, or dedicated graphics for demanding creative applications and modern games. A more portable laptop or one with a powerful GPU would be a better fit.

articles.title: Óscar Puente anuncia su dimisión como ministro de Transportes
articles.text:
Óscar Puente ha anunciado este martes su dimisión como ministro de Transportes tras el accidente ferroviario de Urda (Toledo), que ha dejado 69 fallecidos y se suma a la tragedia de Adamuz (Córdoba), donde murieron 46 personas en enero. El anuncio se ha producido al término de una comparecencia de más de cuatro horas ante la Diputación Permanente del Congreso de los Diputados, donde ha explicado las circunstancias de la tragedia y las medidas de seguridad previstas por el Gobierno. Puente también ha confirmado que renuncia a formar parte de las listas del PSOE para las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre, una decisión que ha justificado por motivos de "dignidad política".
Puente ha explicado que había decidido dejar el cargo pocas horas después del siniestro, aunque quiso esperar a conocer las primeras pesquisas antes de anunciarlo. Durante su intervención sostuvo que ninguna decisión u omisión suya había contribuido directamente a causar el accidente, una afirmación que no equivale a una conclusión de la investigación. Al mismo tiempo, describió su salida como una "medida necesaria y positiva" y pidió no perder de vista a quienes han sufrido la tragedia.
La decisión contrasta con la posición que el Ejecutivo había mantenido apenas unas horas antes. Según informó EFE, fuentes del Gobierno aseguraron este mismo martes que la continuidad de Puente estaba fuera de discusión y descartaron tanto su dimisión como un posible cese por parte de Pedro Sánchez. Sin embargo, la posibilidad de abandonar el cargo ya se había planteado días atrás. Tras el siniestro, el propio ministro había puesto su cargo a disposición del presidente, quien le pidió que continuara al frente de Transportes porque consideraba injusta su salida.
Qué ocurrió en Urda y qué queda por esclarecer
Ahora bien, las causas de la tragedia siguen bajo investigación, aunque las comunicaciones conocidas y las explicaciones de Puente permiten reconstruir algunas de las decisiones previas al choque. Tras la caída del sistema LZB, encargado de supervisar automáticamente la circulación, el centro de control de Adif autorizó a las 8:36 a un AVE a reanudar la marcha con normalidad, aunque el tren no volvió a ponerse en movimiento hasta aproximadamente las 8:43. Cinco minutos después, la maquinista de un Iryo comunicó que seguía detenida. El centro recibió el aviso, pero no ordenó detener el AVE, que terminó colisionando con el otro convoy alrededor de las 8:53.
La marcha del ministro deja ahora abiertas dos cuestiones: quién asumirá la cartera de Transportes y cómo se ejecutarán las medidas de seguridad anunciadas este martes. El Gobierno ha presentado un plan extraordinario que contempla una revisión de los sistemas de la línea Madrid-Sevilla y la doble validación de las órdenes de circulación cuando fallen los mecanismos automáticos de protección. También ha aprobado 30 millones de euros en ayudas y anticipos de indemnizaciones para los afectados. Mientras continúa la investigación, Transportes ha solicitado autorización judicial para reconstruir el tramo dañado. Puente estimaba que la línea podría reabrirse en un máximo de diez días naturales una vez obtenido ese permiso.

articles.title: Roborock F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2 : l’aspirateur laveur à vapeur s’attaque aux zones qu’on oublie
articles.text:
Le Roborock F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2 est commercialisé en France ce 3 novembre, au prix conseillé de 799 euros. Cette nouvelle génération renforce le débit de vapeur et ajoute un bras mobile pour nettoyer au plus près des plinthes.
Encore un F25 chez Roborock ? Le constructeur continue d’étoffer une gamme qui demande désormais un peu d’attention pour s’y retrouver. Présenté à l’IFA en septembre, le F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2 prend la relève du modèle Ultra avec une finition Chocolat Moka, qui change des habituels appareils noirs ou blancs. Le changement ne se limite heureusement pas à la peinture. Le premier F25 Ultra nous avait déjà convaincus par son lavage, avec quelques réserves sur l’autonomie. Son successeur cherche surtout à mieux traiter les taches tenaces et les zones que la brosse laisse parfois de côté.
Plus de vapeur, avec quelques précisions derrière les chiffres
Le mode Turbo Steam annonce un débit de vapeur de 5 000 mg/min, contre 2 000 mg/min sur le précédent Ultra. Roborock promet ainsi jusqu’à 2,5 fois plus de vapeur pour décoller les salissures incrustées. L’appareil conserve également un mode de lavage à l’eau chaude, désormais annoncé à 90 °C, contre 86 °C auparavant.
Attention toutefois à la température de vapeur de 180 °C mise en avant : elle est mesurée à la sortie du chauffage interne, et non à la sortie de vapeur ou sur le sol. Même nuance pour les 30 secondes de préparation : le protocole du constructeur décrit un redémarrage à chaud, après une précédente utilisation du mode Vapeur et trois minutes d’arrêt.
Ces précisions ne retirent pas son intérêt au système, mais évitent de lui prêter des performances que les chiffres ne démontrent pas.
Un petit bras pour les bordures, des roues pour les manœuvres
L’autre nouveauté est le bras SensEdge. Il se relève lorsque l’on pousse l’appareil pour éviter de repousser l’eau sale et les déchets vers l’avant, puis aide à récupérer l’humidité lors du mouvement de retour. Roborock annonce un nettoyage à 0 mm des bordures sur trois côtés, sans pour autant garantir un sol totalement exempt d’eau résiduelle.
On retrouve les roues motorisées SlideTech 2.0, qui accompagnent la poussée et la traction, ainsi que l’inclinaison à 180° pour passer sous les meubles. L’assistance sera bienvenue avec un poids indiqué de 7,6 kg. Les réservoirs accueillent un litre d’eau propre et 720 ml d’eau sale.
L’autonomie annoncée atteint 100 minutes en mode Éco, mais descend à 30 minutes en mode Vapeur. Il faudra donc choisir son chiffre selon le nettoyage envisagé.
Le F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2 est proposé sur le site de Roborock et chez ses partenaires Fnac, Darty, Boulanger et Amazon. Sa station lave et sèche automatiquement le rouleau ; vider le bac à eau sale après le ménage reste, en revanche, à la charge de son propriétaire.

articles.title: CISA Confirms Hackers Exploiting WordPress Core Flaw During Software Upgrades
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added a security flaw in WordPress Core to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.
The high-severity vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-119977 (CVSS score: 8.1), is a case of Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition that could be exploited to achieve arbitrary code execution on affected servers. Patches for the flaw were released late last month.
"WordPress Core contains a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during the upgrade window," CISA said. "This is due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades."
Details of the flaw emerged last week when Wordfence said exploiting the vulnerability does not require an account on the site. That said, it does require an attacker to exploit a brief window during a complete Core update that could allow unauthenticated code execution.
During the first 21 hours after public disclosure, the WordPress security company said it recorded more than 18,500 requests targeting staged "setup-config.php" installer paths. As of writing, 12,632 attacks attempting to exploit the flaw have been blocked in the last 24 hours.
Telemetry data from Previdian shows that three exploitation attempts have been recorded against its honeypot censors from an IP address geolocated in the U.K. The exploitation events were observed on October 30, 2026.
With exploitation now officially confirmed by CISA, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies have time until November 6, 2026, to apply the fixes.

articles.title: Un software espía infectó equipos con Windows que tenían todas las actualizaciones de seguridad instaladas
articles.text:
La empresa de seguridad Kaspersky halló en equipos con Windows un programa malicioso llamado BlackX que se instaló pese a que las máquinas tenían todas las actualizaciones al día. Según la investigación, la protección de Microsoft requiere un paso manual del administrador que pocos realizaron.
Según Kaspersky, el ataque se detectó a comienzos de 2026 contra organizaciones diplomáticas de Asia Central. La empresa de seguridad lo atribuyó, con confianza moderada, al grupo de hackers APT41 y presentó la investigación en la conferencia Security Analyst Summit 2026, en Bali, Indonesia.
BlackX es un bootkit: un programa malicioso que se ejecuta antes de que arranque Windows, cuando el sistema todavía no tiene activas muchas de sus defensas. Kaspersky lo describe como una versión modernizada de BlackLotus, un software que se vendía en la web oscura desde 2022.
Para instalarlo, los atacantes ya habían entrado en las redes internas de las víctimas y obtenido permisos de administrador. El bootkit funciona como un mecanismo de permanencia invisible y prolongada en los equipos.
Una falla de 2022 que sigue abierta
BlackX aprovecha “Baton Drop”, una falla del gestor de arranque de Windows registrada como CVE-2022-21894, que permite saltarse Secure Boot. Esta función verifica que, al encender la computadora, solo se ejecute software de confianza. Según el medio especializado Ars Technica, Microsoft corrigió la falla en 2022.
Sin embargo, la corrección no bastaba: el sistema seguía confiando en el certificado digital con el que se firmaron los gestores de arranque antiguos y vulnerables. En mayo de 2023, Microsoft inició un proceso de varios años: agregó un certificado nuevo y, en 2024, ofreció una forma de revocar el anterior, llamado “Windows Production PCA 2011”.
Pero la revocación no ocurre al instalar el parche. Kaspersky explicó que el administrador debe activarla de forma manual y que Microsoft diseñó el proceso de esa manera. Ars Technica añadió que revocar el certificado antes de instalar el nuevo puede dejar un equipo sin poder arrancar.
“Es extremadamente inusual que un administrador de sistemas tome medidas adicionales después de instalar una actualización”, escribió un investigador de Kaspersky. Según el informe, las instrucciones para activar la protección están “enterradas” en el sitio de Microsoft y resultan difíciles de advertir.
La respuesta de Microsoft y los límites del caso
Un portavoz de Microsoft respondió por correo a Ars Technica que la empresa recomienda seguir la guía de un artículo de su base de conocimiento, publicado dos semanas antes. Según el medio, ese texto no advierte que los parches publicados hasta ahora no protegen contra los ataques con Baton Drop.
El paso manual está descrito en otro artículo de 2023. Ars Technica señaló que no está clara la situación de los usuarios domésticos de Windows. Kaspersky indicó que todas las víctimas de BlackX usaban una versión de Windows completamente actualizada.
El certificado PCA 2011 venció el 19 de octubre de 2026, pero eso no impide que se carguen los componentes vulnerables. Según Kaspersky, mientras los administradores no lo agreguen a la lista de firmas prohibidas, los equipos siguen confiando en él.
Kaspersky sostiene que es probable que los atacantes supieran que pocas organizaciones activaban manualmente el parche. Por eso, afirmó, decidieron invertir tiempo en entender BlackLotus y crear una copia. En el ataque investigado, Kaspersky bloqueó el intento de desactivar antivirus.
De haber funcionado, el siguiente paso habría sido instalar un programa espía que utiliza servicios legítimos en la nube, como Google Drive, OneDrive y Yandex Disk, para robar información y vigilar a las víctimas. Microsoft no ha informado una fecha para activar la revocación de forma automática.

articles.title: Windows 11 8GB RAM configurations get a performance boost — As AI demand keeps pushing prices up, Microsoft says Windows is now 20% more responsive, multitasking 40% faster on memory-constrained machines
articles.text:
Windows 11 8GB RAM configurations get a performance boost — As AI demand keeps pushing prices up, Microsoft says Windows is now 20% more responsive, multitasking 40% faster on memory-constrained machines
Microsoft's claimed performance gains will need to be tested
Following a resurgence of 8GB RAM laptops earlier this year, and in the wake of promises to improve Windows 11 performance using just 8GB of RAM, Microsoft has today announced what it claims are a series of performance improvements. Driven by an ongoing global PC component shortage that is forcing manufacturers to dumb down specs, the company says that with 8GB of RAM, Windows is now 20% more responsive and 40% faster when it comes to multitasking.
The development shared today by Microsoft is an update to a commitment earlier this year to improve the quality and performance of Windows 11, a major bugbear of users since its launch. Microsoft says it has taken a three-pronged approach to memory optimization: making better use of memory in Windows 11 PCs, protecting interactions that need to feel instant, and ensuring key apps and Windows use less memory. While the company admits you'll be able to do more on 16GB or 32GB of RAM, it says "we're making sure you can do more, even with 8GB."
The headline performance gain is a claim that Windows is now up to 20% more responsive on 8GB PCs. Likewise, multitasking is now purportedly 40% faster in Microsoft's lab tests. Of course, these are internal tests conducted in favorable conditions by Microsoft.
Microsoft says it has tuned compression for useful apps and data, and can now keep up to 2GB more of your active data in memory, rather than moving it to storage. In practice, this should mean that apps and tabs left open should be less likely to reload when you go back to them.
The claim of 20% more responsiveness specifically relates to tasks like opening Start, searching, right-clicking, opening Settings, using the Snipping Tool, and opening File Explorer. The company says it has achieved this by backing off background tasks like indexing while you're using your PC actively. Edge now reportedly opens up to 33% faster. There's also an Efficiency Mode for Microsoft Teams, which can be set to on by default, improving launch times by 20%.
Microsoft says that its claims of 40% speed boosts to multitasking are based on a demanding workflow of 20 Microsoft Edge Tabs, a 4K video, large Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files, Outlook, and File Explorer all being opened one after the other.
Other improvements include reducing committed-memory growth by up to 900 MB in apps like Microsoft Edge and 365 apps, and reducing the memory footprint of Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook by 360MB. Third-party apps can also benefit from improved memory management, with Microsoft stating WhatsApp is already taking advantage.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Moving forward, Microsoft says it has plans to make memory compression even smarter and more efficient. Windows features and apps will share common parts, such as Search and Widgets using one web Engine, for instance. WinUI 3 apps like File Explorer and Notepad will be designed to use less memory and open faster, and Microsoft is working with PC makers and silicon manufacturers to reduce how much memory a PC needs to hold in reserve to support its hardware, making more space for Windows.

articles.title: Google offers tepid response to accusations it would hold Search hostage if schools restrict AI tools - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google offers tepid response to accusations it would hold Search hostage if schools restrict AI tools
Google LLC today faced a barrage of criticism after the company warned that if schools restricted their students from using its artificial intelligence tools, the same students wouldn’t be able to use Search.
The fallout came after the company announced a slew of new products for classrooms. Teachers and schools were told that the new AI tools would come with features that will allow for limitations or complete blocks of the features, but if teachers or schools should take that route, students would not be able to use Google Search. Some media described it as rather cunning behavior from the tech giant.
“After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search,” Google said in a blog post. “Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.”
A New York Times article followed the announcement and explained that where schools have banned the use of AI or if they limit AI in the classroom, the students would not have access to Search. Since Google’s suite of products are a mainstay in classrooms all over the U.S., the backlash was imminent.
“Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani wrote on X. “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children. Our public schools exist to serve students, not to grow the profit margins of Big Tech.”
Sen. Bernie Sanders from Vermont was equally chastising, writing on X, “Google is threatening schools” and using what amounts to “extortion.” Lina Khan, former chair of the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, was similarly unimpressed, writing that Google was trying to, “coerce schools into adopting AI.”
Google was quick to respond. In a post on X, the company said its new policy is about giving schools more control over how students use AI. Gemini chatbot, Gemini Notebook, the company explained, will be turned off by default, but “schools are in control.”
“We are also updating Search for schools to make it better for learning,” Google added. “Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork.” The company explained that it was aware of the dangers of students embracing the “AI shortcut” and effectively not engaging their brains.
However, Google seemed to ignore the basis of the criticism regarding Search not being available when AI functions were turned off. Given the company has found itself under the gun many times in recent years for its business tactics, and in light of studies showing overuse of technology can have a harmful impact on children, the response seemed to critics tepid at best.

articles.title: Étudiants qui utilisez ChatGPT, ne ratez pas les 50 € offerts par OpenAI
articles.text:
ChatGPT : OpenAI offre 50 € de crédits aux étudiants français via UNiDAYS
Via UNiDAYS, la plateforme de réductions réservée aux étudiants, OpenAI a une offre difficile à refuser pour les personnes utilisant l'IA : 50 € de crédits ChatGPT.
OpenAI a un petit cadeau à destination des étudiants. En tout cas ceux qui utilisent ou veulent utiliser ChatGPT : un crédit de 50 € (l'équivalent de 1 400 crédits) pour utiliser l'IA. Quelques conditions s'appliquent pour pouvoir en profiter, à commencer par posséder un compte étudiant valide sur la plateforme UNiDAYS.
OpenAI fait un petit cadeau, bien après la rentrée
Alors que Google offre un an d'AI Plus depuis septembre dernier, OpenAI a décidé de timidement rattraper la concurrence pour tenter de motiver des étudiants à préférer ChatGPT. L'offre, disponible sur la plateforme de réductions pour les étudiants, est sans surprise limitée à un seul échange pas étudiant.
Il est à noter que les crédits expirent 60 jours après avoir été appliqués au compte OpenAI, et ne peuvent être utilisés que sur les comptes nouveaux ou existants ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus ou Pro. Il n'est donc pas obligatoire de déjà posséder un abonnement pour pouvoir profiter de ce bonus, qui peut être utilisé pour tester les fonctionnalités les plus puissantes d'OpenAI et les différents outils de ChatGPT, comme ChatGPT Work (l'IA dédiée aux projets, tâches et équipes) ou Codex (IA orientée développement).
Au milieu d'idées d'utilisation de ces crédits (adapter son CV à une offre d'emploi, créer un plan d'étude, coder...), OpenAI précise que les crédits ne sont utilisables que depuis ChatGPT sur un navigateur web.
A titre d'information, UNiDAYS propose de nombreuses autres offres à destinations des étudiants, notamment dans la catégorie logiciels et abonnements. Il est par exemple question de réductions sur des offres chez Proton, Disney+, Deezer, Evernote ou encore NordVPN. Les 50 € offerts pour ChatGPT est la seule offre concernant l'intelligence artificielle pour le moment.

articles.title: Sous-titrer une vidéo à la main ? Ce logiciel gratuit fait le plus gros du boulot
articles.text:
Pour créer des sous-titres, il faut synchroniser les textes avec les dialogues, vérifier leur durée, corriger les erreurs et parfois traduire l’ensemble. Subtitle Edit réunit toutes ces opérations dans un logiciel gratuit et open source, avec des outils capables d’automatiser une bonne partie du processus.
Un simple fichier vidéo est la plupart du temps le point de départ d'un travail de sous-titrage. Subtitle Edit permet de créer ou modifier des sous-titres dans de nombreux formats, mais aussi de générer automatiquement une transcription à partir de la bande sonore. La version 5 fonctionne désormais sous Windows, macOS et Linux.
De la bande-son au sous-titre synchronisé
Le logiciel peut transcrire les dialogues grâce à plusieurs moteurs de reconnaissance vocale, dont différentes variantes de Whisper, développé par OpenAI. Certains de ces moteurs fonctionnent entièrement en local, avec une accélération GPU possible selon le matériel. Les transcriptions peuvent ensuite être corrigées directement dans l’éditeur.
Pour ajuster le timing, Subtitle Edit affiche la forme d’onde de la piste audio, qui montre les variations de volume. Si nécessaire, il peut afficher également un spectrogramme, qui montre la puissance des différentes fréquences. Il devient alors possible de repérer visuellement le début et la fin d’une phrase et de déplacer les sous-titres avec une précision chirurgicale. Les changements de plans peuvent également être détectés, ce qui permet de caler facilement les sous-titres en fonction des transitions.
Un couteau suisse pour la postproduction
Subtitle Edit va plus loin qu’un simple éditeur de fichiers SRT. Il peut traduire automatiquement des sous-titres, utiliser l’OCR sur des sous-titres intégrés sous forme d’images, convertir de nombreux formats et même incruster définitivement les textes dans une vidéo. La version 5 ajoute aussi des outils pour couper ou réencoder une vidéo directement depuis l’application.
L’ensemble est gratuit et open source, avec un fonctionnement principalement local. Certaines fonctionnalités peuvent toutefois nécessiter des services en ligne, notamment pour la traduction ou pour certains moteurs de reconnaissance.
Subtitle Edit s’adresse aussi bien au créateur qui doit sous-titrer ponctuellement une vidéo qu'aux personnes qui travaillent régulièrement avec des contenus multilingues. Un temps d'adaptation est à prévoir pour le prendre en main, mais c’est justement ce qui en fait un outil particulièrement complet.

Black Friday web hosting FAQs
Is this the best time of year to buy web hosting?
In our experience, Black Friday is almost always the best time of year to buy web hosting. The deals are typically deeper than those we see at other times of the year.
What is web hosting?
Web hosting is the infrastructure that makes your website accessible over the internet. More and more web hosting providers also provide website building tools bundled in with hosting. For businesses, creatives, and ecommerce shops, it's an essential tool.
What is WordPress hosting?
WordPress hosting is a service that stores your website on a server and makes it accessible on the internet. There are different types of WordPress hosting for a variety of people. At the bottom end there is shared hosting which usually comes with WordPress preinstalled and is restricted on what you can and cannot do with your site. These come in two flavours: managed and unmanaged. Unmanaged means that you need to take care of updates and security yourself and managed WordPress hosting means that they're taken care of for your. You can go up a level and get a VPS and install WordPress on it which will give you the most flexibility but also the highest management cost.
What is cloud hosting?
Cloud hosting is a type of hosting in which the resources (think CPU, RAM, & storage) are not in one computer but spread across many many many computers in different locations. A hypervisor (basically some fancy software) connects them together and balances the computing loads.
This type of hosting enables features like auto scaling (adding extra CPU, RAM, or storage) when you need it) and geo redundancy (if a disaster happens in one location the workloads can be completed by a computer in a different location).
What's email hosting?
Like a website an email needs an address. Otherwise emails wouldn't know where to go. Mailboxes also need storage. Essentially email hosting is managing the address and providing storage but it often comes with a load of other features like forwarding or marketing tools.
What if I don't like the web host provider after I've signed up to a Black Friday deal?
Not a problem. The majority of the hosts offer money-back guarantees so if you're unhappy with your service you can get a refund. Just double check before you buy.
Will I get these Black Friday deals when I renew the contract?
No, unfortunately not. Renewal rates are priced higher than the Black Friday cost. You can lock in the cheaper rate when you select a longer plan, e.g. 36 months - but even then, once the plan ends, the cost will increase.
When do Black Friday web hosting deals end?
Black Friday is on November 27 this year, so I'd try to lock in a deal before then, as some providers may not carry them through the weekend and into Cyber Monday, which falls on November 30 (although many do, from past experience).

articles.title: mSecure Warns Users to Change Passwords, Reset 2FA and Passkeys After Suspicious Activity
articles.text:
Customers of the mSecure password manager are being urged to act now to protect the confidential information they store in it, possibly by changing passwords, resetting two-factor authentication (2FA), and removing passkeys.
The warning came in an email sent on November 3 in the name of developer mSeven Software. It says the company recently learned of suspicious activity linked to the app but does not say what happened or whether anyone's stored data was exposed.
The email says it went to current and former mSecure customers. A customer who received it posted its text in a thread on mSecure's support forum on November 3.
As of 18:00 UTC on November 3, mSeven had posted nothing about the email on mSecure's X and Facebook accounts. No staff member had replied in that forum thread.
The email says mSeven started an investigation, took steps to limit the problem and brought in outside cybersecurity experts. It does not name the systems involved, say when the activity happened or whether it has stopped, or give the number of people who received the email.
mSecure can sync a customer's vault through mSecure Cloud, Dropbox, iCloud or Wi-Fi. The email does not say whether it matters which of these a customer uses.
mSecure 7 can keep passkeys and 2FA codes in the vault next to passwords, on its Essentials plan and above. The email's advice is about protecting information stored in mSecure. The email does not say whether the 2FA and passkey steps cover those stored items, the mSecure account's own sign-in, or both.
mSecure says vault data is encrypted on the customer's device before it is synced, and that even its developers cannot access customers' information.
In mSecure 6.1.5 for Android, mSeven could, in theory, access stored data, according to Germany's Federal Office for Information Security (BSI), which found this in a study published in December 2025. The BSI tested only that version, and its results may have changed with later updates.
The email does not say whether the suspicious activity reached vault data or the keys that protect it.
What the Email Asks Customers to Do
The email offers its steps as possibilities and does not say which accounts to deal with first or how to carry out each step. It also does not say whether customers should keep using mSecure, including to store their new passwords.
As of 18:00 UTC on November 3, the newest iPhone version of mSecure in Apple's App Store was 7.1.0, released on October 23.

articles.title: AI Hardware’s Hidden Cost: Between Orders and Output - EE Times
articles.text:
Alphabet’s inventory rose from $2.4 billion at the end of 2025 to $13.3 billion in September 2026, reflecting in part Google’s expanding role as an AI hardware supplier.
Google now sells complete Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) systems for deployment in customer facilities, alongside the computing capacity it provides through Google Cloud. Selling hardware brings a different set of working capital demands.
During Alphabet’s third-quarter earnings call, CFO Anat Ashkenazi described the process: Customers sign contracts, orders enter backlog, and Google begins building the systems ahead of delivery and billing. Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian confirmed that components are procured after contracts are signed.
The contracts provide demand visibility. Alphabet, however, does not disclose how much of its inventory consists of TPU systems or how quickly those systems will be delivered.
That leaves an increasingly relevant measure of the AI buildout: the time between committing capital and putting hardware to work.
Intel’s manufacturing tradeoffs
Intel’s third-quarter disclosures show how difficult that conversion can become.
CFO David Zinsner confirmed that manufacturing capacity in Oregon originally planned for Intel 18A-based Panther Lake processors is being redirected toward Intel 3 to support demand for Granite Rapids server CPUs.
The additional Intel 3 capacity is expected in the second half of 2027. Intel continues to develop and manufacture products on 18A, but the reallocation shows how changes in demand can force manufacturers to revisit capacity plans across process generations.
Increasing wafer output is only part of Intel’s challenge.
CEO Lip-Bu Tan also identified shortages of advanced organic substrates used in EMIB packaging as a constraint on scaling production. The company is working to improve yields and cycle times while securing additional substrate supply.
Following the quarter, Intel entered two agreements to secure future substrates, with estimated funding requirements of $5.3 billion to $6.1 billion. Approximately $3.3 billion is expected through the end of 2027, although some contractual terms remained unfinished.
The wafer capacity decision and EMIB substrate constraints affect different parts of Intel’s manufacturing operations. Both illustrate how production plans depend on capacity beyond the fabrication process itself.
Meanwhile, Intel recorded higher inventory-related charges in its client computing business as it adjusted product mix to demand.
Server products faced supply constraints while other products generated inventory charges. The aggregate inventory balance reveals little about which components can be turned into shipments.
A fabricated die still requires packaging and testing. Substrates are engineered for specific electrical, thermal, and mechanical requirements. Components intended for one processor cannot necessarily be redirected to another.
AI accelerators face similar dependencies. TSMC’s CoWoS packaging technology and high-bandwidth memory integration add manufacturing stages that must scale alongside wafer production.
More wafer starts do not automatically produce more shippable processors.
Inventory moves upstream
Lam Research ended September with $4.55 billion in inventory, up from $4.28 billion in June. Nearly the entire increase came from raw materials. Work in process declined slightly, while finished goods remained largely unchanged.
KLA’s inventory increased from $3.65 billion to $4.09 billion over the same period, with increases in raw materials and work in process.
The composition matters. Components and partially assembled equipment absorb capital before completed systems can be delivered. Their accumulation may reflect production plans, supplier lead times, or changes in customer requirements.
Neither company’s figures establish that finished machines are stranded by shortages.
Semiconductor manufacturing equipment contains highly specialized components that must meet demanding optical, mechanical, electrical, and process specifications. Suppliers may need to secure those components well before a machine reaches the customer.
Changes in delivery schedules can therefore affect working capital long before they appear in revenue.
More output from installed equipment
ASML reported €3.29 billion in third quarter installed-base management sales, above guidance, partly driven by demand for productivity upgrades. The figure also includes services and other activities.
For chipmakers, improving the throughput of equipment already installed can provide capacity without waiting for another machine to be manufactured, delivered, and qualified.
But a faster lithography system increases completed wafer output only when the rest of the production line can accommodate it.
Deposition, etch, metrology, and inspection capacity must keep pace. Yield losses and downtime can erase gains in nominal equipment speed.
The economics of an upgrade depend on whether it addresses the operation limiting production. A relatively modest improvement at that point can be more useful than additional capacity elsewhere in the fab.
From packaging to power
The same dependencies continue beyond semiconductor manufacturing.
AI accelerators must be integrated with memory, networking, power delivery, and cooling. Completed systems then need data centers capable of operating them.
Grid connections, transformers, substations, and cooling infrastructure follow development schedules that can differ substantially from semiconductor production cycles.
A system may be ready for installation before the facility intended to operate it is ready to receive it.
Alphabet’s September filing shows the scale of the associated commitments. The company disclosed $924.4 billion in future purchase commitments covering technical infrastructure, inventory, energy, content, and other requirements. It also reported $130.5 billion in future payments for leases that had not commenced, primarily associated with data center and energy infrastructure.
These are different contractual arrangements, including commitments unrelated to AI. They are neither a single capital expenditure forecast nor amounts already spent.
They do, however, illustrate how far ahead companies must plan and commit resources.
A processor generation can change while the buildings, electrical systems, and supply agreements intended to support computing demand remain in place. Compatibility and flexibility become important when assets have such different useful lives.
The timing has financial consequences as well. Hardware suppliers commit working capital before delivery, while cloud operators and AI developers make long-term commitments to future computing capacity.
Signed contracts may improve revenue visibility, but they cannot shorten equipment qualification, grid connections, or facility commissioning.
The longer the interval between capital commitment and productive use, the greater the pressure on working capital and investment returns.
Follow the conversion
The next earnings reports should help establish how quickly the industry’s commitments are becoming productive assets.
At Alphabet, the measures are TPU system deliveries, inventory conversion, and operating cash flow.
At Intel, the test is whether additional Intel 3 capacity translates into server shipments, alongside progress on substrate availability and manufacturing yields.
For Lam and KLA, inventory composition should be assessed against equipment deliveries, customer commitments, and inventory provisions.
At fabs, installed equipment must translate into qualified capacity and completed wafers. For data center operators, the corresponding measures include facility commissioning and utilization of installed computing systems.
A wafer can be finished while its package remains unavailable. A machine can be installed without increasing fab output. A completed AI system can wait for power.
The capital has already been committed at each stage. The financial return depends on when the entire system can operate.
Disclosure: The author previously held finance and operations roles at Intel. This analysis is based on publicly available company filings and earnings disclosures.

Intel Foundry Gains Steam, but External Wins Remain Key

articles.title: Amazon revive el marco digital de fotos con una versión que elige tus mejores imágenes con IA
articles.text:
Los antiguos portarretratos digitales regresan con una propuesta que incorpora inteligencia artificial para organizar fotografías y mostrar recuerdos de forma automática. El nuevo Alexa Photo Frame cuenta con una pantalla táctil de 10 pulgadas, se conecta con Amazon Photos y permite seleccionar imágenes mediante comandos de voz.
Amazon busca recuperar un dispositivo que tuvo popularidad durante los años 2000: el marco digital de fotografías. La compañía presentó el Alexa Photo Frame, un equipo que utiliza inteligencia artificial para seleccionar imágenes, organizar recuerdos y mostrarlos en una pantalla sin que el usuario tenga que buscarlos manualmente en su teléfono.
La propuesta combina las funciones tradicionales de estos portarretratos con las capacidades de Alexa+, el asistente de inteligencia artificial de Amazon. En lugar de limitarse a reproducir una presentación con fotografías elegidas previamente, el dispositivo puede identificar cuáles considera más adecuadas para mostrar y organizarlas según diferentes criterios.
El equipo incorpora una pantalla táctil antirreflejos de alta definición de 10 pulgadas y está disponible con un diseño de paspartú blanco texturizado. Algunas versiones también incluyen acabados de madera auténtica, como abedul o nogal, para integrarse en distintos espacios del hogar.
Cómo funciona la inteligencia artificial del nuevo marco de Amazon
Una de las principales características del Alexa Photo Frame es su capacidad para seleccionar fotografías mediante Alexa+. El sistema analiza diferentes elementos de las imágenes, como las personas que aparecen, el momento en que fueron tomadas y el contenido de cada escena.
Por ejemplo, puede dar prioridad a fotografías en las que las personas estén sonriendo y tengan buena iluminación. También puede adaptar las imágenes que muestra según la época del año y evitar contenidos que no corresponden a recuerdos personales, como capturas de pantalla o recibos.
El usuario también puede establecer qué personas quiere destacar. De esta manera, el marco puede priorizar fotografías de familiares, amigos o cualquier persona seleccionada previamente.
Otra posibilidad consiste en pedirle directamente al asistente que muestre imágenes relacionadas con un tema específico. Mediante comandos de voz, se pueden solicitar fotografías de un viaje, una mascota o una persona determinada.
La inteligencia artificial también puede encontrar similitudes entre imágenes tomadas en diferentes momentos. Así, el dispositivo puede colocar juntas fotografías de una misma persona o de experiencias parecidas, incluso cuando fueron capturadas con varios años de diferencia.
Además, Amazon incorporó una función para añadir notas de voz a las fotografías. Esto permite acompañar una imagen con una explicación o un relato sobre el momento en que fue tomada, de modo que los recuerdos no se limiten a una presentación visual.
Amazon Photos permite compartir fotografías con familiares
El Alexa Photo Frame se conecta con Amazon Photos, el servicio de almacenamiento de imágenes de la compañía. Esta integración permite sincronizar las fotografías del usuario para que estén disponibles en el dispositivo.
Los miembros de Amazon Prime cuentan con almacenamiento ilimitado para fotografías en alta resolución dentro de este servicio. Además, familiares y amigos pueden compartir imágenes directamente con el marco, una función que facilita mantener actualizados los recuerdos que aparecen en la pantalla.
De esta manera, el dispositivo no depende exclusivamente de las fotografías almacenadas en el teléfono de su propietario. También puede recibir imágenes de otras personas, siempre que estas utilicen las opciones de intercambio disponibles.
La integración con Alexa+ busca simplificar la administración de los recuerdos digitales. En lugar de crear álbumes o seleccionar manualmente cada fotografía, el usuario puede dejar que el asistente organice parte del contenido y decidir qué imágenes quiere ver.
Cuánto cuesta el Alexa Photo Frame
El nuevo marco digital ya está disponible en Estados Unidos. Su precio depende del acabado elegido: la versión negra cuesta 199,99 dólares, mientras que los modelos con madera de abedul o nogal parten de los 229 dólares.
Cada dispositivo incluye un periodo de prueba de 90 días de Alexa+. Una vez finalizado, será necesario contar con una suscripción para continuar utilizando algunas de las funciones del asistente.
Por ahora, Amazon no ha anunciado cuándo llegará el Alexa Photo Frame a otros mercados. Su lanzamiento representa una nueva apuesta por recuperar un dispositivo que perdió protagonismo con la expansión de los teléfonos inteligentes, pero que ahora busca encontrar un lugar en los hogares mediante la inteligencia artificial.

Tuesday, November 3rd 2026
GTA 6 Will Need Up to 212 GB of Storage, Pre-Load Now Starts November 10
Rockstar has moved GTA 6's pre-load up by two days. According to an updated Newswire post and support page, digital pre-orders can now start downloading on November 10, instead of the November 12 date announced back in June. The exact timing depends on the console. On PlayStation 5, the pre-load unlocks at midnight local time in the user's respective time zone. Xbox Series X|S gets a single global unlock at 12 a.m. GMT, which works out to 7 PM ET or 4 PM PT on November 9 for players in North America, while the full launch is still set for November 19.
Rockstar also put a number on the file size for the first time, saying the pre-load will need "up to 212 GB of available space depending on your device." That's a touch above the 210 GB figure a dataminer pulled from the PlayStation Store backend last week, but it's safe to say it was an accurate leak. The "depending on your device" bit suggests the PS5 and Xbox builds won't be exactly the same size, though Rockstar didn't share a per-console breakdown. That does mean that on a launch PS5 with roughly 667 GB of usable storage, GTA 6 alone would eat close to a third of the drive.We know that GTA 6 "physical" copies ship with a download code instead of a disc, so physical buyers will be downloading the same files. Those code-in-box editions were slated for November 12, and that date reportedly still stands. A PC version is rumored to be coming in Q1 2027, though Rockstar hasn't announced one yet. Until then, console players looking to jump into Vice City are advised to clear some space before November 10.
Source:

articles.title: OpenAI introduces program to reduce AI data center energy demand during peak hours — company testing Grid Protectors Program system in Georgia
articles.text:
OpenAI introduces program to reduce AI data center energy demand during peak hours — company testing Grid Protectors Program system in Georgia
This move could help data centers operate sooner without waiting for the rest of the grid to catch up to its peak demand.
Electricity consumption is one of the biggest concerns that residents bring up whenever a data center is proposed in their community, which is why OpenAI is taking steps to minimize its impact on the local electricity grid. According to the company, its Grid Protectors Program aims to reduce the power consumption of its data centers as local demand increases, ensuring that the grid is not overwhelmed during peak hours. Aside from ensuring that the lights remain on for everyone, it would also allow its data centers to connect to the grid and go online sooner instead of waiting for the additional power sources to come online.
“Whether it’s heating homes during a northern cold snap or running air conditioning through a southern heat wave, families need reliable electricity. Our goal is to make campus flexibility a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most,” OpenAI said in its blog. It also added, “Through Grid Protectors, our ambition is to make this kind of flexibility a core part of how we build and operate future campuses. That means designing facilities to reduce electricity use when needed and working with utilities to agree on how much demand can be reduced, how quickly and for how long. The arrangements will differ by location, and we will share additional commitments as they are finalized.”
OpenAI is testing the program in its planned Effingham County campus in Georgia, with the company saying that it has already signed a 3.2-gigawatt agreement with Georgia Power that included 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response. This ensures that if demand jumps on the hottest days of the year, there would be enough power to accommodate the hundreds of thousands of air conditioners keeping Georgians cool. With the average American home drawing around 1,200 kilowatts, the 1,000-megawatt buffer is more than enough to power around 800,000 households — nearly 20% of the state’s homes.
This technology, called demand response, has been around for decades now, where large operators reduce their demand in response to a peak in demand from other consumers. Before automation, grid operators would manually call up industrial customers like steel mills and ask them to cut consumption to ensure the reliability of the entire grid. But with modern technologies and IoT, it can now be done automatically, allowing data centers to reduce their load in under a minute. In fact, Nvidia has already been experimenting with a similar system in the UK and has proven that it works.

articles.title: AI cloud startup Applied Compute raises $350M after reaching key revenue milestone - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI cloud startup Applied Compute raises $350M after reaching key revenue milestone
Applied Compute Inc., a fast-growing provider of artificial intelligence infrastructure, has raised $350 million in funding at a $3.25 billion valuation.
The startup announced the deal on Monday. Prominent angel investor Elad Gil led the round with participation from Nvidia Corp., Shopify Ventures, HubSpot Ventures and more than a dozen others.
Applied Compute operates a cloud platform that developers use to train large language models and perform inference, the process of running the models to provide responses to queries. Additionally, it has a team of machine learning researchers that can lend customers a hand with their projects. The group takes on tasks such as creating quality evaluations for newly developed models.
The software stack that AI researchers use to train LLMs usually comprises two main components. One creates multiple copies of the model, assigns a different task to each one and turns the results into training data. The other component uses that training data to refine the LLM’s weights. The two components usually run synchronously, which means that each one has to wait for the other to complete its work before launching.
Applied Compute’s platform uses a more efficient training approach called asynchronous reinforcement learning. It enables a training stack’s data generation and weight adjustment components to run at the same time, which speeds up LLM development. Additionally, the platform supports a second optimization method called self-distillation. It removes the need for teacher models, specialized neural networks that researchers use to supervise LLM training runs.
A built-in AI assistant automates repetitive aspects of customers’ work. It can, for example, summarize what new skills an LLM learned during a training run. Uncovering that information usually requires researchers to review lengthy reasoning logs.
Applied Computing’s platform also lends itself to running inference workloads. An autoscaling engine automatically adjusts the amount of hardware allocated to a model based on user traffic. A so-called online RL feature uses the prompts that the LLM receives to fine-tune its weights periodically, which keeps it aligned with customer requirements.
The company offers its training and inference features alongside a model router called Shift-1. It enables coding agents to send each user request to the LLM that can fulfill it in the most cost-efficient manner. Furthermore, it can split complex tasks among multiple LLMs.
Applied Computing disclosed in its funding announcement that its annualized recurring revenue has topped $100 million. The company, which launched less than 18 months ago, counts Microsoft Corp., DoorDash Inc. and other major tech firms as customers. It will use the newly raised capital to grow its market presence and buy more infrastructure.
“Training, inference, and routing are the first pieces of a much larger stack,” Applied Compute founders Rhythm Garg, Yash Patil and Linden Li wrote in a blog post. “We’re building the AI infrastructure every company will need to fully own their intelligence, from the models themselves to the systems that run, monitor and secure them.”

articles.title: Apocalypse Now, Les Trois Mousquetaires… Les 10 films à ne pas manquer sur HBO Max en novembre
articles.text:
HBO Max : notre top 10 des meilleurs films à voir en streaming en novembre 2026
Et si on regardait un bon divertissement sur HBO Max ? Les Numériques vous propose sa liste des dix meilleurs films à voir sur la plateforme de streaming en novembre 2026.
La fusion massive entre Paramount et Warner Bros a beau avoir été entérinée il y a peu, HBO Max reste encore une plateforme de streaming à part entière, avec un généreux catalogue de films et autres programmes.
Et si vous êtes justement en quête du divertissement parfait pour ce soir, Les Numériques a parcouru cette offre pléthorique pour vous choisir les dix meilleurs films à voir au mois de novembre 2026 sur le service de streaming HBO Max.
Quels sont les meilleurs films à voir sur HBO Max en novembre 2026 ?
Apocalypse Now (Final Cut)
En pleine guerre du Vietnam, le Capitaine Willard est envoyé au cœur de la jungle pour retrouver le Colonel Kurtz, un ancien béret vert régnant sur une armée de fanatiques quelque part au-delà de la frontière cambodgienne…
Près d'un demi-siècle après sa sortie, Apocalypse Now n'a rien perdu de sa puissance et reste une expérience de cinéma unique. Francis Ford Coppola transforme la guerre du Vietnam en voyage halluciné et mélancolique, sorte d'Alice au pays des merveilles aussi fou que fascinant. Un film massif en tous points - de ses images folles à ses scènes cultes, en passant par les prestations habitées de Martin Sheen et Marlon Brando - qui demande qu'on s'y abandonne un peu, mais qui laisse une marque indélébile sur le spectateur.
Disponible le 7 novembre sur HBO Max.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Les Trois Mousquetaires : D'Artagnan
Du Louvre au Palais de Buckingham, des bas-fonds de Paris au siège de La Rochelle… dans un Royaume divisé par les guerres de religion et menacé d’invasion par l’Angleterre, une poignée d’hommes et de femmes vont croiser leurs épées et lier leur destin à celui de la France.
Cette nouvelle adaptation du classique d'Alexandre Dumas arrive à remettre au goût du jour une histoire pourtant bien connue. Le réalisateur Mathieu Bourboulon livre une aventure nerveuse et flamboyante, dôtée d'un souffle épique non négligeable grâce à une production soignée. Du grand spectacle qui ne réussit pas tout ce qu'il entreprend, mais qui reste hautement divertissant, avec (pour ne rien gâcher) un casting cinq étoiles : Romain Duris, François Civil, Vincent Cassel, Eva Green, Lyna Khoudri...
Disponible le 8 novembre sur HBO Max.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Everything Everywhere All At Once
Evelyn Wang est à bout : elle ne comprend plus sa famille, son travail et croule sous les impôts… Soudain, elle se retrouve plongée dans le multivers, des mondes parallèles où elle explore toutes les vies qu’elle aurait pu mener. Face à des forces obscures, elle seule peut sauver le monde mais aussi préserver la chose la plus précieuse : sa famille.
Le duo Daniel Scheinert et Daniel Kwan (Swiss Army Man) s'empare de la notion du multivers, et livre un film unique, déjanté où les idées fusent à chaque seconde. Une aventure tout à la fois drôle, gonzo et tendre, qui met une étonnante perspective sur la famille et les choix dans nos existences. Cerise sur le gâteau, le tout est servi par un casting génial : Michelle Yeoh, Ke Huy Quan, Jamie Lee Curtis, Stephanie Hsu... Un bijou récompensé par 7 Oscars, et à rattraper sans tarder.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Destination finale : Bloodlines
Hantée par un cauchemar terrifiant qui revient sans cesse, Stefanie, étudiante à l’université, rentre chez elle pour retrouver la trace de la seule personne susceptible d’enrayer ce cycle infernal et de sauver ses proches du sort funeste qui les attend…
Véritable carton au box-office l'année dernière, Destination finale : Bloodlines a aussi et surtout une belle surprise en terme de qualité. Le film revitalise son concept à la fois gore et ludique en le connectant à une grande histoire de malédiction intergénérationnelle. Les différentes morts sont toujours aussi inventives, drôles et jouissives à regarder, et le spectateur en redemande.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Pacific Rim
Surgies des flots, des hordes de créatures monstrueuses, les "Kaiju", ont déclenché une guerre qui a fait des millions de victimes et épuisé les ressources naturelles de l'humanité pendant des années. Pour les combattre, une arme d'un genre nouveau a été mise au point : de gigantesques robots, les "Jaegers", contrôlés simultanément par deux pilotes qui communiquent par télépathie. Alors que la défaite paraît inéluctable, les forces armées qui protègent l'humanité n'ont d'autre choix que d'avoir recours à deux héros hors normes : un ancien pilote au bout du rouleau et une jeune femme en cours d'entraînement qui font équipe pour manœuvrer un Jaeger légendaire.
Avec Pacific Rim, le réalisateur Guillermo Del Toro (Le Labyrinthe de Pan, La Forme de l'eau) laisse place à ses fantasmes les plus fous et livre un grand film jubilatoire, spectaculaire tout en restant profondément humain. Une orgie visuelle qui n'échappe pas à quelques facilités scénaristiques, mais qui vous laissera le sourire aux lèvres grâce à son inventivité et sa générosité. Un blockbuster dôté d'un beau casting (Idris Elba, Charlie Hunnam, Rinko Kikuchi, Charlie Day) et qui fait du bien.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Eyes Wide Shut
Conviés à une soirée, le docteur William Harford et son épouse Alice font, chacun de son côté, l’objet de tentatives de séduction. L’un et l’autre résistent à la tentation. Cependant, le lendemain, Alice avoue à son mari qu’elle a naguère songé à le tromper et regrette aujourd’hui de ne pas être passée à l’acte. Ébranlé par cette révélation, William s’enfuit et débute une nuit de révélations.
Ultime film du maître Stanley Kubrick (2001, l’odyssée de l’espace, Shining, Full Metal Jacket), Eyes Wide Shut est une plongée fiévreuse et enivrante dans l’intimité d’un couple, et dans les machinations sombres de notre monde. Un thriller érotique qui convoque les thèmes des sociétés secrètes, du désir, du mariage et du conditionnement social avec, en son cœur, le couple (à l’époque à la ville comme à l’écran) Tom Cruise/Nicole Kidman, d’un magnétisme fou. Un film captivant qui vous restera longtemps en tête.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
The Tree of Life
Dans le Texas des années 50, Jack, âgé d'une dizaine d'années, grandit entre un père autoritaire et une mère aimante et généreuse, qui lui donne foi en la vie. La naissance de ses deux frères l'oblige bientôt à partager cet amour inconditionnel, puis à affronter l'individualisme forcené d'un père obsédé par la réussite de ses enfants. Jusqu'au jour où un tragique événement vient perturber cet équilibre fragile...
Lauréat de la Palme d'or en 2011, le film de Terrence Malick (La Ligne Rouge, Les Moissons du ciel) est une expérience cinématographique et poétique à part entière, et une puissante réflexion sur la vie et le temps qui passe. Un chef-d'œuvre contemplatif et bouleversant, porté par un casting prestigieux (Brad Pitt, Jessica Chastain, Sean Penn) et qui touche en plein cœur.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Mickey 17
Mickey Barnes est un "Expendable" engagé dans une mission de colonisation de la planète glacée Niflheim. Son rôle : accomplir les tâches les plus périlleuses, sachant que chaque décès entraîne sa régénération avec la plupart de ses souvenirs intacts. Après plusieurs réincarnations, Mickey commence à questionner sa propre existence et la moralité de sa mission. Lorsque des événements inattendus surviennent, il doit choisir entre accepter son sort ou défier le système qui le considère comme jetable.
Dernier film du réalisateur Bong Joon-ho (Parasite), cette adaptation du roman éponyme d'Edward Ashton est un blockbuster pas comme les autres. Tout à la fois récit de science-fiction, comédie, critique acerbe du capitalisme, et fable existentielle et écologique, Mickey 17 nous embarque dans un drôle de monde visuellement spectaculaire, et dans lequel on plonge avec plaisir. Si le résultat est imparfait et très inégal, il reste à voir notamment pour son casting savoureux : Robert Pattinson, Naomie Ackie, Mark Ruffalo, Steven Yeun, Toni Collette...
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Sinners
Alors qu’ils cherchent à s’affranchir d’un lourd passé, deux frères jumeaux reviennent dans leur ville natale pour repartir à zéro. Mais ils comprennent qu’une puissance maléfique bien plus redoutable guette leur retour avec impatience.
Récompensé par 4 Oscars, le dernier film de Ryan Coogler a été l'un des derniers événements ciné, et pour cause : le réalisateur de Black Panther et Creed livre avec Sinners un cocktail de drame, d'horreur et de mysticisme fiévreux et enivrant. Coogler croise ainsi la musique, la religion, le folklore du sud américain et le vampirisme et accouche d'une véritable bouffée d'air frais, visuellement sublime et diablement efficace. Si le film est un peu boursouflé par ses ambitions et manque notamment de rythme sur la fin, il reste un incontournable à rattraper sans tarder.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
Le Dernier Samouraï
En 1876, le capitaine Nathan Algren devient conseiller militaire pour le compte de l'empereur japonais soucieux d'ouvrir son pays aux traditions et au commerce occidentaux et d'éradiquer l'ancienne caste guerrière des samouraïs. Le capitaine Algren se trouve bientôt pris entre deux feux, au cœur d'une confrontation entre deux époques et deux mondes avec, pour le guider, son sens de l'honneur.
Avec Le Dernier Samouraï, le réalisateur Edward Zwick (Blood Diamond, Glory) signe une fresque épique, et une aventure inspirante sur le choc des civilisations et la fin d'une ère emblématique du Japon. Si Le Dernier Samouraï est très hollywoodien dans sa forme et a un peu vieilli (notamment les clichés sur les japonais), il reste un excellent long-métrage, dans lequel brille un Tom Cruise habité et un Ken Watanabe toujours parfait, le tout porté par la musique de Hans Zimmer.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film :
HBO Max

articles.title: NVIDIA exige de ses partenaires cloud qu'ils réduisent leur dépendance à la Chine
articles.text:
La firme de Jensen Huang prend une décision assez étonnante vis-à-vis de la Chine. Car NVIDIA veut maintenant que la majorité des clients de ses partenaires cloud ne soient pas chinois.
Parmi les entreprises américaines de la tech, NVIDIA se distingue souvent par sa volonté de freiner le plus possible les contraintes d'exportation de produits high tech américain vers la Chine. Car pour Jensen Huang, ces contraintes seraient la meilleure recette pour que Pékin développe des alternatives lui permettant de devenir à terme indépendant des États-Unis. Pourtant, c'est le même NVIDIA qui prend aujourd'hui une décision destinée à réduire les liens avec la Chine.
Les clients NVIDIA travaillant dans le cloud doivent dorénavant servir au moins à 51% des entreprises non-chinoises
NVIDIA se met au diapason de Washington sur le dossier chinois semble-t-il. C'est ce que l'on peut comprendre de cette nouvelle information, qui nous est communiquée part le Financial Times.
D'après ce média, qui a obtenu l'information de cinq sources différentes, NVIDIA exige dorénavant de ses partenaires opérant dans le cloud que 51% au moins de leurs clients ne soient pas chinois. Il s'agit ici d'une nouvelle règle qui s'impose au contrat qui seront dorénavant signés, et non pas aux contrats précédents.
NVIDIA reste évasif sur le sujet
Ce qui est intéressant de noter ici, c'est que la firme de Jensen Huang n'a pas voulu être très prolixe sur le sujet. En réponse à cette nouvelle, elle s'est ainsi contentée d'affirmer que « les centres de données et les clouds reposant sur des puces américaines sont la base dont les concepteurs de modèles et d'applications américains ont besoin pour être compétitifs à l'échelle mondiale ».
Difficile donc de démêler l'ensemble de cette histoire pour le moment. On peut par contre rappeler que cette information arrive à peine quelques jours après que le New York Times a rendu public un rapport des renseignements américains portant sur Jensen Huang. Produit l'an dernier, il affirmait que le patron de NVIDIA aurait été la cible d'un complot d'espionnage chinois, à travers une femme d'affaires chinoise du nom de Huang Le, qui avait alors une relation étroite avec Jensen Huang.
Source : Financial Times

articles.title: Google recibe un revés ante el TJUE por el uso de noticias en Gemini y los medios ganan terreno para reclamar compensaciones
articles.text:
Una noticia puede llegar a millones de personas sin que todas ellas visiten el medio que la publicó. Durante años, los buscadores han servido como intermediarios entre quienes producen información y quienes quieren encontrarla, proporcionando un flujo de visitas que ayuda a sostener el negocio de la prensa digital. Sin embargo, la inteligencia artificial ha introducido un nuevo escenario: los usuarios pueden obtener respuestas directamente, sin necesidad de acceder a las fuentes originales. Para el lector puede resultar cómodo, pero para los medios plantea una cuestión de fondo sobre el valor de sus contenidos y cómo se remunera su trabajo.
Esa tensión acaba de trasladarse a la justicia europea. Este martes, 3 de noviembre, el abogado general del Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea (TJUE), Maciej Szpunar, ha concluido que Gemini puede vulnerar los derechos de los editores cuando recupera y reutiliza sus publicaciones para generar respuestas en determinadas circunstancias. Su interpretación supone un revés para Google y abre una posible vía para futuras reclamaciones económicas por parte de los medios. Sin embargo, hay un matiz importante: se trata de unas conclusiones no vinculantes, por lo que todavía corresponde al tribunal pronunciarse mediante una sentencia.
Para entender el origen de esta disputa tenemos que trasladarnos a Hungría. Allí, Like Company, una empresa que gestiona varios portales informativos, emprendió acciones legales contra Google al considerar que Gemini utilizaba sus publicaciones sin autorización para elaborar respuestas. El expediente judicial recoge un ejemplo concreto relacionado con una noticia sobre Kozsó, un cantante húngaro que quería instalar un acuario con delfines junto al lago Balatón. El asistente generó un resumen detallado a petición de un usuario, lo que llevó a la editora a cuestionar el uso de sus contenidos. Ante las dudas sobre la legislación aplicable, un tribunal húngaro decidió consultar al TJUE.
La batalla por las noticias y la IA
No todas las respuestas de una inteligencia artificial basadas en noticias constituyen una infracción. La legislación europea distingue entre los hechos que relata un artículo y su forma concreta de expresión, que sí puede estar protegida. Según el abogado general, Gemini puede vulnerar los derechos de los editores cuando reproduce de manera reconocible sus publicaciones o accede a ellas eludiendo medidas técnicas eficaces de protección. El entrenamiento de modelos, en cambio, puede acogerse a las excepciones de minería de textos y datos bajo determinadas condiciones, aunque Szpunar propone no admitir las preguntas sobre esta cuestión porque no hay pruebas de que los artículos de Like Company se utilizaran para entrenar Gemini.
No es ningún secreto que los medios también se juegan parte de nuestro modelo de negocio en esta transformación. Las visitas a nuestras páginas permiten mostrar anuncios, generar impresiones publicitarias y, en algunos casos, captar suscriptores. Pero cuando alguien obtiene una respuesta directamente de Gemini o encuentra un resumen de AI Overviews en el buscador, ese recorrido hasta el artículo original puede no producirse, reduciendo las oportunidades de obtener ingresos por el trabajo periodístico. Algunas plataformas de inteligencia artificial cobran suscripciones y mantienen acuerdos comerciales con determinados editores, pero eso no significa que todas las publicaciones reciban compensaciones por el uso de sus contenidos.
No hablamos únicamente de una preocupación del sector. Pew Research Center observó en 2025 que, entre los usuarios estadounidenses analizados, el 8% de las visitas a páginas de resultados de Google con resúmenes de IA terminó en un clic en los enlaces tradicionales, frente al 15% cuando estos no aparecían. Además, el Reuters Institute recoge datos de Chartbeat que reflejan una caída global del 33% en el tráfico orgánico procedente del buscador hacia más de 2.500 sitios web entre noviembre de 2024 y noviembre de 2025, sin atribuir toda esa pérdida a la IA. Europa ya había intervenido en este terreno: Francia multó a Google con 250 millones de euros en 2024 por incumplir compromisos relacionados con los derechos de los editores, incluidos algunos vinculados al uso de contenidos en Bard, antecesor de Gemini.
Ahora, como explica el propio TJUE en su comunicado oficial, la última palabra sobre la interpretación de la legislación europea la tendrán sus jueces, que deberán pronunciarse sobre las cuestiones planteadas desde Hungría. Su decisión será vinculante, pero corresponderá al tribunal nacional resolver el litigio concreto y determinar si existe una infracción y qué consecuencias tendría, incluidas posibles compensaciones económicas.

articles.title: VIDEO: interview with Proton CEO Andy Yen on the rise and risks of AI
articles.text:
VIDEO: Interview with Proton CEO Andy Yen on the rise and risks of AI, and the future of his company
Yen sat down with The Privacy Lab to talk age verification and more
In early October 2026, digital privacy software provider Proton invited TechRadar to a press event at its Geneva, Switzerland, HQ along with a group of journalists from other publications.
We sat through a day of presentations focusing on the future and development of Proton's products, including the popular Proton VPN and the encrypted messaging service Proton Mail.
Included in that time was an address from Proton's founder and CEO, Andy Yen, who has developed into something of a thought-leader in the digital privacy space through his interviews, social media posts, and his forthright personality.
He impressed upon us the uniqueness of Proton's non-profit ownership, swatted away questions regarding the development of a private browser that was revealed through a job listing, and how, above all else, Proton endeavors to build products its community of users genuinely wants.
Later in the day, we got in some 1-2-1 time with Yen where he quizzed him on camera about the future of Proton, the rise and risks of AI, age verification, and more. Our interview with Andy Yen, published on our The Privacy Lab YouTube channel, is below, in full.
In the interim, from that interview in early October to today, though, it needs to be noted that Proton has featured heavily in the news, with the company coming under considerable scrutiny over the past few days.
Last week, leaked internal messages at Proton showed how both the company and Andy Yen have been enforcing an AI revolution on its workforce, with some employees having to
"re-interview" with a focus on their ability to use AI more in their current roles.
404 Media uncovered what it described as a "culture of fear", as a company insider lifted the lid on Yen’s belittling public Slack messages in the company’s security chat channel. The CEO was described by that source as being in “full AI psychosis”.
After significant backlash from employees and the digital privacy community, on October 30, 2026, Yen posted a personal apology and statement to the Proton subreddit.
The statement claims that Andy takes "responsibility for the failure of communications", that Proton's use of AI "will never be at the expense of security", and that "the 're-interviews'...will not take place, and no one will lose their jobs because of them". The comments in response are as hostile as you might expect.
More recently, Proton CTO Bart Butler published an internal memo on AI use at the company which had been sent to employees earlier in October. This AI @ Proton, Engineering Manifesto can be read in full here.
It underlines the zeal with which Proton, as a company, is looking to further its development with AI tools, and how quickly it's looking to pull its staff – particularly the engineers – into the new world.
It’s against this backdrop that we publish this interview with Andy Yen. There are no controversies or contradictions, nor did we find Yen to be anything other than interesting and courteous throughout the Q&A.
But it’s worth comparing moments like his denouncement of mainstream AI chatbots in the interview with Proton's internal AI-first culture – even though the context is, of course, not the same.

articles.title: Xbox Loses Its First Chief Operating Officer Mid-Reset
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 3rd 2026
Xbox Loses Its First Chief Operating Officer Mid-Reset
Helen Chiang, Xbox's first-ever chief operating officer, has left Microsoft just three months after taking on the role. The news comes from a short internal memo by Microsoft Gaming CEO Asha Sharma, obtained by The Verge, which simply states that Chiang is leaving the company and thanks her for her years of service. No reason was given, and Xbox's VP of communications, Kari Perez, said the company doesn't discuss individual personnel matters. There's no successor yet either, so Chiang's duties will be split among other Xbox leaders for now, with Sharma promising more details on COO leadership once plans are finalized.
Chiang had been at Microsoft for around 21 years, starting in 2005 and moving to Xbox in 2007, where Sharma credits her with helping build Xbox Live. She later led Mojang and became corporate vice president of the Minecraft franchise in 2020. Sharma created the COO position in July as part of her reset of Xbox, and it came with end-to-end profit and loss responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services. That same reset includes around 3,200 job cuts by the end of fiscal year 2027, with hundreds of jobs already gone. Losing the executive meant to hold the whole business together this early into the reset probably isn't the kind of stability Xbox was hoping for.
Update Oct 25th: A verified source familiar with the situation has told Eurogamer that Helen Chiang was "terminated for policy violations." This claim has not been independently verified.
Update Nov 3rd: Helen Chiang has since denied being "fired for a policy violation" in a recent LinkedIn post. She goes on to clarify more points about her departure. You can read her full post below.
Helen Chiang, Former Xbox COOClarity is Kindness
There has been some speculation about my abrupt departure from Microsoft, including claims that I was "fired for a policy violation". That's not accurate and while I won't turn this into a play-by-play, silence should not be mistaken for agreement. What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize. It's important to me to set the record straight.
First, I did not leak confidential company information to the press. I have never communicated with any journalist outside the limited, company-authorized interviews I've done as part of my job. That includes every journalist who reached out this week seeking my side of the story.
Second, I did not leave XBOX to join a competitor. You don't spend two decades somewhere without developing a deep loyalty to the people, teams, and businesses you've helped build. XBOX was never just another stop in my career. My end game was always to keep building here.
Third, I did not engage in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity. I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career. I won't let speculation define my character or erase that record.
Lastly, I did not leave because I was passed over for a bigger role. Since having children, I've been intentional about how I define ambition and success. I haven't actively sought out bigger roles or increased responsibilities, and the last time I interviewed for a job was in 2011. My reputation and results paved the way for the opportunities that followed. I went where the company believed I was needed and where I could have the greatest impact. I did not ask for my most recent role, either. I was promoted into it in July.
I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they're applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously.
I share this because I don't want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That's the legacy I hope to leave behind.
To everyone who has reached out with hugs, love, and support: thank you. So many of you have reminded me of the wonderful times we've shared over the past 20 years and the impact we've had on one another. Some of you I haven't been in touch with for several years, yet you still took the time to check on me. Others are people I've never even met, but you reached out anyway. That speaks volumes about the care and humanity in our industry and the connections that transcend where we work.
This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end. And it is not the whole story.
Sources:
				The Verge, 				via GamesRadar, 				Helen Chiang on LinkedIn
