articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer says he had 'no lack of inspiration from the amazing gameplay itself' and Infinity Ward's sound team were 'integral in shaping the overall vibe' of the soundtrack
articles.text:
'I have no lack of inspiration from the amazing gameplay itself' — Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer says Infinity Ward's sound team were a 'huge creative influence' on the soundtrack and 'integral in shaping the overall vibe'
Jason Graves says the game has "a little bit of vibe inspiration from the OG Modern Warfare 2"
- Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer Jason Graves has revealed some inspirations behind the game's soundtrack
- He attributes much of it to the gameplay and Infinity Ward's sound team
- He confirmed that he didn't reference previous Modern Warfare soundtracks, but there is "a little bit of vibe inspiration from the OG Modern Warfare 2"
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer Jason Graves has attributed the gameplay and the Infinity Ward sound team for helping to inspire the game's multiplayer score.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Graves said, "Fortunately, I have no lack of inspiration from the amazing gameplay itself," when asked where he begins when composing a soundtrack for such an iconic franchise.
"The incredible team at Infinity Ward, led by audio director Stephen Miller, was also such a huge creative influence," he continued. "And the music team, led by Jonathan Mayer, were integral in shaping the overall vibe and giving me everything I needed to be as creative as possible."
Graves, who has also composed for Warzone, Dead Space, Dead Space 2, 2013's Tomb Raider, and a host of other projects spanning video games and movies, added that it was important that the work was a collaborative effort, as scores can be years in the making.
"I can't stress how important cooperation with other creative human beings makes a difference when it comes to working on a project as big as this," Graves said. "This is the kind of thing that slowly comes together over years of work."
As for finding the basis for a Modern Warfare score, Graves explained that he doesn't listen to previous works, but admitted that "there was a little bit of vibe inspiration from the OG Modern Warfare 2."
"But nothing too granular or specific," he added, "I'm very intentional about not listening to music from previous projects in a franchise unless specifically directed by the developer. I think that's especially important here because Infinity Ward has been so supportive of trying new things and creating a soundtrack that's every bit as epic and bespoke as the gameplay itself."

articles.title: Google Pixel Watch : le correctif pour les problèmes de batterie est enfin disponible sur le Play Store
articles.text:
Votre Pixel Watch a vu son autonomie chuter brutalement ? C'est normal, et ce n'est pas la batterie de votre montre qui faiblit d'un coup. Heureusement, il y a désormais une solution pour y remédier.
Google a commencé à distribuer une mise à jour pour résoudre le problème de décharge rapide de la batterie signalé ces derniers jours sur ses montres connectées Pixel Watch. Le correctif passe par le Play Store et non par une mise à jour du système.
Un déploiement étalé sur quelques jours
Le groupe avait reconnu le problème à la fin de la semaine dernière et promis un correctif dès que possible. Dans une déclaration transmise à Android Authority, il confirme que la distribution a débuté et qu'elle « sera complète au cours des deux prochains jours ». Selon Google, le défaut touche « un petit nombre » d'utilisateurs.
L'entreprise indique la marche à suivre : appuyer sur la couronne de la montre, ouvrir l'application Play Store, puis aller dans « Gérer les applications » et appuyer sur « Tout mettre à jour all ».
Google ne publie pas de mise à jour de Wear OS. Il s'agit d'une mise à jour des applications système de la montre. Le déploiement étant progressif, le correctif peut ne pas être disponible immédiatement. Si le Play Store n'affiche aucune mise à jour en attente, il faut simplement réessayer plus tard. Redémarrer la montre une fois toutes les mises à jour installées est également conseillé par l'auteur de l'article d'Android Police.
Tous les modèles récents concernés
Si Google n'a pas précisé la cause du problème, les modèles concernés semblent être nombreux, de la Pixel Watch 2 à la Pixel Watch 5. La dernière montre de Google peut tenir près de deux jours avec une seule charge. Or plusieurs propriétaires ont constaté une autonomie ramenée à 12 à 16 heures, ce qui a suscité de l'incompréhension.
Pour une Pixel Watch 4 qui tenait une journée sans problème auparavant, l'autonomie avait du mal à atteindre les 12 heures selon un utilisateur. Si une chute de l'autonomie en raison de l'âge de la montre peut se faire ressentir, la baisse était ici bien trop soudaine.
Source : AndroidPolice

Surfshark One vs Norton 360 Deluxe : quel pack VPN + protection identité est le plus rentable ?

Les vols de données se multiplient, entraînant souvent des problèmes graves comme l’usurpation d’identité, les piratages de compte et les fraudes financières. Au lieu de se contenter d’un simple antivirus, il vaut donc mieux opter pour une suite de sécurité complète, incluant idéalement un VPN et une protection de l’identité.

Norton 360 Deluxe à 39,99 € la première année

articles.title: Peppermint Robotics bags Rs 100 Cr in pre-Series B funding round
articles.text:
Peppermint Robotics bags Rs 100 Cr in pre-Series B funding round
The startup, which makes autonomous cleaning robots, is backed by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners.
Peppermint Robotics, which makes autonomous cleaning robots, has raised Rs 100 crore (about $10.5 million) in a pre-Series B round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners. Asiana Fund also participated in the round.
The round involved fresh capital and secondary share transactions.
The money arrives on the back of rapid growth by Peppermint.
The Pune- and Austin-based startup said it doubled its revenue last year and grew nearly sixfold between FY24 and FY26. It last raised Rs 34 crore ($4 million) in a Series A round in April 2025. Peppermint has a presence in nine countries, with the US being its biggest market.
Founded in 2019 at the Society for Innovation and Entrepreneurship at IIT Bombay, the company's autonomous cleaning robots are deployed across a range of commercial and industrial environments, including factories, hospitals, airports, malls, warehouses, hotels and universities. Its machines scrub floors and move materials in factories, hospitals, airports, malls, warehouses, hotels and universities. They are designed to fit into existing routines rather than disrupt workflows.
The company primarily serves facility management companies that oversee cleaning operations, including the selection of equipment, chemicals and cleaning processes.
One of its more challenging deployments is at a global pharmaceutical company, where its cleanroom robots have passed qualification testing in an EU GMP Grade cleanroom, among the most tightly regulated settings a cleaning robot can enter, Peppermint said, in a statement.
Cleanroom robots are specialised manipulators engineered to operate in controlled, contamination-free environments.
The startup builds its hardware, software and perception systems in-house and assembles its robots in Pune. They run on proprietary Peppermint OS, using computer vision and LiDAR to map spaces, plan routes, and avoid obstacles. Operators can monitor them in real time through a cloud dashboard. For security-sensitive sites, the company offers fully offline 'stealth' robots that meet stringent information securtiy requirements.
Runal Dahiwade, Founder and CEO of Peppermint Robotics, said, "Cleaning teams keep hospitals, factories and airports running. Our robots work alongside them and take on the most repetitive, physically demanding jobs, like floor scrubbing and material transportation. Our customers judge us on one thing: a clean floor, every shift.
"So we build our robots heavy-duty, to last multiple years, and we stay with every machine for its whole lifecycle. This round lets us build more of them, closer to our customers worldwide."
The newly raised capital will go towards next-generation robotics and expanding manufacturing capacity. An assembly line in North America is also being planned over the coming months.
Peppermint also intends to step up business development in the United States and Asia, grow its presence in Europe, and hire senior leaders and engineers.
On the product side, it plans to widen its range of floor-cleaning and material-handling robots and develop its cleanroom line.
Investors are optimistic about Peppermint's potential and promise.
Shubham Sandeep, Partner at pi Ventures, pointed to the company's "clear ROI" in demanding settings such as healthcare and hospitality. Anandamoy Roychowdhary of Crane Venture Partners said Peppermint has built a production-grade cleanroom robot for mission-critical businesses. Neha Aggarwal of Asiana Fund called the company the kind of advanced manufacturing business India can build for global markets.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Google says schools that ban AI will also lose search
articles.text:
Cutting corners: Google executives appear hell-bent on their effort to turn AI into a real business opportunity, even if the effort ends up undermining the company's revenue streams. This latest move looks like an attempt to push Gemini use among students and educational staff, potentially at the expense of rivals such as ChatGPT, which arguably have more mindshare and mainstream adoption at the moment.
According to Chris Phillips, Google's vice president and general manager for education, K-12 schools will soon have to fully embrace the company's AI services or lose student access to its web search engine.
Under the new policy, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search will be turned off by default for K-12 student accounts until administrators enable them. The change could strain Google's relationship with the education sector, but Mountain View says there is no alternative.
Phillips argues that Search and AI are now deeply integrated services. If a school chooses to ban AI entirely, its students will lose access to Search as well. Instead of results, they will see a message from their school stating that the services are not available.
The move looks like an effort to push Gemini use among students and educational staff, potentially at the expense of rivals such as ChatGPT, which arguably have more mindshare and mainstream adoption at the moment.
Classroom is a free learning tool designed to provide a tailored experience to educational institutions. The service brings Gmail, Drive, Docs, and several other Google services together in a single platform, and is already used by more than 150 million students, teachers, and education professionals worldwide.
The "deep" integration between Gemini's chatbot and traditional web search is apparently the next major evolution in how Classroom works. Phillips said Google is taking a different approach to students' learning needs, one meant to curb cheating among US students while improving their AI-based experience, including a Guided Learning feature that walks students through problems rather than handing over answers.
In August, Mountain View said Gemini and other AI features would become the default experience for K-12 students who were already allowed to access the chatbot. The company is now reversing course and forcing schools to avoid total AI bans if they also want to keep web search.
Google's push to bring AI to K-12 students is likely to clash with the mounting opposition to chatbots in the US. Officials are either banning generative AI for younger students or trying to restrict AI access on school-provided devices.
Monetization of AI Mode is another challenge for Google moving forward. On its most recent earnings call, the company acknowledged that chatbot-based search earns less than traditional search, and investors are growing uneasy about the new business direction. Alphabet shares fell roughly 10% afterward.

articles.title: Apps de namoro e chatbots com romance se tornam 18+ no iPhone • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apps de namoro e chatbots com romance se tornam 18+ no iPhone
No Brasil, esses recursos terão classificação mínima A16 ou A18.
A partir deste mês, desenvolvedores dos apps de iPhone disponíveis na App Store terão de informar se oferecem recursos de relacionamento ou interações românticas. Serviços com esse tipo de interatividade terão agora classificação mínima 18+.
A mudança também atinge recursos de compartilhamento de localização em tempo real, cuja faixa etária poderá variar conforme as regras de cada país. No Brasil, a Apple informa que esses apps receberão classificação mínima A16, enquanto os de namoro serão enquadrados como A18.
A mudança pode afetar até gigantes como o Facebook, até então classificado como não recomendado para menores de 16 anos. O carro-chefe da Meta inclui a aba “Namoro”, que permite conhecer e marcar encontros com outros usuários da rede.
As mudanças foram adicionadas ao questionário de classificação etária do App Store Connect. O primeiro, Dating and Relationships, inclui tanto apps que conectam pessoas para namoro quanto serviços com companheiros virtuais capazes de manter conversas de teor romântico ou sexual.
O segundo novo descritor é o Shared Location, para aplicativos que permitem compartilhar a localização física com outro usuário ou grupo. Aqui, apps como o WhatsApp, atualmente para maiores de 14, poderão ser impactados. Lembrando que o mensageiro possui configurações de controle parental que impedem o compartilhamento de localização com outras pessoas.
No Brasil, as novas regras de classificação indicativa, atualizadas pela Portaria nº 1.048, do Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública (MJSP), já consideram o compartilhamento da geolocalização na avaliação da idade mínima.
Assim como o MJSP, a Apple reconhece que há casos em que a regra pode não representar a finalidade do aplicativo. Um exemplo citado são serviços de monitoramento dos filhos. Nesses casos, o desenvolvedor pode solicitar uma classificação oficial ao órgão oficial, que será exibida na App Store.
Os novos campos serão adicionados ao questionário em 16 de novembro. A partir dessa data, desenvolvedores precisarão preencher as novas informações ao enviar uma atualização de aplicativo ou alterar a classificação indicativa.
Todos os aplicativos na loja deverão fornecer as declarações até 12 de janeiro de 2027. A mudança faz parte de uma revisão mais ampla do sistema de classificação etária da App Store e busca fazer com que a idade indicada para cada aplicativo também leve em consideração recursos específicos, como namoro, companheiros virtuais e compartilhamento da localização.

articles.title: Reddit pidió a la Alta Corte de Australia que anule la prohibición de redes sociales a menores de 16
articles.text:
Reddit y un grupo que defiende la libertad de expresión pidieron a la Alta Corte de Australia que anule la ley que prohíbe a los menores de 16 años tener cuentas en redes sociales. La audiencia comenzó el 3 de noviembre y sigue el 4, en el primer gran desafío judicial a la norma.
La empresa presentó el caso junto con el Digital Freedom Project, una organización que encabeza John Ruddick, legislador libertario del estado de Nueva Gales del Sur. Ambos sostienen que la ley vulnera la libertad implícita de comunicación política que protege la Constitución australiana, según informó The Guardian.
La prohibición alcanza a 10 plataformas: Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, Kick, X, Twitch y Threads. Casi 11 meses atrás, las empresas debieron desactivar o suspender las cuentas de los usuarios que determinaron que tenían menos de 16 años.
El primer ministro, Anthony Albanese, dijo que las plataformas suspendieron más de cinco millones de cuentas desde entonces. Quien infringe la ley y no controla la edad de sus usuarios enfrenta multas elevadas, según la agencia AFP.
Reddit afirma en su escrito que el control de la edad no funciona bien y que no hay consenso científico sobre los daños de las redes. “La evidencia hasta ahora es que la eficacia de la prohibición ha sido limitada”, dice el documento citado por AFP.
Reddit argumenta que sin cuenta hay menos protección
La empresa sostiene además que la ley puede resultar más peligrosa. Las cuentas registradas tienen funciones de seguridad incorporadas, y gran parte del contenido de las redes se puede ver sin iniciar sesión. Los jóvenes que usan esas plataformas sin cuenta quedan sin esa protección, argumenta Reddit.
La compañía también pide ser excluida de la prohibición. Un vocero indicó que comparte el objetivo del gobierno de proteger a los jóvenes en internet, pero que existen “mejores y más efectivas formas” de lograrlo. No obstante, confirmaron que cumplirán la ley durante el proceso.
Digital Freedom Project argumenta que las redes son un medio importante para acceder a noticias y participar en política, incluso para los menores de 16 años. Ruddick dijo que otras tecnológicas de Silicon Valley le expresaron simpatía, pero que Reddit fue la única que se trabajó de forma conjunta.
Los jueces cuestionaron el argumento político
En la sala, la jueza Jacqueline Gleeson expresó que, según su experiencia con menores, la gran mayoría de ellos no tiene la mente puesta en la comunicación política la mayor parte del tiempo, según relató NT News. El abogado Perry Herzfeld respondió que las redes dan a los menores una capacidad de influencia que no tendrían en la calle.
El juez James Edelman preguntó si los jóvenes activistas no habrían podido influir en la opinión pública sin redes sociales, como ocurrió siglos atrás. Herzfeld insistió en que ninguna otra vía ofrece un alcance comparable.
La ministra de Comunicaciones, Anika Wells, defendió la ley. “La pregunta de qué aceptamos de las plataformas que nos ofrecen un mundo en línea es la cuestión de política pública más apremiante de nuestro tiempo”, dijo, y agregó que el gobierno defiende el derecho de los niños a estar libres de daño.
Una investigación de académicos australianos publicada este año halló pocas pruebas de que los adolescentes hayan dejado las redes sociales por la restricción, según AFP. Nueva Zelanda, el Reino Unido, Francia y Turquía manifestaron interés en seguir el ejemplo de Australia.

articles.title: Apple faces unprecedented memory cost increases as RAM prices continue to surge, manufacturing bill climbs by $33 billion — rising component expenses threaten margins through the holiday quarter and into 2027
articles.text:
Apple faces unprecedented memory cost increases as RAM prices continue to surge, manufacturing bill climbs by $33 billion — rising component expenses threaten margins through the holiday quarter and into 2027
AI demand is tightening DRAM and NAND supply, pushing up costs for device makers and leaving less memory available for consumer electronics
Apple is about to feel the squeeze from rising memory prices, with the cost of RAM climbing just as the company heads into its busiest shopping season. According to Reuters, Apple expects to pay more for memory in the December quarter, with the CEO, John Ternus, describing the current price increases as “unprecedented. The company has so far managed to soften the blow by using memory bought at lower prices, cutting costs elsewhere and raising prices on some products. However, it is reported that its manufacturing bill has climbed by $33 billion in just a few months.
But that cushion is getting thinner, and Apple expects memory purchases to become even more expensive into 2027. “What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented. And as we said earlier in the September quarter, we did see higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, which were partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on certain non-memory components. Now for the December quarter, we expect even higher memory costs, partly offset by a few factors. So as you know, we changed the price on many of our products, including Mac and iPad at the end of June and iPhone in September, and these price increases provided some offset.” Ternus said during Apple’s November 2 earnings call.
Memory is used across Apple's hardware lineup, so sustained price increases could affect manufacturing cost for several product categories—although Apple has not announced another round of price increases. Absorbing higher components could, however, indefinitely become difficult. Dave Nicholson, Chief Research Officer at the Futurum Group, also identified memory prices as a growing pressure point for Apple's margins and hardware pricing through the holiday season and into 2027. According to him, Apple is in a different position from companies pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into AI data center infrastructure. The impact of higher component costs is easier to quantify than the eventual returns on massive AI capital expenditure, he said.
And the warnings from Apple's suppliers suggest that the cost pressure is unlikely to ease quickly. Last month, Samsung, a major supplier of RAM(DRAM), NAND flash storage and OLED displays for Apple, said that memory demand would far exceed supply as AI infrastructure continues to expand. Its memory division also reported a quarter-on-quarter increase in DRAM average prices during the third quarter, while NAND prices rose by high-teen percentages. Senior executive vice president of its memory business warned the supply crunch could extend to 2028 and beyond. Elsewhere, SK Hynix delivered a similar warning, saying it had secured long-term agreements covering more than Half of its production capacity for2027 and 2028. Micron, the third major supplier for Apple aside from Samsung and SK Hynix, is also benefiting from the surging demand for memory. Its latest published outlook warns that supply shortages in memory and storage could take “considerable time” to improve.
We have previously reported several signs of the pressure now confronting Apple. In January, the company was already scrambling to secure memory supplies amid strong demand, with then CEO Tim Cook warning that rising prices could have a greater impact on earnings. By June, rising component expenses had translated into higher retail prices. Apple increased prices across several Mac and iPad models, including a $400 increase to the starting price of the MacBook Pro, due to the RAM crisis. In July, Cook described the memory market as a “hundred-year-flood” and said Apple expected to pay more for memory in the September quarter. The company had also increased its inventory to $11.09 billion as it built a buffer against supply and price pressures.

articles.title: Barracuda Flaws Could Be Chained to Bypass Authorization and Gain Root Access
articles.text:
Barracuda has disclosed details of two vulnerabilities affecting its products that, if chained together, could allow an attacker to bypass authorization controls and gain root access to a susceptible device.
The vulnerabilities, a pre-authentication authorization bypass vulnerability and a command injection vulnerability, have been assigned the CVE identifiers CVE-2026-116606 (CVSS score: 9.3) and CVE-2026-111560 (CVSS score: 8.6), respectively.
While CVE-2026-116606 only affects Email Security Gateway, CVE-2026-111560 impacts the following Barracuda products -
- Email Security Gateway
- Load Balancer Application Delivery Controller
- Message Archiver
- WAF Control Center
- Web Application Firewall
- Web Security Gateway
"Successful exploitation requires an attacker to have access to the administrative interface of an affected product," Barracuda said. "If exploited in combination, these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to bypass authorization controls and obtain root access to the device."
Barracuda said that organizations that do not expose their administrative interfaces to the internet are less vulnerable to the attack path, urging customers to follow the steps below -
- Restrict access to administrative interfaces to trusted internal networks
- Use appropriate network access controls to limit exposure
"Customers using these products should verify that their systems are running the latest firmware versions and have received all security patches," it added. "If firmware on a device is multiple versions out of date, customers may need to perform more than one update."

articles.title: Generative media inference startup fal raises $1.3B at a $16B valuation - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Generative media inference startup fal raises $1.3B at a $16B valuation
Generative media inference startup fal today announced it has raised $1.3 billion in new funding at a valuation of $16 billion, according to Bloomberg.
The company will spend the money on computing power and on hiring beyond its current 185 employees.
Fal provides a cloud platform for running image, video and audio generation models, and developers reach all of them through a single application programming interface. Entertainment studios, advertising agencies and game developers are among the customers using those models in production, according to the company.
In-house researchers also post-train some of those models to run faster. Over the past year that work has centered on video, in partnership with the open- and closed-source developers that build the models. Some of the deals pay fal licensing fees or a share of revenue, Bloomberg reported.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Burkay Gur told the outlet the round is as large as it is because demand has surged and serving it takes more compute. “We hit a point in summer where we were not able to serve our customers and had to rate-limit them,” he said. Pretraining a model of fal’s own is not on the near-term agenda, said Gur, who did not rule it out for later.
Annualized revenue at fal passed $800 million earlier this year, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. The valuation puts fal just behind rival inference provider Fireworks AI Inc., which closed $1.5 billion in funding at a $17.5 billion valuation in July. Several people familiar with the finances of inference companies told TechCrunch that gross margins across the sector remain thin because compute is expensive to buy or lease.
Gur started the company in 2021 with Chief Technology Officer Gorkem Yurtseven. His resume includes leading machine learning work at Coinbase Global Inc. and an engineering role at Oracle Corp. Yurtseven was previously a developer at Amazon.com Inc.
Bessemer Venture Partners led the Series F round, and its partner Talia Goldberg is joining the board of Features & Labels Inc., as fal is formally known. Nvidia Corp., Sound Ventures, HOF Capital and T. Rowe Price Group Inc. also participated. Fal described Nvidia as a strategic investor.
Today’s announcement also covered an April round led by Sequoia Capital. That Series E round raised $350 million at an $8 billion valuation, per Bloomberg, and fal said the two rounds come to $1.65 billion combined. Last December, the company raised $140 million at a $4.5 billion valuation.
Investors have now put more than $1.9 billion into the company.

articles.title: 3,3 l/100 km : Toyota redonne une chance au thermique avec un moteur hybride d'un nouveau genre !
articles.text:
Toyota a beau vendre plus d’électriques que par le passé, l’hybride reste bel et bien son fonds de commerce. La marque japonaise continue donc d’investir massivement sur cette technologie avec un tout nouveau moteur qui ravira les automobilistes encore frileux de passer à l’électrique. Cette motorisation fera même d’une pierre deux coups en remplaçant le quatre-cylindres de 1.8 l et le trois-cylindres de 1.3 l. Autant dire qu’il ne faudra pas se louper !
La feuille de route a été claire : ce bloc inédit de 1.5 l a été conçu dès le départ pour fonctionner de concert avec un électromoteur. L’entente devrait donc être parfaite puisque Toyota annonce des frottements mécaniques réduits, une gestion thermique optimisée et des pertes électriques moindres. De quoi rendre cet ensemble 15 % moins gourmand que les mécaniques actuelles. Il sera proposé en version atmosphérique et turbocompressée.
Full-hybride, rechargeable et prolongateur d’autonomie : une polyvalence inédite
D’ailleurs, la partie électrique jouira également de plusieurs déclinaisons. Le système full-hybride qui a fait la réputation du constructeur japonais demeurera, tout comme l’hybride rechargeable, en majorité choisi par les entreprises. La nouveauté résidera sur la compatibilité avec une architecture à prolongateur d’autonomie, où le moteur thermique servira uniquement à produire de l’électricité afin d’augmenter le rayon d’action.
Dans les trois cas, les composants électriques seront plus légers et plus compacts grâce à des électromoteurs entièrement revus pour une meilleure efficience. Bénéfice inattendu de la chose, Toyota profitera de cette conception plus intelligente pour réduire la hauteur du capot par rapport aux modèles actuels. Moins de hauteur signifiant moins de prise au vent, l’aérodynamisme ne pourra qu’être amélioré.
3,3 l/100 km : la future Toyota Corolla prête à battre des records d’efficience
Un moteur unique génèrera en parallèle de confortables économies d’échelle. Ces dernières pourront ainsi être réinjectées dans le développement de projets futurs. Cela signifie donc que cette même motorisation sera déployée sur un nombre considérable de véhicules de la marque. Et carrément plus ? Il n’est en effet pas exclu que Lexus puisse aussi en profiter. Mais quelle sera la première voiture à bénéficier de cet ensemble très attendu ?
Tous les yeux sont tournés vers la future Toyota Corolla prévue pour 2028. La célèbre compacte intégrera dans son catalogue des motorisations hybrides, hybrides rechargeables et électriques. L’auto pourrait alors voir sa consommation mixte abaissée à 3,3 l/100 km en hybride autoréchargeable. De quoi permettre à l’une des voitures les plus populaires au monde de viser de nouveaux records d’efficience.

articles.title: GPU Prices Up Again in October, RTX 5090 Now Sells for 262% Over MSRP Worldwide
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 3rd 2026
GPU Prices Up Again in October, RTX 5090 Now Sells for 262% Over MSRP Worldwide
In a big surprise to no one, graphics card prices went up again in October. TechSpot's latest survey across 10 countries shows GPU prices rising 11% month over month, following a 15% jump in August and 7% in September, or roughly 35% over three months. On average, cards now sell for 44% above MSRP, climbing to 58% in the US and Canada. Keep in mind these numbers track the lowest in-stock price in each region, so most models cost even more. Moreover, there is another GeForce RTX 50-series price hike on the horizon, so these numbers will rise again pretty soon.
The GeForce RTX 5090 is in a league of its own. It got 32% pricier in a month, and its normalized global price of $7,240 sits a staggering 262% above its $1,999 MSRP, almost double the 136% figure from early September. In the US, the cheapest in-stock model now costs $9,400, or 370% over MSRP, and most models now sit above $11,000 comfortably. The RTX 5080 is following a similar path, up 22% in a month to $2,200 in the US, while Newegg had none of its own in stock when the data was collected. TechSpot argues the GDDR7 memory crisis can't explain a jump that big, and some retail sources apparently told them wholesale RTX 5080 costs have gone up recently too.NVIDIA has denied that the RTX 5090 is discontinued, although reports also point to a 24 GB RTX 5080 replacing the current model. That could also be another reason why the RTX 5090 and RTX 5080 16 GB are rising rapidly. Radeon cards rose even faster than GeForce this time if the RTX 5090 is excluded, with the RX 9060 XT 16 GB up 17% month over month. The RX 9070 XT also climbed 12% and is getting close to $1,000 in some regions, and that is before AMD's planned November price hike kicks in. Judging by these pricing trends and the current industry outlook, prices probably haven't peaked yet.

articles.title: Proton VPN 8.0 is coming to iPhone — and it could be the app's biggest upgrade in years
articles.text:
Proton VPN 8.0 is coming to iPhone — and it could be the app's biggest upgrade in years
A new Rust-based VPN engine, an advanced kill switch, and CarPlay-friendly connectivity are all on the way
- Proton VPN has published iOS 8.0.0 on GitHub, but the update is yet to reach the App Store
- Its primary focus is Proton protocols, a new Rust-based VPN engine aimed at stability and censorship resistance.
- An advanced kill switch, an interactive globe map, and better CarPlay support are also on the way.
Proton VPN users on iPhone have a big update to look forward to. The provider has published iOS 8.0.0 on its GitHub releases page, and it could be the most significant change to the app in years.
The biggest addition is Proton protocols, a new VPN architecture that Proton says is designed for improved stability and censorship resistance. It also makes the advanced kill switch possible on iPhone and iPad, a feature that has so far only been available on iOS in beta.
Proton VPN already sits among the best VPN services we've tested, climbing to third place in our latest round of re-testing. Anything that tightens up its iOS app is good news for privacy-minded iPhone owners.
What's new in Proton VPN 8.0 for iOS
The biggest change is one you won't see. Proton protocols, known internally as ProTUN, swaps out the standard wireguard-go code for libpvpnclient, Proton's own WireGuard implementation written in Rust.
Proton says wireguard-go never integrated well with Swift, the language it uses to build its iOS app, which made development and debugging harder.
For users, Proton promises faster updates, fewer platform-specific bugs, and a quicker response when censors change tactics.
The new core also lays the groundwork for post-quantum encryption, which Proton lists as a planned feature. Antonio Cesarano, Product Lead at Proton VPN, says it lets the team experiment with "connection stability, battery usage, and resilience".
A stricter kill switch for your iPhone
A standard kill switch cuts your internet if the VPN connection drops. Proton's advanced kill switch goes further, blocking all internet access unless you're connected to Proton VPN, and it stays active even after you restart your device.
That's a notable step on iOS, where Apple's network restrictions have long made a true kill switch difficult. Proton itself once said a kill switch as it defined it wasn't possible on iOS. Even now, Proton warns that some DNS requests from Apple services can bypass the VPN with the kill switch on.
Version 8.0 also fixes a common frustration. You'll be able to reach LAN devices, like printers, and use Apple CarPlay with either kill switch enabled.
When can you get Proton VPN 8.0?
Proton hasn't announced a release date. However, with the final 8.0.0 build now tagged on GitHub, the App Store rollout could land any time now, though Apple's review process can add a delay.
Monica is a tech journalist with over a decade of experience. She writes about the latest developments in computing, which means anything from computer chips made out of paper to cutting-edge desktop processors.
GPUs are her main area of interest, and nothing thrills her quite like that time every couple of years when new graphics cards hit the market.
She built her first PC nearly 20 years ago, and dozens of builds later, she’s always planning out her next build (or helping her friends with theirs). During her career, Monica has written for many tech-centric outlets, including Digital Trends, SlashGear, WePC, and Tom’s Hardware.

articles.title: Hands-on with the DockCase Mount Ling 2 Pro — handheld dock with a built-in capture card and space for up to 4TB of NVMe storage
articles.text:
Hands-on with the DockCase Mount Ling 2 Pro — handheld dock with a built-in capture card and space for up to 4TB of NVMe storage
Mount Ling 2 Pro offers a lot of flexibility for a gaming dock.
DockCase is no stranger to Kickstarting unique SSD enclosures and docks, with the company’s Visual Smart M.2 enclosure making its way onto our list of the best SSD enclosures. The Mount Ling 2 Pro, however, is gunning for a spot among the best USB-C docks. It’s a dock for handhelds like the Steam Deck and Switch 2, an external enclosure for an NVMe SSD, and a game capture device, all packaged up in a dock that can show off your handheld and expand your port selection.
There are two versions of the dock: the standard Mount Ling 2 and the Pro version. The only difference between them is the internal capture card. The base version is $109 via an early bird deal while the Kickstarter gets underway, and the Pro version is $149. They’ll be priced at $199 and $249, respectively, after the early deals are gone.
It’s the world’s first “smart creator dock,” says DockCase, which is partially true. There are other docks that give you additional inputs, a stand, and capture capabilities with a handheld, and at a lower price. The AVerMedia X’TRA GO, for instance, offers all of that for $160. The differentiator here is the internal M.2 slot that can support up to 4TB of NVMe storage, with points to mount 2280, 2242, and 2230-sized drives. Of course, this external storage only works with platforms that normally support external storage (so, not the Switch or Switch 2).
For PC-adjacent handhelds running Windows or Linux, the Mount Ling 2 Pro is an expensive but useful dock that gives you capture, storage, and port expandability in one attractive package. For the Switch and Switch 2, the usefulness isn’t as clear. You can’t use the SSD with either platform, and Nintendo’s game of whack-a-mole with third-party accessories means a system update could break HDMI passthrough (and, in the process, the capture function of the dock).
Mount Ling Dock 2 specifications
DockCase says the Mount Ling 2 Pro supports the Steam Deck, ROG Ally, Switch, Switch 2, and “more,” presumably wrapping up other Windows- or Linux-based handhelds like the ROG Ally X Xbox or Lenovo Legion Go S. Switch and Switch 2 are supported, as well, though getting Nintendo’s handheld to connect properly isn’t always smooth.
The dock connects to your handheld with a USB 3.2 Gen Type-C connection capable of 10 Gbps, and DockCase includes a small, braided 40 Gbps cable in the box, along with two right-angle connectors. That single connection gives you up to 100W through the USB-C port, along with Gigabit Ethernet, an HDMI 2.0 connection (4K@60Hz), a single USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A port, and a USB 2.0 port. An additional USB-C connection serves as another USB 3.2 Gen 2 port on the Mount Ling 2, while it becomes the capture card output on the Pro model.
Interestingly, there’s also an optical audio output available. Although I don’t suspect most users will put it to use (HDMI transfers audio, as well), it’s a nice fallback if you plan on using the dock with a more elaborate audio setup. It’s a nice bonus, though I would’ve liked a 3.5mm audio jack as well, considering handhelds no longer have access to that connection.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The dock itself is constructed almost entirely of plastic, and holding it in your hands, you can tell it’s filled with more air than hardware. It’s a sizable package at 8.4 x 7 x 3.5 inches. Outside of the shell, there’s a thick layer of firm silicone to rest your handheld on. There are grooves to provide a natural resting place for just about any handheld, as well as a deep central cut that fits the Switch and Switch 2 specifically.
You can install your SSD at the bottom of the dock, with mounting points for 2280, 2242, and 2230 drives. There's a single 40mm fan internally, as well as venting around the back and side edges, to keep the drive cool. The fan will automatically adjust its speed out of the box, but you’re free to manually adjust the speed or turn the fan off, if you want.
Unfortunately, there’s no room for a heatsink. The face of the drive sits nearly flush against the vented cover on the bottom of the dock. Even if you left the cover off, most heatsinks would push past the rubber feet and prop the dock up.
Using the Mount Ling 2 Pro dock
Setting up the Mount Ling 2 Pro is mostly a matter of plugging everything in and getting on your way. The dock goes through a connecting phase when you hook up a new device, and it’s finicky. Sometimes it would drop one part of the connection, like charging, while picking up another, particularly with the Switch 2. You want to have the dock fully connected before hooking up your host.
The main page of the dock’s screen provides HDMI, SSD, and power info at a glance, which is helpful to quickly check, for example, that the HDMI passthrough is operating at the correct resolution and refresh rate without digging into the settings. A swipe to the right brings up five quick-access settings, which just take you into the settings menu, while a swipe to the right gives you access to volume and fan controls. The volume adjustment on the dock is passed through to the host.
Swiping up instead gives you the full settings menu, which has more to monitor than adjust. You can see the SSD details (including SMART monitors), the status of USB connections, and your HDMI info, andother details about the dock. For settings, there are different HDMI transfer modes, in case you run into a broken handshake, along with power delivery settings if you need to roll back to PD 2.0.
For the dock itself, you have some small control over the fan and built-in lighting. For the fan, you can adjust the speed manually, turn it off, or leave it on the default automatic mode. The lighting settings are surprisingly bare. You can choose between blue, red, or a gradient between them, and that’s it. Otherwise, you can just dim or turn off the lights. If you find the screen and lights distracting, there’s a dedicated button on the back of the dock to turn all the lights off (including the screen).
Although the screen is responsive with minimal lag between swipes and taps, the software running here isn’t perfect. Particularly with the Switch 2, if I connected things in the wrong order, the dock would force itself to reboot, only sometimes picking up the Switch 2 when it came back. DockCase offers firmware updates over USB, and hopefully it gets a patch between units shipped to fix some of these quirks.
The firmware updates are a nice sign, but they bring up an unfortunate reality of creating a device for the Switch 2 without Nintendo’s seal of approval. Both the Switch and Switch 2 are infamously fickle with third-party docks and hubs. A system update could break compatibility, forcing a firmware update.
DockCase plays up Switch 2 support on its product page, and that is a big draw. However, the dock can’t get around the limitations that Nintendo itself has placed on its handheld. You may as well fill the SSD slot with concrete if you’re docking a Switch 2, and docking the device is troublesome. It took multiple emails for me to get the Switch 2 to pass through its HDMI signal at all. You have to connect everything in a specific way, and critically, have the Switch 2 already unlocked when you plug it into the bottom USB-C port; the top port won’t work.
With the Steam Deck, everything was seamless, and although I didn’t have a Windows handheld on hand to try out, I don’t anticipate there will be major issues. DockCase may offer a lot of functionality in a single box with the Mount Ling Pro 2, but it’s all operating over standard connections that are well supported in the Windows ecosystem.
You can use the SSD with the Steam Deck, though you’ll need to head to desktop mode to partition the drive and add a folder for Steam games. The process is similar on Windows handhelds if you’re using some sort of handheld-native overlay.
For the capture portion, it serves its purpose. Critically, DockCase doesn’t have any software for capturing or recording like the mainstream capture cards you’ll find from Elgato and AVerMedia, so you’ll need to use something else like OBS. For any of these types of recording/streaming platforms, the DockCase shows up as a simple video capture device, with resolution and frame rate determined by your settings on the host device (assuming it’s within that 4K60 limit that HDMI 2.0 is capable of).
There isn’t much of a need here for HDMI 2.1, considering the types of devices connecting to the Mount Ling Pro 2, though it would’ve been a nice upside. You can still push the refresh rate higher, just not at 4K. And in fairness to DockCase, the devices it’s targeting really have no business driving a 4K display.
Mount Ling 2 Pro SSD performance
You shouldn’t expect wonders out of SSD performance with the Mount Ling 2 Pro, given that it uses a USB 3.2 Gen 2 connection that’s only capable of up to 10 Gbps. High performance in an external enclosure is the game of Thunderbolt 5 docks with M.2 storage, which can often reach sequential reads above 5,000 MB/s over the 80 Gbps Thunderbolt 5 interface. Here, the connection will bottleneck your speeds, all the way down to typical PCIe 3.0 NVMe SSDs.
Still, in the context of gaming on a handheld, that isn’t the end of the world. It’s nice to have that much storage on tap for a device like the Steam Deck, which is otherwise only expandable with a larger internal SSmicroSDicro SD card.
In CrystalDiskMark, the Mount Ling 2 Pro landed with sequential reads and writes around 820 MB/s, with random performance far lower. We tested with a 2 TB WD_Black SN770, which is a PCIe 4.0 drive that boasts sequential reads up to 5150 MB/s when installed directly in a motherboard. In the Mount Ling 2 Pro, it behaves more like an external SSD like the SK hynix Beetle X31 2TB, naturally hamstrung by the connection.
Overall Mount Ling 2 Pro impressions
The Mount Ling 2 Pro does a lot, combining external storage, a capture card, and an attractive dock into a single package that works with both PC handhelds and the Nintendo Switch 2. The SSD performance isn’t great, as is to be expected out of a dock that uses a 10 Gbps USB link for connection, but that downside isn’t much of a concern considering the devices this dock targets.
Although Switch 2 support is a big upside, it’s also fickle. You don’t get access to the SSD, and the connection can fail if you don’t follow the order of operations for connection. The Mount Ling 2 Pro makes sense if you have a Switch 2 and a PC handheld of some kind, but as a pure Switch 2 dock, it doesn’t make much sense. You’d be better off buying an external capture card for use with the official dock.
Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

articles.title: L’iPhone Air passe sous les 900 € : un grand écran 120 Hz dans seulement 165 g
articles.text:
Le smartphone Apple iPhone Air 256 Go est à 899 € chez Amazon (-32 %)
Fin et léger, doté d’un écran Oled 120 Hz, l’iPhone Air 256 Go passe à 899 € chez Amazon, soit 32 % sous le prix conseillé affiché par le marchand.
L’offre concerne le coloris Blanc nuage, vendu et expédié par Amazon. L’écart atteint 430 € face aux 1 329 € de prix conseillé affichés sur la fiche. Aucun code promotionnel ni remboursement différé n’est nécessaire.
Un grand écran dans un smartphone particulièrement léger
Avec ses 5,6 mm d’épaisseur hors bloc photo et ses 165 g, l’iPhone Air mise sur le confort en main. Son cadre en titane accompagne un écran Oled de 6,5 pouces : un format généreux pour consulter ses contenus sans supporter le poids d’un grand smartphone classique.
Notre test souligne la luminosité élevée et la justesse des couleurs de cette dalle, dont le rafraîchissement adaptatif atteint 120 Hz. La puce A19 Pro assure également des performances élevées, même si la chauffe se manifeste lors des sollicitations prolongées.
Une formule séduisante, avec quelques compromis
L’unique appareil photo arrière de 48 mégapixels délivre de bons résultats. En revanche, l’absence d’ultra grand-angle et de téléobjectif dédié limite les possibilités de cadrage. L’Air conviendra davantage aux amateurs de simplicité qu’aux photographes recherchant une grande polyvalence.
L’autonomie reste aussi inférieure à celle de l’iPhone 17 dans nos mesures. Autres éléments à connaître avant l’achat : ce modèle utilise exclusivement l’eSIM et aucun adaptateur secteur n’est fourni. La charge sans fil MagSafe reste disponible.

articles.title: Indian startups over $500M valuation grow to 51 despite low number of AI entities: Report
articles.text:
Indian startups with over $500M valuation grow to 51 despite low number of AI entities: Report
The combined value of these 51 entities is about Rs 3.3 lakh crore ($34.1 billion), with an average valuation of about Rs 6,400 crore, and they employ over 60,000 people.
Indian startups with a valuation of over $500 million have increased to 51 in 2026, from 47 in the year-ago period despite lower number of artificial intelligence (AI) companies, a report said on Tuesday.
The combined value of these 51 entities is about Rs 3.3 lakh crore ($34.1 billion), with an average valuation of about Rs 6,400 crore, and they employ over 60,000 people, as per the 2026 ASK Private Wealth Hurun India Gazelle Index report.
The entities have reported combined revenue of Rs 33,233 crore, growing 50% year-on-year, the report said.
Anas Rahman Junaid, founder and chief researcher, Hurun India, said the list includes three names engaged in AI, including Ema AI, Observe.AI and UnifyApps which is very low when compared with 54 in the US and 23 in China.
However, despite this, the number of Indian gazelles, or the companies with over $500 million, has grown to 51 this year, he added.
The lack of AI-themed companies is often cited as one of the biggest reasons for foreign investors withdrawing from the Indian public equity markets.
The report said seven startups crossed $1 billion to become unicorns in 2026, with Twin Health's valuation rising to $2 billion from $700 million. Financial services and healthcare account for six of the seven.
"It reflects an entrepreneurial base that is diversifying across sectors and geographies and building scalable businesses with the potential to compete globally," said Rajesh Saluja, Co-Founder, CEO & MD of ASK Private Wealth.
Further, the report said AI and CleanTech are the largest of the three frontier sectors, with three startups each.
AI group comprises Ema AI, Observe.AI and UnifyApps, and CleanTech comprises Carbon Clean Solutions, Lohum and Rayzon Solar.
A total of 34 startups have moved up to unicorn status on the CGU Index since inception. Two startups were listed on the public markets, Shadowfax in January 2026 and Turtlemint in June 2026, the report said.
FinTech is the largest sector with 13 startups, followed by SaaS and ecommerce with five each. Bengaluru is home to 17 startups in the list, ahead of NCR with 11 and Mumbai with eight.
The report said 10 startups maintain a headquarters outside India--seven in the US, two in Singapore, and one in the UK. India ranks third globally in startups--behind the US and China.
IIT Kharagpur is the most common undergraduate institution among startup founders with 13, followed by IIT Bombay and IIT Kanpur with six each, the report said.
Further, IIT Bombay is the most common postgraduate institution among startup founders with seven, followed by IIM Ahmedabad with five.
The report added that women founders are present across six startups, Prukalpa Sankar (Atlan), Shruti Aggarwal (StashFin), Sunita Sahney (Finova Capital), Amrita Sirohia (INDMoney), Pallavi Shrivastava (Progcap) and Nikita Prasad (GIVA).

articles.title: El Reino Unido prevé un ataque con IA contra sus servicios esenciales antes de 2028
articles.text:
El Centro Nacional de Ciberseguridad (NCSC) del Reino Unido, parte de la agencia de espionaje GCHQ, advirtió que el país debe prepararse para un ataque informático con inteligencia artificial contra su infraestructura crítica antes de 2028. Lo planteó el 3 de noviembre en su informe anual, que identifica a China como el actor más capaz.
Según el informe, es muy probable que en los próximos dos años se use un programa malicioso con IA en un ataque de secuestro de datos (ransomware, que cifra los archivos de la víctima y exige un pago) contra la infraestructura crítica británica. Esta incluye energía, transporte, defensa, alimentación, salud y finanzas.
The Guardian precisó que el organismo habla de centrales eléctricas, aeropuertos y hospitales como posibles objetivos. El NCSC también estima que, en ese plazo, el uso de inteligencia artificial por parte de actores hostiles aumentará la escala y la eficiencia de sus operaciones, incluidos el engaño a personas y la explotación de fallas de seguridad.
China, Rusia e Irán, en la mira
El director ejecutivo del NCSC, Richard Horne, dijo en el texto previsto de su discurso que China tiene “muy probablemente” la intención y es la mejor posicionada para usar IA contra la infraestructura crítica británica. Su actividad, añadió, representa el desafío cibernético más sofisticado y sostenido que enfrenta el país.
Horne también señaló, según Reuters, que Rusia intenta de forma sostenida penetrar redes militares británicas y que Irán realiza operaciones maliciosas en todo el mundo, incluidas algunas dirigidas al Reino Unido. La evaluación del NCSC prevé que Rusia, China y otros Estados usarán IA “de forma rutinaria” en sus ciberoperaciones hacia 2028.
La evaluación técnica del organismo plantea tres escenarios hasta 2028, que describe como posibilidades plausibles y no como predicciones. Advierte además que “la posibilidad de sorpresa es alta”, porque la capacidad de la IA aplicada a ataques cambia con rapidez.
El problema, según el NCSC, son las fallas antiguas
Horne sostuvo que la IA no inventó nuevas formas de atacar. “Vulnerabilidades que se han tolerado durante demasiado tiempo ahora pueden ser descubiertas y explotadas a una escala antes inimaginable”, afirmó. También habló de una “posibilidad real” de un aumento sin precedentes de incidentes en los próximos meses.
El jefe del NCSC atribuyó esa exposición a décadas de “tecnología barata” en organizaciones y cadenas de suministro. Pidió invertir en tecnología, desconectar de internet los sistemas que no lo necesitan y tomar el programa Cyber Essentials, de medidas básicas, como punto de partida y no como meta.
Horne advirtió que, si los dirigentes no actúan, deberán explicar a inversores, empleados y clientes qué pasó “cuando no hay comida en los estantes, no hay luz” y hay empresas quebradas. Según el NCSC, el informe pide “cambios significativos” para evitar un futuro en que la IA se use contra la economía y la sociedad.
La advertencia llega con anuncios del Gobierno. La semana anterior, el ministro de Economía británico anunció 60 millones de libras para la primera fase de un escudo nacional contra ciberataques y 70 millones de libras para un centro que detecte vulnerabilidades en la infraestructura. También creará en Manchester un centro de excelencia en seguridad de IA, a cargo del NCSC.
El ministro de Seguridad, Dan Jarvis, afirmó que el Gobierno usa la IA para mantenerse por delante de quienes buscan hacer daño. El Ejecutivo impulsa además el proyecto de ley de Seguridad y Resiliencia Cibernética y un Plan Nacional de Acción Cibernética, que aún no se publicó, según el comunicado del NCSC.

articles.title: La salida a bolsa de Anthropic conseguirá algo tan poco habitual como que el 80% de su plantilla se haga millonaria
articles.text:
2026 está siendo un año de infarto para los gestores de fondos, no solo por el nivel de beneficios que está reportando a los inversores las cotizaciones estratosféricas de las grandes tecnológicas, sino por la salida a bolsa de los nuevos pesos pesados de la IA como SpaceX o Anthropic.
La salida a bolsa de SpaceX ya hizo millonarios a muchos de sus empleados, pero en el caso de Anthropic, el fenómeno se intensifica y el resultado es que ocho de cada diez empleados de Dario Amodei y sus socios serán millonarios el día después de esa salida a bolsa.
Cuatro de cada cinco. La empresa ya presentó su documento ante la SEC y, según informó Bloomberg, quiere debutar hacia mediados del mes de noviembre. Aún no se ha fijado un precio de salida para su cotización ni una fecha concreta, pero se habla de una valoración de entre 1,5 y 2 billones de dólares.
Según recoge The Observer, un informe de la plataforma financiera Hill reparte el botín de sus empleados por tramos. Sumados todos ellos, salen unos 4.250 nuevos millonarios de entre los 5.300 empleados que Anthropic declaraba en su informe S-1 ante la autoridad bursátil norteamericana. Eso representa el 80% de la plantilla, una suma que no sale de ninguna fuente oficial. SpaceX hizo algo parecido en junio, convirtiendo en millonarios a más de 4.400 empleados entre su plantilla actual y antigua, pero en este caso se trataba de una plantilla de unos 22.000 empleados. En el caso de Anthropic, la proporción de nuevos millonarios es muy superior.
Siete que ya lo eran. Los cofundadores no cuentan como nuevos millonarios porque, de hecho, ya son milmimillonarios incluso antes de la salida a bolsa de la compañía. Forbes calcula que cada uno de los siete fundadores posee cerca del 1,4% de la empresa.
Con una valoración de entre 1,5 y 2 billones en su salida a bolsa, su parte se colocaría entre los 27.000 y 29.000 millones de dólares por cabeza. Juntos controlan en torno al 10% del capital. Aun así, comparten una acción especial sin derechos económicos que concentra el 50,1% de los votos de los accionistas.
Los empleados más fieles. Un poco más abajo en el reparto de acciones (y beneficios), Hill estima que unos 50 de los primeros empleados y directivos pasarían a tener una fortuna de más de 100 millones de dólares tras la salida a bolsa por el valor de los paquetes de participaciones que han recibido como reconocimiento de "empleados fundadores". Son menos del 1% de la plantilla y entraron en Anthropic cuando la empresa aún tenía que demostrar su valía.
Más abajo estaría un segundo escalón de unos 1.200 empleados de alta cualificación e investigadores que, por las participaciones asociadas a sus paquetes salariales, acumularían más de 10 millones de dólares, casi una cuarta parte del total. Otros 3.000 empleados, con retribuciones de menor cuantía, pasarían del millón de dólares tras la salida a bolsa. Todas estas son cifras mínimas, calculadas en base a una valoración hipotética de 1,5 billones, a los que habría que sumar unos 1.000 empleados que se quedarían por debajo de ese millón de dólares.
Promesas y plazos. Los siete cofundadores prometieron donar el 80% de su patrimonio a fines filantrópicos destinados a paliar los efectos negativos de la tecnología que están desarrollando. Dario Amodei escribió que lo preocupante es "un nivel de concentración de riqueza que destruirá la sociedad". El propio folleto de la salida a bolsa de Anthropic admite que la IA "tiene el potencial de concentrar el poder y la riqueza".
No obstante, el dinero tampoco llegará de golpe a la plantilla de Anthropic, porque los empleados no podrán vender sus acciones inmediatamente después la salida a bolsa, sino que se abrirán por fases a partir de enero de 2027. Anthropic usará parte de lo que recaude para pagar impuestos de las acciones de sus empleados.

articles.title: Zelda le 5 novembre, GTA 6 le 19 : les promos Black Friday Switch 2 et PS5 à ne pas manquer
articles.text:
Le Black Friday 2026 tombe en pleine rafale de sorties : le remake de Zelda Ocarina of Time arrive le 5 novembre sur Switch 2, GTA 6 le 19 novembre sur PS5, et Amazon, Joybuy, AliExpress et Boulanger ont déjà baissé leurs prix gaming. Nous avons retenu 8 offres, des consoles Nintendo aux équipements audio compatibles PS5, en précisant pour chacune avec quelle console et quels jeux elle fonctionne vraiment.
Deux jeux attendus depuis des années sortent à deux semaines d’écart. Le remake de The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time est annoncé le 5 novembre, en exclusivité sur Switch 2, et GTA 6 le 19 novembre sur PS5. Le Black Friday, fixé au 27 novembre, arrive après, mais les remises ont commencé dès ce début de mois.
Cette sélection couvre les deux camps : trois consoles Nintendo, trois accessoires pour la Switch 2 et deux équipements audio compatibles PS5. Les remises vont de 3 % à 40 %, et deux d’entre elles passent par un code promo AliExpress à saisir au paiement. Les prix ont été relevés le 3 novembre 2026 en début d’après-midi et peuvent évoluer.
Les meilleures offres Switch 2 et PS5 repérées pour le Black Friday
- Nintendo Switch 2 à 429,99 € au lieu de 469,99 €
- Nintendo Switch OLED à 229 € au lieu de 349 € avec le code CLU40
- Nintendo Switch Lite Corail à 193,84 € au lieu de 199,99 €
- Manette Nintendo Switch 2 Pro à 53,96 € au lieu de 89,99 € avec le code FRD1108
- Joy-Con 2 bleu et jaune pour Switch 2 à 69,99 € au lieu de 89,99 €
- Nintendo Switch 2 Caméra à 39,99 € au lieu de 59,99 €
- Sony Inzone H9 II à 199,99 € au lieu de 229 €
- Razer Hammerhead V3 X HyperSpeed à 81,99 € au lieu de 109,99 €
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Ce qu’il faut savoir avant d’acheter
Le produit phare de cette sélection est aussi le seul qui fasse tourner le remake de Zelda. Dans notre test de la Nintendo Switch 2, nous lui avions donné 8/10 : design et écran en nette progression, performances enfin à la hauteur, mais une autonomie en recul et un tarif global élevé. Voici ce que nous retenons de six offres.
- Nintendo Switch 2 : à 429,99 €, elle passe 40 € sous son prix de lancement de 469,99 €. Elle apporte un écran LCD de 7,9 pouces en 1080p à 120 Hz, 256 Go de stockage et la rétrocompatibilité avec les jeux Switch. Sur batterie, Nintendo annonce de 2 à 6,5 heures selon les jeux, moins que les modèles précédents.
- Nintendo Switch OLED : la plus forte baisse en euros, 120 € avec le code FRD1140, pour un écran OLED de 7 pouces aux contrastes nettement supérieurs au LCD. Attention au calendrier : elle ne lancera pas le remake de Zelda, réservé à la Switch 2, et reste sur la puce Tegra X1+, plafonnée à 720p en portable.
- Nintendo Switch Lite : la remise se limite à 3 %, et ce modèle se joue uniquement en portable, sans dock ni Joy-Con détachables. Elle s’adresse à un enfant ou à un joueur nomade qui cherche l’entrée de gamme chez Nintendo, pas à celui qui attend Zelda.
- Manette Nintendo Switch 2 Pro : 40 % de remise avec le code FRD1108, la plus forte de la sélection. Elle ajoute deux boutons arrière programmables, une prise jack 3,5 mm et un bouton dédié au GameChat, pour une autonomie annoncée d’environ 40 heures. Elle ne fonctionne qu’avec la Switch 2.
- Sony Inzone H9 II : côté PS5, ce casque sans fil de 260 g combine connexion 2,4 GHz, Bluetooth LE Audio et prise jack, avec réduction de bruit active et micro amovible. Son autonomie de 30 heures reste en retrait de la concurrence, et la remise de 13 % est modeste.
- Razer Hammerhead V3 X HyperSpeed : des écouteurs sous licence PlayStation dont le boîtier sert à la fois d’étui de charge et de récepteur 2,4 GHz à brancher sur la console. Comptez 35 heures d’autonomie avec le boîtier et une protection IPX4, pour 28 € de moins que le prix affiché avant remise.
Switch 2 ou PS5 : où se trouvent les vraies affaires
Côté Nintendo, la hiérarchie dépend du jeu visé. Pour Zelda Ocarina of Time, seule la Switch 2 convient, et ses accessoires de la sélection (manette Pro, Joy-Con 2, caméra) n’ont d’intérêt qu’avec elle. La Switch OLED affiche la plus grosse économie en euros, mais pour un modèle de 2021 qui restera à l’écart des exclusivités Switch 2. Si vous hésitez entre une console Nintendo et une console portable pour PC, notre comparatif des meilleures consoles portables situe ces modèles face au Steam Deck et à l’ASUS ROG Ally.
Côté PS5, la sélection ne contient aucune console : les remises repérées portent sur l’audio. Le Razer Hammerhead V3 X HyperSpeed offre la baisse la plus nette, 25 %, quand le Sony Inzone H9 II ne recule que de 13 %. Pour GTA 6, le choix se fait donc entre la discrétion d’écouteurs intra-auriculaires et le confort d’un casque circum-aural avec réduction de bruit.
Vos questions sur ces promos Switch 2 et PS5
Le remake de Zelda Ocarina of Time fonctionne-t-il sur Switch OLED ou Switch Lite ?
Non. Le remake est annoncé en exclusivité sur Switch 2, pour une sortie le 5 novembre 2026 : la Switch OLED et la Switch Lite de cette sélection ne permettront pas d’y jouer.
Comment obtenir le prix annoncé sur les offres AliExpress ?
La Switch OLED et la manette Switch 2 Pro n’atteignent leur prix qu’avec un code promo saisi au paiement : FRD1140 pour la console, FRD1108 pour la manette.
Quand a lieu le Black Friday 2026 ?
Le Black Friday tombe le vendredi 27 novembre 2026, après la sortie de GTA 6 le 19 novembre. Les prix de cette sélection ont été relevés le 3 novembre 2026 et peuvent évoluer d’ici là.

Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.
Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: Anthropic tells Claude Code to stop recreating existing video games
articles.text:
In context: Vibe coding and AI agents have made game decompilation and recompilation child's play, but things might soon change significantly. Claude Code is now being instructed to avoid performing this type of workload, meaning decompilation enthusiasts will need to turn elsewhere to get the job done.
Claude might soon stop being one of the best AI tools for decompiling and recompiling existing games. According to Anthropic programmer Addy Osmani, the model behind the company's vibe-coding service will now avoid user prompts that request recreations of someone else's video games.
The change was first spotted by decompilation enthusiasts over the weekend. On October 27, Claude Code started picking up a new rule hidden behind the "tengu_heron_brook" flag. The rule is designed to force the AI model to build original games based on users' own designs and assets, rather than content taken from games already on the market.
Read our feature: Decompilation on Steroids: Why AI Is Suddenly Cracking Open Old Software
Soon after the rule was discovered, Osmani confirmed that Anthropic was adding two new sentences to Claude Code's Opus 5.5 model. Recreating someone else's intellectual property is apparently against Claude's usage policy, meaning users should only be able to vibe-code "original" games. Osmani also said the company would continue iterating on the new rules to achieve the "right balance."
 – Addy Osmani (@addyosmani) October 30, 2026
AI-assisted recompilation and decompilation projects have taken the IT world by storm. Vibe coders are now leveraging previous human-made research efforts to "port" console-exclusive games to PC – or vice versa. Projects such as AnyPS5 are even attempting to turn PlayStation 5 games into "native" PC titles.
The vibe-coded decompilation deluge is also having a significant impact on human-led research efforts. The decomp.dev website has now shut down because AI-assisted coding has undermined meaningful efforts to understand and document how game code works. Vibe coders are now forking existing decompilation projects and letting AI finish the job, or racing to port games to different platforms just to plant their flag on the map.
Vibe-coded game recreations might now be more difficult with Claude, but the decompilation "fun" is likely to continue regardless. Users will simply need to switch to other AI models and services, adapt to rapidly improving open-weight models, or resort to offline setups to keep churning out new recompilations and web-based conversions.

articles.title: Salesforce to buy customer service automation startup Cresta for reported $2.7B - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Salesforce to buy customer service automation startup Cresta for reported $2.7B
Salesforce Inc. has agreed to buy Cresta Intelligence Inc., a venture-backed provider of customer service software.
The cloud giant didn’t disclose the financial terms in its late Monday announcement of the deal. The Information reported that Salesforce is paying $2.7 billion.
Cresta’s platform uses artificial intelligence to answer customer inquiries. It can also perform more advanced tasks such as scheduling doctor’s appointments. The platform personalizes its output based on each customer’s preferences, past interactions with the support team and related data.
Companies can customize Cresta by creating AI voice agents optimized for specific support request categories. For example, an electronics retailer could develop an agent focused on processing device returns. Cresta makes it possible to customize details such as the AI model that powers an agent and its regulatory compliance guardrails.
The platform can split complex support requests into smaller tasks to ease processing. A company could use one agent to interpret a ticket, another to find relevant help desk articles and a third to scan those articles for troubleshooting advice. Such agent ensembles often provide faster response times than a single multi-purpose agent. They save time by parallelizing tasks that would usually have to be carried out after one another.
Cresta ships its platform with an agent called Deputy. It’s geared toward particularly complex support tickets that require multiple employees to process. Deputy automatically collects the information needed to fulfill the user’s request and then loops in the relevant workers. From there, it manages follow-up tasks such as sending reminders about outstanding tasks.
Another agent provides human support representatives with real-time guidance during customer conversations. Cresta can, for example, point out potential upselling opportunities. It can also pull relevant information from external systems.
The company offers its core support automation features alongside various related tools. A feature called Opera enables organizations to fine-tune AI models for specific customer service use cases. Another tool, Synthetic Customers, provides AI-generated support conversations. Companies teams can use that data to test the reliability of newly created AI agents.
“By uniting our platform with Salesforce, we will realize our full vision at scale, embedding real-time conversation intelligence and agentic experiences directly into Salesforce’s first-class customer service Platform,” said Cresta Chief Executive Officer Ping Wu.
The deal is the second multibillion-dollar acquisition that Salesforce has made in the customer service market this year. It previously agreed to buy Fin Inc., formerly Intercom Inc, for $3.6 billion. Like Cresta, the company developed an AI platform capable of automatically answering support requests.
Salesforce’s largest acquisition this year is the $5.66 billion purchase of Braze Inc. it signed last month. The deal will buy it an AI marketing platform that can automatically deliver personalized promotions to customers.
Salesforce expects to close both the Braze and Cresta deals in its 2028 fiscal year, which starts next February.
