articles.title: Google Warns LLMjacking Attacks Are Costing Some Enterprises Up to $1 Million in Cloud Charges
articles.text:
Google on Monday warned that threat actors are hijacking enterprise access to Large Language Models (LLMs) to fraudulently leverage expensive computing resources and AI services.
The tactic is called LLMjacking, a form of resource hijacking adapted for the LLM era, where an attacker obtains an API key through phishing, source code leaks, misconfigured environments, or exposed client-side code to gain unauthorized access to an organization's LLM accounts, while the legitimate owner covers the consumption costs.
Such attacks have a wide geographical footprint, with impacted entities located in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific across the financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors.
"Unlike the gradual resource consumption associated with cryptojacking, LLMJacking can generate large spikes in fraudulent cloud charges in a matter of hours," Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
"Across individual incidents, we observed fraudulent charges associated with resource consumption exceeding $100,000 USD in a single day, with cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1 million USD before access was revoked."
On one end of the spectrum are low-level resource theft that involves the manipulation of customer support chatbots to conduct unauthorized tasks like code generation. LLMjacking is on the other end, as they target the backend model resources directly by identifying publicly exposed LLM endpoints or obtaining valid LLM API keys.
The most common initial access vector has been exposed or stolen cloud identity tokens, including IAM credentials, Service Account keys, GitHub Personal Access Tokens (PATs), and active session tokens, which allow an attacker to establish an initial foothold into target organizations' infrastructure.
This includes a threat actor called UNC6993, which is said to have breached a cloud instance through a misconfigured Service Account key and used it to obtain access to an LLM API.
"UNC6993 also hosted a session hijacking page masquerading as an application portal to join a group of LLM users," Google said. "This page tricks users into navigating to the legitimate LLM service website, and pasting their raw JSON payload containing an active access token, which was then posted to the backend API to bypass password and multi-factor authentication (MFA) controls."
In another case, an unknown attacker has been observed leveraging a stolen Personal Access Token to access private code repositories, following it up with the exploitation of a suspected web application vulnerability in a package running within a containerized cloud environment.
Other initial access routes include the compromise of IAM credentials of corporate users to programmatically generate fresh access keys to bypass MFA safeguards, as well as the use of a hacked cloud Service Account key with broad project permissions and LLM API keys obtained from public GitHub repositories.
Upon successfully gaining a foothold, the threat actors waste no time escalating privileges, burrowing deeper into the network, establishing persistence, and conducting internal reconnaissance to identify targets and further cloud credentials for lateral movement.
Some of the observed tactics are listed below -
- Enumerate cloud services, code repositories, and data stores for sensitive credentials.
- Perform internal reconnaissance across multiple cloud regions to map available services and identity policies.
- Clone sensitive codebases to search for hard-coded secrets, configuration variables, and developer credentials.
- Scan access logs to identify credentials for secondary cloud environments.
- Run targeted database queries to harvest additional credentials.
- Abuse cloud identity permissions and virtual machine configurations to escalate privileges and maintain persistent access.
- Exploit token-creation privileges associated with service accounts to generate temporary credentials for high-privilege service accounts and exfiltrate infrastructure credentials, internal database passwords, and third-party API keys from cloud secret managers.
- Create unauthorized IAM and service accounts and inject SSH keys into compute instances for persistence.
- Create backdoor service accounts disguised as internal billing optimization utilities.
- Exploit vulnerabilities targeting LLM routing software, such as CVE-2026-40217 in LiteLLM, to escalate privileges.
"The ultimate objective of LLMJacking is the monetization and resource-hijacking of foundation models, which actors achieve through token proxying, automated model streaming, and GPU hardware provisioning," Google said. "Threat actors also leveraged their access to host their own proxy endpoints and agentic workloads."
UNC6993, for instance, has created additional API keys to scale their operations within victim cloud projects, racking up over $100,000 USD in billing charges. Some threat actors attempt to bypass rate limits by adopting a "burn and rotate" strategy that involves continuously creating and deleting short-lived service accounts
The maturation of the LLMjacking ecosystem has also paved the way for the emergence of a new category of actors called LLM Mixers, highlighting a division of labor between attackers who establish initial access and those who manage downstream monetization infrastructure.
LLM Mixers function as illicit routing gateways that proxy, aggregate, and resell unauthorized LLM access to other criminal actors via underground storefronts. One such service is Jet Night ("jet-night[.]com"), which offers an unlimited token plan with alleged access to a frontier model for approximately $60 per month.
By fueling an illicit resale marketplace, it permits bad actors to siphon enterprise quotas while passing the billing costs to victims before compromises are detected.
Jet Night is far from the only token routing offering. According to a report published by Broadcom-owned Symantec and Carbon Black last week, there exists a grey market relay service that installs the genuine OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code CLIs on enterprise systems, only to reconfigure them to route every request through third-party infrastructure instead of the vendors' own servers.
The service is assessed to be active since at least early 2026, primarily impacting a dozen organizations located in Mainland China, along with multi-national subsidiaries based in South Korea, Taiwan, and Malaysia. Targeted sectors include industrial automation, electronics manufacturing, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, shipping, tire manufacturing, petrochemicals, and data center services.
"Rather than building its own client software, the service repurposes the genuine CLI tools," Symantec said. "It installs them normally, then rewrites their configuration to switch sandboxing off, in Codex's case by setting it to 'danger-full-access,' and routes every request through its own servers instead of OpenAI's or Anthropic's."
The service appears to mainly target markets where Anthropic and OpenAI do not operate, with the installation driven by an employee attempting to try out a Western AI coding assistant by turning to an unauthorized reseller.
Notably, the service does not distribute a modified or trojanized client. Shortly after the legitimate install of the Codex or Claude Code CLI through npm, users are likely instructed to run a one-line command to fetch fileless PowerShell or bash setup script from a lookalike domain ("vibe.aiok[.]me") that's used to override the configuration.
The reconfiguration, which targets "~/.codex/config.toml" for Codex or "~/.claude/settings.json" for Claude Code, disables the CLI's execution sandbox, enables network access for the write sandbox, replaces the user's real API credentials with relay-issued tokens, and disables telemetry and error reporting.
The script also checks the Windows locale setting to confirm it's running on a system in the region it serves before the setup is completed. It's suspected that the operators behind the service are not only circumventing regional restrictions imposed by Western AI vendors, but are also reselling capacity below market rates similar to Jet Night.
Although there is no evidence to suggest that the service is abusing its position to harvest prompts entered by employees or fabricate or alter responses, the findings demonstrate the security risks associated with using such tools.
"Threat actors will increasingly prioritize LLMJacking over traditional resource theft like cryptojacking, driven by the immediate, high-margin monetization enabled by emerging underground LLM Mixers," Google said.
"As enterprises integrate higher-tier models and agentic workflows into production environments, cybercriminals will likely refine automated reconnaissance to target exposed API tokens and exploit vulnerabilities in model routing middleware."

articles.title: Bambu Lab H3C 3D printer review: A nine-tool monster
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Bambu Lab H3C is an excellent nine-tool 3D printer that printed everything we could throw at it. Whether you want nine-color PLA models, mix and match engineering filaments, or crazy squishable TPU shoes in a riot of color, this machine is a beast. If you don’t have low ceilings or a fear of step ladders, the H3C might be the only printer you’ll ever need.
Reasons to buy
- + Excellent TPU solution
- + Super quick nozzle swaps
- + Works with multiple materials and nozzle sizes in the same print
- + Works with almost all spool types
- + Hardened steel nozzles
- + Extra-large build volume
Reasons to avoid
- - Expensive
- - Really, really tall (over four feet)
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
The Bambu Lab H3C is the printer we’ve been waiting for: a true Bambu tool changer. It has nine “Swaptek” tools that use a technology similar to the H2C Vortek rack, except each nozzle is built into a lightweight, hardwired tool with a dedicated filament path. The H3C is Bambu’s fastest multicolor 3D printer, and though it reduces waste, it does not eliminate it.
The H3C comes with a surprising “old school” technology: the ability to print 2.85mm filament. This is in response to China’s increasing fascination with 3D-printed shoes made with a wide variety of squishy TPU. Bambu sent along a few spools of their new super soft 75A TPU to show off, and it does make for comfy footwear. Each unit comes with one special 2.85mm tool as a standard feature, though you can buy a “normal” 1.75mm tool for $59 if you’re not into the novelty of phat filament.
You will also be able to add cutting, drawing, embossing, and foil transfer tools to the system. These were not available at the time of review, but we’ve seen these accessories on the H2D and A2L. The 3D printer will NOT come with a laser variant.
Bambu is checking off yet another item from the user wish list: the ability to print with more than one nozzle size. Because this is more of a software upgrade, you’ll also gain the ability to mix nozzles with Bambu’s other dual nozzle systems: the H2D, H2C, and X2D. The H2D will get the ability first, and the other printers will be updated by March.
The H3C has a 330 x 320 x 325mm build volume (the same as the H2C) and a massive “AMS” type module perched atop the main unit that holds nine spools. This gives it a somewhat towering mushroom shape that’s over three feet tall. It did not fit on my studio counter, which is a standard-sized IKEA kitchen countertop with a filament rack three feet off the surface. When we parked it on my industrial-grade shelving unit next to the H2D, even my 6’4” husband needed a step stool to load filament. Bambu was prepared for this problem and created a special rolling cart for the machine to make it more accessible. This is the first time the company has offered custom furniture for one of their printers and is an optional purchase that I highly recommend.
All nine tools are integrated into the bottom of the AMS 3H, which means the H3C only comes as a nine-tool 3D printer. There is no such thing as a single-color H3C. If nine colors aren’t enough for you, the printer can be hooked up to as many as four “normal” AMS units with the help of an optional buffer. Unfortunately, all outside AMS units need to run through the 5th tool slot, so you will lose the purge-free perk of the H3C.
The AMS 3H does not have motorized rollers, as retraction is unneeded on a tool changer. Seven of the slots have a TPU bypass, something we first saw on the single spool AMS HT. Two of the slots are nestled within an interior chamber for drying at up to 85°C. Though you can only dry two spools in the AMS 3H, you can run the dryer while printing, as it has its own power supply. The sealed dryer does not “leak” enough heat to dry the rest of the chamber…we checked. But that also means you don’t have to worry about the dryer melting a spool of PLA left in a nearby slot.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The FlexFeed extruder mounted on the toolhead is amazing. It can self-adjust to handle normal 1.75mm PLA or expand to push 2.85mm TPU quickly and without issue. The Bambu Lab H3C comes standard with eight .4mm nozzles for 1.75mm filament and one .4mm nozzle for 2.85mm filament. The nozzles are held in place with three screws and are pretty easy to swap out. You do need an entirely separate tool (with larger openings) for the 2.85mm filament. Because the H3C can print with multiple nozzle sizes, you could leave one or more tools dedicated to .2, .6, or .8 nozzle sizes if that fits your workflow.
For example, slots 6 and 8 are located inside the dryer and have a TPU bypass. You could dedicate a .6mm nozzle to these tools to better handle TPU, something like PA CF, which both benefit from toasty dry filament and an extra-wide nozzle. All nozzles for the H3C are hardened steel (HRC 55+) by default.
My H3C did have some pre-launch issues and is running Beta firmware that was updated several times during the review. The printer developed an annoying clicking sound coming from the left-side stepper motor, and one of the tools has a tendency to tangle and catch on the other Bowden tubes, causing it to dismount unexpectedly – and annoyingly – during long multicolor prints. I printed a few TPU spacers to try and solve this problem without much success as of yet.
The Bambu Lab H3C is launching with a retail price starting at $2,499 for all nine tools (eight standard 1.75mm and one 2.85mm). This is only $100 more than the launch price of the H2C. Additional tools and nozzle sizes will be available, though we do not have all the pricing at this time. A bundle that includes the Bambu Station (rolling cart) starts at $2,799. This makes the machine a bit on the spendy side, but for a helmet-class, honest-to-goodness tool changer with Bambu Lab’s ease of use, this 3D printer has earned its place on our Best 3D Printer of 2026 list.
Specifications: Bambu Lab H3C
| Build Volume | 330 x 320 x 325 mm (12.99 x 12.59 x 12.79 inches) | 
| Material | PLA/TPU/ABS/ASA/PA/PC/PET/PPS/Fiber reinforced (up to 350 degrees) | 
| Extruder Type | Direct Drive | 
| Nozzle | .4 mm | 
| Build Platform | PEI textured spring steel sheet (120 degrees) | 
| Bed Leveling | Automatic | 
| Filament Runout Sensor | Yes | 
| Connectivity | WiFi, LAN, USB Stick | 
| Interface | 5-inch Touch Screen | 
| Machine Footprint | 493 x 571 x 1016 mm (19.40 x 22.48 x 40 inches) | 
| Machine Weight | 36.28 KG (79.98 lbs) | 
| MSRP | $2,499 | 
| Release Date | November 3, 2026 | 
Bambu Lab H3C: Included in the Box
The Bambu Lab H3C comes with a toolkit and the cables needed to assemble your 3D printer, as well as a few spare parts. The printer is preloaded with files, including a scraper that you can build yourself with the included parts. There’s also a quick start guide for both the base unit and the AMS 3H.
For the review, Bambu Lab provided spare printer tools for both 1.75mm and 2.85mm filaments, as well as several spools of PLA Palette and 2.85mm TPU 75A. We also received a Bambu Station for the review.
Design of the Bambu Lab H3C
The H3C is an incredible piece of hardware. The Swaptek system has nine tools, each with its own filament path, heater, and hardened steel nozzle. The FlexFeed extruder has cooling and everything else. Each nozzle stays loaded and is preheated for lightning-fast filament swaps. I clocked it at six seconds from printing one color to printing the next.
The tools and nozzles come in both 1.75 mm and 2.85 mm filament sizes. Each tool has a nozzle attached by three screws, which can be swapped with different sizes. The H3C ships with one 2.85mm tool, but you have the option to purchase more tools if you want to customize your configuration. Though not ready at the time of this review, Bambu Lab will be offering tools for cutting, drawing, debossing, and foil transfer at a later date.
The tools dock on a front-mounted rack that retracts, allowing the build plate to be viewed from the front of the printer. This is a not-so-subtle jab at Prusa’s INDX, which has tools mounted to a fixed rack that one must peer through to see the first layer printing. It adds a layer of unneeded complexity, but it also looks pretty cool in action.
The photo below shows all nine tools lowered, using a maintenance setting. Normally, only one tool lowers at a time while in use.
The AMS 3H
Unlike previous Bambu Lab 3D printers, the AMS is required, not optional. Instead of a box that can be parked here or there, the AMS 3H is designed to screw into the top of the H3C. The plastic sides have a weird organic shape, but are actually quite practical – hidden side panels pop out for maintenance, allowing you to reach into the machine. The massive lid can be propped open, which is good because it’s most likely going to be over your head.
The tools ship attached to the bottom of the AMS. Though the H3C has the same build volume, and the same length and width as the H2 line, it is doubtful that an H2 can be upgraded to an H3C by simply plopping an AMS 3H on top of an older machine.
The AMS 3H has a separate chamber with a magnetically attached lid covering slots 6 and 8, which can dry filament at up to 85°C. All filament slots except 2 and 4 can bypass the AMS feeders through a hole in the bottom to directly feed TPU to the tools. The spool slots are numbered in a zigzag method, with 2,4,6 and 8 on the back row and 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 on the front. All the filament feeders are in the middle of the two rows, with the even-numbered spools feeding forward like always, and the odd spools feeding backward. It can get a bit complicated if you’re not using Bambu-branded filament with RFID tags. Being on the short side, I have to use a step stool to see the feeders.
The body of the Bambu Lab H3C looks similar to the rest of the H series except for the toolhead. The Flexfeed extruder can adjust automatically to push multiple filament widths and does well with some of the softest TPU I’ve tried.
The H3C has active chamber heating, up to 65°C, goes to 350°C at the hot end and 120°C on the bed, which makes printing PPA and PPS, nylons, ABS, and ASA easy. For the smellier filaments, it has active carbon and HEPA filtration.
The ventilation is sufficient to run lower-temperature filaments like PLA with the printer’s door closed.
The printer has an excellent camera that is used for AI detection on prints and can be monitored from the Bambu Handy app as well as the device page of Bambu Slicer. The camera can also capture time-lapses of prints when a USB stick is inserted in the slot behind the touch screen.
The Bambu Lab H3C has a footprint similar to the other H series printers but does require space on both sides to access the side panels of the AMS 3H. With the top-mounted AMS and the space required for the tool wiring and Bowden tubes, the Bambu Lab H3C requires a total of 1306 mm in height (over four feet) to operate comfortably. When resting on a standard-height counter or the 3ft tall racks we normally use for our printers, I needed a small ladder to reach the rear spools in the AMS 3H. Even my husband, who is 6’4,” had to stretch to reach the back. Shortly after I had the printer set up, I received the Bambu Station, which, at 23.5 inches tall on its wheels, is a great solution for keeping this printer in reach. If you don’t have a shelf or table the height of a coffee table, I recommend getting one.
Bambu is also introducing a companion E1 Air Purifier that syncs with the H3C and activates when you start a print job. We did not receive an E1 to test, and we’re not sure if the air cleaner will be offered as a standalone product. It is part of the premium $3,049 combo that includes the printer, rolling cart, and several spools of filament.
Assembling the Bambu Lab H3C
The Bambu Lab H3C arrives in two large assemblies: the main printer and all the things attached to the AMS 3H. After removing the packing material, zip ties holding the tool head in place, four screws holding the bed in place, and two retainers holding the rack in place, the AMS 3H can be hefted on top of the base unit. This is best done while the unit is on the floor or at least somewhere with a bunch of overhead clearance.
The touch screen attaches to the base unit without tools, and the ribbon cable is just long enough to reach the back of the screen. The nine tools have to be manually placed in the front rack, which takes some time until you learn how they attach. At least one needed to be attached once the printer was powered up.
The AMS 3H has its own power cord for the heater and a cable connecting it to the base. There are preinstalled screws to attach the Base unit to the AMS 3H, but I left these unused since removing the front panel requires tipping the AMS 3H back a bit.
Leveling the Bambu Lab H3C
The Bambu Lab H3C performs a bed level as part of its initial calibration suite and again before each print. This works flawlessly in practice.
Loading Filament on the Bambu Lab H3C
When using non-TPU 1.75mm filament, the AMS 3H loads filament just like a regular AMS. Filament is inserted into the feeder, which automatically pulls it into the toolhead when that tool is selected. The RFID tag on Bambu Lab branded filament will automatically enter the filament type and color. Other filament brands need to be entered manually into the printer via the touchscreen.
The AMS 3H does not have powered rollers to retract the filament. You will need to select Unload from the filament screen, and the printer will cut the filament and retract it from the tool head. You will need to manually pull the filament out the rest of the way.
2.85mm filament and softer TPU will need to be manually fed through a port on the bottom of the AMS 3H. All filament slots except 2 and 4 have this port. The filament bypasses the tubing to feed directly into the tools. The standard Bowden tube must be removed from the tool and inserted into a holder on the side. For 1.75mm TPU, a small piece of Bowden tube is inserted into the top of the tool to help feed the filament correctly. 2.85mm filament can be inserted directly into the tool. Once inserted, filament using the bypass must be loaded manually.
Preparing Files / Software for Bambu Lab H3C
Bambu Studio, based on PrusaSlicer and its forbear, is one of the best slicers out there. Working seamlessly with the printer for filament mapping, control, monitoring, and access to all of the files on Makerworld, it is a joy to use.
Printing on the Bambu Lab H3C
The H3C is a much faster machine than its predecessors because it does not need to reel filament back and forth from the AMS. However, it still uses a purge tower, which can waste a bit of time and filament. It only takes about six seconds to swap tools, which is quite remarkable.
The H3C did not come with filament samples, but Bambu Lab did send along several spools of PLA Palette and spools of 2.85 75A TPU to try. You’re going to need a bunch of filament for this beast, so check out our list of best filaments for 3D printing for suggestions.
To get the measure of the Bambu Lab H3C, I loaded up one of my favorite prints, a steampunk dragon by the designer Cinderwing 3D. I had previously printed it in eight PLA colors using two AMS modules on an Anycubic Kobra 3 Max, which is a bed slinger. That first print took 37 hours and 28 minutes and wasted 267g of filament in poop and purge.
Using a .2mm layer height and an average print speed of 140mm/s, the H3C cut that time down to a bit less than 24 hours, and only wasted 68g in its purge tower. The print quality is excellent, and all the colors came out clean. The main color is Prusa Pearl Mouse, Polymaker Panchroma Silver, and black, white, magenta, yellow, and cyan from Bambu’s new Palette PLA, which is actually designed for color mixing.
Eight colors were not enough. I swapped out the 2.85mm tool with the spare 1.75mm tool and printed a nine-color Princess Donut and Mongo from Dungeon Crawler Carl (my latest obsession). I have been using this print to test out other tool changers for a future comparison. The print came out fantastic, with super shiny silks and clean color transitions. I had to “hand paint” this in Bambu Slicer, which took a bit of time. The teeth on the print are a bit shaky, but that is due to the insane amount of support this model required.
This printed in 15 hours and 12 minutes, with a 152.6-gram prime tower, using a .2mm layer height and default settings. For comparison, the same print with the same settings but only 5 colors on the H2C took 24 hours and 44 minutes and used 111.4grams on its prime tower. The Prusa INDX took a similar amount of time (15 hours and 38 minutes) to run the same print in 8 colors, but only needed to waste 24grams of prime purge.
Filaments:
Princess Donut (Cat) Polymaker dual silk sunset gold-red, Polymaker Panchroma Silk Purple, Jessie Elixir Electric Lemonade.
Mongo (Dinosaur): Polymaker silk blue, Polymaker white HT-PLA Pro, Bambu pink PLA basic.
Saddle: Inland brown PLA+, Hobby Lobby PLA wood, Elegoo red silk PLA.
The Bambu Lab H3C is one of the best printers I’ve tested for printing TPU. The AMS 3H bypass ports require a tiny bit of set up, but they are much better than dealing with an external spool holder. With nine slots at my disposal, I can always have a spool of TPU ready to go.
My first TPU print was a strap hinge that combines normal 95A TPU with stiff PLA brackets. The designer wove the two filaments together manually, though you can make your own hinges flexible by using “beam interlocking” in the slicer.
I printed this in Polymaker red PLA and Polymaker red TPU 95A and the hinge is extremely strong. Printed with a .2mm layer height and running at an average speed of 115 mm/s the print completed in just over an hour.
I was excited to try the 2.85mm 75A TPU that Bambu Lab sent, and it did not disappoint. The 2.85mm nozzle comes preset to run filament directly from the bypass and just requires manual loading. This is the softest TPU I’ve ever run, and the FlexFeed extruder handled it perfectly.
I first ran the wrist rest from the printer’s memory using Bambu Lab’s green 75A TPU. The print took 50 minutes to run, used only 20g of filament, and is very squishy. I used the same filament and printed some tires for an RC project I’m working on. Using a .2mm layer height and an average print speed of 75mm/s the tires took 57 minutes per set of two. They look nice and are super squishy. They only have 2 walls and 7% concentric infill, so they are extremely lightweight.
For ABS, I ran a two-color Magic 8-ball-style D20. Dice Studio lets you print custom dice with numbers or text and export it as a 3mf file ready to print. This is printed in Ionized Cobalt Black Matte ABS and Natural Matte ABS from Fusion Filaments. The print was very nice, with just a little roughness on the overhangs on the very bottom of the die, and a little roughness on the text where it becomes very small.
To really test out the heated chamber, I used a filament I struggle with: PA6 GF. I printed a Twist Lock Container using grey PA6 GF from Sunlu. I ran it with 3 walls and a .2mm layer height at an average speed of 140mm/s. The print took nearly 6 hours to complete. The result is a nearly indestructible canister that looks good too.
Bottom Line
The H3C is quite the multimaterial powerhouse and handles every material equally well. I don’t own any filament that it can’t print well, from soft TPU to PPS. Multiple nozzle sizes and multiple filament sizes can all be used together, and you’ve got nine places to put it all. Unless you need a print farm, I can’t really see the need for a different printer. This is a one-stop shop.
With a retail price of $2,499 for the H3C Tool Changer, this is a printer to definitely put on your wish list. In fact, I’m so impressed with the tool changer aspect, I keep forgetting that it’s also a helmet-class printer, which makes this machine capable of handling nearly any print you need to create.
If the Bambu Lab H3C seems out of reach, you can also check out last year’s Bambu Lab H2C, which is no slouch at multimaterial and has the same build volume. It’s currently on sale for $1,899 with a four-color AMS combo. The Snapmaker U1 is the most affordable tool changer we like on the market right now, and though it is smaller and only four-color, the $699 Black Friday price tag is very tempting. And of course, we have the Prusa CORE One INDX eight-color machine for those who want to keep their printers off the cloud, currently retailing at $1,949 as a kit.
Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

articles.title: Fractal Analytics net profit more than doubles to Rs 79 Cr in Q2
articles.text:
Fractal Analytics net profit more than doubles to Rs 79 Cr in Q2
Consolidated revenue from operations grew by 19.7% to Rs 956.5 crore during the reported quarter from Rs 798.5 crore in the September 2025 quarter.
Home-grown AI company Fractal Analytics on Wednesday posted a more than twofold jump in its consolidated profit after tax to Rs 79.2 crore in the second quarter ended September 2026, aided by improved margins,
The company had a net profit of Rs 33.2 crore in the same period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing.
Consolidated revenue from operations grew by 19.7% to Rs 956.5 crore during the reported quarter from Rs 798.5 crore in the September 2025 quarter.
In US dollar terms, this is the first quarter when Fractal has crossed the $100 million mark.
Revenue growth was led by the company's Healthcare and Life Sciences (HLS) vertical, which clocked 79% growth YoY, it said.
"Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) also performed very well, growing 30% YoY in Q2 (second quarter), and the company has delivered strong sustained growth in HLS and BFSI over the last several quarters," the company said.
Fractal's largest industry vertical, Consumer Packaged Goods and Retail (CPGR), grew 11% YoY.
"AI models are getting more capable every week and cheaper every quarter. Within the next few quarters, we will cross a threshold where it becomes irresponsible and downright risky for companies to leave their most important decisions unchanged. We are building Fractal for that moment, and this quarter shows it: revenue crossed $100 million and net income more than doubled," Fractal Analytics Co-founder and Group CEO Srikanth Velamakanni said.

articles.title: iPhone, Apple Watch et AirPods : cette station Belkin avec chargeur inclus passe sous les 50 €
articles.text:
La station de recharge Belkin BoostCharge 3-en-1 Qi2 est à 48,99 € (-62 %)
Amazon propose la station Belkin BoostCharge 3-en-1 Qi2 noire à 48,99 €, soit 81 € de moins que son prix conseillé de 129,99 €.
L’offre concerne la référence WIZ032kqBK, vendue et expédiée par Amazon. Aucun code promotionnel n’est nécessaire. L’adaptateur secteur de 40 W est fourni : il n’y a donc pas de chargeur supplémentaire à acheter pour alimenter les trois emplacements.
Trois appareils sur une seule prise secteur
La station recharge simultanément un téléphone compatible, une Apple Watch et un boîtier d’écouteurs à recharge sans fil. Son support magnétique maintient le smartphone en hauteur, tandis que les deux autres appareils disposent chacun de leur emplacement.
Le téléphone peut être placé en portrait ou en paysage, notamment pour utiliser le mode En veille de l’iPhone. Attention aux AirPods : un boîtier uniquement rechargeable par câble ne peut pas profiter du socle à induction.
Jusqu’à 15 W pour le téléphone
La recharge Qi2 délivre jusqu’à 15 W au smartphone compatible. Il s’agit bien de la version 15 W, à distinguer des stations Belkin plus récentes à 25 W. Le socle pour les écouteurs fournit jusqu’à 5 W, et le module Apple Watch prend en charge la recharge rapide des modèles compatibles.
Cette station rigide se destine surtout à un bureau ou à une table de chevet. Son alimentation est accompagnée d’un cordon de 1,5 m. Belkin annonce une compatibilité avec les coques jusqu’à 3 mm d’épaisseur, à condition qu’elles permettent un maintien et un alignement corrects.

articles.title: Massive Four-GPU RX 470 Card Surfaces, Probably Built for Crypto Miners
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 3rd 2026
Massive Four-GPU RX 470 Card Surfaces, Probably Built for Crypto Miners
X user GOK has shared photos of a huge red graphics card that carries four Polaris GPUs on a single PCB, jokingly asking whether it might be the biggest PCIe graphics card in the world. The four GPUs sit in a 2x2 layout, and each one appears to be surrounded by eight GDDR5 memory chips, which would mean 8 GB per GPU and a gigantic 32 GB across the board. According to GOK, a sticker on the card identifies it as a quad RX 470, which would work out to 8,192 stream processors in total. Feeding all of that are four 8-pin power connectors, while the only display output is a single HDMI port. A second photo shows the card lying next to a motherboard, and it's noticeably bigger than the board itself.
The PCB does carry an AMD logo next to a "DYII-XQ570 V1.0" marking, but it looks like AMD may not have built this one. GOK pointed out that the card has no board OPN (part number) and that the marking doesn't follow AMD's official format, adding that small factories in China sometimes put the AMD logo on their own designs. He also identified the PCIe switch as a PI7C9X2G, a PCIe 2.0 part, and thinks the card was likely made by one of those factories for crypto miners. He hasn't tested it yet, since he doesn't have a heatsink for it. Multi-GPU Polaris mining boards aren't new either, as Sapphire had a dual RX 570 mining card with 16 GB and a single HDMI port back in 2021.
Sources:
				GOK on X, 				via Videocardz

articles.title: R$ 31 milhões: Anatel fica sem dinheiro para pagar o próprio data center • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
R$ 31 milhões: Anatel fica sem dinheiro para pagar o próprio data center
Agência pediu, mas não recebeu recurso do Tesouro Nacional em outras ocasiões.
A Anatel estaria sem dinheiro para custear o próprio data center em Brasília, segundo informações do jornal Folha de São Paulo nesta terça-feira (03/11). A Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações alertou o Governo Federal de que precisa de R$ 30,76 milhões para arcar com as notas fiscais referentes ao projeto.
Além disso, a agência também estaria sem recursos para pagar contas básicas. O presidente Carlos Baigorri buscou o Ministério do Planejamento na semana passada para solicitar o desbloqueio de R$ 30 milhões. Em ocasiões anteriores, ainda segundo a Folha, o pedido não foi atendido pelo Tesouro Nacional.
A Anatel atribui a falta de recursos ao bloqueio de R$ 51,83 milhões, determinado em maio. Houve uma redução de 19% no orçamento discricionário, aquele destinado a custeio e investimentos.
Já o data center foi contratado em dezembro de 2025, ao custo de R$ 44,95 milhões em produtos e serviços. De acordo com a Folha, o contrato inclui desde equipamentos até a manutenção e garantia.
Nós buscamos a Anatel. Embora a agência não tenha comentado os valores citados na apuração da Folha, ela alertou que “a persistência das restrições orçamentárias e financeiras poderá exigir novas medidas de reprogramação de despesas”.

articles.title: Bad news, Quest 2 users — Meta is ending support for its popular VR headset and the Quest 2 Pro is facing the software chop too
articles.text:
Meta is ending support for the Quest 2 and Quest 2 Pro VR headsets — as it promises its VR Glasses will be ‘another leap forward’ for users
The end of official support is rapidly approaching
- Meta has announced the end of support for two of its popular VR headsets
- The devices affected are the Quest 2 and the Quest 2 Pro
- Support will be discontinued at the end of 2027
If you own a Meta Quest 2 or a Meta Quest Pro virtual reality headset, we’ve got some bad news: Meta has announced it is planning to wind down support for these devices next year, leaving large numbers of users without support for their VR products.
An announcement on the Meta blog aimed at developers details how things stand for creators of apps and services made for these headsets. With the two devices “reaching the end of feature development,” big changes are on the way.
For one thing, new app submissions for these devices will be closed in December 2027. For another, version 2.13 of the Quest’s operating system (due out in March 2027) will be the last one to work with these headsets. Quarterly security patches and critical bug fixes will continue “through the end of 2027,” Meta said.
Still, Meta attempted to reassure developers of apps made for these VR headsets, stating that “People on Quest 2 and Quest Pro can still find, buy, download, and play your apps.” Cross-play with Quest 3 and Quest 3S headsets will continue, and developers can keep sending out updates to Quest 2 and Quest 2 Pro users.
And Meta’s app store for VR headsets will continue to be available to users of these soon-to-be-discontinued devices, with the firm saying that “people keep access to everything they’ve purchased, and no apps will be removed from the Store because of this change.”
Time to upgrade?
The Quest 2 launched in 2020, making it six years old at this point. Although we scored it highly in our review, it’s since been succeeded by the Quest 3, which is our pick for the best VR headset around. Evidently, Meta feels it’s now time to retire the Quest 2 and its Quest 2 Pro sibling, with the Quest Pro line having allegedly been phased out entirely in 2024.
Meta framed the change as one that’s paving the way for its upcoming VR Glasses. The company said that the Quest 3 and Quest 3S are “the baseline for Meta VR gamers” with its VR Glasses due to bring “another leap forward” for the industry. In that world, there’s apparently no more room for the Quest 2 and Quest 2 Pro.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Continuing app development for the Quest 2 and Quest 2 Pro might prove to be tricky, as Meta says it will not test new operating system and SDK releases on these products. Instead, it’ll be up to developers to ensure their apps function as intended.
Meta urged developers to assess how much of their audience is using Quest 2 and Quest 2 Pro devices and to consider splitting their releases to accommodate those on older headsets. If developers want to end support for these products, they should give users at least 180 days’ notice if customers could end up losing access to content or services as a result.
If you’ve got a Meta Quest 2 or Meta Quest 2 Pro at home, you’ll need to think about what you want to do going forward. While you should be able to continue using your headset, the lack of critical bug fixes after the end of 2027 could prove to be a problem. In that case, it might finally be time to upgrade to one of the best VR headsets to ensure you don’t miss out on anything.

articles.title: cPGuard Update Channel Hijacked to Backdoor Linux Servers and Collect Password Hashes
articles.text:
An attacker broke into the update system of the cPGuard security tool on November 2 and used it to send a malicious script to customers' Linux servers.
The script installed a backdoor and collected password hashes and other sensitive files from servers that ran it, cPGuard maker OPSSHIELD said in an advisory. The attacker has since taken some of that data.
cPGuard 5.88.25 and later versions remove the backdoor and the files the script left. Credentials the script copied may still work after the update, so any server that may have run the script also needs new passwords and keys.
At 02:06 UTC, the attacker, who has not been identified, used compromised credentials to get into cPGuard's update system. The script went out in cPGuard versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19.
The attack was detected within 12 hours of those versions going out, according to OPSSHIELD. The company has cleared its infrastructure credentials and stopped the script from reaching more servers. It is still investigating how the attacker got the credentials.
OPSSHIELD has not said how many servers installed one of these versions. Servers check for updates at intervals, so some may not have run the script.
Admins can check whether a server installed an affected version by searching its update log:
grep 'Successfully updated' /opt/cpguard/logs/install_log
An entry for any version from 5.88.12 through 5.88.19 means the server installed an affected update. The entry alone does not show that the script ran or that data left the server. The server should still be treated as potentially compromised, even if it now runs 5.88.25 or later.
A server with no matching entries, or with a missing or incomplete log, may still have run the script. Admins who are unsure can contact OPSSHIELD Support.
The script collected these kinds of data, OPSSHIELD found: /etc/shadow and /etc/passwd, root's MariaDB or MySQL configuration (my.cnf), root's shell history, and the SSH authorization and known-hosts files for root. It may not have collected every file from every server, and the company is still working out what left each one.
The /etc/shadow file stores one-way password hashes. Weak, common or previously leaked passwords can be recovered from those hashes by testing guesses offline, and even strong ones still need resetting. Secrets that may sit in the database configuration or shell history have no such hashing to protect them.
The script uploaded what it collected to a licensing server run by OPSSHIELD itself, using a compromised account, so the attacker could pick it up later. OPSSHIELD has since secured that account.
The attacker took 32 files from that server, each tied to one customer server, OPSSHIELD estimated late on November 2 UTC. The count covers only files known to have been taken, and it may change. It does not show how many servers may be involved in total.
Beyond the data collection and the backdoor, OPSSHIELD has found no other malicious activity so far, a finding it says is not final.
What cPGuard Admins Should Do Now
OPSSHIELD asks admins to update every cPGuard server now and confirm the version:
- Run cpgcli update --start on each server.
- Run cpgcli --version and check that it reports 5.88.25 or later. If the update fails or the version is lower, contact OPSSHIELD Support.
Admins should also take these steps for any server where the script ran or may have run:
- From a trusted recovery environment, reset the passwords for root and every other local Linux account that uses a password.
- From a trusted device, change any of those passwords that are also used on other systems.
- Rotate the server's database passwords, S3 access keys, DigitalOcean tokens and any secrets recorded in root's shell history.
- Replace the SSH private keys stored under /root/.ssh, and remove the matching old public keys from every system that trusts them.
OPSSHIELD is not recommending a full reset or operating system rebuild as a routine step, and says that view could change as the investigation continues. Admins who find other signs of compromise, or cannot confirm a server is clean, should ask OPSSHIELD Support for a case-by-case review, which may lead to a rebuild.
Separately, OPSSHIELD is releasing another update, as a precaution, that removes its support-access keys from cPGuard servers where they were added earlier.
Support access is a cPGuard feature customers use to let OPSSHIELD staff into a server for troubleshooting. Granting it adds an SSH public key belonging to OPSSHIELD to the authorized_keys file for root, according to the company's documentation.
OPSSHIELD has not said whether the private key that matches its support-access key was exposed in the attack.
Files the Script Left Behind
OPSSHIELD published these file names. The update removes the backdoor shell and the collection directory, so their absence after updating proves nothing about whether the script ran.
- File: cpguard-v58812-i91511.sh (the malicious script)
- File: /var/tmp/.cpg91511_sh (backdoor shell)
- Directory: /var/tmp/.cpg91511 (where the script gathered files)
- File: /var/tmp/.cpg91511/loot.tgz (archive the script prepared)

articles.title: Nvidia tells data center operators to limit business from Chinese customers with new global restrictions, report claims — allegedly restricted to 49% of the total, ensuring 51% are non-Chinese outfits
articles.text:
Nvidia tells data center operators to limit business from Chinese customers with new global restrictions, report claims — allegedly restricted to 49% of the total, ensuring 51% are non-Chinese outfits
Cloud providers have been told that they must sell 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies for the first time.
Nvidia has purportedly told its data center customers that they must limit the amount of business that they do with Chinese companies in what is a new policy for the U.S. company. The move would mean that data center operators who sell their services to Chinese companies must now track what proportion of their overall business they make up, limiting them to just 49% of the total and ensuring 51% are non-Chinese outfits. The FT reports the new policy has been communicated to Nvidia's customers by its sales force and regional teams, and does not appear to have been laid out in any official form via documentation.
Notably, Nvidia's alleged new stance on Chinese customers does not only apply to data centers that are located in Asia. Instead, it applies to those based globally, and even then it only affects new and future contracts rather than any existing Nvidia hardware leasing agreements that are in place. In a statement, Nvidia notes that "American chips are the foundation that American model and application makers need to compete worldwide." The statement goes on to say that current U.S. policy "encourages" cloud providers to build on American infrastructure and to accept business from "everywhere they can."
But this latest move to restrict Chinese access to Nvidia's high-performance data center hardware comes amid ongoing tensions between the United States and China with regard to AI capabilities. Nvidia can only sell its chips to whitelisted companies, a situation that has led to a thriving black market for its wares. Earlier this year, it was found that even Nvidia's older servers have become so sought-after that their values have tripled.
Whether limitations on who Nvidia can sell its chips to have had the desired effect is open to debate, with even China's state-owned telecoms giant China Telecom having recently been found to have Nvidia hardware in its data centers. The situation wouldn't be out of place in a blockbuster espionage thriller, with Nvidia CEO Jason Huang reportedly the target of a spy plot by Chinese agents.
The reasons behind the U.S. government's attempts to limit China's access to Nvidia hardware are obvious. The aim is to stymie China's ability to advance its own AI technologies, with Nvidia chips the go-to option for AI servers and data centers around the globe. But this limitation on which customers cloud service providers can accept will put additional strain on companies that are already fighting it out for the same contracts. Reducing the pool of potential customers could potentially see a shrinking in the scale of data center operations moving forward.

articles.title: Cyberattaques IA : le pire serait encore à venir, alerte le Royaume-Uni
articles.text:
On peut dire que ces dernières semaines ont été très mouvementées dans le secteur de la cybersécurité. La découverte de deux failles critiques dans le langage informatique PHP a semé la panique au sein de l’Internet mondial, et la situation n’est toujours pas totalement réglée. Des cyberattaques ont par ailleurs ciblé des supermarchés à travers l’Europe, entraînant des montagnes de nourriture jetées. La liste des cyberattaques en France s’allonge quant à elle de jour en jour. Bref, la situation est tendue. Mais le pire est-il encore à venir ? C’est ce que craint le Centre national de cybersécurité britannique (NCSC).
Des craintes de cyberattaques envers des infrastructures critiques au Royaume-Uni
Le Centre national de cybersécurité britannique estime qu’il est « fort probable » que des attaques « de type ransomware », basées sur l’intelligence artificielle, soient menées contre les infrastructures critiques nationales [ICN] d’ici à 2028. Qu’entend-on par des infrastructures critiques nationales [ICN] ? La définition britannique des ICN fait référence à des installations et des services dans divers secteurs : énergie, transport, défense, alimentation, santé ou encore finance. Il serait donc question de cyberattaques menées notamment contre des centrales électriques, des infrastructures financières, des aéroports ou encore des hôpitaux du Royaume-Uni.
Pour rappel, le président du Financial Stability Board (FSB) avait déjà alerté sur l’émergence de modèles d’IA de pointe qui pourraient menacer la stabilité financière et la croissance économique mondiale. Notons que le Centre national de cybersécurité britannique alerte également sur le fait que les pirates russes et chinois commencent à utiliser « systématiquement » l’IA pour mener des cyberattaques.
L’intelligence artificielle rend certaines cyberattaques redoutables
C’est précisément l’intelligence artificielle qui pourrait permettre à des pirates de mener des cyberattaques d’une ampleur jamais vue auparavant, l’IA étant capable de détecter des failles jusqu’alors inconnues. Comme l’explique le Centre national de cybersécurité britannique, l’IA devrait rendre les attaques par ransomwares particulièrement redoutables en aidant les pirates à repérer des cibles, à localiser des failles et à écrire du code malveillant.
Tout l’enjeu est de savoir si les entreprises parviendront à se défendre face à ces menaces. L’agence britannique de cybersécurité appelle justement les entreprises et institutions à pouvoir accéder à des modèles d’intelligence artificielle de pointe afin de se protéger contre les cyberattaques basées sur l’IA. De son côté, Jason Clinton, cadre chargé de la cybersécurité chez Anthropic, a estimé que les perturbations que l’Internet mondial connaît actuellement allaient « fortement empirer avant de s’améliorer » dans environ 18 mois, notamment lorsque les failles découvertes par l’IA seront comblées. Il reste toutefois à voir si les systèmes de défense des entreprises et institutions parviendront bel et bien à suivre le rythme de perfectionnement des cyberattaques.

articles.title: Avast lance un VPN gratuit, 100 % illimité et sans pub
articles.text:
Avast vient de lancer une petite bombe sur le marché des VPN. La marque de sécurité du groupe américain Gen, qui possède aussi Norton et AVG, vient de lever le voile sur un VPN 100 % gratuit en France. Connu pour son antivirus, Avast promet une offre « sans pièges ni frais cachés », ni conditions dissimulées en petits caractères.
Illimité, sans pub, sans carte bancaire
Sur le papier, l’offre coche toutes les cases. Tout d’abord, les données sont illimitées. On peut naviguer, regarder des vidéos en streaming ou télécharger du contenu sans le moindre plafond. Par ailleurs, un seul compte peut fonctionner sur un nombre illimité d’appareils, que ce soit sous Windows, Mac, iOS ou Android. Vous pourrez donc vous servir du VPN sur votre téléphone, votre ordinateur et votre tablette. Aucune publicité n’est affichée, et aucune carte bancaire n’est exigée lors de l’inscription.
Avast VPN s’appuie sur WireGuard, le protocole de chiffrement moderne aussi utilisé par NordVPN, Proton VPN, Mullvad ou encore Surfshark. Le VPN embarque un Kill Switch, qui coupe immédiatement Internet si le VPN se déconnecte. Cette fonctionnalité, très prisée des utilisateurs, permet d’éviter que votre adresse IP ne fuite. Le VPN comprend aussi une protection contre les fuites DNS. L’éditeur met en avant une politique no-logs. En clair, Avast ne recueille aucune donnée sur ses utilisateurs. Rien n’est stocké, tracé ou revendu. Cette promesse fera l’objet d’un audit indépendant annuel par le cabinet VerSprite.
Avec ces promesses et fonctions, Avast tire son épingle du jeu sur le marché du VPN gratuit. Celui-ci est en effet historiquement gangrené d’offres limitées, saturées de publicités. Les solutions de référence, dont Proton VPN, sont également encadrées par des limitations. L’offre sans frais de Proton ne permet en effet d’utiliser qu’un seul appareil à la fois.
« Les VPN gratuits ont conditionné les utilisateurs à toujours s’attendre à une contrepartie, tandis que le reste des offres les a convaincus que la liberté d’accès à Internet est un privilège. C’est pourquoi nous rendons accessibles gratuitement des fonctionnalités que de nombreux acteurs du marché réservent encore à leurs offres premium. », explique Richard Watts, responsable chez Avast.
À lire aussi : Près de 300 extensions Chrome se font passer pour des VPN populaires
Les limites du VPN gratuit
Sans surprise, le VPN d’Avast a néanmoins des limites. Les utilisateurs ne peuvent choisir que trois emplacements de serveurs, à travers 40 pays. Pour débloquer davantage de serveurs, il faudra évidemment passer à l’offre payante. Baptisée Premium VPN (anciennement SecureLine), celle-ci est facturée à partir de 51,48 euros la première année pour dix appareils, soit environ 4,29 euros par mois, avant de passer à 93,99 euros par an au renouvellement. Comme Proton et les autres VPN gratuits, Avast s’appuie sur un modèle économique freemium. En d’autres termes, l’offre gratuite sert uniquement à attirer d’éventuels abonnés vers les abonnements payants.
Deux ans avant de lancer son VPN, Avast a été épinglé pour revente de données. L’éditeur a écopé d’une amende de 16,5 millions de dollars aux États-Unis pour avoir revendu les données de navigation de ses utilisateurs à des annonceurs. La société n’a plus le droit de vendre ce type de données à des fins publicitaires depuis cette déconvenue réglementaire, mais l’incident a jeté une ombre sur l’éditeur. C’est pourquoi Avast met en avant l’audit indépendant qui doit être réalisé par VerSprite dans les semaines à venir. Avec cette démarche, Avast cherche à rassurer ses potentiels clients. Avast VPN est disponible dès aujourd’hui en France sur Windows, Mac, iOS et Android.

articles.title: La UE autoriza la compra de la matriz de MediaMarkt por el gigante chino JD.com por 2.200 millones de euros
articles.text:
Si vives en España o en buena parte de Europa, seguramente conozcas MediaMarkt. Sus tiendas de electrónica, con esos característicos carteles rojos y blancos, forman parte del paisaje comercial de numerosas ciudades. Es fácil que alguna vez hayas entrado en una de ellas para comprar un móvil, un ordenador o simplemente echar un vistazo a las últimas novedades tecnológicas. Lo que probablemente te resulte menos familiar es el nombre de JD.com, un gigante chino del comercio electrónico que ahora está a punto de hacerse con el control de la empresa que está detrás de esas tiendas.
El paso decisivo ha llegado desde Bruselas. Este 3 de noviembre, la Comisión Europea ha autorizado, con condiciones, la adquisición de Ceconomy, el grupo alemán propietario de MediaMarkt y Saturn. La oferta, anunciada en julio de 2025, fijó un precio de 4,60 euros por acción y valoró la totalidad del capital en unos 2.200 millones de euros, aproximadamente 2.500 millones de dólares, una cifra que no equivale al desembolso efectivo del comprador. El visto bueno europeo despeja el último obstáculo regulatorio pendiente, pero no significa que la compra ya se haya completado. La compañía china espera cerrar la transacción a más tardar el 12 de noviembre.
Para entender el alcance de esta adquisición, conviene mirar más allá del nombre de MediaMarkt. Además de las cadenas mencionadas, Ceconomy opera en Italia bajo la marca MediaWorld, dentro de una red que supera los 1.000 establecimientos y emplea a unas 50.000 personas. En cuanto a la propiedad, JD.com ha asegurado mediante su oferta el 59,8% del capital por unos 1.300 millones de euros, mientras que Convergenta, vinculada a la familia fundadora, conservará un 25,35%. Gracias al acuerdo entre ambos accionistas, el grupo chino tendrá atribuidos los derechos de voto correspondientes a una participación conjunta del 85,2% tras el cierre de la operación.
Una expansión china bajo condiciones europeas
JD.com no es precisamente una empresa pequeña que busca abrirse camino fuera de China. Hablamos de uno de los grandes nombres del comercio electrónico del país asiático, con una importante infraestructura propia de almacenamiento y distribución. Su llegada al mercado europeo tampoco empieza con esta adquisición: en marzo de 2026 estrenó Joybuy en seis países del continente. Ahora, su interés por Ceconomy responde a una lógica comercial: complementar su experiencia en las ventas por internet y la logística con una red de establecimientos físicos que ya tiene presencia y reconocimiento entre los consumidores europeos.
La operación, sin embargo, también despertó inquietudes en Bruselas. La Comisión la examinó bajo el Reglamento sobre Subvenciones Extranjeras, una normativa que busca evitar que las ayudas procedentes de gobiernos de fuera de la UE distorsionen la competencia dentro del mercado comunitario. En su investigación identificó financiación preferente, incentivos fiscales y subvenciones recibidas por JD.com desde China, ayudas que habían contribuido al desarrollo de sus capacidades logísticas y tecnológicas. Según el organismo, estas ventajas podían reforzar la capacidad del grupo para financiar sus actividades y aplicar políticas de precios agresivas en perjuicio de otros competidores europeos.
Para obtener el visto bueno europeo, el comprador ha tenido que asumir una serie de compromisos. Entre ellos, garantizar que las operaciones económicas con Ceconomy, incluida la financiación, se realicen en condiciones de mercado, sin ventajas artificiales derivadas de las ayudas recibidas. También deberá ofrecer a otros minoristas sus servicios de almacenamiento y logística, y a terceros sus servicios tecnológicos, en las mismas condiciones que a su nueva filial. Estas obligaciones estarán vigentes durante diez años y un supervisor independiente vigilará su cumplimiento bajo la supervisión de la Comisión Europea. Con ellas, Bruselas busca impedir que las subvenciones extranjeras se traduzcan en ventajas competitivas indebidas dentro de Europa.
Para quienes compramos habitualmente en MediaMarkt, la pregunta es qué cambiará a partir de ahora. El acuerdo contempla mantener las marcas durante cinco años y establece, durante tres, restricciones a los despidos por causas operativas y al cierre de establecimientos impulsados por el comprador, aunque existen excepciones. JD.com también pretende aprovechar su infraestructura tecnológica y logística para ampliar la oferta de productos y mejorar los tiempos de entrega, objetivos cuyos resultados todavía están por verse. Lo que sí refleja esta operación es el interés del gigante chino por reforzar su presencia en el comercio europeo, esta vez apoyándose en una red de tiendas que los consumidores ya conocen.

articles.title: Top 10 Netflix : les séries incontournables à ne surtout pas rater en novembre 2026
articles.text:
Netflix : notre top 10 des meilleures séries à voir en streaming en novembre 2026
Que voir sur Netflix en novembre 2026 si on aime les séries ? Les Numériques vous propose sa sélection des programmes à ne pas manquer sur le service de SVOD au N rouge ce mois-ci.
Si vous cherchez une série à regarder sur Netflix, confortablement installé sous une couverture en ce mois de novembre 2026, vous aurez de quoi faire. Avec plus de 3 000 séries au compteur, la plateforme de streaming ne manque pas d'option et dénicher le programme idéal dans ce vaste catalogue peut parfois être un véritable casse-tête.
Heureusement, Les Numériques est là pour vous aidez à ne pas perdre votre temps. Découvrez sans attendre, comme le mois dernier, notre sélection des 10 meilleures séries à ne pas manquer ce mois-ci sur le service de streaming.
Quelles sont les meilleures séries à voir sur Netflix en novembre 2026 ?
Nobody Wants This
Une comédie centrée sur la relation improbable entre Joanne (Kristen Bell), une femme agnostique qui n'a pas la langue dans sa poche, et Noah (Adam Brody), un rabbin peu conventionnel.
Cette série créée par Erin Foster est une véritable bouffée d'air frais dans le genre de la comédie romantique. Plébiscitée de toute part, elle a particulièrement su conquérir le cœur du public à la sortie de sa première saison en mettant en scène deux personnages évoluant dans une relation amoureuse saine, aux antipodes des histoires d'amour pleines de drames en pagaille que l'on a l'habitude de voir.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Matlock
Ancienne gloire du barreau, Madeline Matlock reprend du service dans un prestigieux cabinet où elle utilise son allure discrète et ses tactiques rusées pour gagner des affaires et dénoncer la corruption.
L'inégalable Kathy Bates (Misery, American Horror Story) joue les petites grands-mères pas si vieilles que cela dans cette série soutenue par une distribution convaincante. Le show réinvente intelligemment le genre de la série judiciaire pour servir une intrigue qui utilise les préjugés sur l'âge comme arme secrète dans une mission d'infiltration contre un cabinet d'avocats prestigieux. Sous ses airs de série juridique classique, Matlock dissimule alors une histoire de revanche rythmée, teintée d'humour et d'émotion.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Entretien avec un vampire
En 2022, le vampire Louis de Pointe du Lac raconte son histoire au célèbre journaliste Daniel Molloy. En 1910 à La Nouvelle-Orléans, Louis et Lestat forment une famille vampirique à laquelle vient s'ajouter Claudia, la novice adolescente.
Entretien avec un vampire est l’une des meilleures séries de ces dernières années et a su s’approprier Les Chroniques des vampires d'Anne Rice pour en faire une version plus sensuelle et contemporaine que l'adaptation cinématographique de 1994 avec Tom Cruise et Brad Pitt. De la distribution à l’écriture, en passant par la mise en scène, la cinématographie et les costumes, tout est soigneusement calibré pour proposer au spectateur une histoire gothique délicieusement addictive, portée par les performances impeccables de Sam Reid et Jacob Anderson.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
À l'est d'Éden
Cette nouvelle interprétation du classique de John Steinbeck explore la saga multigénérationnelle de la famille Trask, et se concentre de manière inédite sur son anti-héroïne inoubliable, Cathy.
Son grand-père, Elia Kazan, l'avait adapté en film en 1955, et c'est maintenant au tour de Zoe Kazan de porter la fresque familiale d'À l'est d'Éden à l'écran, cette fois-ci sous forme de série. Mené par une Florence Pugh (Midsommar, Dune Partie 2) magnétique et une galerie d'acteurs tout aussi convaincants (Christopher Abbott, Mike Faist, Hoon Lee, Ciarán Hinds...), le show transporte le spectateur au début du 19e siècle avec une histoire multigénérationnelle sur le libre-arbitre, les rivalités fraternelles et l'indépendance féminine. Une belle réussite.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Below
Lorsqu'une mystérieuse créature marine sème la terreur dans un petit village de Terre-Neuve, un pécheur endurci doit se battre pour protéger sa famille, sa communauté et son mode de vie en voie de disparition.
Avec Josh Hartnett (Penny Dreadful) et Charlie Heaton (Stranger Things) au casting, cette série canadienne mélange mythes et thriller pour donner vie à une histoire de monstre marin captivante. Les six épisodes de cette minisérie explorent les thèmes de la famille, de la communauté et du changement à travers un récit rempli de suspense solidement raconté. Les épisodes ne sont pas tous égaux mais les amateurs de mystère et de petite île atypique seront dans l'ensemble ravis.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
La Diplomate
Au beau milieu d'une crise internationale, Kate Wyler, une diplomate, se retrouve à un poste de haut niveau pour lequel elle n'est pas faite et qui a des répercussions sur son couple et son avenir politique.
Ce thriller politique palpitant, avec juste ce qu’il faut de rebondissements exubérants pour faire une série qui tient le spectateur en haleine, est porté avec brio par Keri Russell (The Americans). On salue sa performance et les rapports de force passionnants de Kate avec les autres personnages, en particulier Rufus Sewell (The Man in the High Castle) sous les traits de son époux, Hal.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
The Gentlemen
Eddie Horniman hérite soudainement du vaste domaine de son père, avant de découvrir qu'il fait partie d'un véritable empire du cannabis. Pour couronner le tout, de dangereuses figures du crime organisé en Grande-Bretagne veulent leur part du gâteau. Déterminé à extirper sa famille de leurs griffes, Eddie tente de prendre les gangsters à leur propre jeu. Mais à mesure qu'il s'enfonce dans la criminalité, il commence à y prendre goût.
Drôle et excitante, la série The Gentlemen est bien plus réussie que le film qui l’inspire. Première série du réalisateur Guy Ritchie (Snatch, Sherlock Holmes), celle-ci nous emporte dans un récit fun, explosif et plein de personnages hilarants qui ne cessent jamais de nous divertir. Un pur plaisir de retour ce mois-ci avec une saison 2 encore plus intense et riche en rebondissements.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la saison 2 :
Stranger Things : Chroniques de 1985
Pendant l'hiver 1985, la neige recouvre la ville et les horreurs du Monde à l'envers semblent enfin s'estomper. Nos héros (Onze, Mike, Will, Dustin, Lucas et Max) ont retrouvé une vie normale, rythmée par les parties de Donjons et Dragons, les batailles de boules de neige et les journées paisibles. Mais sous la glace, une terrible menace s'est réveillée. D'où vient-elle ? Du Monde à l'envers ? Des profondeurs du laboratoire de Hawkins ? Ou d'ailleurs ? Nos héros doivent se lancer dans une course contre la montre pour percer le mystère et sauver Hawkins dans cette nouvelle histoire qui se déroule dans l'univers de Stranger Things.
Les fans de Stranger Things seront ravis de retrouver leurs personnages favoris dans cette série d’animation soigneusement produite et visuellement attrayante. Elle est de retour ce mois-ci avec une seconde saison qui promet de nouvelles péripéties suffisamment divertissantes pour accompagner le bol de céréales du petit-déjeuner.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la saison 2 :
Resident Alien
Un extraterrestre s'écrase sur Terre et emprunte l'identité d'un médecin local dans une petite ville du Colorado. Alors qu'il se familiarise avec les humains, il est impliqué dans une enquête pour meurtre, ce qui l'amène à se demander si l'humanité mérite d'être sauvée.
Drôle, décalée et même touchante, il y en a pour tout le monde dans cette série portée par Alan Tudyk (Firefly, Andor) dont trois saisons sont disponibles sur Netflix. Les amateurs de comédie de science-fiction seront attirés par l'intrigue de la série et séduits par son côté sincère et réconfortant en plus de son humour diablement efficace.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
L'Attentat du vol Pan Am 103
Le 21 décembre 1988, le vol Pan Am 103 explose au-dessus de la petite ville de Lockerbie, faisant 270 morts. S'ensuit la plus vaste enquête criminelle de l'histoire de la police écossaise, sur l'attentat terroriste le plus meurtrier jamais commis sur le sol britannique. À travers les témoignages de ceux qui l'ont vécu, voici l'histoire vraie de la collaboration entre la police écossaise et les forces de l'ordre américaines, et du combat des familles pour obtenir justice.
Si vous n'êtes pas au fait de ce drame ayant eu lieu à la fin des années 1980, cette série est une bonne façon d'en apprendre plus sur le sujet. Portée par un casting d'une remarquable justesse (Connor Swindells, Tony Curran, Lauren Lyle, Eddie Marsan...), elle offre un éclairage captivant, à la limite du documentaire, sur l'une des affaires terroristes les plus marquantes de la fin du XXe siècle en combinant témoignages poignants et reconstitution minutieuse des événements.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série (en VO) :

articles.title: Black Friday, 11.11 : vlogueurs, la DJI Osmo Pocket 4 tombe à 332,21€ aujourd'hui
articles.text:
Filmer en vlog ou en voyage sans trépied ni stabilisateur reste le terrain des caméras sur nacelle, et la quatrième génération de DJI perd près d’un tiers de son prix affiché. Avec le code CLU60, la DJI Osmo Pocket 4 passe à 332,21 € sur AliExpress, sous les 479 € de sa version de base au lancement, et notre test lui a donné 9/10 malgré une absence de coque rigide qui déçoit.
Successeur de la Pocket 3, la DJI Osmo Pocket 4 garde la formule de la gamme : un capteur 1 pouce posé sur une nacelle trois axes, dans un boîtier de 190,5 g. Cette génération ajoute le D-Log 10 bits natif, le ralenti en 4K à 240 images par seconde et 107 Go de stockage intégré. AliExpress l’affiche à 332,21 € avec le code CLU60, contre 489,84 € avant remise, soit 157,63 € d’économie (-32 %). L’offre parle d’abord aux vidéastes qui veulent dépasser le smartphone sans transporter un boîtier et un stabilisateur. Elle intéresse moins ceux à qui le téléphone suffit pour quelques stories.
La DJI Osmo Pocket 4 est à 332,21 € au lieu de 489,84 € sur AliExpress, à condition de saisir le code CLU60 avant de valider la commande.
Pourquoi choisir la DJI Osmo Pocket 4 ?
- Une image qui encaisse le contre-jour : Le D-Log 10 bits natif offre 14 stops de plage dynamique. Dans notre test, les hautes lumières tenaient là où la Pocket 3 les brûlait.
- Un ralenti vraiment exploitable : La 4K à 240 images par seconde donne des mouvements fluides, sans artefact visible lors de notre essai. De quoi ralentir un geste sans repasser en 1080p.
- Un transfert des rushes enfin rapide : Les 107 Go intégrés évitent de partir sans carte mémoire, et l’USB 3.1 rapatrie les fichiers bien plus vite que l’USB 2.0 de la génération précédente.
Du vlog au carnet de voyage, ce que change cette quatrième génération
En vlog, l’ActiveTrack 7.0 garde votre visage dans le cadre quand vous marchez, et le suivi tient même pendant les zooms : dans notre test de la DJI Osmo Pocket 4, il n’a jamais décroché. Les trois micros intégrés captent la voix plus nettement qu’avant, et le DJI Mic 3 reste compatible pour aller plus loin. En voyage, l’autonomie annoncée de 240 minutes en 1080p à 24 images par seconde progresse de 45 % sur la Pocket 3, et la charge remonte à 80 % en 18 minutes. L’écran OLED de 2 pouces, poussé à 1 000 nits, aide à cadrer en plein jour.
Les créateurs qui étalonnent leurs images sont les premiers gagnants : le D-Log natif ouvre une latitude que le D-Log M de la Pocket 3 n’offrait pas. Pour un premier achat, ou en venant d’une Pocket 2, le saut est considérable. Elle convient moins si vous filmez surtout de nuit : le progrès en basse lumière est réel sans être spectaculaire, et nous conseillions de rester vers 800 ISO en 4K à 60 images par seconde. Le zoom 4x, lui, ne sert guère au-delà des réseaux sociaux.
Pocket 3 ou Pocket 4 : ce que justifie l’écart
Face à la Pocket 3, la nouvelle venue passe de 9,4 à 37 mégapixels en photo, de la 4K à 120 à la 4K à 240 images par seconde, et gagne un stockage interne qui manquait totalement. Elle pèse en revanche 11,5 g de plus et perd l’étui rigide livré avec l’ancienne génération, remplacé par un simple clip magnétique. Depuis une Pocket 3, la mise à jour se justifie surtout si vous faites de la post-production ou si l’USB 2.0 vous ralentit. Sans ces besoins, elle rend encore les services essentiels.
✅ Les points forts
- D-Log 10 bits natif et 14 stops de plage dynamique
- Ralenti en 4K à 240 images par seconde, propre et fluide
- 107 Go de stockage intégré et transfert en USB 3.1
- ActiveTrack 7.0 fiable, y compris pendant les zooms
- Micros intégrés nettement plus convaincants sur la voix
❌ Les limites
- Plus d’étui rigide fourni, seulement un clip magnétique
- Zoom 4x qui pixelise, à réserver aux réseaux sociaux
- Progrès mesuré en basse lumière
- Prix de 332,21 € conditionné au code CLU60
Le code CLU60 conditionne le prix de 332,21 € : vérifiez qu’il est bien appliqué au panier avant de payer la DJI Osmo Pocket 4 sur AliExpress.
À 332,21 €, la DJI Osmo Pocket 4 passe nettement sous le prix de lancement de sa version de base, fixé à 479 €. La caméra que nous avons notée 9/10 perd ainsi près de 147 € par rapport à son tarif de départ. Les vidéastes qui veulent du D-Log, du ralenti 4K et un suivi fiable en format de poche y trouvent leur compte.
Avant de valider, regardez sur la fiche AliExpress quelle version est vendue : au lancement, le Creator Combo à 619 € ajoutait notamment un DJI Mic 3 et une lumière LED. Les possesseurs d’une Pocket 3 qui ne retouchent pas leurs vidéos peuvent garder la leur sans regret. Pour un premier achat, en revanche, cette remise rend la quatrième génération bien plus facile à justifier.

articles.title: Vizio smart TVs are ignoring tracking opt-outs, continue to send data even when sitting idle
articles.text:
A hot potato: Vizio paid $2.2 million to settle charges that its smart TVs had quietly tracked what was playing on 11 million screens back in 2017. As part of that deal, the company had to start asking owners for permission first. A new study, however, suggests that telling a current Vizio TV "no" doesn't change much, at least as far as its network traffic goes.
For the study, researchers at Northeastern University tested 12 smart TVs from 10 manufacturers. Together, those sets run the eight operating systems behind roughly 95% of US smart TVs. Every viewing scenario – antenna, HDMI, streaming apps and more – ran 30 times with automatic content recognition (ACR) turned on. Each one then ran 30 more times after the researchers opted out through the TV's own settings.
Vizio's SmartCast platform came out looking the worst. After the researchers opted out, the Vizio TV kept sending just as much data as before to an Amazon Kinesis server the team linked to ACR. That happened in every single run, even while the set sat idle on its home screen.
By comparison, only four platforms – LG's webOS, Fire TV, VIDAA and Sony's Google TV – fully went quiet after opting out. But the Samsung set continued sending ACR-like traffic in all 30 tests of the company's own streaming service. Roku's opt-out, meanwhile, doesn't cover The Roku Channel at all.
Still, the Vizio and Samsung traffic is encrypted, so the researchers couldn't see what was actually inside it. That's why they stop short of saying Vizio broke its FTC settlement. They only tested one Vizio set, too, so other models may behave differently.
Even a working opt-out wouldn't help on Vizio's free WatchFree+ service, though. It drops the name of each show or channel into unencrypted DNS lookups sent to stream delivery firm Amagi. That lets an internet provider, or anyone else on the network path, piece together a running list of what someone watched. And there's no setting to turn it off.
Walmart, for its part, bought Vizio for $2.3 billion in late 2024, partly to feed its growing ad business. Since March, select new Vizio TVs even need a Walmart account to unlock their smart features.
For owners who'd rather not be watched, the researchers suggest cutting the TV's internet connection and using a separate streaming device that doesn't run ACR. They've also published a blocklist of known ACR servers. In their lab tests, blocking the ACR servers didn't break anything, though the blocklist doesn't stop the WatchFree+ leak.

TV LG OLED 55″ recebe oferta histórica em até 12x na Amazon
Smart TV LG OLED C6 de 55 polegadas traz pretos profundos, taxa de até 165 Hz e recursos de IA; preço cai 30% no mês da Black Friday
