articles.title: IBM connects agentic workloads to the demands of always-on AI - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
IBM puts agentic workloads at the heart of its AI operating model
Agentic workloads present a new operating challenge for enterprises putting artificial intelligence into production. As autonomous systems take on ongoing responsibilities, organizations must support decisions and actions across their data, applications and infrastructure.
IBM Corp.’s approach draws on the experiences of clients scaling AI across their organizations. That work helped identify the requirements underpinning its AI operating model, according to Ritika Gunnar (pictured), chief performance marketing officer of IBM.
“As you’re more successful in using AI, especially as AI is taking action, you now have workloads that are continuously being utilized,” she said. “You are incented to be always on because those agents are always taking action for you.”
Gunnar spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and John Furrier for IBM’s AI Operating Model interview series in an exclusive interview on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed enterprise integration, data governance, human oversight and evaluating AI against business outcomes in preparation for IBM TechXchange 2026. (* Disclosure below.)
Connecting agentic workloads across the enterprise
IBM’s AI operating model brings together four components that enterprises may already obtain from different providers. Applying them means accounting for established applications and business processes alongside emerging AI systems, Gunnar explained.
“You need to be able to integrate with your existing systems,” she said. “People aren’t going to run away from their SAP systems that exist, from their Salesforce systems that exist. What does it mean to integrate with those and have workloads that are representative of your past and your future together?”
The components have distinct roles: Data supplies current enterprise knowledge, workloads encompass applications and workflows, automation supports oversight and optimization, and hybrid cloud accommodates distributed operations. Their effectiveness depends on how they function together across agentic workloads, according to Gunnar.
“If you have your data and that data is feeding your systems, but you’re not really taking care of automation in a way where you have complete observability of all of your workloads with that AI infused, then you’re not necessarily having an optimal way of picking the right model or picking the right agents for those kinds of workloads,” she said.
Bringing governance and human judgment into decisions
The information supporting an agent’s decision may span operational systems, edge devices and context generated by other agents. Providing governed context requires enterprises to consider both the completeness of that information and how permissions travel with it, Gunnar explained.
“Our belief is if you can take data and if you can shift left a lot of the governance — a lot of the who has the right access to the right data at the right time — it becomes important because you flow that data in real time with the context and provenance of who actually has ownership of that data,” she said. “Therefore, the agents make much better decisions.”
Enterprises also depend on knowledge employees develop through experience rather than explicitly recording it in their systems. Prompts and other context can help convey that judgment, but capturing it remains an ongoing challenge, Gunnar pointed out.
“When you think about workloads today … there is a lot of it that will be autonomous in nature,” she said. “But in most cases, if you’re talking about your essential systems, you do have humans in the loop to be able to bring some of that tacit knowledge in place where the AI has not yet matured to be able to even get there.”
Evaluating performance against business outcomes
Agent activity generates logs of decisions and actions, while prompts record the instructions supplied to those systems. Together, that information supports an ongoing feedback loop between enterprise data and AI workloads, Gunnar explained.
“You can actually have multiple different permutations of that agent making a decision and having another set of eval loops actually doing an evaluation of, ‘Did that agent actually make the decisions?’” she said. “Would there have been a more performant way, a more accurate way, a more cost-effective way to be able to do that?”
Performance encompasses accuracy, timeliness and cost, with the intended business result guiding how those measures are assessed. Putting AI into production therefore requires organizations to examine the work itself alongside the technology supporting it, according to Gunnar.
“Make sure that you have all of these elements and that you’re really thinking about the outcomes, and you’re willing to start with what it means to take a look at the business process transformation,” she said. “That’s really where it’s at.”

articles.title: HomeView Ultra : Apple prendrait son temps pour proposer la version haut de gamme de son écran domestique
articles.text:
Le HomeView XL serait en réalité déjà dans les cartons, mais la marque à la pomme aurait un problème important et ne pourrait en fait pas encore le sortir. En attendant, certains marchés se contenteront de la petite version.
Alors que le premier écran connecté d'Apple, le HomeView, sera livré dès la semaine prochaine pour les pays éligibles, une version plus grande, dotée d'un bras motorisé, refait parler d'elle. En réalité, l'appareil pourrait être prêt depuis deux ans, mais le logiciel retarderait la sortie de cette version XL.
Une annonce possible en 2027, une commercialisation en 2028
Le mois dernier, Bloomberg évoquait une sortie en 2027 ou en 2028 pour cet appareil. Apple pourrait le présenter en 2027 et le commercialiser en 2028, à un prix estimé à 1 000 dollars, rien que ça. Pour l'instant, ces informations restent à l'état de rumeurs.
Le produit porterait en interne le nom de code J595. Il serait équipé d'un écran de 9 pouces monté sur un bras robotisé, qui le ferait pivoter. Des capteurs lui permettraient de suivre l'utilisateur lorsqu'il se déplace pendant un appel FaceTime.
Un matériel prêt, un logiciel encore en travail
Nos confrères de The Information indiquent que le matériel est prêt depuis deux ans. L'appareil ressemblerait à une lampe de bureau articulée, comparable à celle qui apparaît dans le logo de Pixar.
C'est l'équipe chargée du logiciel qui retarderait le lancement : elle cherche à affiner certaines fonctions d'intelligence artificielle et de domotique, comme l'allumage automatique d'une lumière lorsqu'une personne entre dans la pièce.
Un écart de 700 dollars avec le modèle standard
Le prix évoqué pour cette version, environ 1 000 dollars, est supérieur aux 299 dollars annoncés le mois dernier pour le HomeView standard. Nos confrères du média The Information ont également recueilli les propos de plusieurs anciens employés d'Apple, selon lesquels le modèle haut de gamme pourrait s'appeler « HomeView Ultra ».
Avec 700 dollars d'écart, on ignore pour l'instant ce que ce modèle offrirait de plus que la version de base, hormis le bras motorisé et l'écran plus grand.
Ce que propose le HomeView actuel
Le HomeView standard actuellement commercialisé existe en deux versions : l'une avec un écran de 7 pouces posé sur une enceinte, l'autre composée uniquement de l'écran, conçu pour être fixé au mur. Les deux permettent d'écouter de la musique, de passer des appels FaceTime, de piloter la maison connectée depuis un tableau de bord et de poser des questions à Siri AI.
Une fuite de code récente laisse par ailleurs penser que ces appareils pourraient, à terme, servir aussi de caméras de sécurité d'intérieur.
Source : PCMag UK

articles.title: MariaDB change de visage et veut devenir le moteur caché des agents IA
articles.text:
MariaDB lance ce mardi Enterprise Platform 2027, la dernière version de sa plateforme de base de données, pensée pour les agents IA. L'éditeur open source en profite pour dévoiler une nouvelle identité visuelle et affiche des performances en nette hausse.
Avec Enterprise Platform 2027, dévoilé ce mardi 3 novembre 2026, MariaDB veut devenir le socle sur lequel les entreprises bâtiront leurs agents IA, ces programmes capables d'enchaîner des tâches sans qu'on leur tienne la main. L'éditeur est né en Finlande sous l'impulsion du cofondateur de MySQL et s'est depuis installé entre la Californie et l'Irlande. Il promet plus de vitesse, une mémoire pour les agents et des données enfin réunies au même endroit. Pour marquer l'occasion, il s'offre aussi un sérieux coup de jeune.
Des agents IA mieux nourris, et qui gardent la mémoire
Un agent IA ne vaut que ce que valent ses données. Or, dans la plupart des entreprises, elles sont éparpillées entre plusieurs bases, un entrepôt, des outils de recherche et de transfert, des caches… Chaque passerelle entre ces briques ralentit l'ensemble, crée des décalages et ajoute un risque de panne. « Chaque système que vous ajoutez pour l'IA crée une nouvelle jonction, et les jonctions finissent par céder », résume Rohit de Souza, PDG de MariaDB.
D'où une série d'outils taillés pour ces nouveaux assistants, présents dans la version 2027 de l'Enterprise Platform de MariaDB. Parmi eux, AI Retrieval permet aux agents de puiser dans des documents et des données à jour. Il traduit une question posée en langage courant en requête de base de données, uniquement en lecture, sans rien pouvoir modifier. Agent Memory donne aux agents un carnet de notes qui survit d'une session à l'autre, pour reprendre une longue tâche là où ils l'avaient laissée. Et le Semantic Cache reconnaît une question déjà posée, même reformulée, et ressort la réponse plus vite et à moindre coût. Les développeurs ne sont pas oubliés, puisque des plugins glissent l'expertise maison dans des assistants de code comme Claude Code ou Codex, avec la promesse d'un code juste du premier coup.
Selon le cabinet IDC, l'usage des agents sera multiplié par dix d'ici 2027 dans les 2 000 plus grandes entreprises mondiales, donc autant dire que la pression ne va pas retomber tout de suite. La charge liée aux tokens (ou jetons en français, ces morceaux de texte que traitent les IA) et aux appels entre logiciels sera, elle, multipliée par mille. Pour suivre, MariaDB revendique un débit de pointe en hausse de 56 % par rapport à sa précédente version majeure. La recherche vectorielle, celle qui retrouve des contenus par le sens plutôt que par les mots exacts, traite jusqu'à 30 % de requêtes par seconde en plus. Le chiffre de débit vient d'un test mené par un cabinet tiers, mais financé par l'éditeur lui-même.
Une base de données qui voit plus grand
La stratégie de MariaDB consiste à partir de son cœur transactionnel, qui fait déjà tourner des systèmes critiques dans la banque, les télécoms, le commerce ou le secteur public. Deutsche Bank, Nokia et Samsung figurent d'ailleurs parmi ses clients. Plutôt que de copier les données ailleurs, son module Exa les analyse en direct. Sanjeev Mohan, analyste chez SanjMo, approuve, estimant que « les agents ont besoin d'une base solide qui ne cède pas sous leurs pieds ». Le patron, lui, enfonce le clou : « MariaDB est bien plus qu'une simple base de données. »
L'argument qui pèsera le plus est qu'il n'y a pas besoin de tout reconstruire. La plupart des entreprises « ajouteront des agents aux systèmes qui gèrent déjà leurs activités », prédit Devin Pratt, directeur de recherche chez IDC. La plateforme s'installe sur site, dans n'importe quel cloud ou en service géré. Grâce au clustering Raft, elle grandit plus facilement et résiste mieux aux pannes lorsqu'elle est répartie sur plusieurs régions du globe. Côté sécurité, les mêmes règles d'accès s'appliquent partout, et l'option BYOC permet de garder ses données là où on le souhaite. La norme de cryptographie FIPS 140-3 devrait aussi rassurer les organismes fédéraux américains et les secteurs réglementés. Le code reste ouvert, et MariaDB vérifie les contributeurs avant de livrer des versions renforcées.
Puis il y a ce nouvel habit pour MariaDB, avec un logo redessiné, des couleurs vives et un site repensé. « La nôtre racontait une histoire d'autrefois », reconnaît Tracy Strauss, sa directrice marketing, en parlant de l'ancienne marque.La plateforme Enterprise Platform 2027, qui est le fruit de deux années d'investissements, est disponible dès aujourd'hui et réunit notamment Enterprise Server 12.3, Exa et GridGain. AI Retrieval reste en préversion publique sur MariaDB Cloud.

articles.title: Samsung devrait bientôt lancer ses premières lunettes connectées, mais l’Europe va devoir patienter
articles.text:
En juillet dernier, lors de l’événement Unpacked 2026, Samsung a dévoilé ses premières lunettes connectées. Pour rappel, ces lunettes connectées, sans écran, intègrent une caméra, des haut-parleurs et des micros pour discuter avec Gemini. Elles tournent sous Android XR et disposent du processeur Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 de Qualcomm. Autant dire que les premières lunettes connectées du géant sud-coréen sont très attendues. Bonne nouvelle : elles devraient être commercialisées bientôt. Moins bonne nouvelle : l’Europe, et donc la France, ne seraient pas concernées. En réalité, les premières lunettes connectées signées Samsung seraient lancées dans seulement deux pays. Du moins, dans un premier temps.
Un lancement seulement dans deux pays
Certaines rumeurs avaient évoqué une date de lancement pour l’automne 2026. Selon le média sud-coréen Chosun Biz, les premières lunettes connectées de Samsung sortiront finalement à la mi-décembre. Bonne nouvelle, leur lancement serait donc pour bientôt. Cependant, ce lancement concernerait seulement deux pays : la Corée du Sud et les États-Unis. Les Américains et les Sud-coréens devraient donc avoir l’opportunité de placer les premières lunettes connectées de Samsung sous le sapin. L’Europe devra quant à elle attendre. En effet, un responsable du secteur a expliqué au média Chosun Biz que Samsung veut étudier la demande et les retours des premiers utilisateurs avant de considérer un lancement sur d’autres marchés.
Pour rappel, Samsung a d’abord commercialisé son casque de réalité augmentée Galaxy XR en Corée du Sud et aux États-Unis. Neuf mois plus tard, soit le 8 juillet 2026, l’appareil a fait son arrivée au Royaume-Uni. Il faudra maintenant voir si les premières lunettes connectées de Samsung connaîtront un calendrier de commercialisation similaire.
Nous ne disposons toujours pas de prix
À l’heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, Samsung n’a communiqué aucune information officielle concernant le lancement de ses premières lunettes connectées. Nous ne connaissons d’ailleurs pas leur prix, ni en dollars américains ni en wons. Toujours selon le média sud-coréen Chosun Biz, Samsung n’aurait toujours pas fixé de tarif définitif. Rappelons que Xreal a modifié le prix de ses lunettes connectées Aura le jour de leur lancement. Tout est donc possible.

articles.text:
Awfis Q2 profit jumps 93% to Rs 31 Cr, revenue rises to Rs 464 Cr
During April-September period of FY27, the company's net profit rose to Rs 54.76 crore from Rs 25.95 crore in the year-ago period.
Realty firm Awfis Space Solutions Ltd has reported a 93% increase in its consolidated profit to Rs 30.8 crore for the quarter ended September on higher income amid strong demand for managed workspaces.
Its net profit stood at Rs 15.97 crore in the year-ago period.
Total income increased to Rs 464.29 crore in the second quarter of this fiscal from Rs 392.97 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing on Tuesday.
During April-September period of FY27, the company's net profit rose to Rs 54.76 crore from Rs 25.95 crore in the year-ago period.
Total income also grew to Rs 913.16 crore in the first six months of this fiscal from Rs 746.01 crore in the corresponding period of the preceding year.
Awfis has a presence in 18 cities with more than 250 coworking centres.
Amit Ramani, the company's CMD, noted that the company has reported another quarter of steady performance, supported by continued office demand from large enterprises & GCCs (Global Capability Centres)
The company continues to focus on premiumisation and operational efficiency, he said.
During the September quarter, Ramani said the company has added 6 new centres, taking the total supply to 254 centres with about 1,74,000 seats across 18 cities.
The overall portfolio occupancy stood at 76.2%, he said.

articles.title: Óscar Puente, ministro de Transportes, sobre los cinturones de seguridad: "Valoramos medidas adicionales de seguridad pasiva"
articles.text:
El accidente ferroviario de Urda (Toledo), en el que han fallecido al menos 69 personas, deja varias incógnitas sobre cómo se trabaja la seguridad ferroviaria. Nos hemos preguntado sobre el sistema LZB y si es o no más seguro que el más moderno ERTMS. También sobre el papel de los controladores. Y, por supuesto, sobre el uso o no de cinturones de seguridad.
De esto último ha hablado el ministro de Transportes Óscar Puente.
Seguridad pasiva. "Vamos a valorar la instalación de medidas adicionales de seguridad pasiva en los coches", ha señalado Óscar Puente en la intervención de esta mañana ante los medios. Esta decisión se acometerá en función de las respuestas de los expertos a los que se les encargará el estudio técnico.
Desde que se produjera el choque de trenes en Urda (Toledo) el pasado 28 de octubre, la idoneidad o no de llevar cinturón de seguridad y compartimentos separados para el equipaje es algo que se ha puesto encima de la mesa.
Despedidos.
"Pedí un café en la cafetería del tren a Sevilla. La camarera me lo sirvió. Otro camarero pregonó que estaba listo un sándwich mixto para alguien. Es lo último que recuerdo. Noté un empujón brutal del que no me acuerdo bien y sentí un golpe en la cabeza mientras me preguntaba qué pasaba. Después me vi en el suelo del vagón, en el otro extremo de la cafetería. Alguien dijo que era un accidente y eso me hizo reaccionar y comprender lo que me pasaba"
El relato es de Antonio Jiménez Barca, periodista de El País que viajaba a bordo de uno de los trenes accidentados la pasada semana. En el inicio del mismo señala cómo, en un instante, pasó de estar en extremo de la cafetería del tren al otro, a causa del brutal impacto causado por un tren que choca a otro a una velocidad de entre 160 y 200 km/h.
Además de los pasajeros, los equipajes también salieron despedidos. Y eso preocupa porque a esa velocidad, el impacto de una mochila, por pequeña que sea, es como el de un proyectil. En un coche, a 50 km/h, un objeto multiplica por 50 veces su peso en caso de impacto.
El maletero. En su declaración, Puente ha hecho hincapié en preguntar a los expertos sobre la idoneidad de dejar las maletas y mochilas en un portaequipajes cerrado. Actualmente, las maletas de mayor tamaño van en un portaequipajes abierto en los extremos del vagón. Por encima de las cabezas hay espacio para almacenar, incluso, pequeñas maletas de cabina.
El Gobierno, ha asegurado en rueda de prensa, preguntará si se debe obligar a las compañías a ofrecer trenes donde el portaequipajes sean "compartimentos cerrados que eviten proyecciones en caso frenazos bruscos o impactos. Estamos tomando ideas de medidas de seguridad del ámbito aéreo".
Puente asegura que la idea es evitar que el equipaje pueda convertirse en "misiles" que salen despedidos cuando se produce un choque como el de la semana pasada.
El cinturón de seguridad. A lo que no ha hecho alusión Puente durante su declaración es a la posibilidad de obligar a los trenes a contar con cinturones de seguridad. Esta pregunta ya se puso encima de la mesa pasado el accidente de Adamuz (Córdoba).
El objetivo de un cinturón de seguridad es mantener amarrado al pasajero en caso de accidente y así evitar que salga despedido. Sin embargo hay que tener en cuenta que el comportamiento de un coche y un tren es muy diferente por eso algunos estudios se muestran contrarios al uso del cinturón de seguridad en el transporte ferroviario, al contrario que en coches y aviones.
En un coche existe una jaula de supervivencia que debería mantenerse intacta en caso de accidente. Por fuera, el chasis tiene que absorber el impacto para que la energía que llegue hasta la jaula no la deforme y el pasajero pueda ser rescatado a pesar de sufrir un accidente grave. En el caso de los aviones se utiliza porque si hay grandes turbulencias o un descenso brusco de altura, el pasajero puede salir despedido.
¿Y en un tren? La diferencia entre un coche y un tren es que los estudios demuestran que el cuerpo del pasajero se somete a una desaceleración mucho mayor cuando un coche sufre un impacto, por eso es esencial mantener al pasajero atado al asiento.
En un tren, por brutal que sea el choque, los estudios demuestran que el pasajero se somete a fuerzas de entre 2 g y 3 g (se multiplica dos o tres veces, respectivamente, el peso del pasajero). En un coche, la desaceleración equivale a 30 g. Lo que se hace, al contrario que en un coche, es que los asientos y las mesas estén pensadas para absorber el impacto de una persona en caso de accidente en lugar de afianzarla en el sitio.
Además, se ha analizado si es útil contar con cinturones de seguridad con dos o tres anclajes. En ningún caso se observaron ventajas bien por lesiones en la cadera (el primer caso) o porque el asiento pierde la capacidad de absorción de impactos (el segundo). Además, las labores de extracción del pasajero serían mucho más complicadas en un tipo de accidente que suele convertir algunos coches en un enorme amasijo de hierros.

articles.title: Borderlands is now a 100 million-copy franchise, and Gearbox isn't done yet
articles.text:
In brief: Borderlands, the action role-playing first-person shooter series developed by Gearbox Software and published by 2K, has surpassed 100 million copies sold since its debut. The achievement comes just over a year after the launch of the latest entry in the franchise, Borderlands 4.
Gearbox launched Borderlands 4 on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and Windows PCs on September 12, 2025. Like others in the series, it is playable solo or with up to three others. Gamers have enjoyed a solid first year of post-launch add-on content including two story packs, five bounty packs, and a pair of new vault hunters, on top of several new activities and features.
Gearbox said it's rare for a game series to surpass the 100 million units sold mark, and they aren't wrong. Outside of monster franchises like Mario, Call of Duty, Sonic the Hedgehog, Zelda, and Resident Evil, very few ever reach that milestone.
Only three individual games have ever sold more than 100 million copies on their own: Grand Theft Auto V (230 million), Minecraft (425 million), and Tetris (520 million). Barring any unforeseen circumstances, the next installment in the GTA series will likely be the fourth to join that coveted list.
According to Sensor Tower's sales tracker, Rockstar has already secured 7.71 million pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto VI. That works out to roughly $751 million in revenue, with orders split 74% / 26% in favor of the PlayStation 5. The game is reportedly coming to PC as early as Q1 2027, but that hasn't yet been officially confirmed by Rockstar.
What are your thoughts on the Borderlands franchise? I know several people that swear by it, but have also spoken to others that find it a bit too repetitive in that you're essentially stuck in an endless cycle of grinding to level up only to fight stronger enemies, requiring stouter weapons to defeat them.
Looking ahead, Gearbox pointed to November 6 and the start of a community fundraising event called The Hunt. Earlier this year, gamers raised nearly $120,000 for St. Jude Children's Research Hospital in Memphis, TN through a similar event.

articles.title: The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel Is Official, Release Date Still Nowhere in Sight
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 3rd 2026
The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel Is Official, Release Date Still Nowhere in Sight
The Elder Scrolls VI finally has its full name. Bethesda Game Studios revealed it as The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel at the end of a video celebrating the studio's 40th anniversary, with Todd Howard walking through Bethesda's history first. The short teaser that followed has no gameplay, just a stretch of desert, an Elder Scroll rising out of the sand, and the new logo. It also carries a line of lore text credited to Yazar, Moth Priest to High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell, dated 4E 206. Skyrim takes place in 4E 201, so it looks like Sentinel is set roughly five years later, in the Redguard homeland of Hammerfell. Sentinel itself is one of Hammerfell's major cities, sitting on the Iliac Bay. Both the name and the setting match what The Verge's Tom Warren reported last week.
It seems the name is all fans are getting for now. In a follow-up post on X, Bethesda said development is still ongoing and that it will be "some time" before the studio has anything else to show, adding that it's happy to have the name and location out in the open at last. There's still no word on a release date, launch window, or platforms. The game was first teased at E3 2018, and Bethesda said in July that it remains the studio's primary development focus, although reports suggested the Xbox layoffs could cause delays. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier has also claimed on Bluesky that the game was at least two years out, so anyone hoping for a 2027 launch should probably temper their expectations.

articles.title: Windows fica até 40% mais rápido em PCs com 8 GB de RAM • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Windows fica até 40% mais rápido em PCs com 8 GB de RAM
Atualização do Windows 11 diminui alocação de dados no armazenamento e economiza até 900 MB em cenário de uso intenso.
A Microsoft segue tentando otimizar o Windows 11 para máquinas com apenas 8 GB de RAM. Uma nova atualização reduz o consumo de memória e diminui a necessidade de recorrer ao SSD ou HD quando vários programas estão abertos ao mesmo tempo.
Segundo Pavan Davuluri, chefe da divisão de Windows e Dispositivos, os ajustes deixaram algumas interações do sistema até 20% mais rápidas e melhoraram em até 40% a alternância entre tarefas pesadas nos testes da empresa.
As tentativas de otimização no Windows, que é constantemente criticado por isso, ocorrem num momento de crise na indústria de componentes eletrônicos. Com a expansão de data centers para empresas de inteligência artificial, o foco do setor de semicondutores tem sido alimentá-los, destinando maior parte da capacidade produtiva para chips usados nos servidores.
Enquanto isso, peças chegam ao consumidor cada vez mais caras: o preço de memórias DDR5 saltou cerca de 500% entre 2025 e 2026, limitando a montagem de PCs com mais RAM.
Boa parte das mudanças está na forma como o Windows administra o esgotamento de memória disponível. Quando a RAM fica cheia, o sistema precisa transferir parte dos dados temporários para SDD ou HD, que são mais lentos e diminuem o desempenho na execução de programas.
A Microsoft afirma ter ajustado o algoritmo de compressão do Windows especialmente para computadores com 8 GB de RAM, mantendo até 2 GB adicionais de dados ativos na memória, comprimindo informações em segundo plano antes de recorrer ao armazenamento.
Nos testes internos, ações como abrir o menu Iniciar ou carregar o Explorador de Arquivos ficaram até 20% mais rápidas em comparação com uma compilação do Windows 11 de janeiro desde ano.
A atualização também otimizou o consumo de apps de terceiros. Em outro teste que simulava uma rotina mais pesada, a Microsoft diz ter diminuído o comprometimento da memória em até 900 MB. No caso, foram abertas 20 abas no Edge, um vídeo em 4K, documentos grandes no Word, Excel e Powerpoint e outras atividades.
Os Widgets também deixaram de ser carregados antecipadamente em computadores com essa configuração de memória, consumindo recursos apenas quando aberto pelo usuário.
Outro foco da atualização foi diminuir o tempo para que uma aba no navegador Edge seja considerada inativa. O programa passa a colocá-las em suspensão após 15 minutos, contra as duas horas de antes. Nesses casos, vale lembrar, a página continua aberta, mas reduz o consumo de recursos.
O Microsoft Teams também ativa o Modo de Eficiência por padrão em computadores com 8 GB de RAM. Segundo a empresa, o app passa a iniciar até 20% mais rápido e reduz o uso do processador, podendo reduzir automaticamente a resolução da câmera, por exemplo, para preservar a qualidade de outros recursos durante uma videochamada.
As otimizações fazem parte do Windows 11 26H2, compilação 26300.9818 ou posterior. Para verificar se a versão está disponível, o usuário pode acessar o painel de atualizações em Windows Update, nas Configurações do sistema.
Alguns dos ganhos também dependem de versões atualizadas dos apps. No caso do navegador, é preciso usar o Microsoft Edge 150 ou posterior.
A empresa afirma que continuará trabalhando para diminuir o consumo de RAM no Windows e prevê, no futuro, melhorias na Busca e aplicativos como OneDrive e Fotos.

articles.title: Red Hat Patches 9.8-Rated Linux TCP RCE Flaw While Ubuntu Releases Fixes for Testing
articles.text:
Fixed kernels for a use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP code are now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, while Ubuntu's fixes for its three newest long-term-support releases remain in its opt-in testing channel with no date for a regular update.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, can be reached by a remote, unauthenticated attacker and can lead to remote code execution, Red Hat and Canonical said.
The Linux kernel's own CVE team rates the flaw 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale. Red Hat, which initially rated it Moderate at 5.9, has raised its score to 9.8 and now calls it Critical. The bug has been present since Linux 4.4, and the upstream fix landed in October.
What the Flaw Is
When a server accepts an IPv4 TCP connection, the kernel passes IP options from the incoming request to the new socket without copying them. If the client retransmits its connection request while another processor still reads those options, the kernel can read memory it has already freed.
An attacker triggers the race by sending connection requests that carry IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp options to any listening TCP port. No login is needed. IPv6 is not affected on the main path.
Red Hat shipped RHSA-2026:93414 (RHEL 8), RHSA-2026:93412 (RHEL 9), and RHSA-2026:93413 (RHEL 10) on November 1. A reboot is needed after installing the update.
| RHEL Version | Fixed Kernel | Errata | 
|---|---|---|
| 8.10 | 4.18.0-553.182.1.el8_10 | RHSA-2026:93414 | 
| 9.8 | 5.14.0-687.64.1.el9_8 | RHSA-2026:93412 | 
| 10.2 | 6.12.0-211.72.1.el10_2 | RHSA-2026:93413 | 
Canonical said on November 2 that fixes for Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, and 26.04 LTS are in its -proposed pocket, an opt-in testing channel. Packages there do not install automatically.
Canonical tests kernel updates across more than 2,000 certified servers and devices before releasing them to the regular update channel, and no release date has been given.
| Ubuntu Release | -proposed Kernel | Status | 
|---|---|---|
| 22.04 LTS (Jammy) | 5.15.0-203.213 | In -proposed | 
| 24.04 LTS (Noble) | 6.8.0-149.149 | In -proposed | 
| 26.04 LTS (Resolute) | 7.0.0-43.43 | In -proposed | 
| 20.04 / 18.04 / 16.04 | Pending |  | 
Administrators who need the fix before it reaches the regular channel can enable -proposed and install the kernel update by running:
sudo add-apt-repository --component main --pocket proposed https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu
dpkg-query -W -f '${source:Package}\t${binary:Package}\n' | awk '$1 ~ "^linux-meta" { print $2 }' | xargs sudo apt install -t $(. /etc/os-release && echo $VERSION_CODENAME)-proposed --only-upgrade
sudo reboot
To check whether a system is running a fixed kernel, compare the output of uname -r against the versions in the tables above.
Ubuntu 20.04, 18.04, and 16.04 have no fix yet. Older releases require Expanded Security Maintenance through Ubuntu Pro.
Cloud, FIPS, and real-time kernel variants for Ubuntu are listed as work in progress on the Ubuntu CVE page with target versions, but Canonical's blog post covers only the generic kernel.
Interim Mitigation
Red Hat published an nftables rule on October 30 that drops inbound IPv4 TCP packets carrying IP options. The rule blocks the known trigger for the race but cannot fully prevent exploitation and may break workloads that depend on IPv4 options, Red Hat said.
table inet cve_2026_98432 {
    chain input {
        type filter hook input priority -310; policy accept;
        ip protocol tcp ip hdrlength > 5 counter drop
    }
}
The filter applies only to the host where it is loaded. Traffic between containers on the same host can bypass it, a member of the CIQ kernel team noted on the oss-security mailing list.
Several sources have recommended disabling Multipath TCP (MPTCP) as a workaround. The flaw is in the IPv4 TCP path, not in MPTCP, and that advice alone is not enough, Canonical said. "The Ubuntu Security Team believes that security updates are the only appropriate mitigation."
Exploitation Status
No vendor, CERT, or the kernel CVE team has reported attacks using this flaw. It was not listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of the catalog's October 30 release.
Anthropic said on October 27 that an unreleased, internal Claude research model wrote a remote root exploit for the flaw that works against Linux servers with an MPTCP listener, with no credentials and no user interaction. In its proof of concept, leaking a kernel address took 48 minutes and reaching a root shell took another 5 minutes. Anthropic has not published the exploit code.
Proof-only code that triggers the race and detects the kernel echoing freed memory in a SYN-ACK has appeared on GitHub. It does not implement code execution.
Amazon Linux scored the flaw 8.1 and rated it Important, saying the main outcome is a crash with possible memory corruption. Debian, Oracle Linux, and SUSE shipped fixes in October. Amazon Linux was fixed across all packages between October 24 and 30.

articles.title: LiveX brings engaging, AI-powered intelligent human-sized avatar kiosks to retail and airport sites - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
LiveX brings engaging, AI-powered intelligent human-sized avatar kiosks to retail and airport sites
Palo Alto-based LiveX AI Inc., a company building interactive experience artificial intelligence agents for retail and hospitality environments, today announced AI City, its kiosk-driven, life-size, human-like AI hosts.
The company’s products, currently deployed in more than 100 sites, engage guests through life-sized human avatars across retail, technology, hospitality and entertainment. Customer sites include PUMA stores, San José Mineta International Airport, SAP Center, the San Jose Sharks stadium, El Camino Hospital, and Marriott and Hilton hotels.
“We believe intelligence of this nature should meet people wherever they are, live and in person, where life happens,” said President and Chief AI Officer Jia Li. “AI should be greeting travelers at the airport, guiding a grandmother through the hospital, helping every shopper like the best employee in the building or answering sixty thousand fans at once.”
A traditional interactive kiosk relies on rigid menus and doesn’t converse with the user; it also doesn’t automatically translate into the user’s native language by simply listening to them speak. An AI City kiosk can see and hear the other person and react almost like another person, using real-time discovery to provide personalized help.
The company added that these kiosks are coming as companies try to bring other physical AI products, such as general-purpose robotics, to market, but these are still years away from widespread deployment.
As a kiosk, a user could walk up and see a projected AI person who can assist with navigation, product recommendations, event guidance or answer questions about the venue. According to LiveX, the City kiosk products have been expanded with interactive 3D maps for location-aware navigation and discovery, 3D products and multilingual translation.
LiveX said such a system could assist customers with product, venue and event questions, enabling staff to walk around with more customers at the site and handle more complex problems requiring deeper oversight.
“AI that can understand people and their surroundings is opening new ways to make everyday spaces more helpful and accessible,” said Madison Huang, senior director of product marketing for physical AI at Nvidia Corp.
The LiveX Interactive Intelligence platform runs on Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell Server Edition graphics processing units and uses the Metropolis VSS Blueprint to build visual AI agents powered by Nvidia Cosmos, an open world model builder. Nvidia also provided a surface for supplying libraries from Omniverse, which delivers digital twins for location-aware applications.
LiveX said its platform brings together proprietary models it developed and trained for human interaction, shaped on real-world interaction data and experience through live deployments. Its Omni Model provides multimodal understanding and responses, while a noise management model lets it assist users even with significant background noise.

articles.title: Synology NAS devices could be under attack from new ransomware threat — so update now
articles.text:
Synology NAS devices could be under attack from new ransomware threat — so update now
There's been a wave of attacks against Synology devices
- Synology warned of active ransomware attacks exploiting long-patched DSM vulnerabilities on unupdated NAS devices
- Attackers are reportedly deploying the C3rb3r encryptor and demanding thousands of dollars in ransom
- Users are urged to patch immediately, restrict internet exposure, and secure NAS access to prevent compromise
Synology, a major network-attached storage (NAS) manufacturer, is warning users about ongoing ransomware attacks targeting devices running outdated software. It urged all users to apply provided patches and secure their devices without delay.
In a brief announcement, Synology said it “identified threat actors exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to target devices running outdated versions of DSM.” The goal of the attacks seem to be data encryption and a ransom demand.
“Synology strongly urges all users running vulnerable versions to update DSM immediately to protect their systems. Synology also recommends enabling automatic updates to keep DSM up to date at all times.”
C3rb3r attacks
The announcement is rather stingy on the details. We don’t know which vulnerability the threat actors are exploiting, where exactly, or how successful they are.
We also don’t know how many devices are at risk - the Shadowserver Foundation tracks a total of 380,000 internet-connected endpoints (many of which are, most likely, running the latest software version and are thus protected).
The company also did not say who the threat actors are, but according to BleepingComputer, there has been a “massive wave of reports” from Synology customers whose data was apparently locked down by the “C3rb3r” encryptor. These customers were asked to pay “thousands of dollars” in ransom, in exchange for the decryption key. The publication says the first reports started surfacing more than two weeks ago.
There are two main ways for cybercriminals to access an electronic device and encrypt the data found there - either by exploiting a zero-day vulnerability (one that has not yet received a patch), or by exploiting years-old n-day vulnerabilities (ones that were patched months ago) on devices that were never updated and secured.

With Synology users, the latter seems to be the case. The company said the attackers were exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024, and linked to a November 2024 security advisory, in which it listed three fixed bugs: CVE-2024-10441 (arbitrary code execution), CVE-2024-50629 (arbitrary file read), and CVE-2024-10445 (a bug that allows writing files on compromised devices).
DSM 7.2.2 owners should upgrade to 7.2.2-72806-1 or above, DSM 7.2.1 to 7.2.1-69057-6 or above, and DSM 7.2 to 7.2-64570-4 or above. DSM 7.1 should upgrade to 7.1.1-42962-7 or above, while those running DSM 6.2 to 6.2.4-25556-8 or above. Only in the last version - 6.2 - is the vulnerability labeled as “moderate”. In all other cases it was deemed “critical”.
Why are NAS devices being targeted?
NAS devices are dedicated storage systems that businesses can connect to their local network and allow employees to access, share, and manage files stored in a centralized location. They are rather popular among SMBs that lack the resources to maintain a more complex enterprise storage infrastructure.
Besides being used as a hybrid cloud of sorts, NAS is also used to store business documents and often acts as a centralized backup. The relative low cost, straightforward deployment, and easily expandable storage capacity makes NAS devices an attractive alternative to both dedicated file servers and cloud storage subscriptions.
However, this also makes them a valuable target for cybercriminals, as we’ve seen in this Synology case. The best way to defend against ransomware attackers is to either completely pull the NAS from the public internet or at least limit access to a handful of vetted identities. Keeping the devices updated with the latest firmware and software is also recommended.
It is worth mentioning that NAS devices usually come with RAID redundancy and built-in backup features, but these do not necessarily protect against ransomware encrypting the stored data.

articles.title: India's EloElo nabs $80M from NBCUniversal to bet on the country's rising microdrama market | TechCrunch
articles.text:
More than 118 million users watch microdramas every month as the serialized format has taken off in India. EloElo’s Story TV is one of the top apps for microdramas, with over 33 million active users, according to analysts.
Banking on that scale, the company has raised $80 million in Series C from Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal. This round brings its total fundraising to $130 million, with a valuation of $500 million.
As people spend more time on platforms hosting verticalized videos, serialized content has become popular in multiple geographies, including the U.S., China, and India, with Hollywood celebrities like Issa Rae, James Franco, and Kim Kardashian investing in and starring in the format.
Given India’s massive internet population of more than a billion and the country’s appetite for entertainment content, it presents a big market opportunity, with analysts expecting the industry to cross $3-$4 billion in annual revenue by 2030. Last year, dedicated apps like Story TV, Kuku TV, and Quick TV were among the top downloaded video streaming apps in the country.
Founded in 2020 by former Flipkart exec Saurabh Pandey, the Story TV platform has taken off in the last few years with a catalog of over 5,000 titles in six languages. Pandey told TechCrunch that because of the snackable content format, users log 95 minutes on the app on average through multiple sessions in a day.
“I fundamentally believe that the next billion users will probably not grow up on a diet of watching television; they will grow up on a diet of watching content on their phones, right? And this content has to be, and this entertainment, designed very differently. It’s not going to be appointment viewing. It’s going to be within certain slots throughout the day. And a lot of this was earlier solved for short clips, but serialized storytelling was never solved,” Pandey said about the microdrama format.
He believes that there still will be a place for big-screen viewing with family or friends, but the majority of entertainment consumption would be done through mobile.
All microdrama platforms compete against platforms like YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok, where creators are posting content for free. Some of them are also creating a way for creators to post serialized content. Pandey thinks that producing quality content on the platform will entice users to choose StoryTV over other free platforms. The company points to its partnerships, such as the one with Indian TV production company Balaji Telefilms, to produce content.
The company offers different kinds of subscriptions ranging from monthly, quarterly, and yearly to unlock content. It also offers some free content supported by ads, which might not be as lucrative a medium to make money as subscriptions, according to reports.
Monetization is a challenge in India, as users often stick around for free content, but few convert to paid users. A report from analyst firm Redseer indicates that more than 40 million people have paid for microdrama at least once, but only 15-17 million users pay for it on a monthly basis. A separate survey by Ormax Media suggested that 72% of people haven’t ever paid while consuming microdrama.
AI and other bets
All microdrama platforms want to have enough supply to engage different audiences and want to involve AI to solve that. Some platforms, like Google-backed Kuku, want to improve workflows and create more content, and some platforms like Dashverse’s Shortfree want to use video AI models to create serialized clips.
At the moment, StoryTV falls into the first camp with its Dolphin AI platform. Started as an internal tool to improve video creation, the company is now planning to make the tool widely available. It can act as an editor with templates and an array of models to create images, audio, and video, according to its website.
EloElo’s vision is to have people use this tool for marketing campaigns and ads as well. Notably, while Indian platforms like Pocket and Kuku have built AI tools and given them to creators, it is likely to accelerate their content pipeline. But at InVideo, there hasn’t been a scaled effort to provide a good alternative to CapCut or Instagram Edits to creators from India.
Pandey believes that human involvement is still paramount to producing good stories, and AI tools are still creative directors for steering.
“My belief in involving AI is that AI is a really fast race car where AI is the engine, but you need an extremely capable Formula One driver to be on the steering wheel. That, for me, is the creative director or the showrunner. AI is supposed to work with them, augmenting their skill set. AI can help write stories, but so far the best stories I have loved have all had a very high human x AI element to it,” he said.
Besides microdrama, the company also has a vertical video learning app, Master, competing with the likes of Seekho and Kuku’s Guru, and an AI companion app, Voxy AI. The company said that it has more than 40 million monthly users across its apps. While it didn’t bifurcate users by app, the majority of users belong to Story TV.
EloElo currently has 240 people and wants to hire to increase the size of its AI and machine learning research team. The company is also deploying a good chunk of its capital to produce more original titles.
MIT Investment Co., along with existing investors like Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures, and Griffin Gaming Partners, invested in the round.

articles.title: Google reveals new Gemini 4 Carbon AI model, narrowly beating Claude Opus 5.5 — frontier AI model is also the least likely to hallucinate, benchmarks claim
articles.text:
Google reveals new Gemini 4 Carbon AI model, narrowly beating Claude Opus 5.5 — frontier AI model is also the least likely to hallucinate, benchmarks claim
Tests now push models to reveal their greater weaknesses.
Last week, Google released its latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, topping intelligence rankings charts. The model has landed with a grander splash than most. As Artificial Analysis highlights, Gemini 4 Carbon is now the highest-ranked AI model on its latest Intelligence Index V5 benchmark suite, beating Claude Opus 5.5 by one point. It achieves the number one score across four of the nine evaluations, and does so at a lower cost per task than other high-ranking models, like Claude Opus 5.5. Google is offering access to the model for cyber defenders first through its Fairwind program, with wider availability coming sometime after.
Perhaps more crucially, Gemini 4 Carbon stands apart by topping Artificial Analysis' new AA-Omniscience v 1.1 test that tracks hallucinations and knowledgeable recall of information. As governments and institutions look to maximize value and security from their use of AI, being able to claim the lowest hallucination score could prove a significant selling point.
Then again, even the best scored only 54 on the -100 to +100 scale, suggesting even the best frontier models in 2026 are a far cry from being consistently reliable when it comes to accurately recalling information.
The king is dead, long live the king
AI model rankings change fast and regularly in 2026, and it's no surprise that the latest release from a frontier lab has pushed the envelope, but Google's Gemini 4 Carbon can be seen as a comeback after languishing with irregular releases for much of the year.
Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores a 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index V5 benchmark. That puts it a single point ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback), and two points ahead of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra (max). It's also nine points ahead of Meta's Muse Wonder Full (Max), and 10 points ahead of Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback).
But raw, generalized intelligence isn't the whole picture with frontier models in 2026. As developers chase the Pareto frontier— the best-possible confluence of cost and intelligence — Gemini 4 Carbon is also impressively affordable. Its cost per task on the Intelligence Index test is actually slightly cheaper than Gemini 3.8 Flash (high), priced at $7.76 each. That's several dollars cheaper than either Claude Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5, both max with fallback, and not far off half the price of Claude Fable 5.1, which costs $12.99 per task.
Gemini 4 Carbon is still more expensive than OpenAI's GPT 5 Astra and about six times more expensive than GPT 6.1 Sol (max). It's about 13 times as expensive per task as the open-weight DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, too, although that model measures a mere 32 on the Intelligence Index rankings.
Gemini 4 Carbon isn't the best at everything, but it may be the best at most of the high price points. At least for now. Arena.ai has it holding the top spot on its Pareto Frontier chart at the more expensive end of the spectrum, but at lower price points, the Chinese open-weight models like GLM 5.3-Flash and DeepSeek V4 Pro take over.
Artificial Analysis also highlights that Gemini 4 Carbon isn't as good as Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 at programming, and it falls behind Grok 4.7, Muse Wonder, and Kimi K3.1 Pro on knowledge work.
But perhaps the most impressive score is Gemini 4's 54 on the AA-Omniscience Index, which tracks knowledge and hallucinations, beating out the competition by often significant margins.
Careful and Compliant
In Google's announcement of the new Gemini 4 model, it talked up its collaboration with the U.S. government for model screening and pre-release testing. In a similar manner to the way Anthropic handled Mythos' release in 2025, Google is rolling out access to Gemini 4 Carbon at a slower pace.
"We're taking a deliberate approach to rollout and are actively engaged in the U.S. government’s voluntary process for pre-release model testing," Google's launch statement reads.
To that end, it's opening up Carbon to a subset of "cyber defenders," and will gradually make the model more widely available through trusted partners through its Fairwind Program. Before it makes Carbon available to developers, it wants to iterate on its guardrails to make the AI safer and more effective for cybersecurity purposes, making it harder for nefarious actors to use it for exploits and hacking.
Where the idea of slowing the industry and introducing greater oversight for model development has risen and fallen in the estimations of the major tech companies, it does appear to be cementing itself as more of a foundational idea for future model releases. Google talks up its release on the improved safety and security of its model, highlighting that it thwarted all attempts from the Gray Swan Indirect Prompt Injection benchmark to have it do something it shouldn't.
Google claims Carbon cuts unsupported claims in its responses twice as much as the Gemini 4 Argon model it debuted just two weeks ago. If it can't complete an action, it will just not do so, rather than fabricating an answer or hedging around missing evidence, Google claims.
It also suggests Carbon will present sources and suggested actions to the user more readily, rather than pursuing its own intentions when there are discrepancies or uncertainties, allegedly cutting model overreach by 26%.
As governments and companies look to make realistic use of AI, tracking usage, managing token budgets, and preventing workers from creating new exploit paths through overuse, a model's safety, security, and reliability will be paramount.
A new Pareto Frontier?
For the past year, a clear focus from frontier and open-weight model developers has been on efficiency and cost. While raising intelligence and improving capabilities, particularly through agentic workflows, has seen great development alongside pomp and circumstance, many of the major announcements and developments have also considered cost a clear component.
That's not likely to change, with the latest research from Gartner showing that just 3% of companies are actually achieving cost and productivity improvements from AI use. But as organizations push to find the real value in AI, maximize token budgets, and try to empower workers who have found improvements from using AI, they'll want consistency.
Tracking return on investment with AI is notoriously difficult, with hallucinations making that far harder. If Google can sell its latest model(s) as the safest and least likely to hallucinate, and do so with high intelligence at a relatively low cost, that might be the new winning formula.
At least until the next model drops.
Jon Martindale is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. For the past 20 years, he's been writing about PC components, emerging technologies, and the latest software advances. His deep and broad journalistic experience gives him unique insights into the most exciting technology trends of today and tomorrow.

articles.title: Joe Tsai, président d'Alibaba : “La seule façon pour l'Europe d'atteindre la souveraineté technologique est l'IA open source”
articles.text:
Pour le patron d'Alibaba, l'Europe ne sera souveraine en IA qu'avec l'open source
En pleine course à l'intelligence artificielle, Joe Tsai, président d'Alibaba, exhorte les entreprises européennes à héberger des modèles ouverts sur leurs propres serveurs plutôt que de s'en remettre aux API étasuniennes. Si la sécurité des données y gagnerait indéniablement, cette recette omet deux failles majeures.
Dans les grands laboratoires d'IA outre-Atlantique, 20 à 30 % des effectifs sont européens. Joe Tsai cite volontiers ce chiffre, ressorti le 7 octobre dernier à Turin lors de la conférence Wave by Vento. Pour le cofondateur d'Alibaba, le retard technologique du Vieux Continent “n’est pas un problème de talents”.
Souveraineté des données : l'open source comme unique issue pour l'Europe ?
À l'entendre, ce qui manque à notre continent est la puissance de calcul. Sa solution se veut dès lors limpide : “L’open source est l'opportunité de l’Europe.” Concrètement, un industriel pourrait télécharger un modèle ouvert, l'entraîner sur ses propres données et l'exécuter sur son infrastructure privée, évitant ainsi que ses informations ne transitent par l'API fermée d'un géant technologique. Joe Tsai voit dans cette approche “la seule voie à suivre”, ajoutant qu'aucun pays ne devrait se fier entièrement à la technologie d'un autre, qu’elle soit américaine ou chinoise.
Sur le front de la sécurité des données, l'argument porte. Une fois téléchargés, les poids d'un modèle ne peuvent plus être modifiés ou retirés à distance, et les informations sensibles restent confinées au sein de l'entreprise. Un accès par API dépend à l'inverse du bon vouloir du fournisseur et de la géopolitique de son gouvernement. Anthropic en a fait l'amère expérience en juin, lorsque la société a dû suspendre l'accès à Fable 5 et Mythos 5 pour se conformer à des contrôles étasuniens à l'exportation (finalement levés à la fin du mois).
Modèles ouverts Qwen : le conseil très intéressé d'Alibaba
Le conseiller prêche toutefois pour sa paroisse. Alibaba développe en effet Qwen, l'une des familles de modèles ouverts les plus populaires du marché. D'après Xataka, les poids de Qwen3.8 ont été libérés en août avec une version phare frôlant les 2400 milliards de paramètres et une déclinaison plus frugale de 27 milliards sous licence Apache 2.0. Distribuer gratuitement ses modèles fait mécaniquement exploser la demande en hébergement, or Alibaba Cloud a justement inauguré de nouveaux centres de données en France en juin dernier.
Pour une entreprise européenne, basculer sur des IA chinoises reviendrait avant tout à troquer une dépendance contre une autre. Si les poids sont publics, les données d'entraînement demeurent opaques et les choix d'alignement ont été dictés ailleurs. Pour les itérations futures, tout dépendra du fournisseur, libre de fermer ses licences ou de réserver ses modèles les plus performants à ses propres services. Dans un rapport publié en septembre, Mozilla dresse d'ailleurs un constat sans appel : la Chine domine déjà le terrain de l'IA open source.
Côté européen, Mistral reste fort heureusement dans la partie. La pépite française a dévoilé le 6 octobre Large 4, un mastodonte d'environ 1000 milliards de paramètres dont les poids devraient être publiés à la fin du mois.
Infrastructures et puces : le goulet d'étranglement du calcul européen
Joe Tsai le concède volontiers, l'Europe doit “vraiment se mettre sérieusement” à bâtir l'infrastructure matérielle de calcul adéquate. Faire tourner un modèle de plusieurs centaines de milliards de paramètres exige des grappes entières de processeurs graphiques, un luxe que peu d'entreprises possèdent. À ce jour, la Chine et les États-Unis contrôleraient environ 90 % de la capacité mondiale de calcul dédiée à l'IA.
	
Le vrai problème persiste néanmoins : les puces qui équiperont ces fermes resteront en immense majorité nord-américaines
Bruxelles tente de combler ce gouffre avec le réseau EuroHPC, qui supervise déjà 19 usines d'IA. Un appel à projets lancé fin juillet vise la création de sept gigafactories pour lesquelles 10 milliards d'euros de fonds publics devront attirer au moins 20 milliards d'investissements privés. Les candidatures se clôturent le 12 novembre pour une sélection attendue début 2027. Le vrai problème persiste néanmoins : les puces qui équiperont ces fermes resteront en immense majorité nord-américaines. Arthur Mensch, patron de Mistral, estime d'ailleurs que l'Europe ne dispose plus que de deux ans pour bâtir son indépendance.
Le cadre juridique recèle enfin ses propres zones grises. L'AI Act allège certes la documentation exigée pour les modèles véritablement ouverts, sauf s'ils franchissent le seuil de risque systémique. Toutefois, une entreprise qui branche un modèle ouvert sur un usage à haut risque, recrutement ou crédit par exemple, assume seule la conformité de son système.

articles.title: EloElo Group raises $80M in Series C led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal
articles.text:
EloElo Group raises $80M in Series C led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal
EloElo Group will use the funds to launch original content across local languages, expand into international markets and develop AI platforms.
EloElo Group, a consumer AI and entertainment company that operates micro-drama platform Story TV, has raised $80 million in a Series C round of funding led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal.
This funding round also saw participation from MIT Investment Co. and existing investors Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners and others.
The funding was done at a valuation of $500 million, which is almost a 5X jump from its previous fundraise in April 2025, sources indicated. The new round brings EloElo Group’s total capital raised to $130 million to date.
Bengaluru-headquartered EloElo Group was founded in 2020 by former Flipkart executive Saurabh Pandey and it will use this latest fund raise to fund original content across local languages, launch its micro dramas internationally, and continue investments in Dolphin AI, its proprietary agentic platform.
In an interaction with YourStory, EloElo Group Founder & CEO Saurabh Pandey said, “This funding will expand on our vision and usher in a new era of sorts of mobile entertainment. This entertainment in the form of storytelling has never been solved for the mobile phone.”
Story TV has over 5,000 micro dramas in six languages, a new drama launched every three hours and 95 minutes of time spent per user every day. The group also runs Master (micro learning), Dolphin AI (its agentic AI creative suite) and Voxy AI (an AI companion agent).
Across its apps, EloElo Group has over 40 million monthly active users.
“Story TV shows us what India wants to watch, and Dolphin AI gives us the economics to make it, which is how we have scaled with solid unit economics. Consumer AI will change how content is created, distributed and consumed, and we intend to lead that shift from India,” Pandey remarked.
According to the founder, EloElo Group's key strength has been its ownership across all three layers of mobile entertainment: creating content, distributing content and imbibing AI into the whole process.
This fundraise also gives EloElo Group the ability to go deeper into various languages through a combination of live action shows, hybrid shows with AI, and pure AI shows. These will be original content.
On the investment, Manoj Thakur, Founder and Managing Partner of Hornbill Capital said, “EloElo Group combines strong creative capabilities with the ability to scale content through technology, which is something we deeply believe in. The team’s execution, financial discipline, and AI capabilities position it well for its next phase of growth.”
Micro dramas are among the fastest-growing formats in global entertainment. According to Omdia, the industry will generate $14 billion globally by the end of 2026. In India, Redseer estimates that 40 million people paid for a microdrama at least once in FY26, and Lumikai’s State of India Interactive Media Report projects the market will reach $4.5 billion by 2030.

articles.title: El túnel de la A-5 de Madrid ya tiene fecha de fin: los coches circularán bajo la autovía a partir de diciembre
articles.text:
Tras más de dos años de obras, el túnel de la A-5 en Madrid está dando sus últimos coletazos. Y es que según el alcalde José Luis Martínez-Almeida, a partir del próximo 23 de diciembre los conductores podrán pasar por el propio túnel, dando por finalizada una gran parte del proyecto para renovar toda la zona. Lo curioso es que el calendario apuntaba a 2027 como fecha de finalización, pero el ritmo ha sido mucho mayor del esperado.
Qué nos podemos encontrar. El túnel cubrirá aproximadamente tres kilómetros dentro de un tramo de 3,2 kilómetros entre la avenida de Portugal y la calle Padre Piquer, según cuentan desde Madrid Informa. Tendrá tres carriles en cada dirección, divididos en dos galerías independientes. Por otro lado, el medio El Economista informa que los carriles más cercanos a la mediana funcionarán como carriles bus-VAO, con señalización variable para que su uso pueda ajustarse a la demanda de tráfico.
En qué punto están las obras. La excavación de ambos túneles finalizó en mayo y las obras civiles concluyeron a finales de agosto, tal y como comparten desde Madrid Informa. Las cuadrillas trabajan ahora en los revestimientos, la iluminación, la ventilación y los trabajos de acabado. El Ayuntamiento de Madrid ha situado la inversión en esta primera fase en 410 millones de euros, según comparte El Economista.
El último obstáculo. El túnel todavía debe conectarse con los túneles de la M-30 bajo la avenida de Portugal. Y es que según Madrid Informa, esto requerirá el corte total de la A-5 en ambos sentidos y la demolición de las rampas de entrada y salida restantes. Es un “punto de no retorno”, según el propio Ayuntamiento, ya que una vez eliminadas las rampas, el tráfico dejará de fluir por la superficie y la próxima reapertura llegará cuando el túnel esté terminado.
Fechas de corte. Todavía no se han fijado, y Almeida reconoce que las molestias serán "significativas", así que el Consistorio está buscando el momento en el que se generen menos inconvenientes, según cuentan desde ABC. Según El Economista los cortes se prevén en las primeras semanas de diciembre, cuando el tráfico disminuya de cara a las Navidades y durante el puente, pero aún no se han especificado de forma oficial.
Plan mientras se ejecutan las obras. Desde 20 Minutos señalan que el ayuntamiento se está reuniendo con el Consorcio Regional de Transportes, la empresa municipal de autobuses EMT y los equipos de tráfico y cercanías de la ciudad. Entre las opciones se incluye desviar parte del tráfico hacia la M-40 y aumentar los autobuses de la EMT, el metro y los servicios interurbanos. El ayuntamiento también planea pedir a Renfe que refuerce la línea C-5 de cercanías, que conecta varias localidades del suroeste con la capital. Mientras finalizan las obras se espera que la avenida de Portugal y sus alrededores sean especialmente sensibles.
Acaba el túnel, pero no todo el proyecto. El Paseo Verde del Suroeste, el parque en superficie que sustituirá a la autovía, aún está por construir. Desde El Economista detallan que un consorcio formado por Sarrión, Cyopsa y Becsa ofertó 56,57 millones de euros (46,76 millones antes de IVA) para los trabajos, con un plazo de ejecución de 18 meses, así que se espera que terminen las obras para el primer trimestre de 2028.
Beneficios. Según Madrid Informa, el proyecto recuperará más de 100.000 metros cuadrados y creará un corredor de 3,2 kilómetros que conectará Madrid Río, la Casa de Campo y la Cuña Verde en Latina. Incluye 33 pasos de peatones y un carril bici de unos 3,5 kilómetros. El ayuntamiento pretende reducir el tráfico en superficie hasta en un 90 %, soterrando gran parte de los aproximadamente 80.000 vehículos que utilizan el corredor cada día. Además se unirán los barrios de Lucero, Aluche, Las Águilas y Campamento, que llevan divididos por la autovía desde 1968.
Hay razones de peso para querer que el proyecto estrella de Almeida se complete antes de tiempo, entre ellas las elecciones autonómicas y municipales previstas para mayo de 2027, como bien apuntan desde El Confidencial.

articles.title: What does "Wi-Fi" stand for?
articles.text:
Here's the story behind it
Wi-Fi: the name that never stood for anything
Millions of people and even plenty of tech textbooks will tell you that Wi-Fi is short for "Wireless Fidelity." It isn't. Wi-Fi is not an acronym, and the name doesn't mean anything at all.
The story starts in the late 1990s. The IEEE published the 802.11 wireless networking standard in 1997, and the faster 802.11b revision was finalized in 1999, which topped out at 11 Mbps on the 2.4 GHz band.
The tech worked, but nobody was going to ask for "IEEE 802.11b" compatibility at a store. That's when the Wireless Ethernet Compatibility Alliance (WECA) started to look for something consumers could remember, so in 1999 they hired branding agency Interbrand.
Interbrand is known for coming up with commercial names like Prozac, Nintendo "Wii," and Compaq. It pitched a shortlist of 10 candidates, and the alliance picked "Wi-Fi," a deliberate play on "Hi-Fi," the decades-old shorthand for high-fidelity audio. The name carried the right associations of quality and ease, without describing anything technical. Interbrand also designed the yin-yang style Wi-Fi logo.
But what about the "Wireless Fidelity" confusion?
Early on, some alliance board members worried that a name with no meaning would confuse people, so they attached a tagline: "The Standard for Wireless Fidelity."
According to Phil Belanger, a founding member of the alliance, the tagline appeared on everything for roughly a year. He later called it a mistake that diluted the brand, and said that the phrase doesn't hold up if you take it apart. His summary of the name was blunt: "Wi-Fi doesn't stand for anything." The tagline was dropped, but the damage was done, and it's now one of the most persistent false backronyms in tech.

articles.title: Tesla's Full Self-Driving is dead in the UK and Europe after legislators force rebrand — but BMW says its rival tech is coming in 2027
articles.text:
Tesla forced to rename 'misleading' Full Self-Driving technology in the UK and Europe — as BMW readies its own automated driving rival for 2027
FSD is now ‘Tesla Assisted Driving’ in Europe
- The European Transport Safety Council said Tesla offered to change the name of its tech
- Germany’s transport ministry claimed Full Self-Driving was misleading
- BMW aims to pile on the pressure with its own automated driving tech next year
Following intervention from Germany’s transport ministry, Tesla has agreed to formally change the name of its Full Self-Driving (FSD) partially automated driving technology to ‘Tesla Assisted Driving’ in Europe and the UK.
The move came after Germany’s Transport Minister, Steffen Bilger, aimed to legalize Tesla’s advanced driver assistance systems as quickly as possible, but went on to explain that the name was “somewhat misleading”.
“It is a driver assistance system that can support certain driving tasks such as accelerating, braking and steering. However, the driver must remain attentive at all times,” a statement read.
As a result, Tesla agreed to change the name of the technology to appease European lawmakers, with Tesla Assisted Driving suggested and subsequently agreed on by all involved.
The new name has now been added to Tesla websites in Europe, including the UK site.
It comes as many governments move to tighten the rules around the marketing of assisted driving systems, according to Fleet News.
In the UK, for example, the terms automated, automated driving, autonomous, autonomous driving, drive autonomously, drive itself, driverless, and self-driving will only be reserved for authorized or listed vehicles, such as fully self-driving taxis.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The UK’s Department for Transport released a statement that said that under the 2024 Automated Vehicles act, which is expected to come into force on January 7, 2027, a vehicle only meets the self-driving test if it “does not need to be monitored or controlled by an individual”.
BMW readies its Symbiotic Drive technology
The German automotive giant announced this week that it will expand its urban driver assistance functions in Germany early next year.
A suite of navigation-guided driver assistance functions, under the umbrella title Symbiotic Drive, will provide support from the motorway, through the countryside and into the city, BMW claims.
The SAE Level 2 technology will able to handle turning and right-of-way situations, urban lane changes and navigating roundabouts using the vehicles in-built satellite navigation system.
Unlike other advanced driver assistance systems, BMW says its technology is designed to work seamlessly with the driver, so they can intervene, accelerate, brake and steer without completely shutting off the system.
Lane changes are also handled in an innovative way, with interior, gaze-monitoring cameras detecting a driver’s intention to swap lanes and the steering wheel detecting inputs before the system autonomously executes the maneuver.
BMW says that the system only provides assistance in the form of a “warning and steering intervention” if the driver is actually unintentionally drifting out of their own lane or if the system detects an imminent collision.
However, the company reiterates that Symbiotic Drive is a Level 2 system, so requires a driver to pay attention and be ready to take over whenever the technology requires.
It will be available on iX3, iX4, all models in the 3 Series, 7 Series and X5 range in Germany to begin with, but further countries will soon follow.
The German marque says the hardware is already in place in the majority of circumstances and that BMW Symbiotic Drive will be delivered as an over-the-air software update.

articles.title: Snowflake expands agentic AI platform with business context and governance tools - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Snowflake expands agentic AI platform with business context and governance tools
Snowflake Inc. today announced a sweeping collection of artificial intelligence capabilities designed to bring business context, governance and autonomous development into the same environment, as enterprises increasingly hand over software engineering and everyday operations to AI agents.
The announcements, during the company’s Expedition 2026 virtual conference, include a new Business Ontology framework, expanded agent governance through Cortex AI Gateway, and autonomous data engineering capabilities that allow AI agents to build, monitor and troubleshoot data pipelines with less human intervention.
The company is betting that more coders and engineers will use AI throughout the software development lifecycle as creation moves even faster, while other back-end departments begin to adopt agents in their day-to-day work. For example, sales operations are creating agents that can analyze sales risks and prepare customer outreach without writing code.
“AI is industrializing software creation. Actually, it’s industrializing intelligence,” Chief Executive Sridhar Ramaswamy said. “What once took months can now take hours, days, or even minutes.”
Ramaswamy noted that while AI is changing the economics of software development, as agents take over tasks usually relegated to specialized developers, business users become developers. This is changing the competitive landscape, meaning that the advantage no longer goes to specialists, but to proprietary knowledge.
Snowflake is taking the field by helping ordinary AI models understand and contextualize that business knowledge. It does this with Business Ontology, an extension of its existing semantic views that lets organizations establish approved definitions used across the organization. Without a standard definition, two agents could respond to the same business-related question with incompatible answers, even when both agents have accurate underlying data.
Using information from Business Ontology, Snowflake CoCo, the coding agent for data teams, and Snowflake CoWork, the personal work agent for knowledge workers, use these approved business concepts to ground their responses.
This new feature is currently in private preview, but is headed to public preview soon.
Governing agents like employees
Cortex AI Gateway arrives to become a single front door for agents within an organization. It is not entirely new; Snowflake introduced it in July 2026 as a centralized way to govern and monitor agents.
Today’s announcement expands its capabilities rather than introducing the gateway for the first time. The new updates include agent abuse detection, observability and tracing, Cortex sandboxes, AI cost governance, dynamic model routing and tools integration using technology from Snowflake’s Natoma acquisition.
“An agent that acts on your business has to be trusted, and it has to know three important things: what the data means, which data to trust, and what it’s allowed to do,” said Ramaswamy.
The platform most importantly applies existing security mechanisms, including data masking and access restrictions, to agent-driven operations while adding capabilities to monitor activity, detect potential abuse and maintain records of what agents do. The information technology and security teams can also apply cost controls, select models based on efficiency or accuracy and restrict which external tools agents can access granularly.
The underlying role of this governance, control and transparency is aligned with giving agents the same sort of role observation granted to employees. Treating them similarly in terms of autonomy.
Snowflake’s push comes amid a broader industry race to establish the control layer for enterprise AI agents. SAP has been expanding its Autonomous Enterprise architecture and governed Joule agents, while Salesforce has introduced its Enterprise AI Harness and AI Control Plane to secure autonomous workflows. Snowflake is approaching the same problem from the data platform side, seeking to become the foundation through which agents access trusted business information and operate under enterprise policies.
Training smaller models for specialized tasks
Snowflake also announced the public preview of Cortex Training, which will allow customers to tailor open-weight AI models with their own proprietary information.
The service is designed to make it simpler to create specialized models using post-training without needing vast arrays of graphics processing units. Snowflake lets them train models without managing the underlying infrastructure.
“Specialized, smaller models that come with more efficient responses, faster responses, and frequently cost benefits in terms of tokens,” Executive Vice President of Product Christian Kleinerman said.
Many enterprise companies will require sovereign control of their own AI models as increasing restrictions on foreign open-weight AI or regulations on handling sensitive information. It’s easier to audit what passes through an AI model on your own hardware than in a third-party vendor’s cloud.
Separately, Snowflake announced an expanded partnership with Oracle Corp. to make its platform available as a first-party service on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. The integration will give customers easier access to Snowflake’s analytics and AI capabilities while allowing them to work directly through Oracle databases and applications.
