I think it's pretty bad timing with the new RAM prices but I want enough RAM that I can put the entire OS on a recoverable RAM drive - like I used to do back when Windoze was smaller and RAM was cheaper. :D So Faaaaaaaast!
I'm under the impression the OS itself is fine. It also runs in a default configuration that must run on millions and millions of PCs out of the box. So I expect it to run a little fatter than spending time tuning the system settings for my use case.
It's all the userland applications that make me face palm. Web browsers are multi-gigabyte behemoths. A plaintext editor eats more RAM than Doom 3 or Half-Life 2. This is where we've painted ourselves.
Modern NT kernel memory management operates on the principle that "free RAM is wasted RAM." Having 6GB of an 8GB pool occupied by cached file mapping and pre-fetched binaries (SysMain) is actually desirable, because dropping a standby page when an active process requests memory takes mere nanoseconds in the page fault handler.
Where 8GB machines actually struggle under Windows 11 isn't cache allocation—it's working set pressure and memory compression overhead:
- Compression Pool CPU Cycles: When commit charge approaches physical limits, the kernel's Memory Compression process compresses cold private pages into an in-RAM zram-like pool. On an 8-core desktop this is transparent, but on dual-core / quad-core budget laptop SoCs, the compression/decompression threads fight user workloads for CPU time.
- I/O Thrashing on DRAM-less NVMe: Once the compressed store is full and Windows is forced to trim working sets into [ICODE]pagefile.sys[/ICODE], budget laptops equipped with DRAM-less QLC drives hit massive queue depth spikes. A hard page fault fetching a 64KB page cluster from a slow QLC drive introduces 15–50ms latency bubbles, which is what users perceive as UI hitching.
If Microsoft's latest scheduler optimizations truly refine heuristic working-set decay without causing premature page-out churn on background browser tabs, that's a genuine architectural win for budget hardware.

articles.title: Ted Schlein's Ballistic Ventures seeks $490M for new funds amid AI-driven cybersecurity boom | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ballistic Ventures, the cybersecurity-focused venture capital firm co-founded by former Kleiner Perkins partner Ted Schlein (pictured above, second from the right), is seeking to raise $490 million across two new funds, TechCrunch has learned through regulatory filings.
The San Francisco-based VC firm filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission this week to raise $360 million for its third flagship fund, matching the size of its previous fund raised in 2024, and another $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund B. Neither fund had recorded any sales at the time of filing.
The fundraising plans come as the growing use of artificial intelligence has raised concerns about more sophisticated cyberattacks. The rise of AI agents has also created new opportunities for cybersecurity startups and the venture capital firms backing them.
Founded in late 2021, Ballistic Ventures’ founding team includes Schlein, former AT&T Cybersecurity president Barmak Meftah, and Roger Thornton, who co-founded security companies Fortify Software and AlienVault. The firm has backed companies, including Talon Cyber Security, acquired by Palo Alto Networks, and Pangea, bought by CrowdStrike, alongside startups such as Armadin, GetReal, Nudge Security, and Oligo Security.
Ballistic’s ties to storied venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins, where Schlein spent more than two decades, help set it apart from rivals, a cybersecurity investor at another VC firm told TechCrunch. Its investment strategy, however, is similar to those of other cybersecurity-focused investors, including Forgepoint Capital and Ten Eleven Ventures, the person said.
In 2022, Ballistic announced its $300 million debut fund and raised another $360 million for its second flagship fund two years later. It also raised about $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund A, per PitchBook data. The new Fund B is targeting a similar amount.
U.S. cybersecurity startups raised $11.5 billion in 2025, the highest since 2022, a recent report by JPMorgan Chase said, citing PitchBook data. AI-enabled companies accounted for about 72% of U.S. cybersecurity venture deals through May this year, compared with 36% in 2019, the report said.
Separately, Microsoft, in its annual Digital Defense Report released last month, warned that hackers are increasingly using AI for activities ranging from phishing and social engineering to malware development. The technology is allowing attackers to operate faster and at greater scale, even as many of their underlying techniques remain unchanged.
Ballistic Ventures declined to comment on its fundraising plans.

articles.title: Groenlandia se convierte en la pieza clave del internet europeo: Bruselas planea un cable submarino que esquive a EEUU
articles.text:
Bruselas quiere tender un cable submarino de internet que conecte Groenlandia directamente con la Unión Europea. Y la cosa no acaba solo ahí, sino que también hay planes para ampliarlo a través de Canadá hasta Japón y Corea del Sur. El proyecto, llamado Cable Panártico y publicado por la Comisión Europea, es una de las ambiciones estratégicas de la UE en el Ártico, y una vía del continente para fortificarse en materia de seguridad.
Por qué importa. Por los cables submarinos básicamente viaja más del 99 % del tráfico de internet en todo el mundo, desde transacciones financieras a servicios en la nube, comunicaciones y mucho más. Y ahora que la exposición de Europa está creciendo en varios frentes, la UE quiere tomar medidas.
La mayor parte del tráfico entre Europa y Asia pasa por el mar Rojo, donde los ataques de los hutíes a la navegación han aumentado el riesgo de mantener los cables allí. El mar Báltico ha visto cómo los barcos arrastraban anclas y cortaban cables. Y la relación con Washington se ha vuelto más tensa, lo que hace que la dependencia de la infraestructura controlada por EEUU sea menos cómoda.
En detalle. La estrategia respalda “una conexión de cable submarino soberana, segura y resiliente que enlace Groenlandia directamente con la UE”, según el documento de la Comisión. La UE ya ha destinado 107 millones de euros a la conectividad de Groenlandia, afirma el propio organismo. El proyecto surgió de un acuerdo de 2025 entre empresas europeas, organismos de investigación y un operador de telecomunicaciones de Groenlandia, y ahora se espera que reciba apoyo además través del programa “Conectar Europa”.
El plan también incluye un centro de cables del Ártico, que estaría abierto a los miembros de la UE, Noruega e Islandia, y que supervisaría y protegería los cables en el Atlántico Norte y el Ártico, ayudando a repararlos. Bruselas también afirma que financiará cables con “tecnologías inteligentes” que funcionen como sistemas de alerta temprana.
Geopolítica más que comercial. Elisabeth Braw, investigadora del Atlantic Council, declaraba al medio Ars Technica que la geopolítica “no desempeñó prácticamente ningún papel” en décadas pasadas, y que deberíamos esperar más cables que conecten a países amigos evitando al mismo tiempo las aguas de los no amigos. También añade que hace cinco años el proyecto de Groenlandia no habría resultado comercialmente atractivo.
El papel de Groenlandia también es político. La estrategia de la UE llega semanas después de que EEUU, Dinamarca y Groenlandia firmaran un acuerdo de seguridad para mantener la autonomía de Groenlandia dentro de Dinamarca, a la vez que se amplía el acceso militar de Estados Unidos. Jo Inge Bekkevold, del Instituto Noruego de Estudios de Defensa, declaraba a Nikkei Asia que la estrategia parece centrarse más en construir lazos con Groenlandia, en respuesta a la política estadounidense, que en contrarrestar a China. El medio declara que China solo aparece una vez en el documento.
Los obstáculos. Según Euronews, el texto no fija ninguna ruta definitiva, presupuesto o calendario de construcción, y no dice quién pagará, poseerá u operará el cable. Trabajar en aguas árticas también requiere barcos especializados. Desde el medio se informa además que la propuesta menciona incluso la energía nuclear como forma de propulsar la iniciativa ante las condiciones extremas de la región.
El enlace a Asia. Juha Saunavaara, de la Universidad de Hokkaido, cuenta a Nikkei Asia que Tokio trata la construcción de cables como un asunto del sector privado, y que conseguir la participación pública allí ha sido difícil. También señala que las inversiones de Japón en proyectos de hidrocarburos rusos podrían complicar la cooperación.
El medio informa además de que Polar Connect, liderado por instituciones de investigación nórdicas, pretende conectar el norte de Europa con Japón y Corea del Sur para 2031, y que el proyecto comercial Far North Fiber también está estudiando rutas. Por otro lado, Bloomberg cuenta que la noruega Bulk Infrastructure ya está buscando socios para un cable entre Europa y Canadá llamado Leif Erikson.

articles.title: Why best consumer brands are built on everyday habits, not one-time marketing campaign
articles.text:
Why best consumer brands are built on everyday habits, not one-time marketing campaign
For consumer brands, getting customers to try a product is only the first hurdle. The bigger challenge is getting them to return, particularly in a market where choices are abundant.
Acquiring a customer may take a marketing campaign, but retaining one requires a product that becomes indispensable. At YourStory's Techsparks 2026, Sangeeth Krishna, founder, BRÜK and Nikhil Khurana, co founder of Qubo explained why design, reliability and an obsession with consumer behaviour are key to building lasting brands.
A security camera that lets parents check on their children, or an air purifier that quietly becomes part of a household routine. These products may serve very different needs, but they have one thing in common: their success depends on becoming part of consumers' everyday lives.
For consumer brands, getting customers to try a product is only the first hurdle. The bigger challenge is getting them to return, particularly in a market where choices are abundant, competing products are easily accessible and new brands are constantly emerging.
For Nikhil Khurana, Co-founder of smart devices maker Qubo, the transition from a product being used regularly to becoming a habit is not necessarily reflected in usage metrics alone. "Real product-market fit happens once you've hit those hygiene usage metrics. If you speak to consumers, are they using superlatives? Are they saying things like, 'I can't live without this now'? That is when you realise you have probably hit product-market fit," he said.
The absence of a product, he believes, is often the best indicator of whether it has become a habit.
"A habit is not defined by usage metrics. A habit is defined by how much anxiety it causes you in its absence," said Khurana, drawing a parallel with quick-commerce and food-delivery platforms that consumers increasingly depend on.
Designing for everyday use
Krishna of BRÜK saw that the opportunity in the drinkware market came from observing an emerging consumer trend. He noticed people matching their tumblers with their clothes and bags, much like they did with other lifestyle accessories.
He also saw a gap in the Indian market for premium drinkware with better finishing and build quality. The idea was to create a product that combined functionality with aesthetics, offering consumers an alternative in a category dominated by established players.
BRÜK’s product development focused on everyday convenience, particularly for people working in offices. "These are the small things we were very clear about. It has to be convenient for people to hold, carry and use," he said.
The broader principle is that a product must solve a real consumer problem before a brand can expect it to become a daily-use item.
Qubo's experience in the home-security category offers another example. Khurana said consumers are generally reluctant to experiment with security products because the consequences of a failure could be significant.
"All you need to do is a good job. Provide a reliable service that consumers can depend on," he said. For Qubo, consistent performance and reliability are central to building trust, particularly in categories where consumers are unlikely to switch brands easily once that trust has been established.
Why retention cannot be a marketing function
With customer acquisition becoming increasingly expensive, brands often look at features, incentives and performance marketing to drive repeat usage. But Khurana believes retention should primarily be a consequence of the product's usefulness.
"Marketing can only help you with acquisition, make users try for the first time. The product is responsible for making users come back and use it every day," he said. He cautioned against relying excessively on incentives such as streaks, points and cashback to bring customers back to a platform. Instead, brands should work backwards from consumer needs and build products that naturally encourage repeat usage.
Beyond the first purchase
For brands selling durable products such as tumblers, repeat purchases present a different challenge. Unlike consumables, customers are unlikely to replace their drinkware every few weeks or months.
Besides expanding its product range, BRÜK is also exploring adjacent product categories such as lunchboxes and protein shakers, building on its understanding of consumers' everyday routines. Adding to this, Krishna said founders need to constantly observe how consumers use products, including how they adapt them beyond their original purpose. He pointed to the accessories people add to their tumblers and the different bottles they carry to offices and gyms as examples of opportunities that can emerge from everyday observations.
"If you observe a person from morning to evening, you will get ideas. There is nothing magical about it. Just go around and observe," he said.
Premium pricing needs product value
Another challenge for emerging consumer brands is convincing customers to pay a premium when cheaper alternatives and established brands are already available.
Khurana outlined two possible approaches: competing with established brands on the strength of a differentiated offering, or disrupting the market by providing comparable capabilities at a lower price through operational efficiencies.
As a brand gains consumer trust, it can gradually move away from an initial penetration-pricing strategy and improve margins.
"People are ready to pay if you have a quality product. The most important things are the build, the quality, the materials and the finish," said Krishna. For him, compromising on price simply to chase volumes is not necessarily the right strategy. A smaller but clearly defined customer base willing to pay for the product can be more valuable.
Ultimately, building a lasting consumer brand requires more than visibility or an aggressive acquisition strategy. In a crowded consumer market, that may be the strongest competitive advantage a brand can build.

articles.title: Exclusive: Cogent Security’s VR-1.1 model outscores Claude Code and Codex on vulnerability repair - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Cogent Security’s VR-1.1 model outscores Claude Code and Codex on vulnerability repair
Vulnerability management startup Cogent Security Inc. today released VR-1.1, a new version of its frontier reasoning model that writes fixes for newly disclosed software vulnerabilities.
On a public repair benchmark, the model outscored Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code and OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex.
The release goes after the part of vulnerability management that has not sped up. In July, research group Epoch Artificial Intelligence Inc. counted about 2,500 high- and critical-severity disclosures from major organizations, roughly five times the monthly record set before Anthropic announced Claude Mythos Preview in April.
Each repair still needs an engineer who understands the flaw well enough to change the code without breaking something else. Co-founder and Chief Executive Vineet Edupuganti called that stage “where security teams are stuck.”
To test the model on that repair work, Cogent turned to LiveCVEBench. Researchers at Harbin Institute of Technology and Kuaishou Technology built the benchmark from vulnerabilities disclosed in recent months and add new ones regularly. VR-1.1 produced a working repair for 57.9% of the benchmark’s 190 tasks. Claude Code and Codex tied at 45.3%.
Each task drops an agent into a real development environment with a vulnerability report and the affected codebase, in one of 14 programming languages. To pass, a patch has to close the vulnerability without breaking the software, which the benchmark checks with separate security and functionality tests.
Cogent blocked outbound network access during repairs and hid the grading tests until each agent was done. Inference budgets differed across the three systems, according to the full methodology Cogent Research has published.
Where the environment allows, VR-1.1 starts by writing its own proof of concept that triggers the reported flaw. From there the model follows the vulnerability through the affected code, including related paths that share the same weakness. The fix itself stays small, for example checking an index before use.
Every patch goes to a separate review that starts from a fresh context and hunts for a way around the fix. New bugs introduced by the change are part of that check. The model also leaves behind regression tests, which fail if a later code change reopens the flaw. When an attempt fails, the diagnosis and failure details carry into the next try.
“A patch might block the exact payload from a bug report, but leave the same vulnerability open via a different endpoint or break core functionality for users,” said Geng Sng, co-founder and chief technology officer of Cogent. “We designed VR-1.1 to check its own work for both problems before it finishes.”
Cogent introduced VR-1 in July to find and prove the attack paths an adversary could reach inside an enterprise. The new release extends the remediation capabilities that model introduced.
Founded in 2025, the company sells artificial intelligence agents that detect and fix vulnerabilities, with customers choosing whether a human signs off on each change. According to Cogent, Fortune 500 users have cut the exposure window for critical vulnerabilities by 97%.
Greylock Partners backed its $11 million launch round in July 2025, and Bain Capital Ventures led the $42 million Series A in February that took total funding to $53 million.

articles.title: Engineer creates retro FPGA Game Boy console that can rip your cartridges to an SD card natively — features HDMI, USB-C, and even has Game Link Cable support
articles.text:
Engineer creates retro FPGA Game Boy console that can rip your cartridges to an SD card natively — features HDMI, USB-C, and even has Game Link Cable support
The project was nearly abandoned until a supportive retro enthusiast financed the equipment needed to bring it to life.
Joining the retro console revival movement is the SGBC, a new console that can play Nintendo Game Boy cartridges natively using an FPGA core. Built by Thomas Sanfourche, a French electronics engineer studying in Taiwan, the SGBC aims to give players a way to preserve and play their games with the full Game Boy experience, including a link port for multiplayer and trading.
The SGBC uses a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), a reprogrammable chip that can be configured to replicate the hardware logic of another chip, in this case, the Game Boy’s hardware. It can replicate not just the CPU, but multiple other components of a Game Boy as well, but Sanfourche has yet to specify which of the original Game Boy’s ICs have been consolidated into the FPGA.
The SGBC doesn’t just replicate the Game Boy as a console; it has plenty of features that retro gamers would appreciate — the most interesting among them being the built-in cartridge ripping function. If you insert your favorite Game Boy cartridge into the SGBC’s slot, you can preserve it by copying the ROM onto the microSD card in the console, digitizing your collection. It also outputs in 1080p 16:9 without stretching, and uses integer scaling to keep the game's pixels aligned with the pixels on your monitor or TV through HDMI. The SGBC also features an SNES controller port and a Game Boy Link port for multiplayer and trading.
Thomas Sanfourche almost ditched the SGBC entirely; in an interview with French retro gaming YouTuber GyuGyu, he said he went to Taiwan to study electronics engineering after discovering his strong interest in electronics. He didn’t know the local language and couldn’t enrol without certification, so he gave himself two years but ended up getting the language certification in six months. In his second year, he chose to enrol in the FPGA course after being intrigued by the name, and eventually chose it as the subject of his final-year project — a Game Boy FPGA core.
Sanfourche said his project was dismissed when he presented it to his professors: “What’s the point of doing this on an FPGA?” he was asked. This discouraged him and stopped him from working on it — until one day he went to a warehouse to buy a PVM monitor and struck up a conversation with a fellow customer who was a retro product seller and very active in the local retro scene. The discussion eventually led to his FPGA core Game Boy project, to which the seller asked, “Why don’t you market it?” The supportive stranger then offered, on the spot, to finance the equipment needed to market it or at least bring the project to life. The financier told Sanfourche he doesn’t want to be a part of the business, but that he wants to resell the product when he releases it, further supporting the project by sharing updates and teasers to local retro enthusiast Facebook groups.
The SGBC is yet to be released, but the project joins other FPGA consoles by the likes of retro gaming modding YouTuber Taki Udon’s SuperStation One, ModRetro’s M64, and Analogue’s SuperNT+ and MegaSG+. Not only are projects like these reviving the platforms, but they are also giving them modern features and comforts, bringing the question “What if these consoles were built today?” to reality.

articles.title: L’emblématique Hubble est voué à s’écraser, la NASA cherche une entreprise pour le sauver
articles.text:
Hubble perd un peu d’altitude chaque jour, et sa chute dans l’atmosphère est inévitable. Mais la NASA n’a pas dit son dernier mot : elle cherche déjà qui pourrait le sauver.
Cet été, la NASA a déjà tenté de sauver le télescope Swift pour les mêmes raisons. Le vaisseau robotique LINK, conçu par la start-up Katalyst, devait ainsi le remonter sur une orbite plus haute. Mais après une panne, l’agence a dû renoncer. Si le télescope lancé en 2004 s’apprête à brûler dans l’atmosphère, il semblerait bien que les ingénieurs aient envie de s’en inspirer pour venir en aide aux plus emblématiques des observatoires spatiaux : Hubble.
Six ans pour trouver une solution
Ce 29 octobre, la NASA a en effet lancé une demande d’informations auprès des entreprises du secteur spatial afin de déterminer qui serait capable de propulser Hubble plus haut, de le moderniser, ou de le faire rentrer dans l’atmosphère de façon contrôlée le moment venu. » Hubble a encore de la science importante devant lui », a rappelé l’administrateur de l’agence, Jared Isaacman.
« S’il existe des moyens innovants et rentables de prolonger la durée de vie d’un équipement déjà en orbite, nous nous devons, vis-à-vis des contribuables américains et de la communauté scientifique, de les explorer », poursuit-il.
Tout comme son homologue Swift, Hubble est freiné par les infimes traces d’air qui subsistent à son altitude, et ne peut pas compenser seul sa lente descente. Sa rentrée dans l’atmosphère est ainsi estimée aux alentours de 2033-2034, ce qui impose une mission d’ici à 2032. La NASA a clairement pris les devants cette fois : Katalyst Space n’a eu que quelques mois pour préparer et lancer LINK.
Entre 1993 et 2009, cinq missions de maintenance ont déjà permis de réparer et de moderniser Hubble directement en orbite grâce à la navette spatiale. Mais cette fois, l’agence mise sur l’industrie privée qui a beaucoup progressé ces dernières années dans la capture et l’entretien de satellites.
Hubble a changé notre compréhension de l’Univers
Un tel effort se comprend tant Hubble a apporté à l’astronomie. Lancé en 1990 en coopération avec l’ESA, il a permis de préciser l’âge de l’univers, estimé à environ 13,8 milliards d’années. Ses observations, associées à celles de télescopes au sol, ont aussi montré que son expansion s’accélère, une découverte récompensée par le prix Nobel de physique en 2011.
Il a également contribué à confirmer la présence de trous noirs supermassifs au cœur des galaxies, tandis que ses images des « champs profonds » ont dévoilé des galaxies très lointaines et des visuels à couper le souffle. Et son travail n’est pas fini puisqu’aujourd’hui, il travaille de concert avec le télescope James-Webb, en orbite depuis 2021.
« Hubble est une icône nationale qui, depuis plus de 35 ans, a profondément bouleversé la façon dont l’humanité perçoit notre univers », assure Nicky Fox, administratrice adjointe de la Direction des missions scientifiques au siège de la NASA. Qui pourra le sauver ?

articles.title: Job-Ghosting: Website veröffentlicht Tausende Meldungen frustrierter Jobsuchender
articles.text:
Nach Vorstellungsgespräch geghostet? Website sammelt anonyme Meldungen frustrierter Jobsuchender
Als Job-Ghosting wird das mittlerweile weitverbreitete Phänomen bezeichnet, dass Unternehmen sich nach Bewerbungen oder Vorstellungsgesprächen nicht mehr bei den Bewerber:innen melden. In den USA sollen fast die Hälfte der Jobsuchenden schon einmal entsprechende Erfahrungen gemacht haben.
Job-Ghosting weitverbreitet
Das gilt auch dann, wenn sie schon ein oder mehrmals bei einem Vorstellungsgespräch eingeladen waren, wie eine Umfrage der Bewerbungsplattform Greenhouse unter 1.200 Kandidat:innen ergeben hat. In Deutschland hatte zuletzt eine Indeed-Umfrage ergeben, dass 64 Prozent der 1.000 Befragten nach einer Bewerbung keinerlei Rückmeldung erhalten haben.
Kein Wunder, dass viele Jobsuchende frustriert sind. Wie groß der Frust ist, zeigt der enorme Ansturm auf die erst im Juni 2026 ins Leben gerufene Website Did They Ghost You. Mittlerweile gibt es dort knapp 2.900 anonyme Berichte über Job-Ghosting. Zu den ghostenden Unternehmen gehören demnach einige der im Aktienindex S&P 500 vertretenen größten Konzerne der USA.
An den Start gebracht hat die Website der in Kanada lebende Marketingprofi Gary Meyer. Auf die Idee kam Meyer eigenen Angaben zufolge, als ihm Freund:innen erklärten, dass sie nach Vorstellungsgesprächen nichts mehr von den entsprechenden Firmen gehört hatten.
Jobsuchende stürmen Beschwerde-Seite
Eigentlich sollte die Website nicht mehr sein als ein witziges Nebenprojekt, so Meyer gegenüber CNBC. Nachdem er aber einen Link via Linkedin geteilt hatte, stürmten von Job-Ghosting betroffene Jobsuchende die Seite. Innerhalb der ersten paar Tage soll die Website mehr als zwei Millionen Besucher:innen verzeichnet haben.
„Offensichtlich hat das einen wunden Punkt getroffen“, erklärte Meyer. Der Website-Betreiber überprüft jede einzelne Meldung persönlich und stellt nur anonymisierte Berichte online. Zu Hochzeiten im Sommer sollen minütlich fünf oder sechs entsprechende Einsendungen eingetroffen sein.
Wird Did They Ghost You bald unnötig?
Der Erfolg der Seite habe ihn entsprechend ein wenig überwältigt. Derzeit hätten sich schon einige noch freizugebende Meldungen angesammelt. Zu einem neuen Glassdoor will Meyer Did They Ghost You aber nicht ausbauen. Im besten Fall werde das Problem Job-Ghosting irgendwann gelöst und die Seite sei nicht mehr notwendig.

articles.title: Ver Barcelona vs Aston Villa en Fútbol Libre o Roja Directa puede traer la suspensión del internet
articles.text:
El partido entre Barcelona y Aston Villa por la Champions League puede llevar a muchos usuarios a buscar transmisiones sin costo en sitios o aplicaciones piratas, como Fútbol Libre o Roja Directa.
Esa decisión puede exponer el dispositivo a programas maliciosos y robo de datos, sumado a que el uso de estos servicios puede tener consecuencias para la conexión. a internet del hogar
Según ESET, la retransmisión de contenido protegido sin autorización puede derivar en bloqueos aplicados por proveedores de internet, según las políticas de cada empresa, las órdenes de autoridades competentes y la normativa vigente en cada país.
Por qué ver partidos en apps pirata puede terminar en un bloqueo de internet
Los partidos de la Champions League están protegidos por derechos de transmisión que pertenecen a canales, plataformas y operadores autorizados. Las páginas que difunden esos encuentros sin licencia vulneran la propiedad intelectual de los titulares de esos derechos.
Los expertos advierten que el acceso y la distribución de este tipo de emisiones implica riesgos legales. Los proveedores de internet pueden bloquear dominios, limitar el acceso a determinados servicios o actuar ante requerimientos judiciales. Las medidas varían según la legislación local y las condiciones del contrato de cada cliente.
Qué pasa si se descarga una aplicación fuera de las tiendas oficiales
Muchas aplicaciones que prometen partidos, películas y series sin suscripción no están disponibles en Google Play Store ni en App Store. Para instalarlas, el usuario debe buscar archivos en páginas alternativas, enlaces compartidos en redes sociales o sitios con publicidad invasiva.
Ese recorrido elimina parte de los controles que aplican las tiendas oficiales sobre las aplicaciones publicadas. Los archivos descargados desde fuentes no verificadas pueden incluir código malicioso, versiones alteradas de programas conocidos o componentes adicionales que no son necesarios para reproducir un video.
Cómo puede infectar un malware al celular, la computadora o el televisor
Una aplicación streaming no oficial puede presentarse como un reproductor de contenidos, pero incorporar funciones ajenas a esa tarea. ESET señala que este tipo de software puede abrir la puerta a spyware, troyanos y herramientas destinadas a obtener información personal.
El riesgo no se limita al dispositivo donde se instaló la aplicación. Si ese aparato está conectado al router de la vivienda, una infección puede afectar la seguridad de toda la red doméstica.
Contraseñas, archivos personales, datos bancarios y sesiones abiertas en otros servicios pueden quedar expuestos si el software malicioso logra acceso al sistema.
Por qué las aplicaciones piratas pueden acceder a información privada
Una señal de alerta aparece cuando una plataforma de video solicita accesos amplios que no guardan relación con la reproducción de partidos. Algunos programas pueden obtener datos sobre otras aplicaciones instaladas, revisar archivos, leer contenidos multimedia o modificar información almacenada en el aparato.
Asimismo, pueden mostrar notificaciones con enlaces engañosos, publicidad fraudulenta o mensajes que imitan alertas del sistema. Expertos identificaron que ciertas apps de este tipo tienen capacidades que podrían facilitar el envío de contenido no solicitado, la consulta de fotos, audios y documentos, o la alteración de archivos guardados en el dispositivo.
Otra práctica consiste en mostrar avisos que piden instalar un complemento, una nueva versión del reproductor o una supuesta mejora para ver el partido. El mensaje puede aparecer justo antes de un encuentro de alto interés, cuando el usuario busca una solución rápida para acceder a la transmisión.
Qué alternativas reducen los riesgos al ver partidos de fútbol
La forma más segura de seguir el encuentro es utilizar emisoras, plataformas o servicios que tengan los derechos de la competición en el país donde se encuentra el espectador. Esos servicios operan dentro de marcos de distribución establecidos y cuentan con canales de soporte para sus usuarios.
Se debe evitar la descarga de archivos desde enlaces desconocidos, no ingresar datos personales en páginas que prometen acceso inmediato y revisar las aplicaciones instaladas en celulares, computadoras y televisores.

articles.title: Synology NAS Devices Targeted in Ransomware Attacks Exploiting Patched DSM Flaw
articles.text:
Synology is urging customers to update the DiskStation Manager (DSM) software powering its Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices following ransomware attacks.
The Taiwanese vendor said it observed threat actors exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to target devices running outdated versions of DSM.
"These attacks aim to encrypt data and extort ransom," it said in a statement released last week.
While Synology did not disclose the exact security flaw that's being exploited in these attacks, the company linked to a November 2024 security advisory that listed three vulnerabilities -
- CVE-2024-10441 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the system plugin daemon of DSM that could lead to remote code execution via unspecified vectors.
- CVE-2024-50629 (CVSS score: 5.3) - An improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the webapi component of DSM that could allow remote attackers to read limited files via unspecified vectors.
- CVE-2024-10445 (CVSS score: 4.3) - An improper certificate validation vulnerability in the update functionality in DSM that could allow remote attackers to write limited files via unspecified vectors.
The issues were addressed in the following versions -
- DSM 7.2.2 - Upgrade to 7.2.2-72806-1 or above
- DSM 7.2.1 - Upgrade to 7.2.1-69057-6 or above
- DSM 7.2 - Upgrade to 7.2-64570-4 or above
- DSM 7.1 - Upgrade to 7.1.1-42962-7 or above
- DSM 6.2 - Upgrade to 6.2.4-25556-8 or above
The development comes amid reports from customers that their Synology devices have been hit by C3RB3R ransomware, which has been observed locking users' files with a ".L0CK3D" extension.
In an analysis published last week, Chinese security vendor Qihoo 360 Internet Security Center said C3RB3R has a "long history" of deploying ransomware against NAS devices, including by exploiting two DSM vulnerabilities that were addressed by Synology back in September 2026 -
- CVE-2026-13684 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in SCGI that could allow remote attackers to read or write arbitrary files and conduct denial-of-service attacks.
- CVE-2026-13639 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An insufficient entropy vulnerability in login logic that could allow remote attackers to read or write arbitrary files and conduct denial-of-service attacks.
Once launched, C3RB3R scans files on the compromised device, while skipping 27 directories and certain extensions (e.g., BAT, DLL, EXE, LNK, MOD, MSI, and SYS) to avoid triggering system crashes and impacting its encryption process. Files that are successfully encrypted receive a .L0CK3D extension and a ransom note named "read-me3.txt" is dropped in each encrypted directory.
This is not the first time NAS devices have been the target of ransomware attacks. In 2019, NAS devices manufactured by Taiwan-based QNAP Systems were compromised by QNAPCrypt (aka eCh0raix) ransomware.
Then, in August 2021, Synology warned of brute-force attacks driven by a malware family called StealthWorker that led to ransomware infections.
"These attacks leverage a number of already infected devices to try and guess common administrative credentials, and if successful, will access the system to install its malicious payload, which may include ransomware," it said at the time. "Devices infected may carry out additional attacks on other Linux-based devices, including Synology NAS."
That same month, Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 also disclosed details of an eCh0raix variant targeting NAS devices from both QNAP and Synology by leveraging vulnerabilities like CVE-2021-28799 or brute-force their way in by making use of commonly used administrative credentials.
"Synology strongly urges all users running vulnerable versions to update DSM immediately to protect their systems," the company said. "Synology also recommends enabling automatic updates to keep DSM up to date at all times."

articles.title: Board makers are running out of GeForce RTX 50 GPUs, so distributors are pushing old RTX 3060s instead
articles.text:
Facepalm: Nearly two years after launch, it should be easy for a graphics card distributor to order Nvidia's RTX 50-series cards in bulk. In China, however, some board makers reportedly can't supply enough of them anymore. They're now steering distributors toward the RTX 3060 and RTX 3050 instead, two cards that first hit shelves back in 2021 and 2022, respectively.
Chinese supply chain outlet ChannelGate first reported the shift. According to the outlet, some manufacturers have already run out of RTX 50 stock. The ones that haven't are reportedly shipping what's left in small batches at higher prices.
Essentially, rather than leave distributors with nothing to sell, makers are pointing them toward the RTX 3060 in its 12GB and 8GB versions. The RTX 3050 makes the cut as well. So do a few AMD Radeon cards, though the report doesn't name them. Even so, ChannelGate doesn't expect any of these cards to become cheaper. If anything, the outlet thinks prices on older products could creep up a little.
As for the shortage itself, ChannelGate blames a fresh wave of demand from cryptocurrency miners. China's busy online shopping season is reportedly draining stock, too. It also doesn't help that the RTX 50 lineup was already running thin, since Nvidia reportedly cut production earlier this year amid the AI-driven memory crunch.
In fact, the RTX 3060 only came out of retirement a few months ago. In July, the card landed on Newegg in the US for $329.99, the same price it launched at in 2021.
That price didn't last long, though. By August, the same MSI model had climbed to $479.99. That's about $180 more than Newegg was charging for the newer and faster RTX 5050 at the time.
Meanwhile, the RTX 3060 has also reclaimed the top spot in Valve's October Steam Hardware Survey. It now sits on 3.62% of surveyed systems, just ahead of the RTX 5070 at 3.56%. The newer card had grabbed the lead in September before dropping 2.30 points this month.
System memory flipped back, too. 16GB of RAM is once again the most common amount, found in 41.42% of systems. 32GB had overtaken it in September but now sits at 37.06%.
The October numbers don't mean gamers suddenly ditched their RTX 5070s, though. Hardware Busters traced the swing to Steam's language breakdown. Users running the client in Simplified Chinese dropped from roughly 31% of respondents in September to just under 22% in October. Valve doesn't adjust its results by region, so when fewer players from China take part, the newer midrange cards popular there slide down the charts. A similar spike in Chinese respondents briefly put the RTX 5070 on top back in February, too.

articles.title: Un moddeur transforme une Nintendo Switch originale en iPad Pro grâce à l'émulation — Frandroid
articles.text:
C’est une étrange vidéo qui a été publiée sur X. On y voit l’écran d’accueil d’iPadOS, Safari et les Réglages sur la console de Nintendo. Dans ces Réglages, la Switch se présente comme un iPad Pro 12,9 pouces de deuxième génération, avec 34 Go de stockage dont environ 23 Go libres. L’interface a été recadrée pour l’écran en définition 720p de la console, bien moins défini que celui de la vraie tablette.
Jusqu’ici, les passerelles entre Nintendo et Apple allaient plutôt dans l’autre sens. Plus de 100 jeux Switch tournent en natif sur iPhone, iPad et Mac, certains à 60 images par seconde sur un vieux Mac M1. Et les jeux Switch 2 y sont jouables aussi.
Le 19 novembre, Vice City vous attend. Et votre PS5 ? Avec Next Mobiles, pas besoin de payer 600 € d’un coup, louez-la sur la durée que vous souhaitez, dès 16,90 €/mois.
Pourquoi un iPad Pro de 2017 ?
Bruno St John n’a pas installé iPadOS directement sur la console. La Switch originale embarque une puce Tegra X1 de Nvidia, alors que le système d’Apple réclame ses propres composants. Le moddeur passe donc par QEMU, un logiciel libre qui recrée de toutes pièces une machine virtuelle, ici un iPad. Le Tegra X1 et les puces des iPad partagent l’architecture ARM, ce qui rend l’exercice envisageable sur une console de 2017.
Le modèle émulé colle à la version. Apple a publié iPadOS 17.7.11 le 11 mai 2026 pour trois iPad seulement, dont ce Pro 12,9 pouces. Par contre, la vidéo s’arrête à Safari et aux Réglages. On ne sait pas encore quelles applications tournent, ni à quelle vitesse.
La première Switch, la plus facile à ouvrir
En avril 2018, la chercheuse Kate Temkin a dévoilé Fusée Gelée, une faille gravée dans la mémoire de démarrage du Tegra X1, impossible à corriger sur les consoles déjà vendues.
Elle permet de lancer n’importe quel logiciel (Linux compris), et seules les Switch produites ensuite ont reçu une puce corrigée.
La Switch 2 n’est pas mieux protégée, puisque son premier jailbreak 100 % logiciel fonctionne sur la dernière mise à jour. Un Homebrew Launcher, le menu qui lance les logiciels non officiels, tournait moins de 24 heures plus tard. Et ce jailbreak résiste malgré l’intervention de Nintendo.

articles.title: Intel Moves Select Core Ultra 200H and 200U CPUs to Embedded Market
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 3rd 2026
Intel Moves Select Core Ultra 200H and 200U CPUs to Embedded Market
Intel has released the latest Product Change Notice (PCN) document, stating that the company's mobile "Arrow Lake-H" and "Arrow Lake-U" processors, with the Core Ultra 200H and Core Ultra 200U naming schemes, will no longer be offered as standard parts for consumer products. Instead, Intel plans to transition some of these SKUs to the embedded sector, meaning these processors will continue to exist but under a different licensing agreement. For laptop manufacturers purchasing these processors, Intel has set May 21, 2027, as the final date for submitting orders, with the last shipments scheduled for November 19, 2027. After this date, these SKUs will cease commercial shipments.
The list includes the Intel Core Ultra 5 235H, Core Ultra 5 225U, Core Ultra 5 235U, Core Ultra 7 255U, Core Ultra 5 225H, Core Ultra 7 265U, Core Ultra 7 255H, Core Ultra 7 265H, and Core Ultra 9 285H processors.Intel explained that the company is transitioning these SKUs to its embedded segment, which has its own agreements and rules. All SoCs purchased prior to November 2027 will still remain under commercial use licensing terms, but not after that date.
Intel PCNIntel support for the products listed in the "Products Affected/Intel Ordering Codes" table below is moving to Intel Embedded Architecture for the continued support of Intel Embedded Architecture customers. The Intel Embedded Architecture terms, conditions, and pricing will go into effect for all customers after the "Last Shipment Date Prior to Product Support Change" listed above. Please contact your Intel sales representative if you have any questions regarding this change.
Intel Embedded Architecture Customer definition: Customers who purchase Intel products under terms specifically tailored for networking, edge computing, industrial, storage, communications, and embedded applications. These purchases are governed by Intel Embedded Architecture agreements, which include distinct terms, conditions, and pricing.

				Intel, 				via VideoCardz

articles.title: Hiding inside Palantir's skyrocketing quarter is a foreboding signal | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The data analysis company Palantir delivered such a huge third-quarter earnings report on Monday that its press release even bragged that the numbers were “crushing consensus expectations.”
Yet retail investors were lukewarm on the company on Tuesday, with the stock trading slightly down. That’s because Palantir’s enterprise sales, its big growth area, showed signs of slowing.
First, the good news for the company’s investors. Revenue grew 96% from a year earlier, and 20% from the previous quarter, to $2.31 billion, beating analysts’ expectations of $2.18 billion. It was the first time Palantir has topped $2 billion in a quarter. Palantir also reported adjusted earnings per share (profit per share, excluding certain one-time items) of 44 cents, compared with analysts’ expectations of 41 cents. The company even raised its revenue guidance, or forecast, for the full year. Normally, that alone would send a stock soaring.
The clincher was that Palantir’s U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time ever. The company reported $984 million in commercial contracts (up 148% from the year-ago quarter), versus $953 million in U.S. government revenue.
The reason for all this love from enterprises? They are signing up for the company’s AI software that can run frontier models and custom-train open-weight models securely, without sharing any of their data and business processes with outside AI labs. Plus, Palantir has long offered what is today known as “forward-deployed” software engineering, in which its own engineers work directly with customers to customize the software.
However, Palantir also revealed a less-than-rosy signal: Even as enterprises are moving faster than ever, they are often signing short-term trials.
“What Ryan and I are seeing on the front line and commercial is this much quicker interaction, much quicker to deployment, shorter duration of the contract but then an ability to expand that contract dramatically,” CEO Alex Karp (pictured above) told Wall Street analysts on the quarterly earnings call.
Palantir is experiencing one of the unique phenomena of AI in the enterprise right now. Corporations are willing to quickly try AI software, skipping the usual bureaucracy, but they are also more willing to cancel contracts.
Karp used one off-color metaphor after another to describe how unconcerned he was about holding onto his enterprise business.
“We’ve gone from being the most attractive person in the physics department to being the captain of the football team, kind of thing,” he said, describing the influx of prospective corporate customers flowing in. “Conversely, you know, once you go Palantir, you don’t go back, and that’s just how it is, and you see it in our numbers.”
The numbers don’t yet confirm Palantir’s long-term success. While the company closed a hefty $1.46 billion of total contract value from U.S. enterprises in the quarter, that’s actually a decline from the record $2.13 billion in the previous quarter. That suggests slowing sales, at least in the most recent quarter.
The next earnings will show whether Palantir has solidified its role as a rising U.S. enterprise AI provider. Historically, many enterprises sign their biggest tech purchases in the final quarter of the year. Karp and his team certainly sound confident. They increased guidance for U.S. commercial revenue to be “in excess of $3.559 billion, representing a growth rate of at least 143%.”

articles.title: KI im Orbit: Google-Satellit meldet sich aus dem All – mit einem Gedicht über den Weltraum
articles.text:
KI im Orbit: Google-Satellit meldet sich aus dem All – mit einem Gedicht über den Weltraum
Nach einer dreiwöchigen Inbetriebnahme konnte der Satellit seinen Betrieb aufnehmen: Laut Google wurden in den drei Wochen die KI-Beschleuniger sowie die übrige Hardware hochgefahren und erste Machine-Learning-Tests absolviert. Wie Techcrunch berichtet, übermittelten die Ingenieure am Boden jetzt ihren ersten Befehl: Das auf dem Satelliten vorinstallierte Deepmind-Modell „Gemma 4“ sollte ein Haiku – also ein dreizeiliges Gedicht – über den Aufenthalt im Weltraum dichten. Das Ergebnis war folgendes Kurzgedicht (sinngemäß aus dem Englischen übrsetzt):
„Die blaue Murmel da unten,
Datenströme in stiller Anmut,
Sternenlicht nährt mein Innerstes.“
Googles Projekt Suncatcher
Der Satellit stammt aus dem Google-Projekt „Suncatcher“. Das Forschungsprojekt soll laut Google untersuchen, ob der Weltraum eines Tages eine skalierbare Infrastruktur für maschinelles Lernen beherbergen könnte.
Er beherbergt vier Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) mit Solarpaneelen. Seine Solarmodule liefern zwar eine Leistung von bis zu einem Kilowatt, doch genau da liegt das Problem: Laut Google kann wegen des Strombedarfs der Chips jeweils nur eine TPU gleichzeitig laufen. Außerdem rechnet der Chip nur in kurzen Intervallen von etwa 15 Minuten. Ein Dauerbetrieb würde die Stromversorgung und die Kühlung des Satelliten überlasten. Sollten sich die TPUs an Bord des Satelliten als leistungsfähig erweisen, will Google 2027 zwei weitere Satelliten ins All schießen, die mehr Strom erzeugen können. Perspektivisch sollen mehrere Satelliten ein zusammenhängendes orbitales Rechennetzwerk bilden.
Die Zukunft von orbitalen KI‑Rechenzentren
Der US-Konzern ist mit seiner Vision von Rechenzentren im All nicht allein. Im Januar reichte etwa Elon Musks Unternehmen SpaceX bei der US-amerikanischen Telekommunikationsaufsicht Federal Communications Commission (FCC) einen Antrag ein: Die Firma will bis zu eine Million Rechenzentren in die Erdumlaufbahn bringen. Im vergangenen Winter startete Starcloud, ein Startup mit Sitz in den USA, mit einem Satelliten und Nvidia-Chip an Bord ins All. Das Unternehmen strebt an, bis 2030 ganze Rechenzentren im Orbit zu betreiben, die genauso groß sind wie jene auf der Erde.
Die Befürworter:innen halten schwebende Rechenzentren im Weltraum für sinnvoll, da der KI-Boom die Stromnetze belaste und den Wasserbedarf auf der Erde erhöhe, der zur Kühlung der Server benötigt werde. Gleichzeitig könne die erzeugte überschüssige Wärme in das kalte Vakuum des Weltraums abgeleitet werden. Kritiker:innen warnen hingegen vor den Folgen orbitaler Rechenzentren, da ihr CO₂‑Fußabdruck höher ausfallen könnte als der von Anlagen auf der Erde, wenn Herstellung, Start und Entsorgung berücksichtigt werden.

articles.title: Le robot d'Apple serait prêt depuis deux ans, mais l'IA poserait encore problème
articles.text:
Le projet occuperait les laboratoires de Cupertino depuis 2019, sous le nom de code J595, avec un objectif de départ presque banal : faciliter les appels vidéo à la maison. Sept ans plus tard, la partie matérielle de ce robot domestique serait figée, et ce depuis environ deux ans. Le logiciel, lui, s’est chargé d’ambitions nouvelles en cours de route, au point de repousser le lancement vers2027, voire 2028, rapporte The Information.
À quoi ressemble le robot qu’Apple garde au garage ?
L’appareil prend la forme d’un écran de 9 pouces perché sur un bras articulé, qui pivote pour suivre les occupants et « ressemble à la lampe Pixar ». Sa caméra et ses capteurs doivent lui permettre de comprendre la pièce : contourner un obstacle, repérer une arrivée dans le salon, allumer la lumière au passage. L’engin irait donc bien au-delà de l’enceinte à écran posée sur un meuble, puisqu’il est pensé pour vivre avec le foyer et le suivre du regard.
Côté facture, le tarif envisagé tournerait autour de 1 000 dollars, une estimation qui pourrait encore grimper avec la flambée des composants. Le nom pressenti, HomeView Ultra, rattacherait l’appareil à l’écran connecté HomeView, attendu dans les foyers américains d’ici quelques jours après avoir lui-même patienté le temps que les chantiers de Siri avancent. Le robot en serait la déclinaison haut de gamme, la plus chère et la plus ambitieuse.
Pourquoi le lancement glisse-t-il d’année en année ?
À l’origine, l’engin devait surtout suivre son utilisateur pendant les appels vidéo, un cahier des charges resté raisonnable pendant les premières années du projet. Les fonctions d’intelligence artificielle empilées depuis ont changé l’ampleur du chantier : conscience de la pièce, déplacements autonomes, interactions continues avec les habitants. Résultat, un matériel achevé attend un cerveau qui n’existe pas encore, et c’est lui qui dicte désormais le calendrier.
Début 2025 déjà, l’analyste Ming-Chi Kuo ne voyait pas de production en masse avant 2028 pour les premiers robots de la marque, un pronostic que les dernières indiscrétions rendent crédible. Depuis l’abandon de son projet de voiture, Apple cherche la prochaine grande catégorie capable d’épauler l’iPhone, et aurait déjà réduit la voilure sur le Vision Pro pour dégager des ressources. La maison mise donc sur un produit jamais montré, sans nom officiel, sans prix public ni date de sortie.

articles.title: El fraude eléctrico en Barcelona ha llegado a tal nivel que hasta los supermercados 24 horas se enganchan a la red
articles.text:
El fraude eléctrico en Barcelona ha llegado a tal nivel que ya no hay que buscarlo en pisos con plantaciones de marihuana: lo tienes a la vuelta de la esquina, en el súper que abre a las tres de la madrugada para venderte unos tampones o bolsas de hielo. El pasado 29 de octubre, el Ayuntamiento inspeccionó 23 supermercados 24 horas de la Vila de Gràcia y ordenó 11 cierres cautelares, según El Periódico. Nueve de ellos tenían la luz pinchada o alguna otra anomalía en el suministro. Ah, y otros tres tenían plagas.
Operativo con invitados. La actuación, enmarcada en el Plan Endreça, movilizó a un centenar de efectivos: Guardia Urbana, técnicos municipales, Inspecció del Treball, Agencia Tributaria, Policía Nacional y, ojo, la propia Endesa. La primera teniente de alcalde, Laia Bonet, defendió este enorme operativo porque así permite inspecciones con asesoramiento experto y personal que no pertenece solo al Ayuntamiento.
242 infracciones. Según 3Cat, 99 son de licencias de actividad, 52 de paisaje urbano, 23 de salud pública y otras 23 de residuos. Hay además 10 laborales, cinco de ocupación de la vía pública y 30 tributarias (15 municipales y 15 estatales). Bonet resumió que este modelo está “expulsando al comercio tradicional” y cambiando la identidad de la ciudad. Es la decimoséptima macroinspección en este mismo mandato: desde noviembre de 2023 se han revisado 682 establecimientos, con 5.097 infracciones y 110 medidas cautelares.
Licencias congeladas (algunas). En mayo, el Ayuntamiento suspendió durante un año las nuevas licencias de supermercados 24 horas para frenar el “monocultivo” que denunció el alcalde Collboni. Hay unas 1.300 concedidas. Aun así, os puedo garantizar que varios han abierto en las últimas semanas porque los he visto, unos con licencia anterior a la suspensión y otros sin ella, como el de la antigua librería Ona, en Gran de Gràcia, que será clausurado en breve.
Antecedente. En diciembre de 2025, la operación Nihari descubrió que 24 de 26 supermercados inspeccionados en seis distritos, Gràcia incluido, recurrían a electricidad que no pasaba por el contador. El fraude ascendía a 2,85 millones de kWh, el consumo anual de 814 viviendas. Muchos eran franquicias de cadenas conocidas y por entonces la Guardia Civil abrió diligencias contra 26 personas.
Del cultivo indoor al escaparate. Hasta ahora, la cara del enganche ilegal era la plantación de marihuana, un tema que en Xataka hemos tratado en varias ocasiones. Según Endesa, una plantación indoor media consume lo mismo que 80 viviendas y, en cinco años, su filial de redes desmanteló la instalación eléctrica de unas 10.600. España concentra el 73 % de las incautaciones de marihuana de la UE, y de ahí salen historias como la de un chalet de Madrid alquilado y convertido en un indoor de 391 plantas, o la de una casa en Castellón comprada sin saber que tenía una plantación dentro.
El problema es que… bueno, que el problema no va a menos. Endesa detectó 72.700 fraudes en 2025, la cifra más alta en cinco años; en Barcelona capital hubo 5.487 casos, 891 más que en 2024. La CNMC calcula que estas prácticas encarecen la factura en unos 150 millones de euros. Y claro, esos euros los pagamos todos.
El algoritmo mira Instagram. Las distribuidoras ya no esperan a que alguien denuncie. e-distribución, la filial de redes de Endesa, usa machine learning y aprendizaje profundo para detectar anomalías y, según eEXcellence, encuentra robo de energía en una de cada dos inspecciones, el doble que en 2017. Hace unos días ya contamos cómo su IA cruzó datos de consumo con vídeos de influencers en 16 restaurantes de Barcelona: locales enormes, repletos en redes y con un consumo ínfimo, que no cuadraba con la afluencia.
¿Iberdrola? Su distribuidora, i-DE, no ha detallado públicamente un caso tan concreto, pero la compañía asegura que lleva más de diez años usando IA, con más de 150 casos de uso. También identifica las pérdidas no técnicas, esas causadas por enganches o contadores manipulados, como un problema que quiere atajar desde su centro de innovación en redes inteligentes. También financió el proyecto FRAC, con el que la Universidad Pontificia Comillas desarrolló un sistema de redes neuronales para detectar anomalías y fraude en los registros de consumo.
Lo que dice la ley. Defraudar fluido eléctrico se castiga con multa de tres a doce meses (artículo 255 del Código Penal), aunque la Fiscalía ya ha criticado que no haya penas más duras. La reforma de 2026 añadió prisión, pero solo para plantaciones de marihuana, así que un supermercado se queda al margen. La distribuidora, eso sí, puede cortar el suministro y facturar con efectos retroactivos.
Porque esto no es una cuestión de porosidad ni una IA entrenada. La IA no ha inventado el fraude, pero está erradicando esa comodidad de quien se pensaba que podía enganchar al vuelo o eludir el contador. Los actuales cierres son cautelares (y las infracciones, presuntas hasta que se resuelvan los expedientes). Lo que está claro es que los esquinados 24 horas con sus máquinas de vending y luz mortecina que no pagan luz tienen los días contados.

articles.title: Startup Athena raises $2.5M in pre-seed funding to revamp the revenue model for legal AI - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Startup Athena raises $2.5M in pre-seed funding to revamp the revenue model for legal AI
Athena Circle Corp., an artificial intelligence-native legal technology startup that’s automating the nitty gritty of commercial real estate deals, said today it has raised $2.5 million in pre-seed funding.
The round was led by Andreessen Horowitz’s accelerator program, a16z Speedrun. No other investors were named.
Legal AI technology is nothing new, but its adoption in the industry has been somewhat haphazard, for the technology has exposed an awkward problem: Most law firms are still billing their clients by the hour, and that makes automation less lucrative. If a law firm can use AI agents to get a 10-hour contract review done in just a couple of minutes, then it’s going to let an awful lot of billable revenue slip through its fingers, killing any incentive there might be to adopt them.
Athena’s co-founders Cem Ucan (pictured, left) and Kieran John Keenan (right) and founding engineer José Braz all cut their teeth at the pioneering legal AI tech startup Legora AB, where they quickly realized how AI conflicts with the industry’s standard business model. They came up with an entirely different business model to convince legal firms of the benefits of automation. Instead of selling software tools directly, it provides a legal service through its affiliated law firm, charging a fixed fee per transaction that’s typically 30% to 50% lower than standard rates. In this way, it ensures that revenue is better aligned with efficiency.
“Most legal AI companies sell tools to traditional law firms, but we took a different approach,” Ucan said. “Our AI works hand-in-hand with a law firm designed around it from day one, with experienced attorneys focused on the judgment and negotiation that actually move deals forward.”
The startup is focused on automating the intricacies of commercial real estate acquisitions, sales and financing. Its AI agents are designed to automate the creation and review of purchase agreements and loan documents, and will handle all of the due diligence and administrative closing hurdles needed to get deals done, while ensuring human lawyers remain fully in the loop to make all of the final legal determinations.
In this way, Athena basically takes care of the grunt work, giving commercial real estate firms much more agility. That’s a real advantage, because commercial real estate is an industry where speed is of the essence: The faster a law firm gets things done, the more likely it is to actually secure the deal, which is the end result that everyone wants. With investors often submitting dozens of bids for each property listing, the ability to get the paperwork done in a matter of hours rather than weeks or days means buyers can lock in a deal before their rivals know what’s happened.
Keenan, who serves as the startup’s chief technology officer, explained that each new workflow begins with an incoming agreement that’s ingested by its AI agents. They cross-reference the terms of the deal against their standard deal sheets in order to flag inconsistencies, prepare redlines and draft client communications.
This work is informed by historical transactions, which allow its agents to adapt to each client’s negotiating style, Keenan said. Human attorneys then review this work, make strategic judgment calls when required, and approve all deliverables before they’re sent to clients.
“I measure our progress by how quickly an attorney can review an AI agent’s work and confidently stand behind it,” Keenan explained. “A draft produced in minutes can still leave a lawyer with hours of work. Making that review more efficient is how our platform helps us deliver faster legal services with the quality clients expect.”
Athena’s agents are already proving their worth, with the startup having signed up 22 legal firms as clients so far, just two months after launching its service. By learning continuously from attorney’s edits and client’s preferences, its agents have reduced review times by an average of 70%.
L. Miguel Arce, chief executive of the Texas-based multifamily real estate and property management firm Mox Living, said Athena was able to deliver a complete purchase agreement in less than 48 hours, the fastest turnaround he has ever seen. “A lot of firms in our industry have an AI task force in name only,” he said. “What stood out about Athena is that the system learns from every deal, from what the attorneys change to what we prefer. Speed only matters if it’s quality work, and Athena gets us both.”
Keenan said Athena is primed to strike while the iron is hot. He said the industry is bracing itself for a wave of new commercial deals as properties financed through short-term loans in 2021 and 2022 hit their refinancing deadlines, and he’s hoping that the startup can win a significant amount of that business. In any case, growth is on the horizon, for Athena also plans to expand into new markets and property classes and even new legal domains.
A16z Speedrun’s Troy Kirwin said AI automation is all well and good, but clients still demand to speak to a human who can take responsibility for the work that gets done. “Athena is building around that need with a system that can improve through real legal work and a team that’s obsessed with scaling fast,” he said.

articles.title: Ivanti livre les derniers correctifs pour les failles zero-day exploitées dans son VPN, mais les entreprises ne sont pas encore tirées d'affaire
articles.text:
Ivanti vient de publier les deux correctifs qui manquaient à ses passerelles VPN Connect Secure, prises pour cible depuis début octobre. La chaîne de vulnérabilités exploitée par les pirates est désormais entièrement corrigée.
Début octobre, des pirates parvenaient à compromettre des équipements Ivanti Connect Secure pourtant à jour, en combinant plusieurs failles pour contourner l'authentification et obtenir les privilèges les plus élevés sur le système. L'éditeur avait neutralisé la principale voie d'attaque dès le 13 octobre, mais deux vulnérabilités attendaient encore leur patch. C'est désormais chose faite depuis le 29 octobre, comme l'a confirmé le CERT-FR dans une alerte actualisée le 2 novembre.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Deux nouvelles failles corrigées, mais des intrusions toujours difficiles à détecter
Les correctifs concernent CVE-2026-111357, une vulnérabilité d'élévation de privilèges permettant d'obtenir les droits root, et CVE-2026-118527, qui autorise un utilisateur authentifié à déposer un fichier arbitraire sur l'équipement. Combinées à CVE-2026-104935, corrigée mi-octobre, elles permettaient à un attaquant extérieur de prendre le contrôle d'une passerelle VPN sans disposer d'identifiants valides.
Ivanti avait préféré diffuser son premier correctif sans attendre, celui-ci étant déjà en phase de validation lorsque les autres failles ont été découvertes. Les administrateurs peuvent désormais achever la sécurisation de leurs équipements en installant les versions 22.8R2.6, 25.1.1.3 ou 25.1.3.1, selon leur branche logicielle. Les versions 25.1.3.x ne sont pas concernées par les deux dernières vulnérabilités.
La mise à jour ne permet toutefois pas d'exclure une compromission antérieure. Le groupe UTA0576 effaçait ses traces après chaque commande, échappant ainsi à l'outil de vérification d'intégrité d'Ivanti. Il est donc recommandé aux organisations concernées de rechercher d'éventuels indices d'intrusion et, en cas de compromission avérée, d'isoler les équipements touchés, de mener des investigations pour mesurer l'étendue de l'attaque, puis de réinitialiser les appareils et de renouveler les identifiants, certificats et autres secrets potentiellement exposés.

articles.title: Jewellery brand GIVA raises $100M from Multiples PE
articles.text:
Jewellery brand GIVA raises $100M from Multiples PE
Founded in 2019, Bengaluru-based GIVA focuses on everyday wear, catering primarily to Indian consumers for both self-consumption and gifting occasions. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its leadership team, expand manufacturing and deepen its offline presence.
Multiples Alternate Asset Management along with its co-investors, has led the $100 million funding round in jewellery brand GIVA.
Founded in 2019, Bengaluru-based GIVA focuses on everyday wear, catering primarily to Indian consumers for both self-consumption and gifting occasions. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its leadership team, expand manufacturing and deepen its offline presence.
The brand offers a diverse portfolio spanning 92.5 silver, gold and lab-grown diamond jewellery. It follows an omnichannel distribution model through its own retail stores, D2C website and leading third-party e-commerce and quick-commerce marketplaces.
Currently, the brand retails through 400+ stores across India and Sri Lanka. The latest fundraise is the largest investment in India's new-age jewellery market, according to the company.
Ishendra Agarwal, founder & CEO, GIVA said, "Multiples’ backing is a strong endorsement of what we have built at GIVA since 2019, a high-growth, design-led fine jewellery brand that Indian consumers trust for everyday wear and gifting.”
“As we enter our next phase, we are focused on scaling our omnichannel presence, strengthening our manufacturing capabilities and elevating the fine jewellery experience for modern Indian consumers. With Multiples’ experience in helping new-age businesses scale, we have the right partner for this journey. This $100 Mn+ round, the largest investment in India’s new-age jewellery market, gives us the strength to move faster.”
The company also added that India's jewellery market is estimated to grow at around 6% CAGR to reach $124 billion by 2032.
Multiples has also invested in brands such as Licious, ACKO, PVR and Arvind Fashions apart from in other sectors. Earlier this year, Multiples announced the close of a USD $430 million fund.

articles.title: Claude ya programa más del 90% del código de Anthropic y acelera su propio desarrollo
articles.text:
Anthropic afirmó que Claude escribió más del 90% de las contribuciones al código de la compañía en septiembre de 2026, un nivel de participación que acerca al laboratorio al “progreso drásticamente acelerado atribuible a la inteligencia artificial (IA)” y plantea riesgos para la supervisión humana de sus modelos más avanzados.
La empresa dirigida por Dario Amodei sostuvo que sus previsiones sobre futuros sistemas, y no sobre los actuales, indican que podría alcanzar pronto el umbral previsto en su Política de Escalado Responsable. Ese escenario supone que la IA puede acelerar el desarrollo de una versión posterior con capacidades superiores.
“Usar la IA para ayudar a construir una IA más capaz podría suponer un riesgo considerable para la seguridad, sobre todo si acelera bruscamente el ritmo del progreso”, advirtió Anthropic en la actualización de su documento para la salida a bolsa, identificado como S-1/A.
Qué implicaciones tiene la alta participación de Claude en Anthropic
La participación de Claude en la programación no significa que el sistema diseñe por sí solo las futuras generaciones de modelos. La evolución continúa bajo conducción humana, aunque la herramienta ya concentra la mayor parte de las aportaciones al código de la empresa.
El volumen diario de código incorporado a la base de Anthropic por cada ingeniero durante los tres meses terminados el 30 de septiembre de 2026 fue más de 45 veces superior al promedio diario registrado en el año concluido el 31 de diciembre de 2024.
La preocupación de la compañía se concentra en la posibilidad de que el rendimiento y las capacidades de sus modelos mejoren a una velocidad mayor que la de sus sistemas de medición.
Los datos que utiliza para evaluar esa evolución llegan con demora, así que una aceleración relevante podría ser detectada después de haberse producido.
Por qué genera dudas que la IA diseñe más inteligencias artificiales
Ese proceso se vincula con la llamada automejora recursiva, una práctica en la que un sistema de IA diseña y desarrolla de manera autónoma a su propio sucesor.
Asimismo, Anthropic no prevé usar Claude de forma segura para construir sin intervención humana generaciones sucesivas de modelos de frontera, incluso si esa posibilidad llega a ser viable desde el punto de vista técnico.
“Sin embargo, no prevemos poder usar Claude de forma segura para diseñar y construir de forma totalmente autónoma generaciones sucesivas de modelos de frontera sin una supervisión o comprensión humana significativa”, señaló la empresa, que estudia actualizar su política para mantener a las personas al mando del desarrollo de esos sistemas.
Qué restricciones ha puesto Anthropic en Claude
La empresa incorporó a Claude Code, su asistente de programación, una instrucción que impide crear recreaciones de videojuegos existentes, incluso cuando se les cambie el nombre. La compañía confirmó la modificación el 30 de octubre de 2026 y la vinculó con el uso de la IA para infringir derechos de propiedad intelectual.
La restricción fue detectada por un usuario de X identificado como Chasm, quien indicó que comenzó a activarse alrededor del 27 de octubre. La regla ordena crear juegos originales, obras de un género determinado o títulos basados en diseños y materiales aportados por el usuario, pero no reconstrucciones de un juego específico.
Addy Osmani, integrante del grupo técnico de Anthropic, explicó en X que se añadieron dos oraciones a la instrucción de Claude Code en Opus 5.5 para impedir que reproduzca “el juego específico de otra persona”, porque ese uso contradice las políticas de la empresa.
Osmani añadió que los juegos originales, los basados en géneros y los elaborados con diseños propios “deberían seguir funcionando”. Pidió que los usuarios comuniquen los casos en que reciban una negativa sobre materiales de su propiedad, mientras la empresa ajusta la medida para encontrar un equilibrio.

articles.title: Adieu le petit découvert accordé sans questions : dès le 20 novembre, votre banque passera vos revenus au crible, même pour 50 euros
articles.text:
Découvert bancaire : le tour de vis arrive le 20 novembre, entre fin du forfait d'agios et contrôle des revenus
Le petit découvert de fin de mois, accordé jusqu’ici sans contrôle obligatoire, vit ses derniers jours. Dès le 20 novembre, pour 50 euros comme pour 1 000, votre banque devra vérifier que vous pouvez rembourser avant de vous accorder la moindre facilité, exactement comme pour un crédit à la consommation. La réforme réserve pourtant une bonne surprise, que certains clients verront apparaître sur leurs relevés.
Le 20 novembre 2026 entre en vigueur l'ordonnance du 3 septembre 2025 relative au crédit à la consommation. Elle transpose une directive européenne d'octobre 2023 et soumet toute nouvelle autorisation de découvert au droit du crédit à la consommation, quel que soit son montant. Jusqu'ici, les découverts inférieurs à 200 euros, ou remboursables sous un mois, échappaient à ces règles. Cette exception disparaît, une évolution dont nous avions détaillé les risques pour les ménages modestes dès l'an dernier. Devant les rumeurs d'une interdiction pure et simple, le ministère de l'Économie a publié une mise au point : le découvert reste possible, sous un cadre nettement plus strict.
Découvert bancaire : ce que votre banque devra vérifier dès le 20 novembre
Selon la note publiée par Bercy, l'obligation d'analyser la solvabilité s'étend à tous les découverts, quels que soient leur montant et leur délai de remboursement. Revenus, charges, fonctionnement du compte : la banque fondera son accord sur votre situation réelle. Le contrôle reste proportionné. Sous 200 euros, la consultation du fichier des incidents de remboursement des crédits aux particuliers (FICP) deviendra facultative. Avant la signature, l'établissement remettra aussi une information complète sur le coût du découvert, son taux annuel effectif global (TAEG) et les conditions de remboursement.
	
L'autorisation de découvert n'a jamais été automatique : il n'existe pas de droit au crédit en France.
Le quotidien ne change pas pour autant. Une fois l'autorisation inscrite dans la convention de compte, aucune nouvelle demande n'est nécessaire à chaque passage dans le rouge, dans la limite prévue. Les autorisations accordées avant le 20 novembre restent valables. Plusieurs parlementaires redoutent malgré tout que les ménages les plus serrés en fin de mois se heurtent plus souvent à un refus. Certaines offres fonctionnent déjà sans aucun filet, comme le compte Nickel, qui ne propose pas de découvert autorisé.
Fin du forfait d'agios : une économie pour les petits découverts
C'est la face plus agréable de la réforme. Certaines banques prélèvent aujourd'hui un minimum forfaitaire d'agios : un montant fixe facturé dès que le compte passe dans le rouge, sur les découverts de moins de 400 euros, et supérieur, par construction, aux intérêts réellement dus. Il vient s'ajouter à des frais bancaires déjà orientés à la hausse. Dans sa réponse au Sénat publiée le 30 avril 2026, le ministère confirme que ces forfaits disparaissent et qu'ils seront intégrés au TAEG, lui-même plafonné par le taux d'usure. Pour un client qui passe régulièrement quelques dizaines d'euros sous zéro, la note peut fondre sensiblement.
Le texte protège également le titulaire d'un découvert à durée indéterminée que la banque réduit. Il pourra rembourser, sans frais supplémentaires, la part qui dépasse le nouveau plafond avant toute procédure d'exécution.
Le bon réflexe d'ici au 20 novembre : ouvrir la brochure tarifaire de sa banque à la rubrique "découvert" et repérer la ligne "minimum" ou "forfait". Elle devrait disparaître pour tout découvert accordé à partir de cette date.

articles.title: CrowdStrike Reportedly Paying $495 Million for AI Security Firms Fiddler, Dreadnode
articles.text:
CrowdStrike on Tuesday announced agreements to acquire AI agent observability firm Fiddler AI and AI security testing company Dreadnode, in deals reportedly worth a combined $495 million.
CrowdStrike has not disclosed the financial terms of either acquisition. According to The Wall Street Journal, which reported the deals ahead of the official announcements, the cybersecurity giant is paying roughly $400 million for Fiddler and about $95 million for Dreadnode.
CrowdStrike said both purchases will be paid mostly in cash, with a portion in stock subject to vesting conditions. The deals are expected to close in the fourth quarter of CrowdStrike’s fiscal year 2027, which ends on January 31, 2027.
Fiddler was founded in 2018 and is based in Palo Alto, California. In January, it announced a $30 million Series C round that brought its total funding to $100 million.
The company’s technology monitors AI agents and explains the decisions they make. CrowdStrike says Fiddler will add pre-deployment evaluation of agents, tracing of their reasoning and tool calls, and detection of behavioral drift and hallucinations in production.
It will also log agent activity for compliance audits and track token usage and spending. CrowdStrike plans to sell the technology as Falcon Observe.
Dreadnode, founded in 2023, develops offensive AI security tools. The startup raised $14 million in Series A funding in early 2025.
According to CrowdStrike, Dreadnode’s platform lets users describe in plain language what they want to test. It then runs more than 100 known AI attack strategies, including jailbreaks, prompt injection, and multi-turn and agent-specific attacks.
The tests target AI models, agent reasoning loops, applications and MCP servers. Findings are ranked by severity, mapped to frameworks such as the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, MITRE ATLAS and the NIST AI RMF, and fed to CrowdStrike’s Falcon Guardian AI detection and response product as policy recommendations.
The Dreadnode team, led by CEO Brad Palm, will join CrowdStrike’s Cyber Superintelligence Lab. Dreadnode-based testing capabilities are expected to become generally available in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027.
Alongside the acquisitions, CrowdStrike introduced an AI Kill Switch in Falcon Guardian that allows authorized administrators to halt a misbehaving AI agent, prevent it from restarting, and cut off its network access.
CrowdStrike has made several security acquisitions over the past year. In January, it announced plans to buy identity security firm SGNL for $740 million and browser security company Seraphic for a reported $420 million. In September 2025, it agreed to acquire AI security firm Pangea.
