articles.title: Attackers Target Unpatched CryptoPayment Gateway Flaw That Can Expose Wallet Credentials
articles.text:
Threat actors are attempting to exploit an unpatched maximum-severity security vulnerability in the CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin, according to findings from Defused Cyber.
The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-81648, which carries a CVSS score of 10.0. Successful exploitation of the flaw could permit unauthenticated users to delete arbitrary files on the server and extract sensitive data, including stored wallet credentials.
"The CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin from 1.2.1 to 1.2.2 does not apply an authorization check on one of its AJAX endpoints, allowing unauthenticated users to invoke administrative operations, including deleting arbitrary files on the server, overwriting the payment gateway configuration and recovering stored wallet credentials in cleartext," according to a description of the flaw on the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).
The vulnerability affects versions 1.2.1 through 1.2.2, which is the latest version. There are no known fixes for the flaw, according to WP Scan. As of August 28, 2026, the plugin has been closed on the WordPress Plugin Directory and is no longer available for download due to an unspecified "security issue."
Statistics show that the plugin has been collectively downloaded 1,845 times, including 20 downloads over the last seven days. It's unclear if it's actively installed on any WordPress sites.
"We are observing in-the-wild exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-81648, a critical (CVSS 10.0) flaw in the CryptoPayment Gateway for WordPress," Defused Cyber said in an X post. "The attacks we recorded came from infrastructure that markets themselves as 'Anonymous KYC-Free VPS Hosting.'"
In the absence of a fix, site owners are advised to remove the plugin, rotate wallet keys, and audit for any suspicious changes.

articles.title: Netflix tiene una nueva IA que elige qué ver según tu estado de ánimo
articles.text:
Uno de los problemas más grandes de Netflix y otros sistemas de video en streaming es encontrar qué ver. Las compañías han invertido en algoritmos que recomiendan series o películas basándose en nuestros gustos o en la lista de reproducción, pero muchas veces no es suficiente. Ahora Netflix quiere probar suerte con AI Discover, una nueva función impulsada por IA que te ayudará a encontrar contenido de forma más útil y personalizada.
De acuerdo con el comunicado de prensa, esta herramienta se integrará como una pestaña independiente dentro de la app de Netflix para televisores. A diferencia del algoritmo de recomendación, AI Discover se enfoca en el contexto y el estado de ánimo de las personas. Los usuarios solo tienen que indicarle a la IA cómo se sienten y el sistema se encargará del resto.
Al entrar en la nueva pestaña, Netflix mostrará una serie de temas o categorías genéricas construidos con inteligencia artificial. Algunos están relacionados con emociones o sensaciones, por ejemplo, "Algo ligero" para quienes desean ver una película "palomera" que no requiere pensar mucho. También existen otras para situaciones concretas, como noche de cine en familia, películas cortas o una llamada "Asústame", pensada para los aficionados al terror.
Cada tema incluye un avance de una película o serie que sirve de referencia para saber qué clase de contenido recomendará. Una vez que el usuario selecciona la opción, AI Discover genera una lista de recomendaciones basándose en ese criterio.
La experiencia puede refinarse aún más a partir de temas adicionales o situaciones específicas que ayuden a acotar los resultados de búsqueda. En caso de que no encuentres algo que te guste, podrás elegir "Algo diferente", que sugiere alternativas que se alejan de lo que ya conoces.
El AI Discover de Netflix es personalizable
Una de las características más llamativas de esta función es que permite entrenar las recomendaciones. Tal y como ocurre con las manitas hacia arriba y hacia abajo que encontramos en la interfaz de usuario, AI Discover incluirá un botón llamado "Ajusta tus recomendaciones", el cual permite indicar si la película o serie recomendada fue útil o de plano no volver a verla. Una vez que se guarda, la IA recordará las preferencias para no mostrar contenidos que no generan interés.
Netflix mencionó que la AI Discover se basa en una nueva capa de inteligencia artificial desarrollada internamente. El modelo responde en tiempo real a la información que proporciona el usuario y aprende con el uso. La compañía añadió que esta función es una especie de laboratorio que servirá para experimentar con nuevas formas para encontrar contenido.
A diferencia de las funciones de IA que encontramos en Spotify y otros servicios, AI Discover no tiene un chatbot. Uno esperaría que, al tratarse de una "experiencia personalizada", Netflix ofrecería un modo de "decirle" al sistema lo que queremos ver. Lamentablemente, los usuarios solo pueden desplazarse entre las recomendaciones y acotarlas, pero no tienen la opción de decirle “Recomiéndame películas de Jason Statham que duren menos de 90 minutos”.
Por el momento, AI Discover está en fase de pruebas en la app de Netflix para televisores con un número reducido de usuarios. Netflix señaló que algunas funciones específicas de esta herramienta podrían implementarse en la experiencia principal de la plataforma, siempre y cuando tengan una buena recepción entre los usuarios.

articles.title: Steam Survey shockwaves felt as proportion of 32GB RAM systems drops by more than 5% — the percentage of PC gamers with 1TB+ total storage also shrunk by nearly 5%
articles.text:
Steam Survey shockwaves felt as proportion of 32GB RAM systems drops by more than 5% — the percentage of PC gamers with 1TB+ total storage also shrunk by nearly 5%
The reduced RAM/storage trends have been set in retail for a number of months already.
The latest Steam Survey appears to show that gamers blessed with systems packing 32GB or more RAM and 1TB or more storage are a dwindling breed. This survey is posted without comment by Valve, as usual, but appears to show a significant proportional rise in gamers using 8GB and 16GB RAM PCs, which occurs largely at the expense of the 32GB brigade. The latest stats also show a noticeable increase in storage capacity poverty in the last month. Are the symptoms of the AI industry-induced components crunch now becoming evident among the PC gaming public?
The AI-pocalypse delivered components crunch has been in the headlines for months but it is still jarring to see it impact the vast PC gaming landscape. When we’ve browsed desktop and laptop PCs for the best gaming PC deals over the past months, the trend is clear. Systems that look like they are designed for gamers or enthusiasts are now frequently fitted with just 16GB of RAM as standard, and also feature smaller storage devices that one might have expected. But to see the Steam Survey suggesting that the share of 32GB systems has now collapsed by -5.16% is startling. Only last month, 32GB was the most popular configuration among gamers according to the same survey.
RAM is probably the hardest-hit component segment of AI-driven demand so far. We maintain a RAM price tracking page at Tom’s Hardware and the current state of the market means that DIYers or upgraders need to spend about $250 for 16GB DDR5 or $450 for 32GB DDR5. Those prices change regularly, as well.
Moving onto the sudden recorded change in storage configurations in use by Steam gamers, and we see that folks with 1TB of total fixed storage space or above shrunk by 4.68%. As the categories are currently defined, this appears to show the reduction in the number of systems coming with either a 2TB and 4TB SSD as standard. That’s because the 750GB to 999GB category grew +2.36%, and Windows registers a '1TB' boot disk as a smaller (a quick check shows ours at 924GB). 250GB to 499GB total storage systems were also up a similar amount (+2.30%). Overall, it looks like systems being used for Steam gaming are increasingly fitted with these smaller capacity SSDs. Enthusiasts, gamers, and DIYers wanting to expand their storage at the best prices are advised to keep an eye on our frequently updated SSD price tracking page.
We are currently seeing some extraordinary things in the GPU market, with reports of RTX 5090 and RTX 5080 cards being removed from retail. In the Steam Survey this month the RTX 5080 is still at position 14. However, the joint most popular GPUs are the RTX 5070 and the aging RTX 3060 – both with 3.78% of the market.
We are aware that there are sometimes some strong undercurrents in the Steam Survey that cause unusual fluctuations in the figures. However, the numbers this month don’t look like they have been impacted by a Chinese user or Chinese internet café PC influx, which have previously shown odd trends (such as a rise in Windows 10 usage). Actually, the Steam Survey shows Chinese (Simplified) language users surveyed are sharply down this month, so the survey should more accurately represent the system configurations typical among gamers in the West.

articles.title: Apple doesn't know when it will have a resupply of iPhone Duos
articles.text:
Apple CEO John Ternus has just revealed that he doesn’t know when they will have a resupply of the popular iPhone Duo.
According to an interview with Reuters that was reported on by The Verge, Ternus said that the company is “working hard to get it to as many customers as possible,” but also said that it’s “not able to predict when supply and demand will be in balance.”
To add some context, Apple launched the foldable phone last month for $3,000, the most expensive smartphone in the country, but pre-orders quickly sold out, with wait times extending into late January 2027 for Canada. The Duo also saw a wide range of social media reports that screens were suddenly cracking, and that a piece in the hinge mechanism was protruding into the Duo’s screen’s folding area upon failure, causing the crack.
During the interview, Ternus addressed the screen issue, saying that a “very small percentage” of devices had been sent back to Apple for the problem and that the company is replacing them.
Ternus also discussed the company’s supply chain and rising memory costs during its Q4 2026 earnings call. “What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” he said, adding that the company expects to see “even higher memory costs” during its December quarter, but that is “partly offset” by recent price increases.
Even without the standard iPhone 18 model, though, the company recorded record-breaking iPhone revenue of US$57.58 billion (approx. C$80.62 billion) in its fourth quarter.

Il existait déjà des vans de loisir électriques, mais en version allégée. Volkswagen l’a montré avec l’ID. California Cruise, qui fait l’impasse sur une partie de l’équipement. Le Kia PV5 i-Camper, dévoilé fin octobre par Wellhouse Leisure, une entreprise familiale britannique qui aménage des fourgons, fait le choix inverse avec deux lits doubles et une vraie cuisine. C’est une rivale directe des Volkswagen California et Mercedes Marco Polo, pour moins cher.
Wellhouse part du PV5 Cargo (on a essayé le Kia PV5), le premier utilitaire 100 % électrique de Kia, avec sa grande batterie de 71,2 kWh et son moteur de 163 ch. Kia annonce jusqu’à 416 km d’autonomie WLTP pour cette configuration, et une recharge de 10 à 80 % en une trentaine de minutes sur borne rapide. Par contre, Wellhouse ne dit pas ce qu’il en reste une fois les meubles et le toit installés (et ça pèse). Avec 4,69 mètres de long, le van reste plus court qu’un California.
    Pour aller plus loin

Une cuisine complète en moins de 4,7 mètres
La banquette arrière coulisse sur des rails et se rabat à plat pour former un premier lit double. Le second se déplie sous le toit relevable.
Côté cuisine, Electrek détaille, photos à l’appui, deux plaques à induction, un évier avec pompe électrique, un réfrigérateur de 42 litres et un micro-ondes en option. Moins cher que le Marco Polo, au prix du California

Wellhouse ne donne qu’un tarif britannique et ne parle pas d’une vente en France. Kia a de son côté confirmé deux camping-cars maison sur base PV5, le Light Camper et le Camper, sans date ni prix.

articles.title: Plus de 9 000 liens signalés, Europol s’attaque à la propagande terroriste dans les jeux vidéo
articles.text:
Europol a coordonné une vaste opération contre la propagande terroriste diffusée dans les jeux vidéo en ligne. En mobilisant 16 pays, plus de 9 000 liens ont été signalés vers des jeux de rôle extrémistes susceptibles de servir au recrutement.
Europol s'attaque aux jeux de rôle terroristes qui se jouent sur les plateformes de jeu vidéo et les réseaux sociaux. L'agence a dévoilé ce mardi 3 novembre le bilan d'une journée d'action menée avec l'Espagne notamment contre le « LARPing » extrémiste, du nom anglais du jeu de rôle grandeur nature, transposé ici dans des univers virtuels où l'on se glisse dans la peau d'un membre de groupe terroriste. Sous ses airs de divertissement entre joueurs, la pratique sert aussi à diffuser de la propagande et à recruter, jusque chez les mineurs. Des milliers de liens ont été transmis aux services concernés.
Plus de 9 000 liens signalés sur 47 plateformes
Aux commandes de l'opération, il y avait l'EU IRU, l'unité d'Europol chargée de repérer les contenus terroristes en ligne et de les signaler aux sites qui les hébergent. Pour cette « journée de signalement », menée aux côtés de l'Espagne, elle a fédéré des unités spécialisées de 16 pays. Plus de 9 000 liens, c'est-à-dire des adresses web menant à des publications ou vidéos problématiques, ont été repérés sur 47 réseaux sociaux et plateformes de jeu, puis transmis aux plateformes concernées.
Ces contenus sont aussi bien portés par des individus esseulés que des groupes, des réseaux ou des organisations, avec un éventail idéologique très large, qui va du djihadisme à l'ultradroite, en passant par l'ultragauche et la mouvance anarchiste.
Dans ces communautés, le jeu vidéo devient une scène de théâtre au service de l'extrémisme. Les joueurs y reproduisent l'organisation d'un groupe terroriste, ses symboles et ses récits, c'est-à-dire la façon dont il raconte et justifie sa cause. Ils vont jusqu'à rejouer des attentats. Ce qui ressemble d'abord à une simple partie peut ensuite se structurer. Des contenus de propagande sont fabriqués puis diffusés, et l'on cherche à attirer de nouveaux membres, mineurs compris. Europol considère qu'en plongeant les joueurs dans ces idéologies à travers une expérience interactive, où l'on agit au lieu de simplement regarder, ces communautés contribuent à la radicalisation.
Europol signale, mais ce sont les plateformes qui tranchent
La portée de l'opération conduite par Europol doit tout de même être nuancée, car un signalement n'équivaut pas forcément à une suppression. L'agence européenne alerte les plateformes qui hébergent les contenus, et c'est à elles de décider de les retirer, ou non. L'enjeu, selon Europol, est d'enrayer la diffusion de cette propagande avant qu'elle ne serve à recruter ou à pousser au passage à l'acte violent. Le communiqué de ce 3 novembre ne nomme ni les plateformes ni les jeux concernés, pas plus qu'il ne chiffre les retraits effectifs.
Ce n'est pas une première dans le genre pour Europol, qui avait déjà mené une première opération sur ce phénomène en 2025. Ces « journées de signalement » font partie d'un programme au long cours de l'EU IRU, qui s'attaque tour à tour aux différentes formes de propagande terroriste en ligne. Dans le TE-SAT 2026, son rapport annuel sur l'état du terrorisme dans l'Union européenne, Europol classe d'ailleurs l'exploitation des jeux vidéo en ligne parmi les menaces émergentes, autrement dit un danger récent, encore en train de se dessiner.
De son côté, la Commission européenne, dans son programme antiterroriste ProtectEU présenté en 2026, appelle à travailler plus étroitement avec l'industrie du jeu vidéo. Pour traduire ces priorités en actions concrètes, comme cette journée de signalement, l'EU IRU s'appuie sur un réseau spécialisé, l'Online Gaming Network. D’autres journées de signalement devraient suivre prochainement.

articles.title: “No podemos predecir cuándo se equilibrarán la oferta y la demanda”: CEO de Apple, sobre el iPhone Duo
articles.text:
Apple enfrenta dificultades para satisfacer la demanda de su primer teléfono plegable, el iPhone Duo. Los pedidos del dispositivo superaron las previsiones de la compañía y los plazos de entrega se extendieron hasta finales de enero de 2027. Ante esta situación, John Ternus, director ejecutivo de la empresa, reconoció que todavía no puede determinar cuándo se normalizará el abastecimiento.
“No podemos predecir cuándo se equilibrarán la oferta y la demanda”, afirmó Ternus en una entrevista con Reuters. El directivo explicó que Apple trabaja para incrementar la producción, aunque existen dificultades para responder al interés que despertó el nuevo dispositivo entre los compradores.
El problema representa un desafío para la compañía, que busca consolidar su entrada en el mercado de los celulares plegables. A diferencia de otros lanzamientos, el iPhone Duo llega con una demanda que supera la capacidad de fabricación disponible, mientras Apple también enfrenta el encarecimiento de componentes necesarios para producir sus equipos.
El iPhone Duo agotó sus reservas en pocos minutos
El primer teléfono plegable de Apple generó una fuerte expectativa desde que se habilitaron las reservas. Según señalaron varios usuarios, los pedidos iniciales se agotaron en pocos minutos y los tiempos de espera comenzaron a extenderse conforme aumentaba la cantidad de compradores.
Los plazos de entrega llegaron hasta finales de enero de 2027, una señal de que la compañía no consigue abastecer el mercado al ritmo que exige la demanda.
Ternus señaló que Apple está trabajando para aumentar la producción, pero evitó comprometerse con una fecha para recuperar la normalidad. La compañía todavía debe ajustar su capacidad de fabricación para responder a los pedidos pendientes y evitar que los compradores tengan que esperar varios meses para recibir el dispositivo.
La situación resulta relevante porque el iPhone Duo representa una nueva categoría de producto para Apple. La empresa busca competir en un segmento donde fabricantes como Samsung ya cuentan con varios años de experiencia y diferentes generaciones de celulares plegables.
La inteligencia artificial también encarece la fabricación
Otro factor que complica la producción del iPhone Duo es el aumento del precio de determinados componentes electrónicos, especialmente las memorias RAM.
La expansión de los centros de datos dedicados a inteligencia artificial ha incrementado la demanda mundial de chips de memoria. Estas infraestructuras necesitan grandes cantidades de componentes para procesar información y ejecutar modelos de IA, lo que genera una mayor presión sobre la disponibilidad y los costos.
Ternus describió el encarecimiento de estos componentes como una situación sin precedentes y reconoció que está teniendo consecuencias sobre los costos de fabricación de Apple.
Este escenario afecta a toda la industria tecnológica. Los fabricantes de celulares, computadoras y otros dispositivos deben competir por el acceso a componentes que también son utilizados por las empresas que desarrollan infraestructura para inteligencia artificial.
En el caso del iPhone Duo, el problema se suma a las dificultades propias de fabricar un celular plegable, cuya estructura y pantalla requieren procesos de producción específicos.
Apple también enfrenta reportes de problemas en la pantalla
A las dificultades de abastecimiento se agregaron reportes de usuarios que detectaron roturas en la pantalla interior del iPhone Duo. Algunos compradores informaron daños en el panel flexible, lo que generó interrogantes sobre la resistencia del dispositivo.
Apple indicó que los casos corresponden a un porcentaje muy pequeño de las unidades comercializadas y habilitó reemplazos sin costo para los afectados, incluso para quienes no cuentan con AppleCare+.
Aunque la compañía sostiene que los inconvenientes no representan un problema generalizado, estos reportes llegan en un momento delicado para el lanzamiento. La disponibilidad limitada y las dudas sobre la durabilidad de la pantalla pueden influir en la percepción de los compradores interesados en adquirir el primer plegable de Apple.
Los ingresos del iPhone también reflejan el interés por sus dispositivos
La demanda del iPhone Duo se produce en un contexto en el que el negocio de celulares continúa siendo una de las principales fuentes de ingresos de Apple.
Según los resultados financieros de la compañía de Cupertino, la división del iPhone registró ingresos de 57.580 millones de dólares durante el cuarto trimestre de 2026.
El desafío para Ternus será mantener el interés por el nuevo dispositivo mientras la compañía incrementa su capacidad de fabricación y enfrenta el encarecimiento de los componentes.
Por ahora, Apple no tiene una fecha concreta para equilibrar la oferta y la demanda del iPhone Duo. La respuesta dependerá de cuánto pueda acelerar su producción y de cómo evolucione el suministro de las piezas necesarias para fabricar el dispositivo.

articles.title: Hacienda obliga a tributar por las propinas que reciben los trabajadores, pero cotizarán si lo recoge el convenio o las gestiona la empresa
articles.text:
Cualquier tipo de propina que reciban los trabajadores de bares y restaurantes tiene repercusiones fiscales. Es decir, que aunque los clientes den la propina de manera voluntaria, esto va a suponer que los trabajadores deben tenerlo en cuenta a la hora de calcular los rendimientos del trabajo (impuesto sobre la renta de las personas físicas). Además de ello, debe analizarse si deben cotizar a la Seguridad Social.
El IRPF alcanza a las propinas
En primer lugar, en el artículo 17.1 de la Ley del IRPF están incluidas las cantidades que provienen directa o indirectamente de la relación de trabajo o del propio trabajo personal. Es decir, que además de los salarios se incluyen otros rendimientos relacionados con el trabajo (utilidades). En este sentido, las propinas que reciben de los clientes van a estar sujetas al IRPF.
Además, están previstas las retenciones. En efecto, en el artículo 76 del Reglamento del IRPF se habla de los casos en que el que realiza la actividad económica tiene que abonar a sus trabajadores las cantidades que los terceros le entreguen en concepto de propinas. En el caso de que sean repartidas por la empresa, deberá realizar en su caso la correspondiente retención (que se ingresará en Hacienda).
Es importante destacar que estar sometido a IRPF quiere decir que están en la base de dicho impuesto. Sin embargo, no es necesario que haya obligación de presentar la declaración (ver artículo 96 de la ley).
La propina voluntaria queda fuera de la base del IVA
En el impuesto sobre el valor añadido (IVA) es diferente. En efecto, las cantidades que el cliente entrega de manera voluntaria (y que no son exigibles por el servicio) no entran en la contraprestación que el restaurante recibe.
En este sentido, la Dirección General de Tributos en consulta 2174-03 de 11 de diciembre de 2003 ha indicado que estas cantidades no entran en la base imponible del servicio de hostelería.
Cuándo puede haber cotización
Para ello es necesario analizar la naturaleza de este ingreso. En primer lugar, en el artículo 147 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social se indica que en la base están incluidas las remuneraciones que corresponden al trabajador por su empleo. Por otro lado, la gratificación que hace el cliente de manera voluntaria puede ser extrasalarial y, si se configura como una remuneración empresarial, será diferente.
Carlos Déniz, del departamento laboral de Garrigues, indica que en el caso de que sea el propio cliente el que la entrega al trabajador (sin que intervenga la empresa), es diferente. En el caso de que se configure como retribución, es salario (y, por tanto, debe cotizar).
También es importante analizar cómo se gestiona el reparto y cómo está previsto en el convenio que resulte de aplicación. Sin embargo, no es cierto que todo bote gestionado por la empresa sea salario. Es necesario ver qué se paga y bajo qué condiciones.

articles.title: India's data centre capacity set for 5x surge by 2030: Crisil
articles.text:
India's data centre capacity set for 5x surge by 2030: Crisil
The growth of data centres in India will also depend on factors like timely power supply, regulatory clearances and project execution capabilities.
India's data centre industry is poised for an unprecedented investment boom, with installed capacity expected to increase five-fold to around 7.5 gigawatts (GW) by March 2030, attracting investments of more than Rs 3 lakh crore over the next four financial years, Crisil Ratings said in a report on Tuesday.
The expansion, fuelled by generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), enterprise digitalisation and rising data consumption, is set to transform the country's digital infrastructure landscape.
However, the industry's ability to translate demand into sustainable returns will depend critically on timely power connectivity, regulatory clearances and disciplined project execution.
"Nearly half of the upcoming capacity is already committed under long-term contracts, limiting speculative development and reducing offtake risk," Crisil Ratings said. "Upfront tie-ups with hyperscalers, driven by cloud adoption and compute-intensive GenAI workloads, provide revenue certainty from the outset. This helps de-risk projects, even as the scale and speed of the planned build-out intensify execution requirements."
Strong demand from global hyperscalers, driven by cloud adoption and increasingly compute-intensive GenAI workloads, is also supporting investment decisions and reducing offtake uncertainty.
India's competitive cost structure is adding to its appeal as a data centre destination. Development costs are around 20 per cent lower than in several competing Asia-Pacific markets, reflecting relatively competitive land, construction and labour costs. Combined with lower power tariffs, this enables rental rates to be 30-35 per cent below those in peer markets. The availability of large campuses powered by renewable energy also strengthens India's proposition for hyperscalers seeking to meet sustainability commitments.
Says Anand Kulkarni, Director, Crisil Ratings, "India's structural cost advantages further strengthen its attractiveness as a data centre destination. Development costs are around one-fifth lower than in several competing Asia-Pacific markets owing to more competitive land, construction and labour costs.”
He further said, “Combined with lower power tariffs, this translates into rentals that are 30-35 per cent lower than in peer markets. The ability to develop large, renewable-powered campuses also aligns well with the sustainability goals of hyperscalers, reinforcing India's competitive positioning."
However, the scale of the planned expansion is placing considerable pressure on power infrastructure. Nearly three-fourths of the approximately 6 GW of upcoming capacity is expected to be concentrated in Visakhapatnam, Mumbai and Hyderabad, Crisil said.
By fiscal 2030, data centre capacity in these cities could be equivalent to around 80%, 60% and 20%, respectively, of their current peak electricity demand. This concentration makes timely grid connectivity and transmission capacity augmentation critical to avoiding commissioning delays and cost overruns.

articles.title: La carrera espacial privada tiene cada vez más “juguetes”: pronto tendrá también un telescopio en el espacio
articles.text:
La carrera espacial ya no es solo cosa de las grandes agencias públicas, como la NASA o la ESA. Las compañías privadas están teniendo un papel cada vez más relevante, especialmente en lo que respecta al desarrollo de cohetes y satélites. Hasta ahora, uno de los pocos terrenos inexplorados para el sector privado era el de los telescopios espaciales. Sin embargo, si todo va bien, eso cambiará muy pronto con el lanzamiento de Lazuli, el telescopio desarrollado por Schmidt Sciences para estudiar los exoplanetas que otros no han podido analizar en profundidad.
23 colores. Lazuli dispondrá de un espejo primario de 3 metros, por lo que es más grande que el del Hubble, y será capaz de observar el cielo en 23 colores, desde la luz visible hasta el infrarrojo cercano. También dispondrá de un espectrógrafo, que le permitirá discernir la composición de los objetos celestes gracias al análisis de la luz que estos emiten o reflejan.
Su instrumento principal. Más allá de su amplio rango de colores y su análisis espectral, Lazuli destaca por un instrumento llamado ExtraSolar Coronagraph (ESC). Su objetivo es bloquear la luz de estrellas lejanas para que esta no interfiera con la luz que reflejan los planetas que giran en torno a ellas. Dicho a muy grosso modo, creará pequeños eclipses artificiales para centrar toda la atención en los exoplanetas que se quieran analizar.
27 candidatos. Dos científicos de las Universidades de Michigan y Arizona han publicado recientemente un estudio en el que se exponen 27 exoplanetas gigantes que serían candidatos ideales para que Lazuli los estudie. Esto no quiere decir que sean necesariamente los que se van a estudiar, pero sí parecen ser buenos candidatos.
Gigantes fríos. Por limitaciones técnicas relacionadas con el tiempo y el enfoque, la mayoría de exoplanetas en los que se centran los telescopios espaciales son Júpiter calientes. Estos exoplanetas están muy cerca de su estrella, por lo que tienen tránsitos más cortos y dan más vueltas alrededor de la estrella por unidad de tiempo que un planeta que se encuentra más lejos. Esto hace más fácil detectarlos.
El problema es que los gigantes de nuestro sistema solar, Júpiter y Saturno, están mucho más lejos del Sol. Por lo tanto, sus características son bastante diferentes. Lo ideal sería estudiar los gigantes gaseosos fríos. Hasta ahora era un reto técnico, pero Lazuli sí está mejor preparado para hacerlo gracias a su coronógrafo, que le permite captar la luz tenue de planetas lejanos. Los 27 candidatos son precisamente de este tipo.
Más instrumentos. Lazuli trabajará en equipo junto con otros instrumentos desarrollados también por Schmidt Sciences: los arrays ópticos terrestres Argus y LFAST y el radiotelescopio Deep Synoptic Array. Todos ellos compartirán software y datos, de modo que un hallazgo de uno pueda seguirse fácilmente con otro.
También agencias públicas. En el estudio que han hecho estos científicos, aún sin revisión por pares, señalan que otros telescopios que ya están en funcionamiento podrían trabajar igualmente sobre los mismos candidatos. Es, por ejemplo, el caso del recién estrenado Nancy Grace Roman o del veterano Very Large Telescope (VLT). De nuevo, los datos podrán compartirse, para que telescopios públicos y privados trabajen en equipo.
La fecha. Aún no hay una fecha definitiva para la puesta en marcha de Lazuli. No obstante, si todo va bien, Schmidt Sciences espera poder lanzarlo en 2028 o, como mucho, 2029. Hasta entonces, se seguirá trabajando tanto en su desarrollo como en la búsqueda de candidatos para que pueda analizarlos.

articles.title: Fibre cuts threaten Nigeria's digital economy, who pays?
articles.text:
When Nigeria’s president, Bola Tinubu, signed the Designation and Protection of Critical National Information Infrastructure (CNII) Order in June 2024, the Federal Government aimed to shield telecommunications assets from relentless vandalism and physical damage. By classifying fibre lines, base stations, and data centres as vital national security installations, the order sought to impose deterrent penalties and curb unauthorised tampering.
Yet two years on, chronic breaches continue to impose steep financial penalties on operators, diverting capital from network expansion to nonstop emergency repairs and destabilising internet reliability across the country.
In 2023, before the order, MTN Nigeria suffered more than 6,000 fibre cuts in a single year—averaging roughly 16-17 severed lines per day.
Fast-forward to 2025, past the presidential order: the numbers increased; between January and July, the telco recorded 5,478 fibre cuts. That pushed its daily average to over 26 snapped cables.
In plain terms, instead of scaring reckless diggers and vandals away and improving coordination between construction firms and other key stakeholders, the new rules led MTN Nigeria to fix about eight more broken cables per day than before the order was introduced.
The broader telecoms industry recorded 19,384 cuts between January and August 2025, further pushing the daily average to 80. In the first nine months of 2026 alone, Telecom networks suffered over 44,000 fibre cuts—averaging more than 160 cuts every single day, mostly from uncoordinated road construction, ditch digging, and theft. The primary culprits remain uncoordinated civil engineering projects, road expansions, and persistent vandalism.
These disruptions expose significant enforcement gaps, raising a central question of who ultimately pays when statutory protections fail to stop contractors and vandals from repeatedly severing the nation’s digital backbone
Building on Tinubu’s signing of the executive order, the legal framework establishes vital statutory mechanisms to defend the nation’s digital backbone.
Under the CNII Order, telecommunications assets—including submarine landing cables, terrestrial fibre-optic lines, switching centres, and data storage hubs—are formally designated as vital national security installations.
The framework empowers security agencies, led by the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), to monitor, inspect, and defend digital infrastructure against willful destruction, uncoordinated civil works, and cyber-physical intrusions.
Even so, its ultimate success hinges on swift and consistent prosecution.
Fibre cuts drain expansion capital
Constant network degradation forces telecommunications operators to absorb substantial operational costs, squeezing capital investment. In the first half of 2026, direct repairs across 5,934 fibre incidents cost operators over ₦2.2 billion ($1.64 million).
These emergency expenses undermine the ₦2.13 trillion ($1.58 billion) in capital expenditure committed by network and tower companies, diverting critical resources from new rollouts to restoring existing footprints.
This financial drain has a long track record; it is not new. According to the GSMA Nigeria Digital Economy Report, MTN Nigeria spent ₦11.1 billion ($8.26 million) repairing and relocating 2,502 kilometres of fibre across 2022 and 2023. That figure comprised ₦4.4 billion ($3.27 million) for 1,069 km in 2022 and ₦6.7 billion ($4.98 million) for 1,433 km in 2023—money that GSMA notes could have funded 870 kilometres of greenfield fibre in underserved communities.
Across the wider industry, losses in 2023 alone reached an estimated ₦27 billion ($20.08 million) in direct repairs and lost revenue.
The economic stakes are huge for a country where its ICT sector delivered over ₦6 trillion ($4.46 billion) in real output in Q2 2026, with telecoms contributing 9.72% (₦5.20 trillion / $3.87 billion) to total real GDP: every severed cable is no longer just a temporary network glitch, but an immediate drag on national GDP.
Connectivity gap worsens local challenges
Nigeria’s infrastructure struggles unfold against broader regional constraints. A recent GSMA report on African spectrum policy highlighted that African operators averaged 570 MHz of spectrum below 7 GHz in 2025—far below the global baseline of 750 MHz—while paying 24% more per unit of spectrum. GSMA cautions that every 10% increase in spectrum costs relative to revenue trims 5G coverage expansion by six percentage points.
Fast 5G networks require robust underground cabling to ensure that banking apps, POS machines, and online money transfers work instantly and without failure.
Underlying infrastructure carried massive financial volumes in early 2026: transactions on the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS) surpassed ₦1.053 quadrillion ($783.2 billion) in Q1 alone, alongside millions of daily mobile money and point-of-sale payments. Governed by a 23-year-old regulatory model dating back to the 2G voice era, the sector is directly threatened by physical fibre cuts, which directly threaten overall financial stability.
Fibre backhaul links network base stations directly to core data centres. When cables are cut, the impact cascades into dropped voice calls, crippled data throughput, and widespread service outages.
For enterprises, cuts mean payment gateways collapsing, staff hours lost, and cloud downtime. For subscribers, disruptions translate into sluggish connections, failed payments, and paying higher rates for diminished service.
These disruptions compound consumer frustration following the NCC’s tariff revision, which permitted price hikes of up to 50% to offset soaring operational costs. When operators sink recurring revenue into avoidable repairs, network optimisation stalls, and users pay the price through degraded reliability.
Why has the CNII Order not solved the problem?
The NCC acknowledged the continuing challenge of stakeholder coordination in its August 2026 intervention: “Our interests are aligned; what has too often been missing is a dependable system of early coordination,” said the Executive Vice Chairman of the Nigerian Communications Commission, Aminu Maida.
But coordination can only work when manpower is adequate. The NSCDC’s limited manpower and operational resources expose the enforcement challenges facing one of Nigeria’s agencies tasked with protecting critical national infrastructure.
With roughly 63,000 personnel deployed across 774 local government areas to manage a broad range of national security duties, dedicated static protection for thousands of kilometres of buried fibre is logistically impossible. Even with its efforts on surveillance technology and systematic prosecution, legal protection on paper cannot secure infrastructure without adequate personnel.
The government must therefore measure the success of the CNII Order by tangible results: fewer cuts, faster remediation, and lower repair bills. Until enforcement deters would-be offenders, operators will keep burning through capital on repeated repairs instead of expanding coverage—leaving subscribers to foot the bill for an unprotected digital economy.

articles.title: Reddit tells Australian court it isn't a social media site, calls the country's under-16 ban "ill thought out" and "inept"
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Reddit is continuing its long-running legal fight against Australia over the country's ban on under-16s using social media. The company has called the rule "ill thought out" and "inept," while repeating its earlier argument that Reddit is not a social media platform.
Australia passed its under-16 social media law in 2024, and the restrictions took effect on December 10, 2025, making it the first country to introduce a ban that has since spread around the world.
The law requires platforms including Facebook, Instagram, Kick, Reddit, Snapchat, Threads, TikTok, Twitch, X (formerly Twitter), and YouTube to take reasonable steps to prevent Australians under 16 from creating or keeping accounts. Companies that fail to do so face court-imposed civil penalties of up to AU$109.2 million (about $76 million).
Unsurprisingly, these companies weren't happy about the change, especially Reddit. Soon after the law was introduced, Steve Huffman's firm challenged the law, emphasized that the platform is a "collection of public fora," rather than a social media site. It also filed a lawsuit in Australia's High Court to overturn the ban or, failing that, make itself exempt.
Reddit and a libertarian advocacy group say the law should be declared invalid because it violates an implied freedom of political expression in the country's constitution.
As for why it shouldn't qualify as a social media site, Reddit says it lacks certain features central to the likes of Facebook, including a reliance on friend networks.
Australia's eSafety Commission has published flowcharts to help companies establish whether they fall under the ban. Based on these criteria, Reddit would likely qualify as an age-restricted social media platform.
Reddit's legal team added that the ban prevented under-16s from posting or replying on platforms it described as the most important means of communication today.
"That is a very profound restriction on political debate in Australia," said Perry Herzfeld, representing Reddit. "There is a very substantial restriction on what young people can now do."
It's also argued that the ban simply isn't having the desired effect of keeping kids off social media. That claim is supported by studies, including one in April that found 61%, or three in five, Australian 12- to 15-year-olds who had accounts on restricted platforms before the ban came into force still have access to one or more accounts.
Reddit said the law did not call for any specific measure to keep out minors, and noted that vast amounts of material on social media were visible to those with no accounts.
"If the Commonwealth is worried about particular features (of social media), it should regulate the features, which it has not done," Herzfeld said.
The questions over how well Australia's ban is working haven't stopped other countries from following its lead. France voted in July to keep under-15s off social media, while the UK plans to introduce its own ban in spring 2027.
Norway, Greece, and Spain are some of the nations to have announced similar plans. Canada proposed an under-16 ban in June, though platforms could apply for an exemption if they can show they have enough safeguards in place to protect kids.

articles.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra : Samsung s'inspirerait en partie de l'iPhone 18 Pro
articles.text:
Le média Android Headlines a reproduit un Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra à partir des plans qui ont fuité ces derniers mois. De quoi prendre en main le téléphone avant même sa sortie, mais aussi de se rendre compte de ce à quoi il ressemblera. Ce smartphone Samsung reprendrait même un élément de design inspiré de l’iPhone 18 Pro.
Un design qui ressemblera un peu plus à l’iPhone 18 Pro
Premier point, la taille : elle ne changerait quasiment pas par rapport au Galaxy S26 Ultra, et aurait des dimensions de 163,76 par 78,25 par 7,97 mm. Mais le point qui change surtout est le bloc photo à l’arrière. Finie la longue barre verticale avec trois objectifs : tout serait réuni de manière plus compacte dans une sorte de rectangle. Un peu comme un certain iPhone 18 Pro arrivé en septembre dernier. Oui, Samsung reprendrait cet élément popularisé par Apple sur son futur téléphone haut de gamme.
Avec un bloc photo réhaussé, cela laisserait de la place à des aimants intégrés pour avoir de la recharge magnétique et pourquoi pas une meilleure compatibilité avec les accessoires MagSafe. Aujourd’hui, Samsung ne peut pas mettre de véritables aimants Qi2 sur son modèle Ultra, à cause de l’emplacement pour le S Pen. Les aimants peuvent en effet interférer avec le stylet. Avec le nouveau design, les accessoires pourront mieux se connecter, ce qui évitera de la chauffe, mais aussi une charge lente avec les batteries externes. Autre amélioration attendue avec ce nouveau bloc photo, la stabilité : posé sur une table, ce bloc photo serait plus stable puisqu’il prendrait toute la largeur du téléphone.
Le dernier indice que nous donne cette maquette du Galaxy S27 Ultra, le volet photo du smartphone. On remarque qu’un capteur manque à l’appel : il s’agirait du téléobjectif x3 que Samsung abandonnerait. La marque conserverait néanmoins le capteur principal de 200 Mpx, l’ultra grand-angle de 50 Mpx et le téléobjectif x5 de 50 Mpx. Un choix qui s’explique par le fait que le capteur 200 Mpx, en zoomant numériquement dedans, peut remplacer un téléobjectif x3 ; c’est aussi une petite économie pour le constructeur.
Ce qu’on sait du Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra
Ce Galaxy S27 Ultra conserverait un écran d’environ 6,9 pouces et Samsung travaillerait sur un Privacy Display v2. Cet écran de confidentialité proposerait de meilleurs angles de vision, une meilleure résolution lorsque la protection est activée, et surtout une image plus claire. Côté performances, le téléphone embarquerait le Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, la dernière puce haut de gamme de Qualcomm, tandis que d’autres sources évoquent un Exynos 2700 de Samsung pour certains marché. Une puce alimentée par une batterie de 5 700 mAh à 5 800 mAh environ, contre 5 000 mAh sur le Galaxy S26 Ultra. Une batterie plus grosse qui pourrait offrir une autonomie un peu meilleure.
Quant à la date de sortie, on s’attend à la période entre janvier et février comme c’est le cas chaque année. Ce Galaxy S27 Ultra serait livré avec One UI 9.5, surcouche de Samsung basée sur Android 17. Avec la hausse du prix des composants et de la crise de la RAM, on peut s’attendre à des tarifs plus élevés que l’année dernière, sans qu’aucune fuite ne vienne corroborer cette hypothèse pour le moment.

articles.title: Google Launches LiteRT Tensor API for Building, Customizing, and Optimizing ML Models for On-Device
articles.text:
Google has introduced the LiteRT Tensor API, a lightweight C++ API that allows developers to build, customize, and optimize machine learning models directly for on-device execution. According to Google, it combines the flexibility of native model authoring with cross-platform portability.
The traditional approach, Google says, is for developers to write computations manually in C++ for maximum control, which comes with a significant drawback:
Implementations are tightly coupled to specific backends (such as Metal, OpenCL, or Vulkan) and must be rewritten for each new hardware target. Furthermore, managing zero-copy buffer interoperability and synchronization across CPU, GPU, and NPU, while gluing together pre-processing, inference, and post-processing, demands substantial manual engineering effort.
The LiteRT Tensor API aims to address these challenges by allowing developers to build computation graphs operation by operation in C++. This provided greater control over model architecture, optimization, and accelerator execution, while enabling the same graphs to run through LiteRT on CPU, GPU, and NPU hardware without requiring a rewrite for each new target.
Beyond providing full control over model graphs, other key capabilities of the API include direct weight ingestion, allowing developers to load weights directly from checkpoints, including Hugging Face .safetensors files; zero-copy buffer interoperability, which avoids copying accelerator buffers across pre-processing, inference, and post-processing; and compatibility with AI coding agents, which can construct, modify, validate, and benchmark model graphs by generating C++ code.
Google used a coding agent to create a real-world app demonstrating how to use the LiteRT Tensor API for multi-object segmentation and tracking. The application also served as the basis for benchmarking performance across platforms:
We ran the same C++ code for the SAM 2 model on the GPUs of three devices: a macOS laptop (Metal), an iOS phone (Metal), and an Android phone (OpenCL). In our tests on the MacBook Pro, it ran about 1.5x faster than Apple MLX (fp16, image encoder plus mask decoder).
Google emphasized the fact that the coding agent could make a number of optimizations thanks to the model graph being defined in plain C++. Specifically, it "moved SAM 2's per-frame decisions, such as whether the object is still visible, from CPU code into the graph" and rewrote operations that triggered CPU fallback on WebGPU using GPU-compatible arithmetics.
Commenting on the announcement on LinkedIn, Arm director of AI Laurence Moroney emphasized that developers should always start with model conversion and turn to the C++ API only "when you need graph-level control or want pre and post-processing to stay on the accelerator". He also highlighted the benefits of defining model graphs in plain C++:
Going from under 10 to over 30 frames per second at 512x512 on WebGPU, with a coding agent doing the iteration, shows how much structured primitives help agents do real optimization work.
Google is also working on several planned improvmeents, including direct ML Drift backend support, additional NPU-friendly operations, automatic full-graph quantization, and expanded dynamic-shape for different image sizes, batch sizes, and sequence lengths.

articles.title: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
articles.text:
The New York Times and other newspaper companies sued Brave Software yesterday, alleging that the browser maker illegally bypasses paywalls and sells stolen news content to AI companies.
“Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content for its own users and many of the most prominent GenAI companies, including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere,” the NYT alleged in a lawsuit filed in US District Court for the Southern District of New York. Citing third-party revenue estimates, the suit claimed that “Brave has made more than $100 million by copying and reselling publishers’ work without consent or permission,” while “publishers have received nothing.”
The lawsuit said, “AI companies pay Brave to provide them with real-time online content from the Brave search index,” and use content from the Brave index “to train their own AI models” and “to respond to specific user queries.” The NYT lawsuit points to Brave’s website, which says the Brave Search API is “used by some of the biggest names in AI, including Cohere, Mistral, Perplexity, and You.com.”
The lawsuit accused Brave of all the major types of copyright infringement: direct infringement, contributory infringement, and vicarious infringement. The lawsuit claims Brave infringes copyrights directly by scraping articles for its search index, for its “Ask Brave” AI search feature, and for the Brave API that “serves as an illicit source of unlicensed copyrighted material, including Times journalism, to other AI companies.”
The NYT accused Brave of being “a contributory and vicarious infringer when it deliberately induces, facilitates, controls, and profits from its users’ and GenAI customers’ copying of the copyrighted content.” Finally, the lawsuit said Brave violated the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) by circumventing technological measures the NYT and other content owners use to restrict access to their articles.
“The Brave Browser includes a default setting that, when activated, causes the browser to go behind website paywalls and provide the paywalled content to the user,” the lawsuit said. The browser “blocks advertising that would otherwise appear on The Times’s website, and instead shows its own ads, offering its users a cut of the revenue even as it deprives The Times of digital advertising revenue that helps it fund the expensive effort of producing journalism,” the lawsuit said.

articles.title: All the news about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake
articles.text:
Ahead of the release of Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI, Nintendo is launching its own fall juggernaut: a Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
The remake, which is releasing 28 years after the launch of the original version on Nintendo 64, has a much more realistic visual style and some modern improvements like a jump button, a way to sprint, full voice acting, and a “Threads of Time” feature that helps you keep track of your progress. But while the game has a new coat of paint, it appears many elements will still remain faithful to the classic N64 release. Nintendo has also launched a special version of the Switch 2 and Switch 2 Pro Controller with Triforce imagery to celebrate the game.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is scheduled to release on November 5th. You can follow along with all of our coverage of the game right here.
- Keep on rolling. For the Ocarina of Time remake, Nintendo developers said in a new interview that they wanted to “preserve the experience of spamming the Roll Attack to forward roll your way across Hyrule Field.” I have very fond memories of rolling around the world in the original. In the remake, you can still spam Roll Attack, but you can also dash.
- A link to the past. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launches later this week, and in the lead-up Nintendo has put out the first half of a lengthy developer Q&A, covering everything from what changed gameplay-wise, to the new visual style, which was inspired by puppet shows. As art director Aya Shida explains: Neither puppet shows nor practical effects films reproduce reality exactly as it is. Even so, both create a convincing sense that the characters truly exist within their respective fantasy worlds. We also felt that there was some overlap between these forms of expression and the distinctive nostalgia evoked by the original game.
- There’s one week left to preorder the Ocarina of Time remake for $10 off The long-awaited remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 launches next Thursday, November 5th. In other words, you have a week remaining to secure your physical edition with a $10 discount at Amazon and Walmart. Once the game launches, the physical version will almost certainly go from $59.99 to $69.99 while the digital version will stay at $59.99. Nintendo had the unenviable task of reimagining its Nintendo 64-era masterpiece for the Switch 2, and based on our hands-on time with some sections of the game, it’s a lot of fun to play. The graphics and art style are fantastic, and the controls have been modernized to be simpler to pick up for those who are already experienced with third-person action games, including other modern Zelda titles. Read Article >
- Here’s Nintendo’s overview trailer for the Ocarina of Time remake. I’ve really warmed up to the game’s art style, especially in this new trailer. And after reading my colleague Cameron Faulkner’s hands-on preview, I’m looking forward to returning to Hyrule even more. The game launches on Switch 2 on November 5th.
- The Ocarina of Time remake feels remarkably modern — and surprisingly terrifying With its upcoming remake for the Switch 2, Nintendo might have nailed the best thing about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time: its timelessness. The 1998 3D action adventure game for the Nintendo 64 that pioneered so much — 3D graphics, movement, exploration, openness — has been reengineered with changes that make it feel more modern, and surprisingly terrifying at times. Based on my early hands-on time with the game, it’s shaping up to be the best-looking, best-playing version of the game that addresses the most frustrating aspects of playing the original. More than just sanding off its roughest edges, Nintendo also fitted Ocarina of Time with modern trappings to make it more welcoming to those who were introduced to Zelda through more modern releases, like Breath of the Wild. The remake has a new progression marker, called Threads of Time, that’s viewable when you pause. It also has Zelda Notes integration within the Nintendo Switch app to let you view game maps and other info on your phone. Oh, it also has a dedicated jump button. Read Article >
- Hori’s electronic Ocarina of Time requires no musical talent. It was briefly shown during Nintendo’s The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct today, but Hori’s website now has a listing for its $49.99 electronic ocarina. You can play your own songs by pushing buttons, play one of 12 pre-programmed songs from the games, use it with the Ocarina of Time remake’s sound recognition feature, or connect headphones for a private jam session.
- Nintendo’s Ocarina of Time remake launches in November Link’s next adventure now has a release date. During a Legend of Zelda stream for the franchise’s 40th anniversary, Nintendo announced that the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake for the Switch 2 is launching on November 5th. The release date makes Ocarina of Time one of just a few big-budget titles launching in the same month as Grand Theft Auto VI. Nintendo first teased the remake in June, though it didn’t reveal much aside from a brief trailer. Today’s event provided a clearer glimpse at how the company is approaching remaking one of its most influential games and the first 3D Zelda adventure. The updated version of Ocarina of Time will be the first Zelda release that’s exclusive to the Switch 2, and longtime Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma described the remake as “a faithful interpretation using modern technologies.” Read Article >
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is getting a remake for the Switch 2 Nintendo announced a remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time during its Nintendo Direct presentation on Tuesday. It will launch sometime in 2026 on Nintendo Switch 2. More details will be announced “in the future.” This new title is the first major release in the franchise since 2024’s Echoes of Wisdom, which starred Princess Zelda herself. Echoes followed 2023’s Tears of the Kingdom, a direct sequel to Breath of the Wild — both of which got upgraded Switch 2 versions alongside the launch of the new console last year. In November, Nintendo also launched the hack-and-slash title Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment. Read Article >

articles.title: Reddit tests ads in search results as traffic declines and growth concerns mount | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Just days after warning investors about declining search traffic and a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast, Reddit is looking for more ways to make money from its existing users. On Tuesday, the company announced that it’s beginning to test ad placements in its search results pages, allowing advertisers to reach users as they search for products, recommendations, and other information on its platform.
“Ads in search may appear based on a range of factors, including contextual relevance to a user’s search query,” Reddit shared in its announcement about the new ad placements. “This is an initial test with a select group of eligible advertisers. During this test, we will evaluate and understand how users respond to these ads so we can refine the experience for users and advertisers over time.”
The company offered examples of what sort of ads might appear, suggesting that a search for “espresso station” might display ads for espresso machines, coffee, or mugs, while a search for “home office setup” could surface ads for things like monitors, desks, and office chairs.
The ad test comes at a time when Reddit is reckoning with how AI has been changing the web’s landscape, and subsequently its reach.
Despite beating Wall Street’s estimates for revenue and earnings per share, the company’s stock dropped after it reported its third-quarter results last week, with fourth-quarter guidance that predicted sales of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below expectations of $1.05 billion. This was tied to Reddit’s declining search traffic referrals resulting from Google’s move to an AI-powered search experience. AI search now sends less traffic to publishers’ websites, as features like AI Mode provide answers directly on Google’s Search Result pages, reducing clicks to other websites.
Reddit also said that its global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in the quarter, and were down 2% year-over-year. The company noted that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low double-digit percentage by the fourth quarter.
This leaves the company needing to earn more revenue from its existing users, which is where these new ads come in. The ads could prove to be more valuable to Reddit after it makes its planned shift to a logged-in experience, which was also announced during earnings. The company said it will make the transition gradually, initially in markets outside the U.S.
The decision to limit its content to logged-in users serves multiple purposes — it protects Reddit’s site from unauthorized AI scraping, and it increases its value to advertisers. Logged-in users are worth more to advertisers because they provide additional signals about their interests and behavior, allowing for better-targeted, more profitable ads.

articles.title: Hackers hijack cPGuard autoupdate to deploy backdoor, steal data
articles.text:
Attackers have compromised the update infrastructure for the cPGuard web security suite to distribute a backdoor and a data-stealing script.
OpsShield, the cPGuard developer, published an alert earlier today saying the attack began on November 2 at 02:06 UTC and affected versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19.
The vendor says that it detected the compromise and stopped the malicious distribution within 12 hours after the attacker pushed the compromised cPGuard versions.
Although the company could not confirm, it said that some servers may have not received and run the malicious script due to update checks occurring at specific intervals.
The attacker leveraged legitimate credentials to gain initial access, although it remains unclear how they were obtained.
“On 2 November 2026 at 02:06 UTC, an unidentified attacker used compromised credentials to gain unauthorized access to OpsShield’s update distribution infrastructure (CDN),” OpsShield said.
“The attacker used this access to distribute a malicious script through the cPGuard update channel.”
cPGuard is a Linux web-server security suite offering malware scanning, firewalls, and attack protection.
It is commonly used by hosting firms and server administrators alongside panels such as cPanel, DirectAdmin, and Plesk. Namecheap offers it on VPS and dedicated servers.
Users updating cPGuard during the compromise window received a script that targeted sensitive data on their machines:
- Linux password hashes
- Root database (MariaDB/MySQL) configuration
- Root shell history
- Root SSH authorization and known-hosts files
The stolen data was uploaded to OpsShield’s licensing server through a compromised account, which the attackers then used to retrieve it.
While OpsShield has not established what data was collected from each server, the company's evidence from the investigation shows that the threat actor retrieved 32 files from each customer.
System administrators are advised to update every cPGuard server to version 5.88.25 or later, reset passwords, and rotate database credentials, cloud secrets, and SSH keys.
OpsShield notes that updating to the latest cPGuard version removes the backdoor and staged files; however, stolen credentials must be invalidated as soon as possible.
The vendor also said that, as an extra precaution, it would release an update to remove previously installed OpsShield support-access keys.
BleepingComputer has contacted OpsShield to learn more about the attack, and a spokesperson told us that the incident has impacted nearly three thousand servers.
"We detected 2946 servers were affected and copied the information mentioned, and our billing system database was copied over as well. We are working on blocking all access, rebuilding the affected systems, and preparing for a public announcement at the earliest possible time," the company representative said.
The company also advises customers to follow the instructions and update cPGuard to version 5.88.25 or later, and reset or rotate credentials that may have been exposed on potentially compromised servers.

articles.title: Roborock adelanta el Black Friday en El Corte Inglés con fuertes rebajas en robots aspiradores
articles.text:
Roborock decidió adelantarse al Black Friday y anunció una serie de ofertas en El Corte Inglés que estarán disponibles hasta el 30 de noviembre. La campaña incluye rebajas en algunos de sus robots aspiradores más recientes, como los Q7 TF+, Qrevo Edge 2 Pro y Qrevo 2 ProX. Dependiendo del modelo, algunos descuentos alcanzan el 56% y la empresa confirmó que se extenderán a otros canales de venta durante esta temporada.
Uno de los modelos de tope de gama que encabeza la lista es el Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 Pro. Este robot aspirador ofrece una potencia de succión de hasta 25.000 Pa y cuenta con un cuerpo de apenas 7,98 centímetros de altura, lo que facilita la limpieza bajo los muebles. El Edge 2 Pro ofrece tecnología antienredos, mopas de alta precisión y una estación multifunción capaz de automatizar tareas como el lavado y secado de las mopas.
Por último, el Qrevo Edge 2 Pro integra un chasis dinámico AdaptiLift, el cual permite elevar el robot hasta 10 milímetros para mejorar el desempeño sobre alfombras. Además, se incluye el sistema RetractSense, que mejora la navegación en espacios reducidos, así como la posibilidad de salvar obstáculos de hasta 4 centímetros de altura.
El Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 Pro tiene un precio sugerido de 1.299 euros, pero durante la campaña de descuentos puedes comprarlo por 499 euros.
Roborock Qrevo 2 ProX: equilibrio entre prestaciones y precio
El siguiente en la lista es el Roborock Qrevo 2 ProX, un robot enfocado a quienes buscan funciones de gama alta a un coste menor. Este modelo comparte algunas especificaciones del Edge 2 Pro, como la potencia de succión de 25.000 Pa, e incluye un sistema dual antienredos con cepillos Duo Duvide. También se añade un sistema de cepillo lateral y arrastre retráctil para limpiar las esquinas y acabar con la suciedad en los bordes.
El Qrevo 2 ProX puede elevar la mopa hasta 15 milímetros para evitar humedecer las alfombras durante el fregado. En caso de que no necesites el módulo de fregado, este modelo también permite retirarlo de la estación base cuando se trabaja en modo aspiración. Roborock ha añadido funciones de autolimpieza en la base, lo cual ayudará para que lo dejes funcionando cuando sales de casa.
Si te interesa el Roborock Qrevo 2 ProX, puedes comprarlo por 299 euros, que resulta una ganga frente a los 699 euros habituales.
Roborock Q7 TF+: navegación LiDAR y base de autovaciado
El último de la campaña de ofertas es el Roborock Q7 TF+, un robot aspirador enfocado a quienes desean automatizar la limpieza del hogar. Este modelo cuenta con una potencia de succión HyperForce de 10.000 Pa, así como un sistema de doble protección antienredos en el cepillo principal y lateral.
Otras funciones incluyen navegación PreciSense LiDAR, capaz de crear mapas de tu casa, y un sistema de fregado con control del caudal para adaptarse a diferentes tipos de suelo. En la parte de automatización, su estación de autolavado reduce la frecuencia con la que es necesario intervenir manualmente en el mantenimiento del robot.
Durante la promoción, el Roborock Q7 TF+ pasa de 299 a 129 euros, lo que representa una reducción del 56% respecto a su precio habitual. Las ofertas de estos robots estarán disponibles en El Corte Inglés hasta el 30 de noviembre de 2026 y forman parte de la campaña de Black Friday anunciada por la compañía.

articles.title: Hubble der Absturz: Wer kann das Uralt-Teleskop retten?
articles.text:
Anfang 2026 machten Meldungen die Runde, wonach das Hubble-Weltraumteleskop aufgrund erhöhter Sonnenaktivität schlimmstenfalls schon 2029 in die Erdatmosphäre eintreten und damit abstürzen könnte. Ein echter Verlust für die Beobachtung des Weltalls, weil vor 2040 mit dem Habitable Worlds Observatory wohl kein Ersatz für Hubble im Orbit sein dürfte.
Hubble im Sinkflug: Absturz droht bis 2034
Zwar haben sich die Befürchtungen eines dermaßen verfrühten Absturzes nicht bestätigt. Das ändert aber nichts daran, dass sich das Hubble-Teleskop weiter im Sinkflug befindet. Spätestens 2033 oder 2034 soll der kritische Punkt von 400 Kilometern Höhe erreicht sein, an dem sich die Umlaufbahn nicht mehr stabilisieren ließe.
Zur Einordnung: Beim Start 1990 wurde Hubble in gut 600 Kilometern Höhe ausgesetzt. Aktuell gibt der sogenannte Hubble Reentry Tracker für das Weltraumteleskop eine Höhe von gut 469 Kilometern an.
Letzte Service-Mission fand 2009 statt
Bisherige Service-Missionen, die Hubble bis 2009 jeweils um einige Kilometer angehoben hatten, sind aufgrund des Fehlens der dafür eingesetzten Space Shuttles nicht mehr wiederholbar. Die Nasa sucht jetzt fieberhaft nach Alternativen, wie Golem berichtet.
Einer entsprechenden Ausschreibung zufolge hat die US-Weltraumbehörde dafür vor allem Privatunternehmen im Visier. Diese sollen im besten Fall dafür sorgen, dass das Teleskop in seinen Zielorbit von 600 Kilometern über der Erdoberfläche zurückkehren kann. Dann könnte es einige weitere Jahrzehnte in Betrieb bleiben.
Anheben, stabilisieren oder abstürzen lassen
Die zweite Option wäre eine Art Wartungsmission, die Hubbles Umlaufbahn wenigstens um einige Kilometer nach oben verschieben und die technische Ausrüstung instand setzen könnte. Sollte das ebenfalls nicht möglich sein, bliebe eine dritte Möglichkeit. Dann soll eine Mission für einen kontrollierten Absturz sorgen. Hubble besitzt nämlich selbst kein Antriebssystem.
In den vergangenen Jahren gab es schon verschiedene Pläne, wie sich Hubble möglicherweise retten ließe. Das von zwei ehemaligen Blue-Origin-Ingenieuren gegründete Startup Orbital Robotics etwa setzt dabei auf einen KI-kontrollierten Roboterarm. Für sein Konzept ist das Unternehmen aber auf Partnerfirmen angewiesen, die ein Roboter-Raumschiff zur Verfügung stellen können.
Nasa sucht nach technischen Lösungen
Ob Orbital Robotics für die von der Nasa sondierte Mission zur Wartung oder Rettung des Hubble-Weltraumteleskops zum Einsatz kommt, muss sich noch zeigen. Mit der aktuellen Ausschreibung prüft die Behörde zunächst, welche Firmen überhaupt infrage kommen und lotet technische und wirtschaftliche Möglichkeiten aus.

articles.title: OpenAI offre 50 € de crédits ChatGPT aux étudiants français
articles.text:
Les géants de l’IA se disputent les étudiants, et la bataille se joue à coups de cadeaux. Google courtisait déjà ce public en proposant 12 mois de Gemini Pro et 400 Go de stockage aux étudiants. Après les États-Unis et le Canada, OpenAI étend à son tour son offre étudiante à la France.
Le dispositif passe par UNiDAYS, la plateforme de réductions réservée aux étudiants. Après avoir vérifié votre statut avec votre adresse e-mail universitaire, vous pouvez y récupérer 50 € de crédits ChatGPT, soit l’équivalent de 1 250 crédits.
C’est quoi, ces 50 € de crédits ChatGPT ?
Sur le papier, « 50 € de crédits ChatGPT » sonne comme un chèque à dépenser librement dans l’application. Ces crédits servent surtout aux fonctions dites « agentiques » d’OpenAI, celles qui mènent des tâches complètes à votre place, et seulement une fois atteintes les limites prévues par votre forfait.
Le premier usage concerne Codex, l’agent de programmation d’OpenAI. Il s’agit d’une IA à qui l’on confie des tâches de développement entières : Codex peut écrire du code, le corriger ou le documenter à votre place. Chaque forfait ChatGPT plafonne cet usage, et les crédits prennent le relais quand ce plafond est atteint.
Les crédits couvrent aussi ChatGPT Work, qui puise dans la même enveloppe que Codex pour les tâches de longue haleine confiées à ChatGPT, ainsi que ChatGPT pour Excel, l’intégration de l’assistant d’OpenAI dans le tableur de Microsoft. Les conversations classiques, elles, ne sont pas concernées. Elles sont de toute façon illimitées sur tous les forfaits, y compris la version gratuite.
À qui ces crédits ChatGPT profitent-ils vraiment ?
ChatGPT a accueilli un nouveau GPT-6 et des réponses interactives, même sans abonnement. Cette version demeure en revanche moins poussée que les formules payantes dès qu’il s’agit de raisonnements complexes ou de longues recherches.

articles.title: Coup de froid pour OpenAI : pourquoi le créateur de ChatGPT peine à boucler sa méga-levée de fonds
articles.text:
Après des levées records, Sam Altman et son équipe doivent revoir leurs ambitions et courtiser les grandes fortunes. Ils n’auraient réuni que 11 milliards de dollars d’engagements sur les 30 initialement visés alors qu’Anthropic prépare son entrée en Bourse avec une croissance bien plus rapide.
Les grandes fortunes pourraient aider OpenAI à compléter une levée que certains investisseurs institutionnels hésitent à financer. L’ambiance a changé depuis le printemps, lorsque le groupe avait clôturé un tour de table de 122 milliards de dollars, après une première annonce de 110 milliards en février.
Des ambitions de financement et de valorisation revues à la baisse
Selon le Wall Street Journal, qui cite des personnes proches du dossier, OpenAI aurait réuni environ 11 milliards de dollars d’engagements pour sa nouvelle opération. Un peu plus du tiers de l’objectif de départ alors que le tour de financement doit encore se poursuivre.
Le groupe viserait désormais jusqu’à 20 milliards de dollars avec une valorisation de 1 250 milliards, contre 1 400 milliards espérés initialement. Pour compléter l’enveloppe, il se tournerait vers des particuliers très fortunés et des family offices, les structures qui gèrent le patrimoine de grandes familles.
La croissance d’Anthropic attire les regards
Les investisseurs ont aussi de quoi comparer les trajectoires des deux rivaux, OpenAI et Anthropic. Au deuxième trimestre 2026, l’entreprise de Sam Altman a réalisé 6,7 milliards de dollars de chiffre d’affaires, en hausse de 18% par rapport au trimestre précédent. Sa perte opérationnelle s’est néanmoins creusée. Sur la même période, Anthropic a plus que doublé ses revenus, rapporte le Wall Street Journal. OpenAI met toutefois en avant une accélération de ses revenus depuis juillet, selon le Financial Times.
Le créateur de Claude prépare parallèlement son introduction en Bourse. Les deux entreprises sollicitent donc des capitaux au moment où les investisseurs comparent davantage leurs performances.
Baisser les prix sans perdre la maîtrise des coûts
OpenAI aurait toutefois regagné des parts de marché après avoir réduit les tarifs d’accès à ses modèles, selon le quotidien américain. Cette stratégie peut relancer les ventes, mais elle oblige aussi à compenser la baisse des prix par davantage d’activité ou une réduction des coûts.
Or il faut financer les puces et les centres de données nécessaires à l’entraînement, puis à l’exécution quotidienne des modèles. La croissance des revenus ne suffit donc pas à rassurer lorsque les dépenses de calcul augmentent en parallèle. C’est cette équation qui nourrit les inquiétudes sur la rentabilité du secteur.
La collecte intervient aussi dans un climat boursier moins favorable. Selon le Financial Times, le recul des valeurs technologiques et les inquiétudes sur l’ampleur des dépenses liées à l’IA ont refroidi les investisseurs. Certains auraient réduit le montant qu’ils prévoyaient d’engager dans ce tour de table, compliquant la tâche d’OpenAI pour atteindre son objectif initial. Sam Altman doit désormais composer avec des investisseurs beaucoup moins faciles à convaincre…
Sources : Wall Street Journal, Financial Times et OpenAI.

articles.title: WorkOS says attacker used ARTEX AI to breach internal sales app
articles.text:
Developer platform WorkOS suffered a data breach after a threat actor accessed business contact records and summaries of customer communications.
According to the company, the attacker used an AI offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts.
Based on evidence from the investigation, no WorkOS app data or production services were accessed or affected.
WorkOS is a developer infrastructure company that provides APIs, SDKs, and tools for integrating services such as enterprise authentication, single sign-on (SSO), user management, and identity management into applications.
According to its website, at least 3,000 companies use its services, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, Perplexity, Snowflake, Plaid, Webglow, and Netlify.
“On October 30, 2026, we identified unauthorized access to an internal WorkOS application used by our sales team,” the company says in an incident alert.
Data accessed by the attacker includes:
- Business contact details (names, email addresses, job titles, and company affiliations from the CRM systems)
- Customer account histories (product usage and connection or directory health)
- Customer communications (summaries and excerpts from sales calls, support discussions, and customer Slack conversations)
- Business account and relationship information (account histories, information about sales and customer relationship)
After detecting the intrusion, WorkOS disabled external access to the affected application and reviewed its access controls on internal tools.
The company also contracted an independent forensics and incident response firm to track the unauthorized activity and determine its full impact.
The company promised to notify affected customers directly, and warned its users to remain vigilant for phishing or social engineering attempts leveraging the exposed information.
ARTEX AI likely powering the attack
WorkOS’s announcement says the attack used an AI-powered offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts.
Company founder Michael Grinich shared more details, saying that the attacker used the ARTEX AI penetration testing suite that has been observed in multiple incidents this year.
Released earlier this year by Chinese developers, the platform was available as an open-source project for offensive security.
ARTEX AI became private after it was used in attacks targeting South Korean banks, but several forks of its code are still available.
More recently, CrowdStrike revealed that cyber-espionage group “Vapor Panda” used the pentesting framework in a global campaign targeting 200 organizations.
Previously, the non-profit cybersecurity organization DIVD also revealed that the same framework powered the attacks it suffered last September.
Grinich explained that the investigating team identified user agents such as ‘artex-enrich/1.0’ and ‘norma/0.4’ in web requests from the threat actor.
The founder assured that the cybersecurity incident has now been fully contained and promised to share more information about the attack after the investigation completes.
