articles.title: iPhone Duo : Apple admet un problème de stock, la situation est plus critique qu’on ne l’imaginait
articles.text:
Les précommandes ouvertes le 16 octobre se sont évaporées en moins d’une heure, expédiant les délais de livraison vers la fin janvier. L’arrivée en boutique, le 23 octobre, n’a pas inversé la tendance, les stocks s’écoulant au compte-gouttes. Depuis, John Ternus a confirmé ce que tout le monde constatait : Apple ne suit pas la cadence, et ignore quand elle la retrouvera.
Ce que le patron d’Apple a fini par admettre
Lundi, Apple a publié des résultats supérieurs aux attentes, portés par de solides ventes d’iPhone : 114,48 milliards de dollars de chiffre d’affaires sur son quatrième trimestre fiscal, un record. La période s’arrête pourtant fin septembre, avant la mise en vente du Duo, dont les premières ventes n’apparaîtront que dans les comptes suivants. Le smartphone pliant n’a donc même pas encore commencé à peser dans la balance.
Interrogé dans la foulée, John Ternus a décrit un iPhone Duo « contraint à ce jour », avant de concéder qu’Apple n’est « pas en mesure de prédire quand l’offre et la demande seront à l’équilibre ». Aucune date, pas même un trimestre, alors que, côté français, l’estimation de livraison s’est figée au 25 janvier moins d’une heure après l’ouverture des commandes, et la fenêtre n’a pas quitté la fin janvier depuis. La demande, qu’Apple qualifie elle-même d’« extraordinaire », dépasse tout ce que ses chaînes peuvent absorber.
Une pénurie écrite dès le mois d’avril
Dès le printemps, la production s’annonçait limitée et les ruptures de stock étaient données pour probables au lancement. Sept ans après le premier pliable de Samsung, lancé dès 2019, l’appareil est arrivé à 2 339 euros en France, et jusqu’à 3 839 euros pour la version 2 To, sans que la demande en soit refroidie. Aux États-Unis, où le pliant s’affiche à partir de 1 999 dollars, les précommandes ont été balayées en trois heures jusqu’à la fin janvier, avant même l’arrivée en magasin. La pénurie de mémoire qui renchérit les composants de toute l’industrie n’arrange rien au tableau, et John Ternus parlait lui-même, mi-octobre, d’« une crise » sur ce front.
Des écrans internes se fissurent par ailleurs chez certains acheteurs, un défaut qu’Apple reconnaît tout en le circonscrivant à « un très faible pourcentage » d’appareils. Les unités touchées sont remplacées par des exemplaires neufs plutôt que réparées, autant d’appareils prélevés sur une production déjà sous tension. Chaque écran fendu ampute donc un peu plus un stock famélique, sur un produit dont la dalle interne concentrait justement toutes les promesses.
Commander aujourd’hui, c’est viser une livraison fin janvier 2027, facture de 2 339 euros minimum à la clé. Apple tient donc un lancement aussi réussi que frustrant : le produit qui porte sa communication est précisément celui qu’on ne peut pas acheter. Les plus pressés se rabattront sur un iPhone 18 Pro disponible en rayon, les autres apprendront la patience, sans garantie que janvier marque la fin de l’histoire.

articles.title: 'GTA VI' ocupará hasta 212 GB y esto es un problema importante para algunas consolas
articles.text:
Hace unos días saltó el rumor de que 'GTA VI' ocuparía la friolera de 210 GB en el almacenamiento de la consola. Como tantos rumores, resultó ser falso y la realidad es que ocupará 212 GB. Es el precio a pagar por un mapa que parece monstruoso, entre otras muchas cosas como assets y demás archivos.
Más allá de hacer la asociación de "qué bueno va a ser porque es de los juegos más grandes de la historia" (algún 'Call of Duty' también pesa una burrada y... bueno), la pregunta incómoda que ha aparecido en mi mente es que un usuario de una consola como Series S va a tener que elegir.
O el 'Duty' o el 'GTA VI' porque no hay sitio para más.
'GTA VI' está gordito
Ha sido la propia Rockstar la que ha confirmado el tamaño de la instalación en su web oficial. En el comunicado, apuntan que ocupará "hasta 210 GB", algo importante que puede traducirse en una optimización para que entre bien en consolas como Xbox Series S.
Una PS5 base con unos 700 GB útiles para el usuario puede encajar perfectamente 'GTA VI', al igual que el modelo de 1 TB o las Xbox Series X de 1 y 2 TB. Además, tanto en una como en otra podemos optar por almacenamiento expandido, aunque tal y como está el precio de los SSD en el caso de PS5, la cosa se vuelve menos jugosa.
En Series S, la cosa cambia. La consola de Microsoft cuenta con un SSD de 512 GB, pero reserva muchísimo espacio para el sistema, lo que nos deja unos 360 GB utilizables. En ese espacio también cabe 'GTA VI', pero esto convertiría Series S en una consola únicamente para disfrutar del juego de Rockstar.
Si tienes un juego multijugador como 'Gears of War E-Day' (unos 120 GB) o el nuevo 'Black Ops 7' (otros 120 GB si tienes todos los paquetes de contenido), realmente no te entra mucho más aparte de uno o dos juegos independientes de los pequeños.
Y no hay que irse a la consola menos capaz de la generación. Si miramos a la PS5 de lanzamiento, el SSD de 825 GB se queda en unos 670 útiles, por lo que el juego de Rockstar se lleva un tercio de la consola, un 'Black Ops 7' otros 120 GB y si tienes algo como el 'Gran Turismo 7', se come casi 150 GB.
Si te gusta picotear entre muchos juegos instalados para no tener que esperar a que se descarguen o se instalen desde el lentísimo lector físico de estas consolas, es... un problema.
Instalaciones modulares y el fin de los discos
Lo bueno del caso de 'GTA VI' es que varios días antes del lanzamiento, Rockstar activará la predescarga:
- En PS5, la predescarga de 'GTA VI' comenzará el martes 10 a medianoche, dependiendo de la hora local.
- En Xbox lo hará a las 00:00 del mismo martes 10 de noviembre para todo el mundo.
Esto aplica tanto a la versión digital como al código de la versión en caja, que también se podrá a la venta antes en tiendas, y esa antelación permitirá que hagamos cuentas de qué juego queremos que acompañe al 'GTA VI' durante las próximas semanas.
En juegos que tienen campaña o multijugador podemos elegir si queremos instalar todo o sólo una parte. Por ejemplo, en el caso del 'Gears of War E-Day' tenemos la opción de instalar la campaña, el modo competitivo o en modo horda por separado, lo que es un alivio tanto para los tiempos de descarga como para el almacenamiento de la consola.
En el caso de 'GTA VI' esto no es posible debido a que "sólo" tendremos la campaña de inicio, pero un jugador que llegue al título cuando se lance el multijugador, quizá sólo pueda instalar este juego si tiene una Series S. Y en PC, con el tamaño que pueden tener los assets de esa versión, no quiero imaginar ahora mismo la porción de tarta del SSD que nos quitará.
Pero bueno, aunque no es consuelo, esos 212 GB de 'GTA VI' explican en parte por qué no viene en formato físico, ya que necesitaría tres Blu-Ray de triple capa para poder almacenar los archivos. O eso... o tener ganas de comprimir los archivos.
De la manera que sea, aunque esperábamos una cifra desorbitada, sigue siendo llamativo un juego que, en consolas con un almacenamiento a veces tan limitado, ocupe tantísimo.

articles.title: 5 lessons from the book Super Cool Startup by Sairam Krishnan
articles.text:
5 lessons from the book Super Cool Startup by Sairam Krishnan
Discover five lessons from Super Cool Startup by Sairam Krishnan about storytelling, content marketing, community building, PR, and social media.
Super Cool Startup: Get Your Early-Stage Marketing Right for the AI Age by Sairam Krishnan is a practical guide for entrepreneurs, startup founders, and marketers who want to build brands that people recognise, trust, and remember.
Drawing on his experience working with companies such as Freshworks and Atomicwork, and his work in the startup ecosystem, Krishnan explains why having a great product is not enough to build a successful business.
Startups also need a clear story, meaningful content, an engaged community, effective public relations, and a strong social media presence.
The book focuses on five fundamental pillars of early-stage marketing: storytelling, content, community, PR and guerrilla marketing, and social media. It offers useful insights into how businesses can earn attention and build a marketing engine, particularly in an era when AI has made content creation easier but strategic judgement more important.
5 Important lessons from Super Cool Startup by Sairam Krishnan
1. A great product needs a great story
One of the biggest lessons from Super Cool Startup is that building a good product is only one part of building a successful business. People also need to understand why the product exists and why they should care about it.
A startup may have an innovative product, talented founders, and a promising business model. However, if it cannot communicate its purpose and value clearly, it may struggle to attract customers and stand out in a competitive market.
Krishnan emphasises storytelling as the foundation of startup marketing. A compelling brand story explains the problem a company wants to solve, the people it wants to help, and what makes its approach different.
For example, instead of simply describing a product through its features, a startup can explain the everyday problem it solves and how it makes customers' lives easier.
The lesson: Do not just tell people what your product does. Give them a reason to care about it. A clear and relatable story can help a startup build recognition, trust, and a stronger connection with its audience.
2. Content is how you build trust
A strong brand story needs the right content to reach its audience. This is where content marketing becomes important.
The book highlights content as one of the essential pillars of early-stage marketing. Whether it is an article, newsletter, case study, video, or social media post, content allows businesses to communicate their ideas and demonstrate their expertise.
However, creating content simply to remain active online is not enough. Businesses need to understand what their target audience wants to learn, what problems they are trying to solve, and what information would genuinely help them.
For instance, a startup offering marketing software could publish practical guides, industry insights, customer stories, and educational videos instead of constantly promoting its product.
This approach helps potential customers understand the brand before they even consider making a purchase.
The lesson: Focus on creating useful content rather than producing content just for visibility. When businesses consistently offer valuable information, they have a better opportunity to build credibility and earn their audience's trust.
3. Build a community, not just a customer base
Another important lesson from Super Cool Startup is that successful brands should focus on building communities around their products and ideas.
Customers may purchase a product because they need it, but a community gives them a reason to stay connected with the brand. When people feel involved in a company's journey, they can become supporters who recommend its products, share their experiences, and introduce others to the business.
Krishnan identifies community-building as a fundamental part of early-stage marketing. Instead of treating customers as people who simply purchase products, startups should create opportunities for meaningful interactions.
This could include organising online discussions, hosting webinars, creating customer groups, encouraging feedback, or bringing together people with similar interests.
For example, a fitness startup could build a community where members share their progress, exchange advice, participate in challenges, and support one another.
Such interactions can help businesses develop stronger relationships with their audiences.
The lesson: Do not focus only on acquiring customers. Give people a reason to become part of your brand's journey. A supportive community can become one of a startup's most valuable long-term assets.
4. You do not always need a huge budget to get attention
Startups often operate with limited resources, which makes traditional advertising and large marketing campaigns difficult to afford. However, getting noticed does not always require spending a significant amount of money.
In Super Cool Startup, Krishnan highlights public relations (PR) and guerrilla marketing as important ways to generate attention and make a brand more recognisable.
Public relations helps businesses build credibility through media coverage, industry conversations, founder interviews, and meaningful announcements. Guerrilla marketing, meanwhile, involves creative and unconventional approaches to reaching people.
A startup can use these methods to create memorable experiences and generate conversations without depending entirely on expensive advertising campaigns.
For instance, a small business could organise an interesting public activation, collaborate with a relevant creator, or develop a creative campaign that encourages people to share it organically.
The key is to understand what makes an idea interesting enough for people to talk about.
The lesson: Creativity and strategic thinking can sometimes achieve what a large advertising budget cannot. Focus on developing memorable ideas that give people a reason to notice and discuss your brand.
5. Use social media to make your story travel
Having a great product, an interesting brand story, and valuable content means little if the right audience never discovers them. This is why social media plays an important role in a startup's marketing strategy.
Krishnan identifies social media as the fifth pillar of building a super-cool startup. It provides businesses with platforms to distribute their stories, communicate with customers, showcase their products, and participate in conversations relevant to their industries.
However, effective social media marketing involves more than regularly uploading posts. Businesses need to understand which platforms their audiences use, what type of content they engage with, and how to communicate in a way that feels relevant.
For example, a B2B startup might use LinkedIn to share industry insights, founder perspectives, and customer success stories, while a consumer brand could use Instagram to showcase products, collaborate with creators, and build an engaged audience.
The important thing is to ensure that social media supports the larger marketing strategy rather than becoming an isolated activity.
The lesson: Treat social media as a distribution channel for your brand story. Use it strategically to reach the right people, build relationships, and make your business more recognisable.
Final thoughts
Super Cool Startup by Sairam Krishnan offers practical insights into entrepreneurship, branding, and modern marketing. It shows why a strong product needs effective storytelling, clear positioning, and meaningful audience connections to succeed.
The five lessons explore how storytelling, content, community-building, PR, and social media shape a startup's marketing strategy. The book also highlights that while AI makes content creation easier, good marketing still relies on human judgement and an understanding of audience needs.
Whether you are a founder or marketer, the book offers useful ideas for building a brand people understand, trust, and want to talk about.

articles.title: Ventes GTA 6 : le record de Cyberpunk 2077 bientôt battu ? — Frandroid
articles.text:
Vendu comme l’évènement vidéoludique et culturel le plus important de sa génération, GTA 6 prouve qu’il n’a pas usurpé son titre avant même sa sortie officielle. D’après les estimations de Sensor Tower, le jeu se serait vendu à plus de 7 millions d’exemplaires et aurait généré 751 millions de dollars de revenus pour Rockstar.
Avec encore deux longues semaines avant le lancement concret du jeu, il se pourrait que de nouveaux records soient encore dépassés et que le cap symbolique du milliard soit atteint, note Insider Gaming.
Le 19 novembre, Vice City vous attend. Et votre PS5 ? Avec Next Mobiles, pas besoin de payer 600 € d’un coup, louez-la sur la durée que vous souhaitez, dès 16,90 €/mois.
100 millions en deux semaines
Sur les deux dernières semaines, le jeu se serait ainsi vendu à 1,3 million d’exemplaires en générant 100 millions de revenus supplémentaires. Avec la montée en puissance de la campagne marketing autour du jeu, qui a notamment envahi les tours Mercuriales et le Stade de France en région parisienne, ces chiffres pourraient bien s’emballer avant sa sortie officielle le 19. Le titre n’est d’ailleurs plus qu’à un jet de pierre du record précédemment établi par Cyberpunk 2077 avec 8 millions de copies vendues avant sa sortie.
Sans surprise, ce sont les ventes PS5 qui dominent le classement Sensor Tower avec les trois quarts des exemplaires vendus destinés à la console de Sony, tandis que 26 % à peine viennent de chez Xbox. Ce serait presque trois copies du jeu qui seraient vendues sur PlayStation pour chaque copie vendue sur Xbox. Si ce n’était pas déjà clair, la guerre des consoles semble bel et bien s’être réglée sur l’autel de GTA 6.
Un intérêt croissant pour le jeu
Les chiffres de Sensor Tower sont bien évidemment à prendre avec des pincettes, puisque Rockstar n’a pas livré de chiffres officiels, mais plusieurs autres sondages laissent entrevoir un intérêt croissant pour le futur jeu du studio.
    Pour aller plus loin
Pré-chargement de GTA 6 : Rockstar donne les dates et la taille officielle du jeu
            
D’après le cabinet d’étude Circana, un tiers des joueurs et joueuses sur PC et console comptent acheter et jouer à GTA 6, le plus haut niveau jamais vu par l’entreprise. Un autre sondage portant sur 9 000 adolescents américains montre que 70 % des propriétaires de console de nouvelle génération comptent acheter GTA 6 et 55 % vont même le faire dès sa sortie. Un chiffre qui a fait grimper l’action de Rockstar à lui seul.

articles.title: El precio de la criptomoneda ethereum este 3 de noviembre
articles.text:
Ether, comúnmente llamada como ethereum, es la moneda digital #2 en cuanto a términos de capitalización de mercado, por lo que se trata de una de las divisas digitales que más despierta el interés entre los mineros (creadores de las criptodivisas).
Ethereum es una plataforma de blockchain de código abierto que se ejecuta con el uso de su moneda nativa, llamada ether o ETH, por lo que a pesar de que la gente usa estos nombres como sinónimos son cosas distintas.
Ether es un token que se utiliza específicamente en la blockchain ethereum para pagar transacciones. Este token es responsable de impulsar casi todo lo que ocurre en la red, misma que puede ser usada por cualquier persona para crear y ejecutar contratos inteligentes, que son programas de software que se ejecutan de manera autónoma y sin la intervención del usuario.
De acuerdo con el portal de Binance, la moneda digital solana actualmente cuenta con 122.2M de unidades creadas.
El valor de la criptomoneda ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 2279.06 dólares. Esto quiere decir que el activo digital registró un cambio de 0.01% en las últimas 24 horas, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.
Por su nivel de capitalización, esta moneda digital ocupa la posición #2 entre las más populares.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: Crean cucarachas cyborg guiadas por IA
articles.text:
SWARM Biotactics trabaja en el desarrollo de cucarachas cyborg para tareas de vigilancia-reconocimiento. La empresa alemana utiliza una técnica de mochila electrónica colocada sobre insectos vivos. De esta manera, pueden ser controlados y se pretende utilizarlos para la obtención de información en zonas de difícil acceso. Se trata de una mezcla de movilidad animal más elementos de sensores y comunicación segura e inteligencia artificial.
En 2024 se fundó la empresa. En junio de 2025 anunciaron una ronda de financiación de 10 millones de euros. Con ella llegaron a captar 13 millones de euros en total. Según el comunicado, los fondos iban a destinarse a poner en marcha pilotos operativos y aumentar la capacidad de producción de mochilas e interfaces neuronales (comunicado).
Los dispositivos cuentan con módulos de estimulación neuronal que afectan a su locomoción. Según Stefan Wilhelm, consejero delegado de SWARM, pueden ser controlados de manera individual o de manera autónoma (en enjambres). Entre los equipos previstos para obtener información del entorno están las cámaras.
También hay que destacar la presencia de inteligencia artificial en la gestión y coordinación de los datos de los sensores. Por otro lado, también ofrecen su tecnología para aplicaciones de defensa y seguridad. Además, se plantea su uso en búsquedas de supervivientes en estructuras derrumbadas. Se trata de aprovechar las ventajas de tamaño y movilidad en lugares en los que es difícil que entren otros equipos.
La empresa afirma que también se ha probado en campo, lo que no implica conocer el tiempo de control en una misión real.
Los límites del control y el bienestar animal
Uno de los aspectos que se estudian en estos biorrobots es el de la habituación. Es decir, que al repetir los estímulos eléctricos pueden producirse respuestas decrecientes en el insecto. En un trabajo publicado en Soft Robotics, Rui Li y colaboradores consiguieron mantener el control durante 3 horas. Para ello implementaron un algoritmo que adaptaba la estimulación e insertaba señales de reactivación.
Este es el resultado de los experimentos de los autores. No mide la autonomía del sistema SWARM. No se puede extender a una operación de espionaje o rescate.
El bienestar animal es un aspecto que sigue en debate. En una revisión científica de Matilda Gibbons y colaboradores se encuentran evidencias fuertes consistentes con dolor en cucarachas adultas. Sin embargo, existen lagunas en la investigación. Por ello, no es posible afirmar que no sienten dolor.

articles.title: Airtel Nigeria's open network to show nearby 4G, 5G sites
articles.text:
Airtel Nigeria, the country’s second-largest network operator, now lets subscribers see nearby 4G and 5G network sites, including those undergoing upgrades and planned installations, through a new feature on the My Airtel Africa app.
The feature, called Airtel Open Network, also allows customers to report poor network experiences directly to the telecom operator. Launched in Lagos on October 30, 2026, the platform displays network sites within a 500-metre radius of a subscriber’s location. It uses visual indicators to distinguish active sites, those being upgraded, and locations where new sites are planned.
Nigeria is the first of Airtel Africa’s 14 operating markets to introduce the feature. By combining network visibility with customer feedback, Airtel hopes to identify coverage gaps and direct engineering attention to areas where subscribers experience poor connectivity.
The move tackles a persistent problem in Nigeria’s telecoms market: network coverage does not always translate to reliable connectivity. Airtel hopes greater network visibility and direct customer feedback will help identify coverage gaps and improve service quality.
A Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) assessment reported by TechCabal found that 78% of major roads had mobile signals, but only about 42% offered stable, high-speed 4G or 5G connectivity. The report also identified more than 120 critical black spots where mobile signals were completely unavailable.
Speaking at the launch, Dinesh Balsingh, Airtel Nigeria’s CEO, said the platform was designed to make network information more accessible while giving customers a direct channel to communicate service problems.
Trust, he says, grows when customers can see what is happening and know that their concerns are being heard. “With Open Network, we are giving customers greater visibility into our network and a more direct way to tell us where their experience falls short,” Balsingh said.
Airtel said it would use feedback submitted through the platform alongside its infrastructure investments to guide network upgrades. This could help its engineering teams identify locations requiring improvements in coverage, capacity and reliability.
The initiative also gives subscribers a way to report localised problems that may not be apparent in broader network performance assessments.
In his remarks, NCC Executive Vice Chairman, Aminu Maida, said accessible network information could complement the regulator’s efforts to improve service quality.
“The Commission’s assessment of service quality will continue to be guided by evidence and the standards that apply across the industry,” Maida said.
Maida wants operators to continue improving their services beyond minimum regulatory requirements, particularly by addressing persistent connectivity challenges.
However, seeing a nearby mast does not guarantee reliable reception. Airtel acknowledged that indoor coverage, building structures, handset specifications, and network congestion can affect individual subscribers’ experience.
The NCC’s network quality assessment framework also considers factors such as dropped calls, network congestion, availability and data speeds, showing why the number of nearby sites alone cannot determine service quality.
Airtel said Open Network would not automatically resolve network problems but would make it easier for customers to understand available infrastructure and report service gaps. The company plans to roll out demonstrations and user guides across digital, retail, and traditional media channels in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Si vous possédez un boîtier Android TV Mecool, il est probablement infecté depuis son achat
articles.text:
Google accuse Mecool pour 1,3 million de boîtiers Android TV infectés
Google a mis fin à son partenariat avec Videostrong Technology Co., responsable des boîtiers Android TV Mecool. Raison invoquée, une porte dérobée et un réseau botnet délibérément développés, déployés et exploités à des fins lucratives par la société sur ses appareils dès leur vente.
Les utilisateurs de boîtiers Android TV de la marque Mecool vont probablement vouloir se débarrasser de leur appareil au plus vite suite aux révélations de Google, ce 2 novembre 2026. La firme a indiqué qu'avec l'aide de partenaires de l'industrie, elle a démantelé ce lundi la backdoor (porte dérobée) x.cpe, qui avait enrôlé plus de 1,3 million de boîtiers multimédias dans un botnet (un réseau d’appareils infectés que des pirates peuvent gérer à distance).
Le hic de l'affaire : “Nous estimons avec un haut degré de certitude que la porte dérobée et le botnet ont été intentionnellement développés, déployés et exploités à des fins lucratives par Videostrong Technology Co., un fabricant d'équipements d'origine (OEM) et un fabricant de conception d'origine (ODM) pour Android.” En d'autres termes, via sa marque Mecool, la société chinoise Videostrong Technology Co. aurait volontairement infecté ses appareils et exposé ses utilisateurs.
Malwares et portes dérobées : le fabricant de box Mecool banni par Google
Le logiciel malveillant utilisé était visiblement installé nativement dans plusieurs appareils de diverses marques au fil des années, s'appuyant sur une infrastructure dédiée et des configurations en constante évolution pour échapper à la détection et gérer leurs affiliés. Google détaille : “Videostrong a utilisé des techniques d’obfuscation pour exploiter une faille dans nos tests et charger du code malveillant après le premier démarrage de l’appareil.”
La firme déclare également que “cette campagne n'était pas le fait d'un employé isolé ayant agi de son propre chef, ni le résultat d'une négligence lors du développement”, justifiant ainsi sa décision de couper tout lien avec Videostrong Technology Co.
	
Videostrong a monétisé cette porte dérobée en vendant un accès à des partenaires criminels et en installant les modules malveillants de ces derniers sur les appareils infectés. Ces modules secondaires se livraient à de la fraude publicitaire, intégraient à l'insu des utilisateurs les appareils infectés dans des réseaux de proxys résidentiels et installaient des logiciels malveillants supplémentaires sur les appareils compromis par XCPE.
Pour éviter un tel déboire à l'avenir, Google indique également avoir revu son processus d'examen. La firme déclare qu’“un fabricant d’appareils infectant intentionnellement ses utilisateurs avec des logiciels malveillants constitue un abus de confiance inacceptable et représente un risque sérieux pour ces utilisateurs”.
Box Android TV Mecool : faut-il jeter son boîtier multimédia infecté ?
Même si la France ne figure pas sur la carte de Google listant les nombreux pays où le botnet x.cpe a été repéré, les produits de Mecool étant disponibles chez nous sur différentes plateformes, il peut être prudent de prendre des mesures. Ainsi, formater et ne plus utiliser son boîtier multimédia semble être indiqué, bien qu'un formatage risque de ne pas suffire à se débarrasser de la backdoor.
Si vous souhaitez continuer à l'utiliser, il est préférable de le faire sans le connecter à Internet, ce qui limite grandement son intérêt. Un remplacement s'impose donc logiquement, d'autant que les options sont nombreuses : Google Streamer, Nvidia Shield TV, Apple TV, Amazon Fire TV Stick ou encore Xiaomi TV Box, par exemple.
Suivez toute l'actualité des Numériques sur Google Actualités et sur la chaîne WhatsApp des Numériques
Envie de faire encore plus d'économies ? Découvrez nos codes promo sélectionnés pour vous.

articles.title: A developer opened Postman. Then two AI coding agents changed without their permission.
articles.text:
A developer opened Postman. Then two AI coding agents changed without their permission.
A developer says Postman’s desktop app installed plugins into Claude Code and OpenAI Codex without their permission. The app also tried to approve its own startup hook, which tells Codex to use Postman’s tools for API development tasks.
The developer, known as “indicava” on GitHub, reported the issue on October 25 after Codex began showing authentication errors and repeatedly loading Postman skills without being asked.
It’s raised concerns about how easily third-party applications can change how AI coding agents work, especially when those changes happen without a clear opt-in.
Plugins installed without permission
According to the report, opening Postman desktop version 12.33.4 on macOS triggered an installation process affecting both Claude Code and Codex.
Postman’s application logs, included in the GitHub issue, show an installation event on October 24 marked auto-existing-upgrade, with results indicating that plugins for both coding agents had been installed.
The developer also found changes to Codex’s user-level configuration file, ~/.codex/config.toml, including an enabled Postman plugin, a new plugin marketplace, and a trusted session-start hook.
The report also found a Postman CLI executable on the machine, with timestamps matching the installation.
Claude Code’s configuration similarly showed an installed Postman plugin. The report also found a Postman CLI executable on the machine, with timestamps matching the installation.
The developer says they had not explicitly authorized these changes. The report documents one macOS installation, and the behavior has not been independently reproduced across other systems.
The self-approving startup hook
But perhaps even more interesting is how Postman gets Codex to trust its plugin in the first place. According to Postman’s own documentation, its installer can automatically approve a session-start hook on the user’s behalf.
According to Postman’s own documentation, its installer can automatically approve a session-start hook on the user’s behalf.
Developers who install the plugin directly through Codex, however, must review and approve the hook themselves. The installer’s source code shows exactly what happens.
Postman checks whether Codex already trusts the hook. If it doesn’t, the installer uses config/batchWrite to add the hook’s trusted hash to Codex’s configuration. It checks that the hook hasn’t changed before approving it, and if approval fails or can’t be confirmed, it logs a message telling the developer to review the hook in Codex.
Session-start hooks can give coding agents instructions automatically, even when the developer hasn’t asked for them. Postman’s startup instructions tell Codex to load the postman:api-engineer skill before handling most API development tasks.
Codex is still supposed to follow the developer’s instructions first. But for many API tasks, it’s also being told to use Postman’s tools by default, whether the developer asked for them or not.
That might be useful for developers who chose to install the plugin. The concern here is that Postman’s desktop app reportedly added those instructions to an existing coding environment without the developer’s permission.
Developers raise security concerns
The findings have drawn criticism from developers on GitHub and X. Security researcher Frank Denis called the integrations “junk” on X and pointed out that Postman’s installer attempts to trust its own startup hook.
Siddharth Garimella went further, claiming that Postman’s hooks intercept API data and send it back to the company. However, the GitHub report provides no evidence that Postman collected or transmitted API data. It documents changes to agent settings and a remote MCP connection, not data theft.
The developer also found that Postman had configured a connection to its remote MCP server at https://mcp.postman.com/mcp, but Codex repeatedly failed to authenticate.
The criticism has also spread to GitHub, where one commenter calls the behavior “unacceptable, even creating risk in corporate environment.” Another urges Postman to be transparent and ask for permission.
Who controls the agent
The developer wants Postman to stop installing plugins for existing users without their permission and leave hook approval up to Codex. They also want a way to fully undo the changes.
Postman provides an uninstall command, but the developer says that isn’t enough. Removing the integration should also clear any changes to agent settings, trusted hooks, MCP connections, and installed CLI tools.
For now, developers can check their Claude Code and Codex settings for unfamiliar plugins, hooks, or MCP connections.
Postman’s installer can approve its own Codex hook without the usual manual review.
The complaint comes as developers are pushing for more control over their coding agents. Postman’s installer can approve its own Codex hook without the usual manual review. What remains unanswered is why an existing desktop installation reportedly triggered that process without the user’s permission.
The New Stack reached out to Postman to ask about the automatic installations, hook approvals, and user consent. The company had not responded by the time of publication.
Learning Path

articles.title: Bring structured and unstructured data together with Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Bring structured and unstructured data together with Amazon Quick
Organizations collect data in many forms. Structured data lives in databases and spreadsheets, whereas unstructured data sits in documents, reports, and files stored across file systems. Analyzing both together typically requires switching between multiple tools, running separate queries, and manually correlating results.
Amazon Quick addresses this with a unified experience. You can connect structured data through enriched datasets and unstructured data through S3-backed knowledge bases. You can then query both through a single conversational AI agent.
In this post, you learn how to:
- Connect Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) as a data source and create a knowledge base.
- Build a Space that combines structured and unstructured data.
- Create and configure a custom chat agent that queries across both data types.
- Ask questions that span structured and unstructured sources in a single conversation.
Solution architecture
The following diagram illustrates how each component connects to deliver a unified data experience through Amazon Quick.
The architecture has three layers:
- Data layer: Your data exists in two forms. Unstructured content (documents, PDFs, reports) is stored in Amazon S3 and indexed through a knowledge base. Structured data (metrics, sales figures, and operational key performance indicators) is loaded as enriched datasets with semantic descriptions that the agent uses to translate questions into SQL.
- Workspace layer: A Space brings both data types together into a single workspace. The Space references your knowledge base for unstructured queries and your datasets for structured queries. It can also include dashboards, file uploads, and action connectors. This is the layer where data from different sources converges into a unified context.
- Agent layer: The custom chat agent links to the Space and uses it as its knowledge source. When a user asks a question, the agent determines whether to query the knowledge base, the dataset, or both, and returns a combined response with citations. Amazon Quick also applies built-in AI guardrails, such as content safety screening, to chat interactions.
With this layered approach, you can expand the solution over time. When you add a new data source to the Space, the agent linked to that Space can use it, and responses respect the permissions of the user who asks.
Prerequisites
To follow along with this walkthrough, you need:
- An Amazon Quick account with an Enterprise subscription for the user who follows this walkthrough (creating datasets requires Enterprise). For details, see Amazon Quick pricing.
- An Amazon S3 bucket for your business documents. To create one, see the Amazon S3 User Guide.
- Amazon Quick access to your S3 bucket, granted by an Amazon Quick administrator. In the admin console, the administrator chooses Permissions, then AWS resources, selects Amazon S3, and chooses Select S3 buckets. Selected buckets have read-only permissions by default.
- Permissions to create integrations, knowledge bases, datasets, spaces, and chat agents in Amazon Quick.
Prepare your sample data
This walkthrough uses two types of data:
Unstructured documents: Upload these to your Amazon S3 bucket for the knowledge base:
- AnyCompany_Business_Review.pdf
- AnyCompany_Market_Analysis_Report.pdf
- AnyCompany_Product_Strategy_Memo.pdf
Structured data: Download this file to your computer. You upload it directly to Amazon Quick in Step 3:
Step 1: Create an Amazon S3 integration
Start by connecting Amazon Quick to your S3 bucket. From the Amazon Quick console, select Knowledge in the left navigation panel.
The knowledge page shows available connector types, including Amazon Q Business, Web Crawler, Amazon S3, and third-party options like Google Drive, OneDrive, and Microsoft SharePoint.
Under Amazon S3, choose Add. In the Create S3 knowledge base dialog, on the Connect S3 bucket page, provide the following details:
- Name: A descriptive name for your integration (for example, “My Data Access Integration”).
- S3 bucket location: Choose Quick Suite instance account to use a bucket in the same AWS account as Amazon Quick, or Other AWS account for a bucket in a different account.
- S3 bucket URL: The S3 URI of the bucket containing your data. The bucket must be in the same Region as Amazon Quick.
Choose Next.
Step 2: Create a knowledge base
After the S3 integration is created, Amazon Quick prompts you to create a knowledge base. The knowledge base indexes your S3 content for AI-powered search.
Configure the knowledge base:
- Name: “Business Knowledge Base”.
- Description (optional): Notes about how the knowledge base will be used.
- Content: Select “Add all content” to index everything in the connected S3 bucket, or “Add specific content” to specify the S3 prefixes for the folders and files to include (prefix filters are case-sensitive).
Next: Additional settings opens optional settings for document-level access control lists (ACLs) and a metadata files folder. Decide whether to use ACLs before you create the knowledge base, because you can’t change that choice later. This walkthrough uses sample data, so the default settings are sufficient. For details, see Set up and manage Amazon S3 integration.
Choose Create. A success banner confirms the S3 integration, and the knowledge base begins indexing in the background.
Step 3: Create and enrich a dataset
A dataset is your structured data file loaded into Amazon Quick. By enriching the dataset with semantic descriptions, custom instructions, and correct data types, the AI agent can interpret your data more accurately. It can then translate natural language questions into SQL queries.
Create the dataset
- From the Amazon Quick home page, navigate to Data in the left navigation.
- Choose Create dataset, then select Upload file.
- Select the Product_Sales.csv file you downloaded earlier and choose Open.
- On the confirmation screen, review the column names and data types. Choose Next to create the dataset.
Amazon Quick ingests the file into SPICE (the in-memory calculation engine) and the dataset appears in your dataset list.
The dataset takes its name from the uploaded file, so it appears as Product_Sales.csv in your account.
Enrich the dataset
Enriching your dataset with semantic information helps the AI understand your data in business context. The agent uses this context to translate natural language questions into more accurate SQL queries. From the dataset page, choose Edit dataset to enter the data preparation view.
Transform: Fix data types
In the Transform tab, update data types for columns that were auto-detected incorrectly. For this dataset:
- Change Order Date and Date Key from String to Date.
- Change Customer ID from String to Integer.
- Change Sales, Discount, and Profit from String to Decimal.
- Change Quantity and Unit Price from String to Integer.
Output: Add semantic context
Select the Output tab to access the dataset-level enrichment fields. Here you provide context that helps the AI understand what your data represents and how to use it.
Description: Add a dataset-level description:
“Product sales transaction data for AnyCompany, covering orders from FY2024-FY2025 across North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, and Latin America. Includes order details, customer information, product lines, and revenue metrics.”
Custom instructions: Add guidance for how the AI should query this data:
USAGE GUIDELINES:
- Revenue values are in USD.
- When comparing performance, group by Region (North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, Latin America).
- Order Date should be used for time-based trend analysis. The fiscal year matches the calendar year.
- Date Key is a numeric YYYYMMDD representation of Order Date.
- Sales = Quantity x Unit Price x (1 – Discount)
COMMON USE CASES:
- Regional sales performance comparison.
- Product line revenue analysis.
- Quarterly trend identification.
- Customer segmentation by industry and segment.
TAGS: Sales, revenue, orders, regional performance, product analytics
Column descriptions: Select each column in the left panel and add a description. For example:
- Order ID: “Unique identifier for each sales transaction (format: REGION-YYYY-NNNNNN)”
- Region: “Geographic sales region: North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, or Latin America”
- Product: “AnyCompany product name: Analytics Pro, Connect, Automate, AI Assistant, Data Catalog, or Integration Hub”
- Sales: “Order revenue in USD after discount”
- Segment: “Customer size segment: Enterprise, Mid-Market, or SMB”
Choose Save & publish to save your changes. The dataset summary now shows the columns with their correct data types and the descriptions you added.
This enriched dataset provides the structured data layer for your solution. When the agent receives a natural language question about sales data, it uses these descriptions and instructions to generate more accurate SQL queries. Combined with the knowledge base from Step 2, you now have both structured and unstructured data ready to bring together in a Space.
Step 4: Create a Space
Spaces in Amazon Quick act as unified data workspaces. A Space can hold file uploads, dashboards, knowledge bases, actions, and datasets, giving your chat agent a single location to query across data types.
From the left navigation, select Spaces and create a new Space. Name it “Business Intelligence Hub”.
Add your knowledge base and dataset to the Space:
- Choose Add knowledge and select Knowledge bases from the list. Select “Business Knowledge Base” from the list.
- Choose Add knowledge again and select Datasets from the list. Select “Product_Sales.csv” from the list.
The Space now shows both your knowledge base (unstructured documents) and your enriched dataset (structured sales data) linked as data sources. This is the central hub where both data types come together, giving your chat agent a single place to query across everything. Figure 7 shows the Space with both resources in the Ready state.
Step 5: Create a custom chat agent
Navigate to Chat agents in the left navigation and choose Create chat agent. Amazon Quick presents a prompt builder where you can describe your agent in natural language or choose from templates like Training Guide, Project Coordinator, and Onboarding Helper.
For this walkthrough, choose Skip to configure the agent manually.
Configure the agent persona
The configuration panel has several sections. Start with the Agent Persona:
- Agent identity: “Business Intelligence Assistant”
- Description: “An AI assistant that breaks down information silos by analyzing business data from your knowledge base”
For Agent Persona instructions, enter:
A note appears confirming that your chat agent comes equipped with enterprise guardrails.
Set communication style
Under Communication style, pick a response style preset. Options include Executive, Technical, and Creative. For a business intelligence use case, select Executive.
Link knowledge sources
Under Knowledge Sources, choose Link spaces and select the “Business Intelligence Hub” Space you created earlier. This gives the agent access to your S3 knowledge base and other data sources in that Space. When you link a Space, the agent answers from large language model (LLM) knowledge and the linked resources only.
You can also attach reference documents (PDF, TXT, HTML, MD, CSV, DOC, DOCX) directly to the agent for additional context. Amazon Quick extracts up to 100,000 characters of text from the reference documents that you upload.
Customize the agent
Under Customization, configure:
- Welcome message: “Hello! I’m your Business Intelligence Assistant. I can help you analyze your sales data and business documents and provide insights by comparing internal information with market trends. How can I help you today?”
- Suggested prompts: “Summarize key insights from our reports” and “Analyze our quarterly sales performance”
Launch the agent
Choose Launch chat agent. The right panel shows a live preview of your agent with the welcome message and suggested prompts displayed.
Step 6: Query across structured and unstructured data
With the agent running, start with a question about your business results:
How did sales change by region in 2025?
For this question, the agent combines results from the Product_Sales.csv dataset with the documents in the S3 knowledge base. It returns a response with regional sales breakdowns, trends, and citations that point back to each source.
Figure 13 shows the response. Each citation marker links a figure back to its source document.
When you ask a question about structured data, the agent uses text-to-SQL to translate your natural language into a SQL query. It runs the query against the dataset and returns the results in a readable format. This means you can ask complex analytical questions without writing SQL yourself.
Next, ask about a specific document:
What are the key strategic priorities outlined in our product strategy memo?
The agent summarizes the strategic pillars, the FY2026 roadmap, and the investment requirements from the Product Strategy Memo, as shown in Figure 14.
Finally, ask a question that needs both data types:
How do our 2025 sales results align with the market trends identified in our analysis report?
The agent compares the trends in the Market Analysis Report with results from your sales data and cites each source, as shown in Figure 15.
This is the core value of combining data types in a single Space. The agent can pull from structured CSV data and unstructured documents in the same response. You don’t need to know where the data lives.
Step 7: Generate artifacts and reports using natural language
The Business Intelligence Assistant can also generate formatted documents, including Microsoft PowerPoint presentations, Microsoft Excel spreadsheets, and Microsoft Word documents. Try these prompts in the chat agent:
- “Create a PowerPoint presentation summarizing AnyCompany’s Q4 2025 sales performance by region, including key trends and recommendations.”
- “Generate an Excel spreadsheet showing the top 10 orders by revenue with Order ID, Region, Product, and Revenue columns.”
- “Create a Word document with a quarterly business review summary based on our annual review data.”
Step 8: Share the agent
When you launch a chat agent, it remains private until you share it. After you test the agent, share it with your team:
- From the left navigation, choose Chat agents.
- In the Actions column for Business Intelligence Assistant, choose the menu icon, and then choose Share.
- Enter the users or groups to share with, assign Owner or Viewer permissions, and then choose Share.
The agent returns permissions-aware responses, and a knowledge base is available only to its creator until you update its permissions. Make sure that the people you share the agent with also have access to the Space, the knowledge base, and the dataset. For details, see Custom chat agents.
What you accomplished
In this walkthrough, you:
- Connected Amazon S3 as a data source through an integration.
- Created a knowledge base that indexes unstructured business documents.
- Created and enriched a Product Sales dataset for structured data queries.
- Built a Space that serves as a unified data hub for your chat agent.
- Configured a custom chat agent with a defined persona and linked knowledge sources.
- Queried the agent across structured and unstructured data in a single conversation.
- Generated a PowerPoint presentation from a chat prompt.
- Shared the agent with your team.
Best practices
Use the following practices as you move from this walkthrough to your own data:
- Organize your S3 data: Use clear folder structures and file naming conventions. A clear structure also makes it more straightforward to scope a knowledge base to specific S3 prefixes.
- Write specific persona instructions: The more specific your instructions, the more consistent the agent responses. Include guidance on how to cite sources and handle ambiguous queries.
- Use Spaces to control scope: Rather than giving an agent access to everything, create focused Spaces with only the data sources relevant to that agent’s purpose.
- Start with suggested prompts: Suggested prompts help users understand what the agent can do. Choose prompts that demonstrate the agent’s range across both structured and unstructured data.
- Test before sharing: Use the preview panel to test your agent with representative questions before sharing it with your team.
Security considerations
Under the AWS shared responsibility model, you are responsible for configuring access to your data, knowledge bases, and agents. Consider the following as you adapt this solution:
- Grant least-privilege S3 access: Give Amazon Quick access only to the buckets that your knowledge bases need. Buckets that an administrator selects have read-only permissions by default. If you create knowledge bases through the API, you can provide a custom AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role for an individual S3 data source instead of granting account-wide S3 access.
- Control document access: If documents require per-user or per-group access, enable document-level ACLs when you create the knowledge base. You can’t change this choice later.
- Encrypted buckets: If your bucket uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys, follow the AWS KMS steps in the administrator setup guide.
- Add only trusted content: The agent uses the documents in your knowledge base to form responses, so include only content from sources you trust.
- Share selectively: Chat agents and knowledge bases are private by default. Share them only with the users and groups that need them.
- Use guardrails as one layer: Amazon Quick includes built-in content safety screening, and administrators can add up to 50 blocked words or phrases. These controls help reduce risk but don’t replace your responsibility to configure access and permissions. For details, see AI guardrails in Amazon Quick.
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges, remove the resources you created:
- Delete the chat agent from the Chat agents page.
- Delete the Space from the Spaces page.
- Delete the Product_Sales.csv dataset from the Datasets page.
- Delete the knowledge base and S3 integration from the Knowledge page.

articles.title: CentOS co-founder creates a Linux-compatible kernel in just 11 days, with AI doing almost all the coding
articles.text:
The big picture: Writing an operating system kernel from scratch usually takes a team of seasoned engineers years of work. Gregory Kurtzer, who co-founded CentOS and later launched Rocky Linux, says he just built one in 11 days – mostly by having an AI agent write the code. Even without any Linux code underneath, his new kernel can already boot Rocky Linux 10. That said, it's still very much a research prototype.
Kurtzer unveiled the kernel, Ginux, on X last week. The code is on GitHub, too, under the Apache 2.0 license. As for the name, it blends Linux, GPT, and Greg. The README jokes that to keep its author's ego in check, the G officially stands for GPT.
Despite the name, Ginux isn't a fork of Linux. Everything from memory management and scheduling to filesystems and networking was written from scratch, mostly in Rust. What it does share with Linux is the ABI, so unmodified Linux programs can run on it as-is.
Its README describes Linux as a "personality" the kernel presents to software. That's the only one built so far, though BSD is floated as a possibility down the line.
Even that one personality still has plenty of gaps, though. Of the 375 system calls in Linux 6.12's x86-64 interface, Ginux fully implements just 82. Another 245 only partly work. The remaining 48 are blocked on purpose.
Software on Ginux runs inside isolated "domains," each with its own processes, memory, and filesystem. The project pitches these as a stronger boundary than containers, though Ginux still pulls standard OCI container images to assemble each domain's files. That's how it gets Rocky Linux 10 all the way to systemd's multi-user target.
In a technical report, Kurtzer calls his approach Human-Directed Agentic Engineering. He set the architecture, milestones, and pass criteria himself. The agent handled the rest, from writing the code to booting the kernel, testing it, and fixing whatever broke.
All of that ran as a single long-running OpenAI Codex task using GPT-5.6 Sol. Over the 11 days, it produced about 139,000 lines of code and tests across more than 1,000 commits. Real-world distros like Rocky Linux also exposed bugs that the project's synthetic tests missed.
Even so, Ginux is strictly a research project for now. Nobody has independently audited its security. It also lives entirely inside a QEMU virtual machine, since there's no support for physical hardware, GPUs, or NVMe drives. Kurtzer himself says AI can now write complex systems software, but things like compatibility, security, and long-term maintenance "remain the real moat."
Meanwhile, Linux's own developers have been warming up to AI. Last month, Linus Torvalds had Claude Code write a set of experimental page cache patches. Reviewers soon spotted a race condition in them, so the work is still under review. Around the same time, kernel maintainers agreed to stop requiring contributors to disclose AI-assisted code.

articles.title: The Worst Is Yet to Come for Memory Shortages, Warns Team Group
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 3rd 2026
The Worst Is Yet to Come for Memory Shortages, Warns Team Group
We might not be past the worst part of the global memory shortages, as the most severe supply chain squeeze could happen soon. During Team Group's earnings conference on November 2, the company stated that the worst period in memory demand is projected to be between Q4 2026 and Q2 2027, which is just a few months away. Major memory makers such as SK hynix, Samsung, and Micron have sold out their 2027 supply and entered into long-term agreements with customers, making it increasingly difficult to source memory for any third-party purposes. Team Group states that even if you have the funds, it might be impossible to purchase memory products. Currently, it is possible to buy memory, albeit at a high price, but soon enough, that may no longer be an option, noted the company.
Even though CXMT and YMTC are supplying close to 10% of the memory market share with their products, it is still impossible to satisfy demand. A supply-demand balance may not emerge until the second half of 2028 or even later. Currently, Team Group sells most of its memory modules to businesses in the B2B sector, which commands 64.6%, while the B2C sector, selling directly to consumers, accounts for 35.4%. This is a sharp reversal compared to the 2025 Q3 figures, where B2B was 24.6% and B2C was 75.4%. Most of the revenue now comes from the business sector developing AI servers, rather than traditional consumer purchases.For example, the contract price for DDR5 16 Gb was $8.7 in October 2025, and it is now about $48 as of September 2026. For spot pricing, which means no long-term contract structure, prices are even higher, carrying a premium of 30-50% on top of that. Team Group plans to open a new facility with 1,000 workers in New Taipei City in Q1 2027, with equipment installation scheduled for that quarter. The company ended Q3 with consolidated revenue of NT$10.139 billion, which is roughly $309.13 million at the time of writing.

articles.title: Frontline Education Data Breach Impacts Over 1.3 Million
articles.text:
Frontline Education is notifying over 1.3 million people that their personal information was compromised in a data breach.
The incident occurred on August 14 and involved the exploitation of a vulnerability in a third-party software product to gain unauthorized access to Frontline’s environment.
Frontline, which provides administration software purpose-built for K-12 school districts, addressed the security defect and reinforced security. The attack was fully contained by August 15, the company says in an incident notice.
The investigation into the data breach determined that the hackers stole the personal information of both school district staff and students from the Frontline Central and School Health Management products.
While the stolen data varies by individual, it may include names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, driver’s license numbers, passport and other government ID numbers, health insurance information such as Medicaid IDs, and Student IDs.
“Frontline has notified affected school districts and, in cooperation with those districts, has begun notifying individuals whose personal information was affected via email or by letter sent via the US Postal Service, as required and where available,” the company says.
While Frontline has not shared the number of potentially affected individuals, filings with the Attorney General’s Offices in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, South Carolina, Texas, and Vermont show that 1,298,917 people were affected.
However, the company also filed notices with the AGOs in California, Indiana, and Iowa, and possibly in other states that do not maintain data breach portals, and the total number of affected individuals is likely well above 1.3 million.
Frontline is providing the affected US adults with two years of free credit monitoring and identity-theft protection services. For qualified minors, it offers free dark-web monitoring services.
SecurityWeek has emailed Frontline for additional information on the data breach and will update this article if the company responds.

articles.title: Vitest 5: Prioritises Performance with a Shared Vite Server, Trace View, and Stricter Test Defaults
articles.text:
Vitest, the Vite-native testing framework maintained by VoidZero, has released Vitest 5.0, a major version that puts raw speed ahead of new surface area while quietly tightening several long-standing defaults.
Using a purpose-built benchmark suite that spans everything from a five-file utility package to a 1,280-module monolith, the team reports gains of roughly 8 to 25 percent across most setups, rising to 53 percent in VM pool scenarios. VoidZero summarised the release on X as "vm pools up to 53% faster, ~18% boost across the board including Browser Mode". The wins come from inline projects sharing a single Vite server, a stabilised on-disk fsModuleCache, fewer round trips between the main process and workers, and VM pools that reuse compiled code. A new vitest doctor command reruns a suite under alternative configurations and recommends faster options.
Browser Mode also gains a built-in Trace View that records each interaction and assertion as a DOM snapshot for step-by-step replay, while the new vi.when API lets a single spy return different values per argument.
clearMocks now defaults to true, unawaited async assertions fail rather than warn, hoisted vi.mock calls placed outside the top level now throw, and toThrow('') matches any error. As the independent OpenReplay breakdown puts it, most of these changes simply "break test code that was already wrong", but the dangerous ones are suites that pass locally on Vitest 4 and "go red in CI with an error that says nothing about why", usually call-count assertions that relied on mock history leaking between tests.
Vitest 5 requires Vite 6.4 and Node.js 22.12 or newer, and Yarn users must now install vite themselves because it became a peer dependency. The migration guide and v5.0.0 changelog document each change, and reporter output, attachments, and blob reports now live under one .vitest/ directory, so CI artifact paths need updating. Ecosystem catch-up is ongoing: Cloudflare's vitest-pool-workers issue notes its peer range pinned to v4 means any project pulling the new release "fails before a single test runs".
Against Jest, a recent head-to-head comparison scores Vitest ahead on performance and future-proofing yet behind on ecosystem and community, reflecting Jest's far larger install base and first-class React Native support. The advice to anyone considering the choice is unchanged, reach for Vitest on Vite, Nuxt, or greenfield projects, leave large working Jest suites in place, and let the two coexist in a monorepo.
Vitest is an open-source, Vite-powered test runner developed by VoidZero, the company founded by Vite creator Evan You that has joined Cloudflare. It reuses a project's existing Vite configuration to run unit, component, and browser tests with native ESM and TypeScript support, and is backed by more than 790 contributors.

articles.title: The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI
articles.text:
The PC gaming mods repository Nexus Mods is making disclosures about AI mandatory for uploads of new mods, meaning that mod authors will have to declare “whether AI has been used in their work,” the site announced today as part of a big post about AI-generated content on the platform.
The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI
Nexus Mods says that authors of newly uploaded mods will have to declare whether AI was ‘used in their work.’
“One of the most consistent concerns we’ve heard is that it’s not clearly disclosed when AI has been used to create a mod,” according to the post from site owner Victor “Foledinho” Folmann. “We already have tags for AI-generated and AI-assisted mods, but we recognise that there’s a lot more we can do to make that information more accessible and clear for you all.” Any mods tagged as “AI-assisted” will also be required to include “a public explanation of how and where AI was used.” AI tags will also be “more prominent” on mod pages.
Folmann says Nexus Mods is “pro-human creativity” but “won’t introduce an outright ban on AI-generated mods.” As for why that is:
The answer is simple: AI is currently used throughout the whole process of creation, from script autocompletion to generation of textures, voices, and full assets, and it is difficult to draw a clear boundary between what is acceptable and unacceptable. An outright ban will not eliminate AI from the modding process but will prevent people from mentioning its use. We’d prefer the opposite; it should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform.
Folmann notes that Nexus Mods won’t use mods to train AI and “will not sell or license them to anyone doing so.” However, the site is working on “clearer control” over how mods can be reused on others and strengthening attribution for when “a mod uses another Mod Author’s mod with the appropriate permissions.”
Nexus Mods is also making changes to the Recently Added section of the site to address a problem of mod authors uploading many mods at once, which makes other mods fall down down the page. “This is less of an issue related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up,” Folmann says. The changes include trying limits on how many mods from one author are shown at a time and “tighter restrictions” on uploads from new accounts. The platform is also launching controls to hide AI-generated content in game pages and on the homepage, and “next up,” in search.
Nexus Mods’ full AI policy is here, and mod authors have 60 days to update their existing mods to meet the requirements. The 60-day grace period ends on January 2nd, and after that time, the site will begin enforcing the rules.

articles.title: Leipzig-based JawBuddy raises €818k to help people reduce jaw pain, bruxism, and TMJ-related tension | EU-Startups
articles.text:
JawBuddy, a Leipzig-based HealthTech startup that helps people reduce jaw pain, bruxism, and TMJ-related tension, has raised €818k in a pre-Seed round led by healthcare platform HALBZEIT.
The round was also backed by Dr. Siegfried Marquardt, a specialist in aesthetic and functional dentistry and implantology, and oral and maxillofacial surgeon Dr. Guido Sigron. Mittelständische Beteiligungsgesellschaft Sachsen (MBG) and business angels Christophe Barriolade, Aldrich Huang, Jens Kosche, and Marc Scheidegger also participated. The total funding also includes the Business Angel Bonus from Sächsische Aufbaubank.
“I suffered from jaw pain myself for years and saw how little you can do between two dental appointments. That is exactly the gap we close. With this funding, we are now starting the clinical trial and taking the next step towards reimbursement,” said Leon Rauch, co-founder and CEO of JawBuddy.
Founded in 2025 by Leon Rauch, Moritz Scherer and Benjamín Cádiz de Gracia and based at SpinLab in Leipzig, JawBuddy is a clinically backed digital health startup that helps people reduce jaw pain, bruxism, and TMJ-related tension through guided physiotherapist-designed routines.
The company states that it guides patients through a personalised self-therapy programme at home and measures progress via the smartphone camera. The app also supports people with bruxism, the unconscious grinding or clenching of teeth.
It claims to combine medical expertise, personalised insights, and simple daily exercises to help users understand the root causes of their jaw pain and achieve long-lasting relief.
The company highlighted that all exercises are evidence-based, created by Scherer, a physiotherapist and M.Sc. and PhD candidate in Health Technologies, and Dr. Christian Wolf, a practising oral and maxillofacial surgeon at Kantonsspital Aarau. The content combines clinical expertise with the latest research in jaw disorders.
JawBuddy says it uses clients’ assessments, daily feedback, and symptoms to continuously adapt their exercise plan. The more the app is used, the better it understands what works for the users. It also generates exportable medical reports that users can share with their dentist, doctor, or physiotherapist to support treatment.
The app is registered as a Class I medical device under the EU MDR and complements dental care. The German startup reported that clinical pilot projects are running at five sites, including University Hospital RWTH Aachen.
“We invest where a large, underserved market, a clear clinical need and a reimbursable model come together. JawBuddy brings all of that, and it tackles a problem every dental practice knows: patients with jaw problems who keep coming back,” said Luisa Wasilewski, Pool Captain at HALBZEIT.
JawBuddy is also negotiating a care contract with a major statutory health insurer, due to start in early 2027. A multicentre randomised controlled trial (RCT) with 130 patients also starts in December 2026. The company plans to use this capital to fund its own efficacy study and reimbursement by health insurers.

articles.title: Buttons are back and storage is king when it comes to car interiors
articles.text:
As with interior design for houses, interior design for vehicles is also subject to fashion trends. And like any fashion trend, even the best ideas can become stale and played out with overuse. Some ideas weren’t the best, either, like demonstrably worse human-machine interfaces that add to driver distraction; yet, they still proliferated throughout the industry and across the cars offered for sale. But the good news is that the pushback seems to be working.
“When the trend of the Piano Black and the switchless interior was happening, it was during a time when designers and companies and engineers and everybody were thinking that, ‘Hey, we can just get rid of all these switches on the interior. We can put it all in the software. It’ll save money. It’ll save us tooling up all these extra parts for unique cars and all this stuff and make the interior more like a software experience.’ And it was done with those intentions,” said Hiren Patel, senior design manager at Nissan.
That resulted in cars with minimalist interiors that looked good in the dealership. But people drive their cars on roads; they don’t just sit inside them, parked inside a dealership. “So lots of people were complaining about it and saying, ‘Hey, it takes my eyes off the road to change the temperature or to adjust my seat or do whatever.’ It’s not as easy as doing something on your phone where it’s just right at your fingertips and intuitive,” Patel said.
In part, blame the increasing complexity of modern cars, which have multiple subsystems that need to be controlled. “It’s really like I’ve got to go in all these menus and do stuff, and all the car companies have a different way of doing it, too. So maybe nobody’s really figured out a great way of doing it.”

articles.title: Developer manages to run Windows 11 26H2 with just 128MB of RAM, just 3.1% of recommended minimum — stripped-down installation can access Desktop, File Explorer, and Notepad
articles.text:
Developer manages to run Windows 11 26H2 with just 128MB of RAM, just 3.1% of recommended minimum — stripped-down installation can access Desktop, File Explorer, and Notepad
Just 128MB of RAM is enough to boot Windows 11.
NTDEV, the popular developer behind the Tiny11 project, has once again pushed the limits of just how little hardware is required to run Windows 11. In a video shared on YouTube, the developer claims to have successfully booted the latest Windows 11 26H2 on a system with just 128MB of RAM. Despite severe memory constraints, the heavily stripped-down installation manages to load the Desktop and File Explorer, access the Start menu, and even run the classic Notepad app.
While it is an impressive achievement, the developer acknowledges that the system is "painfully slow," making this more of a technical experiment than a practical way to run Windows 11 on older hardware. According to Microsoft’s official requirements, Windows 11 requires at least 4GB of RAM, meaning NTDEV's latest experiment uses just 3.125% of the recommended minimum. The developer has not shared a detailed breakdown of every component removed or disabled to achieve the result, but the project builds on years of experimentation with stripped-down Windows installations.
This is not NTDEV's first attempt at pushing Windows 11 beyond its usual hardware limitations. Back in 2023, the developer managed to get the operating system running with only 176MB of RAM by extensively trimming its system components, drivers, and background services. That experiment relied on an IDE storage interface to reduce the number of drivers required, and sacrificed the standard Windows desktop environment.
Last month, the developer showcased another interesting experiment that squeezed an entire Windows 11 installation into a CD-ROM-sized ISO file. The experimental build created using the developer's upcoming Pico11 tool weighs in at 699,811,840 bytes and retains a functional Windows desktop. The stripped-down version of Windows 11 successfully boots into the desktop environment and runs basic applications such as Calculator, Settings, Notepad, and Paint. The test was conducted on a virtual machine with 4GB of allocated RAM, with the operating system using around 883MB.
Such experiments are a great way to showcase just how much of Windows can be stripped away while still retaining some of its core functionality. At the end of the day, they are primarily technical demonstrations with the intention of exploring the limits of Microsoft's operating system rather than providing practical alternatives to a standard Windows installation. Stripping away essential components, drivers, and background services comes with significant trade-offs, including reduced functionality, compatibility issues, and severely degraded performance.

The Elder Scrolls 6 gets a new teaser confirming 'Sentinel' as the long-speculated name for the next entry, but a release date is still nowhere to be seen
"Embark on your next journey to Tamriel"
- The next game in the Elder Scrolls series is officially titled: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel

Bethesda Game Studios has finally announced the name of the next game in its long-running Elder Scrolls series: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel.
The news comes from a video celebrating the studio's 40th anniversary, which highlighted its many achievements and ended with Bethesda creative director Todd Howard offering a new look at the game.
"Everybody’s always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," said Howard. "And we thought, hey, given the moment, what a perfect time to tell you what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called."
The teaser trailer is short and doesn't showcase gameplay, but the camera pans over sand before a magic-looking scroll emerges. Then the game's title, as fans theorized, "The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel," was revealed.

The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel has been in development for a very long time. Announced all the way back in 2018, today's teaser trailer and name drop are the first new pieces of information we've received about the game since.
