articles.title: Manchester-based Crediflow AI secures €1.8 million to automate commercial loan processing | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Crediflow AI, a Manchester-based FinTech aiming to remove manual work from commercial loan processing, has secured €1.8 million (£1.5 million) in funding.
The funding was led by NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II), a €790.84 million (£660 million) vehicle covering the entire North of England, providing loans from €29,957 (£25,000) to €2.4 million (£2 million) and equity investments of up to nearly €6 million (£5 million). The round also saw participation from early-stage venture firm Haatch and a group of angel investors.
“Businesses of all sizes and across all sectors often rely on commercial finance for a multitude of reasons, but the processes involved in granting this finance are often largely manual, making the process inefficient and slowing down lending decisions. By automating this area of the sector, Drey and the Crediflow AI team are not just supporting lenders but also removing barriers for companies that need funding to grow,” said Joe Ball, senior investment associate at PXN Ventures.
Crediflow AI was founded in 2024 by Drey Kenfack, who spent more than a decade in commercial lending and private credit, holding senior credit roles at Ford Credit Bank, DF Capital Bank, and Advance Global Capital before founding the company.
The company has built a platform that consolidates the information credit teams currently gather by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions, and borrower documents, and structures them into credit analysis ready for approval by a lender. Its flagship product, FlowSpread, automates financial spreading by extracting income statements, balance sheet data, and cash flow figures directly from PDFs, tax returns, and bank statements, eliminating manual data entry.
It also offers a Bank Statement Analysis tool that adds an additional layer of intelligence, automatically categorising transactions across multiple accounts, reconciling them against submitted financials, and flagging risk signals such as unusual activity, cash flow volatility, or concentration risk.
Crediflow AI says its platform can reduce the process that could take several days to between 10 and 30 minutes. It is already in use by hundreds of credit professionals across the UK, Europe, and the United States, including clients such as AddWorking Capital and Iveco Capital.
Kenfack, CEO and founder of Crediflow AI, said, “Growing a loan book takes more than finding borrowers and having capital available. You need the capacity to assess those businesses, get decisions through approval and stay on top of risk once the money is out the door. I’ve spent much of my career doing that work.”
“When every transaction requires hours of manual preparation, it affects how much business a lender can take on and which deals are worth pursuing. We built Crediflow to bring that workload down and give credit teams more time to understand the borrower and structure the financing,” he added.
Crediflow was previously selected as one of eight companies to receive investment through PXN’s PraeSeed programme, a 12-week cohort-based initiative run in partnership with the British Business Bank and NPIF II.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate platform development, expand the engineering and product team, and onboard more banks and specialist lenders. It also plans to use the capital to extend automation across the full loan lifecycle, from origination to monitoring, with workflows designed to meet each lender’s own credit policies.

articles.title: 'GTA 6' confirma fecha y hora de la precarga: desde cuándo lo podrás instalar en tu PS5 o Xbox
articles.text:
Cada día que pasa, el hype por GTA 6 está un poco más alto. El nuevo juego de Rockstar Games estará disponible a partir del jueves 19 de noviembre y tiene todo para ser el lanzamiento más grande de la historia de los videojuegos. Con tamaña expectativa, toda noticia sobre su lanzamiento dispara la ilusión de los fanáticos.
Hoy, Rockstar ha confirmado la fecha y el horario de inicio de la precarga de GTA 6; es decir, desde cuándo se podrá descargar el juego completo en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S antes de que se libere para comenzar a jugarlo.
El estudio menciona que la precarga de GTA 6 se iniciará el próximo martes 10 de noviembre. Esto significa que el nuevo Grand Theft Auto VI podrá residir en tu consola con poco más de una semana de antelación a su debut formal, lo que seguro no será de mucha ayuda para tu ansiedad.
Tengamos en cuenta que la precarga o descarga anticipada de un juego implica que este se puede instalar al completo en la plataforma, pero que no se puede jugar hasta el día de lanzamiento. Lo que esto permite es disminuir las horas de espera, algo crucial cuando se trata de propuestas tan anticipadas como GTA 6, así como evitar un potencial colapso de las tiendas al momento de su debut. Así, el día del estreno solo tienes que instalar un pequeño parche que quita el cifrado de los archivos y desbloquea el acceso.
Los horarios de precarga de GTA 6 en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S
Como ya dijimos, la precarga de GTA 6 estará disponible tanto en PS5 como en Xbox Series X|S el próximo 10 de noviembre. Sin embargo, los horarios no serán los mismos para las dos plataformas. En el caso de la consola de Sony, los usuarios podrán comenzar a descargar el juego a partir de la medianoche de su zona horaria. Esto quiere decir que en Oceanía y Asia serán los primeros en poder iniciar el procedimiento, que gradualmente se abrirá al resto del mundo.
Por su parte, los usuarios de Xbox Series X|S sí tendrán de un horario único a nivel global a partir del cual la precarga de GTA 6 estará habilitada. Para ser más específicos, el inicio de la descarga se activará a las 00:00 horas GMT; es decir:
- 01:00 horas de España;
- 21:00 horas del 9 de noviembre en Argentina;
- 18:00 horas del 9 de noviembre en México.
Tanto la fecha como el horario de la precarga de GTA 6 corresponden a las descargas digitales desde las tiendas de PS5 y Xbox. Rockstar ha menciona que las versiones en "físico", que no incluyen un disco sino que traen un código de descarga dentro de la caja, deberían estar disponibles en tiendas minoristas a partir del 12 de noviembre.
Por último, el estudio también ha confirmado cuánto espacio ocupará el archivo de precarga de GTA 6: 212 GB. Así que asegúrate de desocupar el almacenamiento de tu consola con tiempo para garantizar que podrás instalar el nuevo Grand Theft Auto antes de su lanzamiento oficial.

articles.title: The government's AI translation tool keeps making mistakes
articles.text:
The Canadian government has an AI-powered translation tool that’s reportedly been riddled with errors for months.
The federal government’s AI-powered translation tool, GCtranslate, has only been around for about six months, but in that time, it’s racked up a concerning number of errors, including some really unfortunate translations.
According to documents CBC/Radio-Canada obtained through a Freedom of Information Act request, GCTranslate introduced several mistranslations and hallucinations in government documents, particularly when used for translations from English to French.
Errors range from simpler mistakes, like translating a common abbreviation for the transportation bureau, TB, to Tuberculosis, to more severe errors, like changing someone’s name from “Mike” to “Stephanie.” There were also some other funny translation errors, such as the tool translating “Buy Canadian Policy” into “Achetez une politique canadienne,” which means “Buy a Canadian policy.”
One of the more… unfortunate changes spotted by Radio-Canada was translating a shorthand for “cumulative growth” to “sperme croissance,” which certainly does not mean cumulative growth.
Bad (and funny) translation mistakes might seem innocuous, but they can have an outsized impact on Canadians. Experts warned Radio-Canada that an incorrect translation of a tax form could mean French-speaking Canadians are excluded from a credit or benefit that an English-speaker might get. Similarly, experts warned that poor translations of instruction manuals for weapons or equipment could lead to injuries or worse.
Of course, it’s also worth noting that GCtranslate is a pilot project and is receiving regular updates to improve and fix problems. Further, translators are assessing the quality of translations and helping retrain the models to improve performance.
Source: CBC/Radio-Canada

articles.title: Ten years later, 'Pokémon Go to the polls' still haunts the internet | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In the lead-up to a presidential election that would irrefutably transform American culture, Hillary Clinton took the stage at a rally in Virginia as she campaigned to become the first female president.
“We’re going to have a lot of jobs — jobs from building infrastructure to coding. Creating new apps,” she said. “I don’t know who created Pokémon GO, but I’m trying to figure out how we get them to have Pokémon Go to the polls.”
Ten years later, it is once again Election Day in the United States. Now, most app developers aren’t even writing their own code anymore, thanks to AI, and Pokémon GO has been sold to a company wholly owned by Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. The only thing about that political moment that hasn’t changed is that “Pokémon Go to the polls” memes still crop up on every Election Day.
“It was very bold and confident, and also just sounded so terribly out of touch and corny,” Cesar Ruiz de Castilla, an elected ward committee member in Philadelphia, told TechCrunch. “I don’t know if the mainstream media cared that much about it, but everyone was making a meme about it and talking about it online.”
Since then, digital culture has become increasingly inextricable from the fate of American politics. Donald Trump tweeted his way through his first term, then later started his own social media platform; presidential campaigns hire meme managers; the White House invites podcasters and content creators to press briefings; Elon Musk even spun up his own advisory group under Trump that named itself after the cutesy doge meme and then slashed international aid programs.
“The 2016 election was such a monumental moment in internet history, and we were all there for it — our politics have become more, not just divided, but segmented online,” Organizer Memes, a political influencer who teaches Gen Z activists how to reach their peers online via memes, told TechCrunch. “It’s a relic of an optimistic, bygone political era.”
Now, people who weren’t even old enough to vote in 2016 reflect on the year as a cultural turning point, even calling it “the last good year.” It’s a sentiment that isn’t so much political as it is rooted in nostalgia for an era of internet culture before AI slop, when we used social media to connect with friends, rather than doomscrolling through an algorithmic feed of people we don’t even follow.
At the start of the new year, this yearning for the old internet became a viral sentiment as millions of people shared throwback photos from 2016 on Instagram.
Spotify reported that user-generated playlists featuring 2016 in their titles spiked 790% in the first three weeks of the year, and the company changed its Instagram bio at the time to say it’s “romanticizing 2016 again.”
Never mind that, at the time, the internet perceived 2016 as a cursed year, even before the election — months earlier, one Slate columnist wondered how 2016 compared to 1348, the year the Black Death took hold in Europe.
“[Pokémon Go to the polls] is in that era of the singular internet, when Facebook and Twitter and Tumblr were all kind of bouncing content back-and-forth and not just this complete anarchic mess of 25 platforms that we now have and don’t use,” Organizer Memes said.
Organizer Memes also notes that some cultural touchstones that felt more significant then — like the obsession with Harambe the gorilla — haven’t had as much staying power as “Pokémon Go to the polls.”
Perhaps this is because we’re bound to remember “Pokémon Go to the polls” every few years on Election Day, and because it appeals to both sides of the aisle. On the right, it’s a way to make fun of Democrats, and on the left, it’s a shared groan of embarrassment.
“It’s like if all the kids in a class are making a joke, and then the teacher gets in on the joke, and it stops being funny,” Mack Finkel, who canvassed at the polls on Tuesday on behalf of a healthcare workers’ union, told TechCrunch. “I think there’s a key essence of millennial cringe happening here, and it’s the same reason that all my friends are rewatching [HBO’s] ‘Girls.’”
Clinton’s decade-old, corny comment can be seen as a precursor to the “Kamala is brat” meme. While the former vice president’s record as a prosecutor initially made her unpopular among some left-leaning young voters, they rallied around her once she became the only alternative to Trump. Gen Z rallied around Harris by creating flashy, absurdist “fan cam”-style edits of the candidate’s best quips in the aesthetic of Charli XCX’s album “Brat,” which soundtracked the summer of 2024.
“Previously the views I saw about Harris were making fun of her being a cop, like her history as attorney general in California with truancy laws,” Jess Rauchberg, an assistant professor of communications at the University of Leeds, told TechCrunch at the time. “Now we see that same style of memeification, but it’s an endorsement.”
It’s hard to say why “Pokémon Go to the polls” jokes still make us laugh — whether we’re mocking Clinton or expressing solidarity with others who keep showing up to vote, even as each passing year leaves us feeling more cynical.
“Pokémon Go to the polls” is a way of urging others to make the time to vote and take Election Day seriously, while still acknowledging disappointment with aging lawmakers who don’t know what it’s like to come of age in the social media era. It’s shrouded in enough irony to project a sense of jaded detachment, yet remains a desperate, earnest plea to our friends: Please, just go vote.

articles.title: Ya está disponible: Bizum amplía los pagos en España y los compradores pueden pagar en tiendas físicas sin necesidad de tarjeta, siempre que acepten el servicio
articles.text:
Con el pago presencial es posible realizar operaciones en tiendas físicas. Basta con pasar el móvil por el datáfono. Así se carga directamente en nuestra cuenta bancaria. Para poder hacerlo sin tarjeta, es preciso que el servicio esté activado en nuestro banco y en el establecimiento. Tener Bizum para enviar dinero a los amigos no es suficiente para poder pagar en la caja de cualquier tienda.
El despliegue de pago presencial ha empezado el pasado mayo. Después ha llegado el lanzamiento de Bizum Pay para las tiendas de apps (Android e iPhone). Se trata de una transferencia inmediata entre cuentas; por tanto, no pasamos por una tarjeta (Visa/Mastercard) para realizar la operación. Desde nuestra aplicación de banco o desde la cartera de Bizum podemos hacerlo.
Es similar a otros tipos de pago desde móvil. Preparamos el teléfono y lo pasamos por el terminal. En este caso, utilizamos la tecnología NFC (comunicación de corto alcance). Es un pago sin contacto; la diferencia es que el dinero viene de nuestra cuenta vinculada a Bizum.
Para nosotros es gratis. En el caso del comercio, puede haber comisiones pactadas con su entidad; además, que el datáfono esté preparado no significa que nuestro banco nos haya activado el servicio.
Cómo activar y utilizar Bizum Pay
Para empezar a utilizar Bizum Pay, tenemos que instalar la app. Es necesario activarla. En el caso de Bizum, tenemos varias opciones para activar esta función. Una es desde la nueva app, introduciendo nuestro número de teléfono de registro en el servicio, y otra opción es desde nuestra app de banco, en el apartado Bizum Pay. En el primer caso nos lleva a nuestra entidad para finalizar el alta.
Posteriormente, podemos indicar que queremos que sea nuestra aplicación predeterminada de pago. De hecho, en el momento de activarla nos pregunta si queremos hacerlo.
También tenemos la opción de modificarlo posteriormente desde los ajustes de nuestro teléfono. En la guía de cómo configurar Bizum Pay podemos ver cómo hacerlo en Android e iOS.
Es importante saber, como explica CaixaBank en sus condiciones de pago presencial, que en aquellos establecimientos donde no esté disponible el pago desde cuenta, podemos utilizar las tarjetas que hemos añadido en nuestra aplicación. Para ello es necesario que tengamos alguna tarjeta compatible añadida. Si queremos pagar solo con Bizum, debemos asegurarnos de que la tienda lo admite.
En el caso de Bizum, se explica en su documentación de límites que no tienen límites en los pagos en tiendas y establecimientos. Los límites los pueden poner los bancos tanto en Bizum como en las tarjetas que utilicen desde la cartera. El importe máximo hay que consultarlo con nuestra entidad.

articles.title: Bitcoin: cuál es el valor de esta criptomoneda
articles.text:
El bitcoin, la primera moneda virtual lanzada al mercado, fue creado por Satoshi Nakamoto (pseudónimo) en 2008 tras la crisis financiera que afectó al mundo; esta divisa digital tenía como base un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales.
Conocido en el mundo de los mercados bajo las siglas BTC, el bitcoin utiliza la criptografía para garantizar que su gestión sea descentralizada, es decir, que no pueda ser regulado por ninguna institución u organismo bancario, lo que a su vez hace que las criptomonedas sean volátiles.
A pesar del avance y alcance que ha tenido el Bitcoin y otros activos digitales de gran talla como Ethereum, organismos como el Banco Mundial, el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) y el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) aún se muestran dudosos sobre los "pros" de este tipo de criptomonedas.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El costo de la criptomoneda de bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 77624.88 dólares por unidad.
Esto quiere decir que el activo digital mostró un cambio del 0.12% en las últimas 24 horas, así como una variación del 0.0% en la última hora.
Actualmente, bitcoin se encuentra en el lugar #1 de popularidad en el mercado digital. Cabe mencionar que el máximo histórico que ha alcanzado esta criptodivisa es de 126.198 dólares por unidad.
Bitcoin alcanzó su máximo histórico
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: Avast lance un VPN gratuit, sans pub, illimité et « sans compromis » : y a-t-il un piège ? — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les VPN gratuits traînent une réputation tenace : quelques gigaoctets par mois, de la publicité et une politique de confidentialité souvent floue. Avast, l’éditeur tchèque de l’antivirus gratuit du même nom, le dit lui-même par la voix de son patron 
Richard Watts : « Les VPN gratuits ont conditionné les utilisateurs à toujours s’attendre à une contrepartie ».
C’est pourquoi la firme présente une nouvelle offre en France avec Avast VPN. Elle promet un service gratuit, sans plafond de données ni publicité et « sans compromis ». Aucune carte bancaire n’est demandée à l’inscription et un seul compte couvre autant d’appareils Windows, Mac, iOS ou Android qu’on veut.
Avast change là de politique : son VPN SecureLine n’avait jusqu’ici aucune version gratuite permanente, seulement un essai de 60 jours avec moyen de paiement obligatoire et passage automatique à un abonnement annuel. Seule la suite gratuite Avast One intégrait un VPN bridé à 5 Go par semaine et à un seul emplacement.
Pour rappel, un VPN fait passer toute la connexion par un tunnel chiffré jusqu’à un serveur distant. Le fournisseur d’accès ou le Wi-Fi public d’une gare ne voient plus les sites consultés, et ces sites voient l’adresse du serveur à la place de la vôtre. Pour construire ce tunnel, Avast VPN utilise WireGuard, un protocole récent et open source que les VPN payants emploient aussi. L’application intègre un kill switch, qui coupe Internet si le VPN décroche afin qu’aucune donnée n’apparaisse en clair. À cela s’ajoute une protection contre les fuites DNS, ces requêtes qui traduisent le nom d’un site en adresse et qui peuvent trahir votre navigation si elles sortent du tunnel.
Trois emplacements au choix, et l’offre payante en embuscade
L’annonce paraît presque trop belle, mais Avast VPN a ses limites. Les utilisateurs gratuits choisissent trois emplacements de serveurs dans un réseau qui couvre 40 pays. La version payante, en comparaison, revendique 103 pays et plus de 140 emplacements. Avast ne s’en cache pas : ceux « qui souhaitent bénéficier de fonctionnalités supplémentaires, comme l’accès à un plus grand nombre de serveurs ou des options avancées de confidentialité et de protection de la vie privée, peuvent choisir de passer à l’offre supérieure, selon leurs besoins ».
L’offre payante est facturée 11,99 euros par mois ou 99,99 euros par an.
Côté vitesse, la version gratuite d’Avast VPN n’est pas la plus rapide. Lors d’un court essai avec un emplacement similaire aux États-Unis, connecté depuis le même smartphone au Wi-Fi de nos locaux dans Paris, nous avons obtenu de meilleurs débits avec Proton VPN sur le speedtest d’Ookla.
|  | Avast VPN | Proton VPN | 
| Ping (ms) | 146 | 94 | 
| Descendant (Mb/s) | 69,3 | 90,8 | 
| Ascendant (Mb/s) | 41,7 | 85,1 | 
Avast traîne aussi un passif sur les données personnelles. De 2014 à 2020, sa filiale Jumpshot a revendu l’historique de navigation collecté par l’antivirus et ses extensions de navigateur à plus de 100 entreprises, dont des courtiers en données, selon la FTC, l’autorité américaine de protection des consommateurs. En 2024, le gendarme a interdit à Avast de vendre ces données à des fins publicitaires et Avast a écopé d’une amende de 16,5 millions de dollars. Le VPN n’était pas en cause, et Avast a fermé Jumpshot en janvier 2020.
Pour son nouveau VPN, Avast promet une politique dite no-logs, c’est-à-dire qu’il s’engage à ne garder aucune trace de l’activité de ses utilisateurs, et donc à ne rien en vendre. Un audit indépendant du cabinet VerSprite doit vérifier cette politique chaque année.
Avast VPN est disponible dès ce mercredi en France sur Windows, Mac, iOS et Android, sans abonnement à résilier. D’ici le premier rapport de VerSprite, attendu ce mois-ci, la promesse no-logs ne repose que sur la parole d’Avast.

articles.title: Fast wie in Minority Report – diese KI soll Gewalt verhindern, bevor sie passiert
articles.text:
KI im Gefängnis: Michigan will gefährliche Häftlinge erkennen, bevor etwas passiert
In Steven Spielbergs Science-Fiction-Thriller Minority Report sehen sogenannte Precogs dank hellseherischer Fähigkeiten Morde voraus, die erst in der Zukunft stattfänden. Die Namen von Tätern und Opfern sind ebenso bekannt wie der Zeitpunkt der Gewalttaten – die potenziellen Täter werden aus dem Verkehr gezogen.
Recidiviz-KI bewertet Häftlinge in Michigan
Letztlich stellt sich aber heraus, dass das System Fehler hat, da die Precogs auch Situationen vorhersehen, in denen ein Mord wahrscheinlich ist, aber nicht stattfindet. Ein neues KI-System, das die Justizvollzugsbehörde des US-Bundesstaates Michigan einsetzen will, erinnert im Kern an Spielbergs filmische Zukunftsvision, wenn das Ganze in der Realität auch weniger drastisch ausfallen dürfte.
Konkret geht es um eine KI-gestützte Software, die in Gefängnissen in Michigan künftig vorhersagen soll, welche Gefangene eine potenzielle Gefahr darstellen könnten. Diese Risikoeinschätzung dient dazu, die Häftlinge in eine von insgesamt fünf verschiedenen Sicherheitsstufen einzuordnen, wie Futurism berichtet.
Michigan Department of Corrections plant fünf Sicherheitsstufen
Die Gefängnisbehörde erhofft sich dadurch eine um 30 Prozent genauere Vorhersage als mit den aktuellen Verfahren. Ein entsprechendes Pilotprojekt soll Anfang Dezember 2026 in mehreren Männergefängnissen starten, wie die Behörde mitteilte. Ziel ist demnach, die zuletzt stark gestiegene Zahl von Angriffen auf Beschäftigte sowie Gewalt zwischen Inhaftierten zu senken.
Das Programm hat die Behörde zusammen mit der aus Google hervorgegangenen gemeinnützigen Organisation Recidiviz entwickelt. „Ich bin zuversichtlich, dass wir mit diesem Pilotprojekt und der Nutzung wissenschaftlich fundierter sowie historischer Daten ein dynamisches und objektives Instrument entwickelt haben, das die Sicherheit unserer Einrichtungen stärken wird“, erklärte die Direktorin Heidi E. Washington.
Allerdings erklärte Washington nicht, welche Daten die KI erhält. Das wiederum ist aber mitentscheidend dafür, wie korrekt das System arbeitet. Und davon hängt viel ab. Je nach Einstufung erhalten die Gefangenen während ihres Aufenthalts unterschiedliche Programme oder Ressourcen. Zudem entscheidet sich dadurch, mit wem sie untergebracht werden.
Propublica kritisiert Biases in Louisiana
Macht die KI hier Fehler, etwa durch nicht korrigierte Vorurteile, kann das zu strengeren Haftbedingungen und einer möglicherweise schlechteren Vorbereitung für die Zeit nach der Haft führen. Bei einem ähnlichen Programm zur Risikobewertung im US-Bundesstaat Louisiana sollen die zur Einstufung verwendeten Daten rassistische und sozioökonomische Biases enthalten haben, wie eine Untersuchung von Propublica zeigte. Mit negativen Folgen für das Strafvollzugssystem.

articles.title: Acecores wins $10,000 grand prize at TC Battlefield 2026
articles.text:
Acecore, a Nigerian startup that builds home energy storage systems, won TC Battlefield 2026 at Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos on Thursday, October 29, taking home the $10,000 grand prize.
Supplya, which gives informal retailers stock on credit, came second and won $5,000. Navidyn, a maritime robotics startup, came third with $2,500.
Caleb Iwuoha, Acecore’s founder and chief executive, told the judges at Wednesday’s final that the system’s casing and battery management software were “all built here in Nigeria by our very own hands.”
Acecore sells a home battery system and a smart socket that lets users control their appliances. It says its system costs more than 20% less than comparable products, and a partner bank lets customers pay in instalments
The startup is building locally in a market that imports most of its power hardware. Nigeria imported 1,721 megawatts of solar panels from China in the 12 months to June 2025, making it Africa’s second-largest importer after South Africa, according to the energy think tank Ember.
The three winners were chosen from 10 finalists that also included Growwr, Kuraway, Fertitude, Lena, QiqiFarms, Riwe and Swiftway Shippers. The judges were Folakemi Osho, general manager of HoaQ; Elijah Shokenu, head of ventures at SWIT; Kosen Kenta, principal at Antler; and Adeniyi Adebayo, chief business officer of Yango Group, which sponsored the competition.
Acecore faced the toughest questions on price. One judge pointed out that imported Chinese systems land in Nigeria at a price similar to Acecore’s, which starts at about $5,250, and pressed Iwuoha on his unit economics. He said the company runs a 62% margin.
Navidyn, which builds underwater robots to inspect offshore oil and gas sites, made the broader case for hardware. “So far, Africa has invested in fintech, logtech, agritech, edtech. Now it’s time to invest in advanced AI and robotics,” its co-founders told the judges. The startup says a Sahara Group representative brought it a $5,000 inspection job before its product was ready.
Supplya, the runner-up, says it has extended more than $150,000 in credit to small shops since October 2024, and that 98% has been repaid.
Navidyn and Supplya, along with the women’s health app Fertitude, also won places in Antler’s residency programme, where they can raise up to $250,000 in pre-seed investment.
Two of this year’s three podium spots went to startups building physical products in Nigeria, a slower and costlier path than software. If Acecore and Navidyn can hold their margins against imports, they will show investors that hardware made in Nigeria can compete on price as well as on story.

articles.title: Google will let schools skip AI tools, but they have to give up search, too
articles.text:
While Google is trying to move beyond Chromebooks, the ubiquity of these devices has made the company’s education products huge in schools. Now, Google says it will let educators choose whether to allow its AI tools in the classroom. However, blocking AI tools also means giving up search, leaving schools with a difficult decision.
Google’s new overarching approach to AI in K-12 classrooms sounds good on the surface. After consulting educators, researchers, and lawmakers, Google has decided that schools using its education products will be opted out of AI tools by default. It will be up to administrators to manually enable them when these changes roll out in the coming months.
When you look at what Google considers to be an AI tool, the nature of the Faustian bargain becomes clear. The affected products are Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. There’s no picking and choosing—you either allow all the AI or none of it.
This is actually consistent with Google’s approach in the consumer space. Google executives have said in no uncertain terms that Google Search is AI search. Most searches now provide an AI Overview at the top, and the company is constantly coming up with new ways to nudge people toward the conversational AI Mode chatbot function. Google sees this as the future.

articles.title: Ferrari’s controversial Luce EV is sold out for 2027 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The Luce, Ferrari’s first electric car and one of its most polarizing models, isn’t just selling. It’s selling out.
The five-seater EV designed by Jony Ive, Apple’s longtime design chief, was mocked and widely panned when it debuted in May, sending Ferrari’s stock price lower. But all that criticism hasn’t dampened demand, according to CEO Benedetto Vigna.
The 2027 production run of the Luce, which starts at about $615,000, is “fully allocated,” Vigna said Tuesday during the company’s third-quarter earnings call, meaning every car Ferrari plans to build next year already has a buyer. “If someone comes, he has to wait one year to get the cars,” Vigna added. The first deliveries of the Luce are expected to begin in the fourth quarter.
Just how many Luce cars that represents is unclear. Ferrari has never publicly disclosed how many Luce vehicles it plans to produce. Financial Times reported earlier this year, citing unnamed sources, that Ferrari planned to sell just under 500 units this year. The company’s longer-term target is to sell 2,500 units by 2030, or about 600 a year, according to Financial Times.
Speculation on who these buyers are — ahem, the founders of multibillion-dollar AI labs, perhaps? — will have to remain just that until Luces are spotted in the wild. Vigna wouldn’t provide a breakdown of who these Luce customers are, only noting it was a “good mix in terms of client, it is a good mix also in terms of geography.” He later added that there is no specific pattern or demographic of Luce buyers.
While Luce deliveries have yet to begin, Ferrari’s existing lineup and growing demand for personalized options helped fuel its financial performance in the third quarter. Revenue from customizations, which executives said accounted for more than 21% of revenue from cars and spare parts, helped boost profits. The company said deliveries of the F80, its limited-run hypercar, and customization reflect its clients’ “ever-deepening desire” to make each Ferrari uniquely their own. As a result, the company raised its full-year guidance, saying it now expects adjusted earnings of at least €3 billion ($3.36 billion), up from €2.97 billion.
Ferrari, which enjoys some of the highest profit margins in the auto industry, reported third-quarter revenue of €1.9 billion, up 7% from a year earlier, and net income of €431 million, up 13%. Operating profit was €563 million, for an operating margin of 29.7%, meaning the company kept roughly 30 cents of every dollar of revenue as profit from its core business.

articles.title: Safari gets Siri AI actions and Vertical Tabs with macOS 27.3
articles.text:
Apple’s iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 betas are now available, sporting several updates to Apple apps, like the Health app, and more.
But Safari is also getting a few notable upgrades, so let’s do a deep dive into what’s new with Safari.
Vertical Tabs
A new vertical layout for navigating and managing your tabs lets you maximize your space. The tabs on the side appear as icons so they take up less room, and hovering over the icon will show the name first, but hover a little longer and Safari will show a small preview of what’s open in that tab.
Vertical Tabs will be available on MacBook, iPad and the iPhone Duo. You can turn it on by heading to Safari settings on these platforms.
Adaptive Dark Mode
Safari can automatically apply Dark Mode to webpages that don’t support it natively. When you’re in Dark Mode and hit a page with a bright background, Safari will have a pop-up saying ‘Try Adaptive Dark Mode.’ Tapping it will render a Dark Mode version of the webpage.
However, for webpages that must be bright for some reason, developers can exclude their site from Adaptive Dark Mode.
This update is coming to iOS, macOS, and iPadOS.
Siri AI Actions
With Siri AI custom actions on Safari, you can ask the assistant to sort your tabs, move them around, sort, organize and close them by asking. Further, Siri AI is aware of your webpage and even other tabs, so if you’re shopping for shoes and land on a page with a pair you like, but have five other tabs open, you can ask Siri to compare the ones you’re looking at to the other ones on your tabs.
This feature is coming to Apple Intelligence-supported devices.

articles.title: Astronautas da NASA votam nas eleições dos EUA a mais de 400 km da Terra
articles.text:
Estar a mais de 400 quilômetros da Terra não impediu três astronautas estadunidenses de participar das eleições legislativas dos Estados Unidos nesta terça-feira (3). A bordo da Estação Espacial Internacional (ISS, na sigla em inglês), Anil Menon, Jessica Watkins e Luke Delaney preencheram cédulas eletrônicas e enviaram seus votos às autoridades eleitorais em Harris County, no Texas (EUA).
A participação foi confirmada por Menon em publicação nas redes sociais. Em vídeo, o astronauta mostrou o pequeno compartimento onde dorme e que também serviu como cabine de votação. Com um computador, ele preencheu o formulário eletrônico e encaminhou a cédula de volta à Terra.
“Sim, você pode até votar do espaço! Todos os três tripulantes americanos tiveram o privilégio de votar a bordo da estação espacial. Preenchemos uma cédula eletrônica e a enviamos com segurança às autoridades eleitorais”, escreveu Menon.
Como funciona o voto dos astronautas?
O procedimento começa antes mesmo da votação. Assim como outros estadunidenses que estão longe de suas residências, os astronautas podem solicitar uma cédula de votação ausente por meio de formulário federal chamado Federal Post Card Application.
Depois de receber o documento em formato eletrônico, o tripulante pode preenchê-lo a bordo da estação espacial e enviá-lo de volta à Terra pela infraestrutura de comunicação da NASA.
O caminho envolve diferentes etapas:
- O astronauta preenche a cédula eletrônica em seu computador na ISS;
- O documento é transmitido pelo sistema de satélites de comunicação da NASA até uma antena terrestre no White Sands Test Facility, no Novo México (EUA);
- A agência encaminha o arquivo ao Centro Espacial Johnson, em Houston, no Texas (EUA);
- O documento chega ao cartório eleitoral responsável pelo registro do astronauta, onde o voto é processado.
A segurança também faz parte do procedimento. Segundo a NASA, a cédula é criptografada e só pode ser acessada pelo astronauta e pelo funcionário eleitoral responsável por recebê-la.
Leia mais:
- NASA procura ajuda para salvar o Hubble
- Telescópio espacial da NASA está prestes a cair na Terra – Brasil pode ser atingido?
- Desviar asteroide com bomba nuclear depende de um detalhe surpreendente
Votar do espaço é possível desde 1997
A possibilidade de participar de eleições diretamente do espaço existe há quase três décadas. Em 1997, o Texas aprovou lei que permitiu aos astronautas registrados no Estado votar eletronicamente durante missões espaciais.
Naquele mesmo ano, David Wolf se tornou o primeiro estadunidense a votar fora da Terra. Ele estava a bordo da estação espacial russa Mir, antes mesmo da chegada dos primeiros tripulantes à ISS, em novembro de 2000.
A concentração de domicílios eleitorais de astronautas no Texas tem explicação prática: o Estado abriga o Centro Espacial Johnson, em Houston, responsável pelo treinamento e pelo suporte às missões tripuladas da NASA.
Desde então, o procedimento permite que profissionais em missões de longa duração mantenham o direito de participar das eleições estadunidenses, mesmo quando estão em órbita.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Anthropic employee wages are now costing the AI giant over $100,000 per person per month
articles.text:
Anthropic employee wages are now costing the AI giant over $100,000 per person per month
Anthropic spends billions on personnel every year
- Anthropic workers are likely making a good salary, plus stock-based compensation
- Revenue per employee is more than 2x Meta's and 2.6x Google's
- The company is targeting a valuation of around $1.5 trillion
Anthropic has confirmed in a recent S-1 filing that it spent $1.711 billion on personnel in its most recent three-month period, down slightly on the previous quarter's $1.857 billion but up around 3.5x compared with the same quarter in 2025 ($489 million).
With around 5,300 people on the books, it means the average worker set the company back over $322,000 for the quarter, or over $107,000 per month.
While these figures are likely wild overestimates for the average worker's pay, they show just how much the AI giant is having to spend on talent compared with last year.
Anthropic is spending billions on workers' salaries
Crucially, the average worker did not receive $107,000 in a single month, because these figures also include bonuses, employee benefits, payroll taxes and stock-based compensation. An estimated $1.1 billion of the quarterly total came from stock-based compensation, accounting for nearly two-thirds of the total sum.
Still, personnel costs accounted for around 15% of the company's revenue over the first nine months of 2026, which puts Anthropic in a positive position. The company spent $4.8 billion on personnel in the first three quarters.
Flip those figures around and we have a company that's making an estimated $6.6 million in revenue per employee, compared with $3.2 million at Meta and $2.5 million at Google, per Business Insider calculations.
Recruiting AI talent is expensive
Anthropic doesn't publish salary information, but given its huge expenditure relative to the number of employees, it's clear that recruiting AI talent is expensive. With stock-based compensation accounting for two-thirds of Anthropic's personnel expenditure, workers are likely being attracted by the potential of huge future wealth, rather than immediate compensation.

articles.title: Can agent standards keep up with the companies building them?
articles.text:
Can agent standards keep up with the companies building them?
Mazin Gilbert, executive director of the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation, left Google earlier this year to lead the new AAIF, and he recently shared with The New Stack a truth central to its mission: The AAIF has to move faster than its members.
Gilbert, speaking in an interview at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America in San Jose last month, said on The New Stack podcast, “If this foundation does not move at the speed of light, it becomes irrelevant.”
He also talked about how he gets OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google to agree on standards — even though they compete on products. Those companies are going to build products “with and without the standards,” he says.
All of this is happening while the foundation’s own members are often still figuring out how to build and use agents themselves. Some contribute to protocols and ship products, but others are still trying to get their agents out of the lab and into production. Gilbert says a third group of companies “frankly are panicking,” because they don’t have an agent strategy yet.
The San Jose event drew 4,300 registrants, he says, double the size of the foundation’s previous largest event in Amsterdam earlier this year.
How MCP gets built
Before our recording, Gilbert had just met with a group of maintainers from “very fiercely competing companies” who were working on the protocols together. All of those companies depend on these standards, he says, so they have a reason to get the work done.
“These protocols are the air you breathe.” 
—Mazin Gilbert, executive director, AAIF.
“These protocols are the air you breathe. These protocols are the plumbing,” Gilbert says. “They may not be that sexy, maybe, but if we don’t get those right, that entire agentic AI space will be a mess, expensive and prohibitive basically for any company to deploy this at scale.”
As an example, he points to the July release of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification, which made the protocol stateless. “Every one of those companies not only contributed to it, but they ended up completely updating their entire stack to the stateless MCP,” he says.
MCP downloads grew tenfold in the protocol’s first 10 months at the foundation, according to Gilbert, after Anthropic donated it last December. Today, fewer than 15 percent of its maintainers work at Anthropic, and more than 1,000 organizations contribute 75 percent of the pull requests, he says. Those contributors include U.S. retailers and companies around the world.
At the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), many projects started at startups before they were donated. At the AAIF, Gilbert says, large companies tend to contribute the protocols, and smaller companies extend them and build businesses on top.
Some of those startups were doing something “very different” six months or a year ago, he says, and some didn’t exist yet. Now they’re building enterprise products on MCP and the foundation’s gateway projects to connect agents to companies’ back-end systems.
Getting members to contribute
The AAIF now has 305 members, and Gilbert said in his keynote that about one new company joins every business day. He calls it the fastest-growing foundation in the Linux Foundation’s history. About 40 percent of its members are startups, and 19 percent are nonprofits, national labs, and academic institutions.
“None of us have done this before, so I just want to be very clear about that. We are learning this as we go,” he says.
Part of the job is making membership worth enough that companies actively contribute. “It’s not about the money. Their time is far more valuable than their money. Their people are far more valuable than the money,” Gilbert says.
He’d like every member to contribute, but also acknowledges that’s not the case yet. He knows who does, because he uses his own agents to track contributions across the foundation.
Some companies are still trying to understand what agents can do for them and what they’d get back on the investment. Others don’t know how to contribute. Gilbert encourages them to start by joining a working group and listening, and says they don’t have to arrive as experts. For companies still learning, the foundation launched its first certification in September: the Model Context Protocol Associate (MCPA).
The Gates Foundation, which joined in September, now sits on the AAIF’s board. Gilbert says it’s helping developers in parts of Africa and South Asia get the training and certification they need to contribute, and to attend events they couldn’t otherwise afford.
Pressed on whether nonprofits and for-profit companies clash inside the foundation, Gilbert says he hasn’t seen it yet. “Whether you are a nonprofit, for-profit, small, large, your value, your impact, your power in this foundation really depends on contributions,” he says.
How many gateways do you need?
The foundation is also choosing which projects to accept. The community has submitted 65 projects through its public intake process, Gilbert says, and the AAIF has declined some. The first 10 to 20 projects “really define the DNA of this foundation,” he says.
With the four projects it announced in San Jose (Agent Skills from Anthropic, Open Responses from OpenAI, OpenEnv from Hugging Face, and OpenSandbox from Alibaba), the AAIF now hosts 10.
In some cases, the foundation is taking in technologies that are already widely adopted, like MCP and Agent Skills. In others, nobody agrees yet on what a standard should look like.
Gateways are one example. The AAIF approved two gateway projects this year, Solo.io’s agentgateway and Agent Router, which moved over from the CNCF’s Envoy project in September. Gilbert says five or six more companies want to contribute their own. Does the community need “six gateways or 10 gateways,” he asks, “or do we need to harmonize those together?”
He doesn’t have an answer yet, and says the community doesn’t either. The foundation gives those companies neutral governance to work it out together, he says.
The technical committee and governing board evaluate each proposal, including whether the AAIF is the right home for it, Gilbert says. They look at every layer of the stack, including agent frameworks, execution harnesses, gateways, guardrails, memory, protocols, observability, and identity. Not every project the foundation accepts will become the standard, he notes.
Agents that can transact
Gilbert wants the foundation to work on identity, security, trust, and observability. He also wants it to take on agent commerce.
“These agents, the internet of agents, must be transactional,” he says. An agent making a purchase would need to discover a catalog, talk to a merchant’s agent, negotiate, pay, and handle returns or disputes, and Gilbert says each step still needs a protocol.
He’s also excited about physical AI, meaning protocols for agents that talk to machines and appliances instead of databases. “Your refrigerator, your washing machines. It’s so cool,” he says. “It’s like science fiction, but it’s happening now.”
Wherever the protocols fall short, Gilbert says, companies will write custom code, and customers will end up paying to support it. A standard that arrives after a customer has built and deployed its own integration still leaves that customer with code to maintain.

articles.title: ServiceNow on-behalf-of token exchange with Bedrock AgentCore Gateway | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
ServiceNow on-behalf-of token exchange with Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
AI agents that interact with enterprise APIs on behalf of users need to maintain user identity throughout the request chain. Without identity propagation, API calls arrive at downstream services as the application itself rather than the user who initiated the action. This breaks audit trails, bypasses user-level access controls, and violates the principle of least privilege.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. This post shows how to configure AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, for an on-behalf-of (OBO) token exchange with Microsoft Entra ID. An AI agent can then call the ServiceNow REST API while preserving the calling user’s identity. You configure the token exchange on the gateway target, and AgentCore Gateway performs the exchange on each request. The pattern can be applied to other REST APIs protected by OAuth.
In production, you can additionally pair identity propagation with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to filter harmful content and validate the agent’s inputs and outputs.
Solution overview
The architecture involves three key components connected through AgentCore Gateway:
- An AI agent application, protected by Microsoft Entra ID through an OAuth application registration.
- A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, implemented using AgentCore Gateway, sitting between the agent and ServiceNow.
- The ServiceNow REST API, configured with an inbound OAuth integration tied to Microsoft Entra ID.
The following figure shows the end-to-end solution architecture, including components within AWS, Microsoft Entra ID, and ServiceNow.
As shown in Figure 1, the user acquires a JSON Web Token (JWT) to invoke the agent 1. The agent authenticates to the gateway with a JWT token scoped to the agent’s own application registration 2. The gateway then exchanges that token, using the OBO flow, for a new token scoped to the ServiceNow API connector, with the original user’s identity preserved 3. ServiceNow receives a valid token whose preferred_username claim maps to an existing ServiceNow user and applies that user’s permissions to the API call 4.
How OBO token exchange works in this context
When the agent calls the gateway, it presents a JWT with an audience claim matching the agent’s client ID (for example, 3ff88e17-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX). ServiceNow, however, expects a token with an audience claim matching its own API connector client ID (5d4a7a11-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX).
The OBO flow bridges this gap. AgentCore Gateway sends the inbound token to the Entra token endpoint along with the agent application’s client credentials, the target scope, and a parameter requested_token_use: on_behalf_of. Entra validates that the calling user consented to the delegation, then issues a new token for the ServiceNow API with the original user’s claims intact.
Prerequisites
Before you begin, you need the following:
- An AWS account with access to AgentCore Gateway.
- A Microsoft Entra ID tenant with permissions to create application registrations. Your account needs at least the Application Developer role to register applications.
- A ServiceNow instance with administrative access to configure inbound OAuth integrations. You can create a ServiceNow personal developer instance (PDI) at the ServiceNow personal developer instance signup page https://developer.servicenow.com/.
- Two Entra application registrations: one representing the AI agent, and one representing the ServiceNow API connector.
Configuring Microsoft Entra ID
Start by creating an application registration to represent the ServiceNow API connector. The following screenshot shows the application registration page for the ServiceNow API Connector in Microsoft Entra ID.
After creating, in the Overview page note the Application (client) ID.
In the navigation menu expand Manage and select Expose an API and add a scope named user_impersonation using the default Application ID URI. This scope is what the OBO flow requests when exchanging tokens. The following screenshot shows how to expose an API in Microsoft Entra ID.
Next, create an application registration for the AI agent. The following screenshot shows the application registration page in Microsoft Entra ID for the ServiceNow Agent application.
Note the Application (client) ID for the ServiceNowAgent.
Create a client secret on this registration. The gateway needs these credentials to perform the OBO exchange. The following screenshot shows how you can create a client secret on the ServiceNow Agent application registration in Microsoft Entra ID.
Then configure the agent application to have API permissions to call the ServiceNow API connector application. The following screenshot shows the API permissions that you need to configure on the ServiceNow Agent application registration in Microsoft Entra ID.
No changes to the Entra configuration are needed beyond what you would set up for any standard OBO integration between two applications.
Configuring ServiceNow
In the ServiceNow administrative console, navigate to System OAuth > Inbound Integrations and create a new inbound integration (Third party ID token issued by OIDC supporting identity provider). Specify the client ID from the ServiceNow API connector application registration you created in Entra. The following screenshot shows the configuration of the inbound integration in ServiceNow.
In the same screen, create a new OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider configuration and enter the OIDC metadata URL for your Entra tenant. Map the user claim to the appropriate user field. For example, if your Entra tenant places the user’s email in the preferred_username claim, map that to the Email field in ServiceNow. Clear JTI verification if your Entra tenant doesn’t include it in tokens. Entra uses an internal claim named uti on tokens it issues, which is equivalent to JTI. Consider mapping this uti claim to a jti claim to provide additional replay protection and denylisting. The following screenshot shows how to configure the OIDC provider in ServiceNow.
Finally, in the same screen, create an auth scope for the integration (for example, APIConnector). The following screenshot shows how to create a new auth scope in ServiceNow.
Limit the auth scope to the Table API, or whichever ServiceNow APIs your agent needs to access, as shown in the following screenshot.
After this configuration is complete, ServiceNow accepts authorization tokens with an audience of your API connector’s client ID and resolves the calling user from the preferred_username claim.
Configuring AgentCore Gateway
With Entra and ServiceNow configured, you can now set up AgentCore Gateway to handle the OBO exchange natively.
Step 1: Create an outbound auth configuration
Create a new outbound auth configuration (choose Build > Identity > Add Outbound Auth > Add OAuth client) in AgentCore and select Customized provider. Enter the client ID and client secret from your agent application registration, along with the Entra discovery URL as shown in the following screenshot.
Expand Additional configurations and select JWT authorization grant as shown in the following screenshot. This tells the gateway to use a JWT-based grant type for token exchange.
Step 2: Create the gateway with MCP version 2025-11-25
Create a new AgentCore Gateway (Build > Gateways > Create gateway). When defining the gateway details, expand Additional configurations — optional and select MCP version 2025-11-25 as shown in the following screenshot. This version is required for native OBO support. You can’t turn on native OBO for gateways created with earlier MCP versions.
Configure the inbound identity using your agent’s application registration (select Use existing identity provider configurations), as you would for any gateway that accepts Entra-authenticated requests.
Under JWT Authorization Configuration add the Application ID we documented earlier for the ServiceNowAgent as shown in the following screenshot.
Step 3: Add a target with token exchange
Add a target to the gateway pointing to your ServiceNow REST endpoint. Define the schema inline. For example, to expose a tool called ListIncidents that calls the ServiceNow Table API, you can use the following OpenAPI specification (replace the server URL with that for your PDI).
The following screenshot shows how to configure the REST API target in AgentCore Gateway with the OpenAPI schema.
For the Outbound Auth configuration on the target, select OAuth as the outbound identity provider and choose the outbound auth configuration you created in Step 1.
Now expand the Additional configurations section and select Token exchange grant. Configure the following:
Scope: api://5d4a7a11-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/user_impersonation
This is the scope you exposed on the ServiceNow API connector application registration in Entra.
Custom parameter (key-value pair): requested_token_use:on_behalf_of
This parameter is critical. Without it, Entra doesn’t perform the OBO exchange and the call to ServiceNow fails with an authentication error.
The final configuration is shown in the following screenshot.
Step 4: Save and test
Save the target configuration. AgentCore Gateway now automatically exchanges inbound tokens for valid ServiceNow tokens, preserving user identity, with no custom code.
When an agent calls the gateway, the following happens transparently:
- The gateway receives the agent’s JWT (audience: agent client ID).
- The gateway sends the token to Entra’s token endpoint with the OBO grant type.
- Entra issues a new token (audience: ServiceNow API connector client ID) with the original user’s claims.
- The gateway forwards the request to ServiceNow with the exchanged token.
- ServiceNow resolves the user from the token and applies their permissions.
The following code snippet shows a minimal chat agent that interacts with ServiceNow through the MCP server.
Troubleshooting
If you receive authentication errors from ServiceNow, verify that:
- The preferred_username claim in the exchanged token maps to a valid user email in ServiceNow.
- The auth scope on the ServiceNow inbound integration permits access to the API endpoints your agent is calling.
- The agent application has API permissions to the ServiceNow API connector application in Entra.
Cleaning up
To avoid ongoing charges, delete the following resources if you created them for testing:
- The AgentCore Gateway and its targets.
- The outbound auth configuration.
- The Entra application registrations (if created specifically for this walkthrough).
- The ServiceNow inbound integration and OIDC provider configuration.
Conclusion
The native OBO support in AgentCore Gateway removes the need for custom AWS Lambda interceptors to perform token exchanges. You configure the token exchange directly on the gateway target, and the gateway handles it transparently on every request. This approach maintains user identity across the agent-to-API chain, supports ServiceNow’s user-level access controls, and eliminates custom code that would need to be maintained separately.
To get started with AgentCore Gateway, see the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore documentation. For more on Microsoft Entra’s OBO flow, refer to the Microsoft identity platform documentation.

articles.title: Macronix Adds Hardware Security to NOR Flash Ahead of EU CRA - EE Times
articles.text:
The European Union’s Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), which becomes mandatory in December 2027, is raising the bar for cybersecurity in connected devices. Rather than relying on software patches to address vulnerabilities after they emerge, manufacturers are under growing pressure to build security into products from the outset. For connected devices, that shift puts flash memory in a new role: alongside storing code and data, it must help protect device identity, data integrity and software updates.
Donald Huang, director of product marketing and cybersecurity manager at Macronix International, said software updates alone cannot adequately address threats such as physical attacks and the interception or manipulation of communications. The CRA’s Security by Design principle calls for protection to be built into products from the earliest stages of development, extending a hardware root of trust (ROT) beyond the processor and into storage components.
Donald Huang, director of product marketing and cybersecurity manager at Macronix International
Why Security Must Extend Beyond Software
Securely Update Millions of DevicesThe CRA sets requirements for secure product design, protection of critical assets, and identity and supply-chain authentication. Manufacturers must ensure that components are trustworthy and that keys, code and data are protected from the beginning of the design process. Products must also be built to withstand cyberattacks at the system level. These requirements are putting the hardware ROT, which combines physical protection with cryptographic authentication, in the spotlight.
As Huang explained, attackers have several ways to get around software-based defenses. They can manipulate voltage, temperature or clock signals to launch physical attacks, tap the bus between flash memory and the host to intercept data, or replay previously valid commands. Security measures confined to software leave potential entry points in the hardware and communication interfaces.
Macronix developed its ArmorFlash family to address these threats by building security functions directly into NOR flash. Huang noted that the company introduced its security memory portfolio in 2019, embedding security into the storage architecture instead of relying on a separate security chip alongside conventional flash.
A conventional design pairs standard NOR flash with a separate secure element (SE), requiring additional hardware and an interface between the SE and the system-on-chip (SoC). ArmorFlash takes a different approach, integrating a secure engine, authentication functions and security protocols into the flash device itself. It connects to the host through a standard Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) and provides both general-purpose storage and a configurable secure area.
The integrated approach can also ease the addition of security to existing products. Because redesigning an established system’s SoC and circuitry can be costly and disruptive, ArmorFlash uses a standard SPI interface and pin-compatible design to add hardware security without extensive circuit changes. This can reduce both the hardware cost and the design complexity associated with a separate secure element.
ArmorFlash Combines Secure Boot, PUF and Data Protection
Macronix offers several products to address different security needs. For instance, ArmorBoot (MX76) supports secure boot, while ArmorFlash (MX75/MX78) provides data security.
The ArmorBoot MX76 verifies the integrity of boot code stored in flash when a system starts up, helping prevent code tampering and unauthorized execution. The same protection can extend to over-the-air (OTA) updates: before new code runs, the system verifies its source and integrity. A recovery mechanism can then restore a secure version if an update or startup process encounters an abnormal condition.
The MX78 ArmorFlash focuses on protecting data and communications. It supports multiple independent data regions, each associated with a root key, with access controls configurable for ordinary reads, authenticated reads or encrypted reads. A 128-Mbit device, for example, can be divided into 32 independent 4-Mbit regions, allowing access privileges to be separated at the storage level.
The MX78 also supports encryption of host access requests and message authentication using mechanisms such as Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC). These features help guard against data and command exposure through bus snooping. Its monotonic counter, which can only increment, also helps prevent rollback attacks during OTA updates by blocking the reuse of older software versions or commands.
Another key technology in ArmorFlash is the physically unclonable function (PUF), which gives each chip a unique fingerprint. A PUF derives distinctive identification information and keys from minute physical and electrical variations that naturally occur during chip manufacturing. Beyond device authentication, it can help bind hardware to a host by establishing a cryptographic relationship between the flash device and an authorized SoC.
ArmorFlash also incorporates physical defenses. An active metal shield and environmental tamper-detection sensors monitor conditions such as voltage surges, temperature changes and clock anomalies. When abnormal conditions are detected, the device can trigger protective responses to help reduce the risk of physical probing and other attacks.
Automotive Qualification Opens Doors for Secure Flash
Automotive and industrial systems are among the main markets for secure flash, where reliability and long-term product support are essential. The ArmorFlash family meets AEC-Q100 Grade 1 automotive reliability requirements and has passed ISO 26262 ASIL D functional safety and ISO/SAE 21434 automotive cybersecurity standards. It also supports compliance with FIPS 140-2/140-3 cryptographic module requirements.
Huang said ArmorFlash is in mass production, with cumulative shipments exceeding several million units. The devices have been adopted in autonomous driving and advanced driver-assistance systems development platforms from multiple major international companies. Demand could expand beyond automotive as networking and communications equipment place greater emphasis on device identity, data protection and secure updates. Other potential applications requiring long-term data protection include medical equipment, financial services, digital rights management, and AI systems.
With the EU CRA deadline approaching, connected-device manufacturers face the challenge of adding hardware-level protection to existing designs while meeting the requirements for access to the European market. By combining high-performance storage, a secure engine and chip-level trust mechanisms in a single device, Macronix aims to offer a more cost-effective way to strengthen the security of existing systems and support their transition toward zero-trust architectures.
As connected-device security requirements evolve, the integration of hardware protection and nonvolatile memory (NVM) is becoming more consequential. Macronix will showcase its latest NVM technologies and application solutions at electronica 2026, taking place in Munich, Germany, from November 10 to 13. The portfolio will cover automotive electronics and edge AI, including security Flash technologies. Macronix will exhibit at Hall C5, Stand 279.
