articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 3, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, November 03, 2026.
India continues to remain an important growth market for Apple as startups continue to raise funding across cheque sizes. YourStory brings you this and other latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
India shines in Apple’s record September quarter
India emerged as a stellar growth market for Apple in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, registering an all-time company revenue record in the country. “We also set September quarter revenue records in both developed and emerging markets, in addition to an all-time record in India,” Apple Chief Executive Officer John Ternus said. The performance in India was propelled by a September quarter record for iPhone upgraders, with Worldpanel survey data ranking iPhone among the top-selling smartphone models in the country.
VC funding into Indian startups plunges 66% in October
Venture capital (VC) funding into Indian startups touched a new low in October, with a decline of 66% against October of last year. When compared with the VC funding raised in September 2025, the drop was 49%. The total VC funding in October came in at just $581 million as compared with $1.6 billion in October 2025, according to YourStory Research. In September 2026, the funding amount was $1.1 billion.
Funding news
PowerUp Money raises $10M to expand AI-led wealth management
PowerUp Money, a wealthtech platform offering mutual fund advice and digital wealth management services, has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Flourish Ventures, an early-stage investment firm. Existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC also participated.
The Bengaluru-based company plans to use a significant portion of the capital to develop its AI-powered wealth management platform and expand its managed advisory business.
Sachin Tendulkar backs Hitwicket maker Metasports Interactive
Metasports Interactive, the Hyderabad-based maker of cricket strategy game Hitwicket, has brought cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar on board as a strategic investor. He will also serve as the game’s brand ambassador.
The financial terms and valuation remain undisclosed. Existing backers include venture-capital firms Prime Venture Partners and Singapore’s Horizon Ventures, as well as cricket commentator Harsha Bhogle.
Upsurge India leads Rs 50 Cr secondary transaction in iD Fresh Food
Upsurge India has led a secondary transaction worth over Rs 50 crore in Bengaluru-based fresh-food brand iD Fresh Food, facilitating the exit of early investor Blue Ashva Capital. The transaction involved the transfer of approximately 1% equity in the company, with TG Fund and WW Ventures participating as co-leads.
Founded in 2005, iD Fresh specialises in preservative-free ready-to-cook products, including idli and dosa batter, Indian breads and chutneys. The company reported a revenue of over Rs 870 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 681 crore in FY25, representing growth of more than 25%. The transaction highlights growing institutional investor interest in established Indian consumer businesses and the increasing importance of secondary liquidity in private markets.
The Croffle Guys raises Rs 14 Cr in funding round led by V3 Ventures
Mumbai-based quick-service restaurant startup The Croffle Guys has raised Rs 14 crore in a funding round led by V3 Ventures, backed by Verlinvest, at a post-money valuation of Rs 100 crore. N.A.N. Partners also participated in the round. Founded in 2025, the company has expanded from two outlets to eight within a year and achieved an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 24 crore.
The startup plans to add more than 40 outlets, primarily across Mumbai and Delhi, with a selective presence in Pune. It is targeting an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 100 crore over the next 10-12 months. The company had earlier secured a Rs 2.5 crore investment on Shark Tank India at a Rs 50 crore valuation.
Solgram raises over $1M in pre-seed funding
Gurugram-based premium grocery platform Solgram has raised over $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by DSG Consumer Partners and Saama Capital, with participation from hospitality entrepreneur Kapil Chopra. The capital will be used to expand its temperature-controlled cold-chain infrastructure, strengthen technology capabilities and deepen sourcing relationships. Launched in Gurugram, Solgram offers fresh produce, dairy, meat, seafood, bakery products and gourmet groceries through an integrated supply chain covering sourcing, storage and last-mile delivery. The platform also offers a health-focused selection through its Mindful Mode feature. Solgram plans to expand across the National Capital Region before entering other Tier I markets. Its business model focuses on product quality, provenance and reliability rather than delivery speed alone.
Unify Foodworks raises Rs 5 Cr to expand restaurant brands
Unify Foodworks, the exclusive pan-India master franchisee of Moe's Casa Mexicana and Carvel, has raised Rs 5 crore in seed funding through compulsorily convertible debentures. The capital will support expansion of both international food brands across the National Capital Region (NCR), where they made their India debut.
The company plans to strengthen store density, consumer awareness and operational capabilities before entering additional markets. Moe's Casa Mexicana offers Mexican-inspired dishes, including burritos, bowls and tacos, while Carvel is an American ice cream brand founded in 1934. Unify Foodworks has outlined a long-term expansion roadmap of more than 100 stores across India. The company is also developing integrated supply-chain and operating systems to support its expansion.
ECOPATH raises Rs 2.25 Cr to scale zero-cement construction tech
Bengaluru-based climate-tech startup ECOPATH has raised Rs 2.25 crore in seed funding from Social Alpha and Gemcorp to scale its zero-cement construction technology. The company has built an order book exceeding Rs 40 crore within two years of operations.
Founded by Sourabh Kumar and Abhishek Chhazed, ECOPATH develops cement-free concrete using industrial by-products, including steel-industry waste, and proprietary binders. The funding will support manufacturing capacity expansion, supply-chain development, research and team building. The company has secured over 40 commercial customers, including Lodha, Tata Power and Jindal Steel. ECOPATH says its materials can reduce carbon emissions by approximately 75% compared with conventional cement-based alternatives, depending on application and project specifications.
Mahesh Babu invests in gaming studio Shortgun Games
Actor Mahesh Babu has joined Mumbai-based gaming development studio Shortgun Games as a strategic investor to support the development of premium PC and console games. The partnership will focus on creating original intellectual properties for international markets, including North America and Europe.
The studio's flagship project, PROJECT TAKEDOWN, is a high-budget, narrative-driven action-adventure game being developed for platforms such as PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
Founded by Jeet Chandan and Vidhit Mehta, Shortgun Games is focusing on building cinematic gaming experiences from India for global audiences. The company has also brought on action director Vicky Arora to lead the game's combat design, incorporating motion-capture choreography and physical stunt mechanics.
Cellegant Energy Systems raises Rs 2.61 Cr for hydrogen-powered drones
IIT Gandhinagar professor-founded startup Cellegant Energy Systems has raised Rs 2.61 crore from investors, including GVFL Prarambh Fund Trust, CoCreate Aarambh and IIEC, IIT Gandhinagar's incubator. The funding will support the development of indigenous hybrid hydrogen fuel-cell electric drivetrain systems designed to extend the endurance of drones and unmanned aerial vehicles.
Founded by Dr Atul Bhargav, the startup's immediate priority is to demonstrate a 35-kg hydrogen-powered drone. It aims to advance the programme from technology readiness level three to six over the next six to 12 months. Cellegant is also developing energy solutions for autonomous robots, marine vehicles and other applications. The investment will support technology development, intellectual property protection and team expansion.
DBS Foundation awards Rs 7.4 Cr to India's Khyaal
DBS Foundation has awarded SGD 3 million, approximately Rs 22 crore, to four purpose-driven businesses across Asia under its Impact Beyond Award programme. India's Taisho Ventures, which operates senior citizens' platform Khyaal, will receive SGD 1 million, equivalent to approximately Rs 7.4 crore. Khyaal has more than five million users and provides services spanning physical, emotional, cognitive, social, financial and digital well-being for people aged 50 and above. The funding will help strengthen its platform and expand services into Tier II and III cities, besides exploring opportunities in Southeast Asia. The other award recipients are Hon Yang Healthcare in Taiwan, One Bite Design Studio in Hong Kong and Shanghai Fuyuan Elderly Care Service in China.
OBSESS raises angel funding to build fitness technology platform
Delhi NCR-based fitness and sports technology startup OBSESS has raised angel funding to develop an integrated digital ecosystem for India's fitness and wellness industry. The round saw participation from investors including Pushpendra Singh, Co-founder of Centricity, Amitt Goel and Harshit Vij, Co-founder of Freecultr.
Founded in 2026 by Tushar Sharma and Yash Kumar, the company is developing a platform covering gym discovery, memberships, personal training, sports venue bookings, fitness products, nutrition and wellness services. The funding amount was not disclosed. The capital will support technology development, expansion of its network of gyms and trainers, user acquisition and partnerships. OBSESS also plans to introduce AI-powered capabilities for workout planning, nutrition recommendations and personalisation.
Other news
Adobe launches programme offering free tools to eligible startups
Adobe has launched Adobe for Startups, a programme designed to help early-stage companies strengthen their branding, content creation and customer engagement capabilities. Eligible startups will receive 12 months of free access to Adobe Firefly Pro Plus, Acrobat Studio, Adobe Express Premium and Semrush.
The programme is open to startups founded within the last five years that have raised less than $15 million in funding, subject to eligibility and country availability. The offering combines AI-powered creative tools, document productivity solutions and marketing intelligence capabilities. Adobe will also provide opportunities for founders to participate in workshops, events and learning programmes with its experts. The initiative aims to help startups build their brands and scale marketing activities with limited resources.
Smarten Power Systems reports 77.4% revenue growth in H1 FY27
Smarten Power Systems has reported a 77.4% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue from operations to Rs 204.54 crore during the first half of FY27, compared with Rs 115.26 crore in the corresponding period last year. Consolidated profit after tax more than doubled to Rs 11.99 crore, registering growth of 103.8% against Rs 5.88 crore in H1 FY26. Profit before tax increased 111.9% to Rs 15.83 crore, while earnings per share stood at Rs 6.31. On a standalone basis, revenue grew 87% to Rs 201.37 crore.
The company manufactures power backup and solar energy products, including home UPS systems, solar inverters, batteries and solar panels, with operations across 23 states and two Union Territories.
Indian enterprises lose $3M per major IT outage: New Relic
Indian enterprises are losing an average of $3 million for every high-impact IT outage, according to New Relic's 2026 Observability Forecast: India Edition. The report, based on a survey of 500 Indian respondents, found that 61% of organisations experience major outages weekly or more frequently. Nearly 31% encounter such disruptions multiple times a day.
The study also found that 56% of Indian organisations monitor AI agents in production, compared with the global average of 35%. However, developers spend nearly half their time addressing system disruptions. India also leads in OpenTelemetry standardisation, with 42% of respondents fully standardised. New Relic said fragmented monitoring tools continue to limit the benefits of advanced observability investments.
365squared launches AI-powered voice fraud protection platform
365squared, a Route Mobile company within Proximus Global, has launched 365callguard, an AI-powered voice fraud protection solution for mobile and fixed-line operators. The platform is designed to identify and prevent fraudulent calls before they reach subscribers. It addresses seven categories of fraud, including vishing, caller ID spoofing, Wangiri, international revenue share fraud, SIM box fraud, flash calls, and robocalls.
The solution combines AI models with rule-based detection to provide real-time analysis and enable automatic actions such as call blocking, caller ID modification and subscriber alerts. The launch expands 365squared's existing communications security portfolio, which includes its AI-powered messaging protection platform, 365smsguard.
FirstClub enters beauty and personal care category
FirstClub, the quality-focused consumer platform, has expanded into the beauty and personal care category under its 'Filtered for Good' initiative. The launch brings together more than 80 brands across skincare, haircare, body care and personal care, with products priced between Rs 300 and Rs 3,500.
The company has introduced an ingredient-first evaluation framework covering shampoos, cleansers, moisturisers and sunscreens. It has excluded more than 100 ingredients from its beauty selection and requires listed products to have customer ratings of at least four stars. The platform will also offer 100% ingredient disclosure on product pages and a Samples Selector feature. The expansion follows its earlier entry into grocery, pet care and home and kitchen products.
BIT Mesra and IIT Kanpur sign five-year research collaboration MoU
Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra, and IIT Kanpur have signed a five-year memorandum of understanding to strengthen academic engagement and joint research. The agreement provides for student and faculty exchanges, joint supervision of research scholars, access to specialised facilities and collaborative academic programmes. It also establishes a framework for jointly submitting research proposals to national and international funding agencies.
The MoU covers undergraduate and postgraduate research, internships, joint Master's and PhD supervision, academic programmes and staff training. Students from both institutions will be able to participate in joint research projects and access specialised laboratories. The partnership is aimed at strengthening research capabilities, technology development and academic cooperation between the institutions.
Straive partners with Anthropic for responsible enterprise AI deployment
Global data and AI company Straive has partnered with Anthropic to help enterprises build and deploy AI solutions across business workflows. The collaboration will focus on responsible AI adoption, combining Anthropic's approach to safe AI with Straive's expertise in data readiness, domain knowledge, governance and operational delivery.
The partnership aims to help organisations integrate AI into industry-specific workflows while maintaining human oversight and appropriate operational controls. Straive's Build AI and Run AI capabilities cover solution design, deployment and continuous improvement. The companies will work with enterprises to identify where AI can support business processes and where human intervention remains necessary. Straive serves sectors including financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, media, education and publishing.
Vartis Platforms launches UdhaarSaathi loan marketplace for small merchants
Vartis Platforms, the parent company of LenDenClub and InstaMoney, has launched UdhaarSaathi, a digital loan marketplace targeting UPI QR-enabled micro and small businesses. The platform aims to facilitate Rs 1,000 crore in loan disbursements by the end of the current financial year. It offers collateral-free business loans ranging from Rs 15,000 to Rs 2.5 lakh, with an average ticket size of approximately Rs 1 lakh.
Target customers include kirana stores, pharmacies, street vendors and small retailers. The platform uses banking and payment transaction data shared with merchants' consent to facilitate credit assessment by lending partners. Operating as a loan service provider, UdhaarSaathi works with multiple NBFCs and offers daily repayment structures aligned with merchants' cash flows.
TEXMiN partners Magnora to strengthen India's rare earth magnet ecosystem
TEXMiN, the Technology Translation Research Park established by the Department of Science and Technology at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, has entered into a strategic alliance with Magnora RE Tech to explore opportunities in critical minerals, rare earth elements and rare earth permanent magnets. ELITech Earth Science will provide project management consultancy and technical coordination support.
The collaboration aims to strengthen India's domestic value chain for rare earth permanent magnets, which are essential for electric vehicles, renewable energy systems and advanced electronics. The partnership will combine research expertise, industry investment and project execution capabilities. The initiative is aligned with the National Critical Mineral Mission, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047, with the objective of reducing import dependence.
AMU Leasing sees 65% of EV financing disbursements from non-metro markets
AMU Leasing, an RBI-registered NBFC focused on green mobility and electric vehicle financing, has reported that 65% of its disbursements come from non-metro markets. The company has acquired approximately 14,000 customers and is strengthening its presence across 10 states. Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Haryana are among its fastest-growing markets. Commercial electric vehicles account for the entire financing portfolio in these markets, reflecting the company's focus on last-mile connectivity and goods transportation.
AMU Leasing is also working to establish operations in Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh. The company offers financing across electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, four-wheelers and commercial vehicles, targeting underserved rural and semi-urban markets.
E2E Networks launches Blaze pay-per-token AI inference service
E2E Networks has launched Blaze, a pay-per-token inference service for open AI models, targeting developers and enterprises. The platform provides a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint to access multiple open models, with customers paying according to their token consumption.
Powered by NVIDIA GPU infrastructure and components from NVIDIA DSX OS, Blaze is designed for applications such as voice, coding agents, document AI, OCR and image and video generation. The service is hosted on E2E's India-based cloud infrastructure, addressing demand for data sovereignty and cost-efficient AI deployment. E2E is also expanding its AI infrastructure capacity to approximately 14.6 MW, including a 1,024-GPU NVIDIA Blackwell cluster that has been operational since May 2026.
Azim Premji Foundation launches Social Startups Programme
Azim Premji Foundation has launched a Social Startups Programme to support development sector professionals in establishing and leading civil society organisations focused on underserved communities. The first cohort will include approximately 100 participants across Odisha, Northeast India, Eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bengaluru Urban.
The programme will support areas such as rural livelihoods, healthcare, mental health, disability, children's welfare and community sanitation. Applicants must be below 40 years of age, hold a graduate degree and have at least three years of grassroots development experience. Selected participants will receive financial assistance and guidance during an eight-month seeding phase, followed by an opportunity to apply for a two-year seed grant. Applications are open from November 1 to December 31, 2026.
mFilterIt removes over 2 lakh fraudulent digital assets during festive season
Digital trust and ad-fraud intelligence platform mFilterIt has removed more than two lakh fraudulent digital assets targeting a leading Indian bank during the festive shopping season. Its monitoring uncovered 2.4 lakh fraudulent cases across 10 digital platforms, including fake websites, phishing pages, impersonation accounts and bogus promotional offers.
The company reported a takedown success rate of over 97%, with 80-85% of identified scam assets removed within 24 hours of detection. The cases included brand impersonation, coupon abuse and deceptive referral schemes. According to mFilterIt, the findings highlight the growing scale of digital fraud during high-traffic shopping periods. The company advocates continuous monitoring and digital crawling to identify and remove fraudulent infrastructure before consumers are affected.
Airtel and District rename Bengaluru concert venue Airtel Arena
Bharti Airtel and District have announced a collaboration to enhance digital connectivity at a major live entertainment venue in Bengaluru, which will be renamed Airtel Arena. The 16-acre open-air venue will receive dedicated digital infrastructure investment from Airtel to improve connectivity for fans, artists and event organisers. The venue can accommodate more than 17,000 people and has hosted performances by artists including Arijit Singh, Anirudh Ravichander and Bryan Adams.
The partnership will support high-speed connectivity, digital payments, livestreaming and other services during large-scale events. District will continue managing the consumer-facing entertainment experience, while Airtel will strengthen the venue's technological infrastructure. The initiative reflects growing investment in India's live entertainment ecosystem.
Medi Assist reports 60.2% growth in H1 FY27 net profit
Medi Assist Healthcare Services has reported a 13% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 478 crore in H1 FY27. Operating EBITDA grew 19% to Rs 97.2 crore, while profit after tax increased 60.2% year-on-year. Profit before tax rose 47% and total premiums under management reached Rs 24,752 crore. The company's group health benefits market share stood at 34.1%, with client retention of 90.5%. Technology monetisation also improved, with SaaS and licensing revenue growing 83.8% to Rs 18.1 crore during the first half.
The company's board has approved a share buyback of up to Rs 49.3 crore, funded through internal cash flows. Medi Assist said the buyback would support shareholder returns while preserving funds for expansion and technology investments.
Decentro launches Soundbox range for UPI merchant payments
Fintech infrastructure platform Decentro has launched a range of Soundbox devices aimed at small merchants and businesses accepting digital payments. The offering includes a Static QR Soundbox and a Dynamic QR Soundbox featuring a display, keypad and NFC capabilities. The devices provide audio payment confirmations and are designed to support merchants in Tier II and smaller markets, which account for approximately 45% of UPI transaction volumes.
The Static QR device supports 4G connectivity, with 2G and optional Wi-Fi backup, while payment alerts are available in multiple languages. The company is targeting one million devices by the end of 2028 and is in discussions with five partners for large-scale deployments. Decentro currently has over 5,000 offline UPI QR deployments.
Porter appoints Gaurav Jain as CFO, elevates technology and marketing leaders
Digital goods transport platform Porter has strengthened its leadership team with the appointment of Gaurav Jain as chief financial officer. The company has also elevated Shubham Gupta as chief technology officer and Mohit Rathi as chief marketing officer.
Jain joins Porter from Amazon, where he spent more than a decade, and brings over 20 years of experience in finance and strategy across e-commerce, financial services and FMCG. Gupta, who joined Porter in 2015, has led engineering and technology initiatives, including infrastructure modernisation, security and AI adoption. Rathi has been with the company for over a decade and has handled expansion and customer growth initiatives. The leadership changes come as Porter prepares for its next phase of expansion.
MathCo appoints former Unilever executive Vijay Raj to advisory board
Enterprise AI and analytics company MathCo has appointed Vijay Raj to its advisory board as it enters its second decade of operations. Raj brings three decades of experience in the insights industry, including 26 years at Unilever, where he worked on consumer behaviour and business strategy. In his new role, he will advise the company's leadership on market opportunities, customer priorities and long-term growth strategy.
His experience is expected to support MathCo's expansion in the consumer packaged goods sector and strengthen its engagement with enterprise clients.
Fulcrum Digital appoints Latha Nathan as SVP of India delivery operations
Enterprise AI and digital transformation company Fulcrum Digital has appointed Latha Nathan as Senior Vice President of India Delivery Operations. She will oversee the company's delivery organisation across its centres in Pune, Coimbatore and Mumbai. Her responsibilities will include delivery excellence, talent development, client success and scaling India operations.
Nathan joins Fulcrum Digital from Fidelity Investments, where she served as Vice President and led a business unit focused on digitisation and customer-facing platform products.
AstraZeneca appoints Naveen Krishna Yamarthi to lead Chennai innovation centre
AstraZeneca has appointed Naveen Krishna Yamarthi as managing director of AZIPL and the head of its Global Innovation & Technology Centre in Chennai, effective October 30, 2026. In his new role, he will lead the centre's development as a strategic, multifunctional innovation hub, supporting the company's global operations and Bold Ambition 2030 strategy.
Yamarthi brings more than 22 years of experience in building and scaling global capability centres (GCCs), with expertise in technology and business transformation.
UiPath appoints Yashdeep Vaishnav as India country manager
Business orchestration and automation company UiPath has appointed Yashdeep Vaishnav as managing director and country manager for India. He will lead the company's business operations, drive adoption of its automation solutions and expand its customer and partner ecosystem in the country. He has previously held senior positions at Snowflake, Salesforce, VTEX, Melento and Oracle.
AscentHR recognised as leader in NelsonHall Payroll Services 2026 assessment
HR technology and payroll services provider AscentHR has been recognised as a Leader in NelsonHall's Payroll Services 2026 – Overall assessment. The company was also named an Innovator in the Multi-Country Payroll Capability category.
The evaluation was conducted through NelsonHall's Vendor Evaluation & Assessment Tool, which assesses payroll providers on market presence, client value and technological innovation. NelsonHall cited AscentHR's payroll expertise, broad service portfolio and technology capabilities, including intelligent anomaly detection, Tia 2.0 and Smart Rules.
GoKwik announces Rs 7.57 cr ESOP liquidity programme for employees
Bengaluru-based commerce enablement platform GoKwik has announced an employee stock option liquidity programme involving a combined payout of Rs 7.57 crore to 69 employees. The participating employees are expected to realise an average return of approximately nine times their original grant value among the earliest ESOP holders.
The programme comes as the company turned adjusted EBITDA positive in October 2026, based on unaudited management accounts.
1Crowd partially exits Mojro investment, retains 75% stake
Early-stage investment firm 1Crowd has partially exited its investment in logistics technology company Mojro, generating returns of several times its original investment. The firm has sold 25% of its holding while retaining the remaining 75%, signalling its continued commitment to the company.
1Crowd first invested in Mojro in February 2018 and has supported it through three subsequent funding rounds. The partial exit took place as part of Mojro’s Series A financing, in which 1Crowd also participated alongside other investors. Mojro provides an AI-native B2B SaaS platform that helps enterprises automate logistics planning, route optimisation, scheduling and delivery operations. The platform is designed to improve efficiency, reduce logistics costs and provide visibility across goods movement.
Mobavenue reports 72% growth in H1 FY27 profit
Mobavenue AI Tech reported a 72.2% year-on-year increase in profit after tax to Rs 22.9 crore for the first half of FY27, while revenue rose 48.6% to Rs 149.6 crore. EBITDA grew 59.6% to Rs 31.6 crore, with the margin expanding 140 basis points to 21.1%. For the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, revenue increased 41.3% to Rs 76.7 crore and EBITDA rose 47.3% to Rs 16.2 crore. Profit after tax was up 54.8% at Rs 11.3 crore. Growth was driven by demand from advertisers in quick commerce, BFSI, fintech, entertainment, travel and commerce. International markets contributed 23.8% of Q2 revenue, while direct clients accounted for 64.7%. India contributed 77.7% of first-half revenue.
Avanade report highlights gap in Indian enterprises’ AI transformation
Indian businesses report high confidence in their use of artificial intelligence, but many have yet to fundamentally transform operations around the technology, according to an Avanade survey. The company’s AI Reality Report found that 82% of Indian business leaders are confident in their teams’ AI use, while only 23% said their organisations had reshaped how they work. The survey found that 44% of Indian respondents reported significant improvements in operational efficiency and 42% cited gains in employee productivity. However, 75% said AI had yet to deliver returns that justified the investment, while 74% had not formally calculated its return on investment. Integration and scaling remain challenges, with 47% reporting deployment problems. Avanade said enterprises must strengthen foundations and measure financial outcomes.
Taghash launches AI assistant for investment funds
Investment fund technology platform Taghash has launched Taghash Brain, an artificial intelligence assistant designed to streamline portfolio monitoring, reporting and daily operations for venture capital firms and other investment funds. Integrated into Taghash’s fund management platform, Brain enables investment teams to analyse fund data, generate reports, build live dashboards and execute tasks through a conversational interface. It uses information already maintained within the platform, including portfolio data, deal records and operational workflows. Taghash plans to introduce further agentic AI capabilities in the coming months.
Deel launches workforce security solution to detect hiring fraud
Global HR and payroll platform Deel has launched Deel Security, a workforce security solution designed to detect identity fraud during recruitment and throughout employment. The platform analyses risk signals across resumes, digital footprints, interviews and identity documents to identify deepfakes, proxy interviewers and suspicious identities. The launch follows rising concerns about fraudulent remote job applications. Deel research involving 1,011 HR professionals in the UK and US found that 66% of organisations had seen an increase in suspicious or potentially fraudulent remote worker applications over the past year. Some 93% of HR leaders expressed concern about deepfake or AI-generated workers.
Zelio E-Mobility begins production at new Hisar facility
Zelio E-Mobility has commenced commercial production at its new manufacturing facility in Patan, Hisar, Haryana, adding annual capacity of 48,000 electric two-wheelers and 24,000 three-wheelers. The expansion takes the company’s total installed capacity from 2.4 lakh to approximately 3.12 lakh units. Spread across six acres, the facility has a built-up area of 2.61 lakh square feet and represents an investment of more than Rs 20 crore. Production has begun for Zelio electric scooters and Tanga electric three-wheelers. The additional capacity is expected to come on stream during the third quarter of FY27. Zelio currently operates four plants and has more than 400 dealers across over 25 states.
IKF Finance targets Rs 25,000 crore AUM by 2030
IKF Finance is targeting assets under management of Rs 25,000 crore by 2030, supported by technology investments, product diversification and expansion beyond its traditional southern markets. The lender ended FY26 with consolidated AUM of more than Rs 8,600 crore, up around 30%, and reported profit after tax of Rs 215 crore. The company has expanded to more than 350 branches across 13 states and operates in vehicle, construction equipment and MSME finance. Its housing finance subsidiary offers affordable home loans. Vehicle finance now accounts for less than 70% of the group’s assets.

articles.title: « On est juste en train de le nettoyer, mec » : la NASA jette un froid sur le mythique SR-71 Blackbird
articles.text:
C’est une affaire qui intrigue les fans d’aviation depuis quelques jours : le légendaire SR-71 Blackbird va-t-il de nouveau fendre les cieux, 27 ans après son dernier vol ? L’hypothèse circule depuis que l’on a constaté que l’exemplaire SR-71 numéro 844 a fini par disparaître de son emplacement plus tôt cette année.
Le SR-71 numéro 844 est justement le dernier Blackbird à avoir volé, le 9 octobre 1999. Cet avion espion conçu par Lockheed (aujourd’hui Lockheed Martin), capable de dépasser trois fois la vitesse du son, était exposé en plein air depuis 2002 au centre de recherche Armstrong de la NASA, sur la base aérienne d’Edwards, en Californie.
Alors, bien sûr, tout le monde souhaite connaître les intentions de la NASA, propriétaire de l’avion. « Est-ce que le 844 a déjà été mis sous tension ? » : Eric Johnson, enseignant en sciences et streameur, a posé la question à Jared Isaacman, patron de l’agence spatiale américaine, dans un épisode du podcast The Flame Trench de NASASpaceflight, mis en ligne le vendredi 30 octobre 2026.
Alors, le SR-71 Blackbird est-il en train de préparer son retour dans les airs ? Jared Isaacman a répondu calmement, avant de se mettre à rire, comme s’il s’agissait d’un non-sujet : « On est juste en train de le nettoyer, mec. » Il a ajouté que l’avion était « tellement poussiéreux, là-bas dans le désert », qu’il avait besoin d’un bon nettoyage. On a un peu de mal à y croire : l’avion a quitté son socle il y a au moins 6 mois, ce qui fait un long dépoussiérage.
Si cette question est revenue, c’est en raison d’une enquête d’Aviation Week publiée le 29 septembre. Le journaliste y révèle que la NASA a retiré l’avion de son socle au début de l’année (avant le 17 mai, d’après des images satellites), puis l’a installé dans l’ancien hangar de la navette spatiale. Il n’en fallait pas plus pour que naissent les spéculations.
La piste d’un nouvel avion de la Nasa
Le magazine a aussi affirmé que l’agence avait proposé cet été un poste à d’anciens ingénieurs du programme. Parmi eux, Mike Relja, un retraité qui approche les 80 ans, a répondu qu’il était « trop vieux » pour ça. L’avion lui-même n’est pas de toute première jeunesse : le premier vol d’un Blackbird remonte à 1964, il y a 62 ans.
La NASA, elle, n’a jamais confirmé le projet de remettre le SR-71 en vol. Un porte-parole a seulement indiqué que l’agence n’avait « pas d’information supplémentaire à partager » sur l’avion « pour le moment ».
Jared Isaacman a pourtant lui-même entretenu le mystère. En juillet, au salon aéronautique EAA AirVenture, quand on lui a demandé s’il avait le pouvoir de faire revenir le SR-71, il a répondu « c’est classifié ».
Mi-septembre, à l’All-In Summit de Los Angeles, il a montré la silhouette d’un avion très proche du Blackbird. Jared Isaacman assure qu’il ne s’agit pas d’un SR-71, et promet que la NASA volera bientôt « aussi haut et aussi vite » qu’il y a quelques décennies.
Faire revoler le SR-71, malgré ses six décennies, aurait pourtant du sens pour préparer de nouveaux avions, d’après Tim Conners, interrogé par The War Zone.
Cet ancien ingénieur du programme SR-71 à la NASA, qui fait d’ailleurs partie des anciens que l’agence a contactés cet été d’après Aviation Week, pense que les simulations informatiques reproduisent très bien l’aérodynamique à ces vitesses, mais elles reproduisent mal le comportement d’un nouveau moteur monté sur un avion aussi rapide.
Il faudrait pouvoir tester cela en vol. Et le Blackbird serait alors un banc d’essai volant pertinent pour moteurs à haute vitesse.

articles.text:
Le Black Friday est l’occasion idéale pour préparer les cadeaux de Noël sans se ruiner. Cette année encore, Xiaomi est bien représenté : des smartphones accessibles aux traqueurs d’activité, la marque chinoise couvre un large spectre de besoins tech. Nous avons retenu cinq offres, avec des remises qui peuvent dépasser 150 euros sur certains modèles. La sélection mêle entrée de gamme et milieu de gamme, avec à chaque fois un rapport qualité-prix que le Black Friday rend encore plus difficile à ignorer.
Les meilleurs deals Xiaomi à saisir lors du Black Friday
- Pack Xiaomi 17T à 599 euros au lieu de 803 euros
- Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G à 399 euros au lieu de 553 euros
- Xiaomi Poco C81 Pro à 109 euros au lieu de 139 euros
- Xiaomi Electric Scooter Elite à 329 euros au lieu de 349 euros
- Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Active à 32 euros au lieu de 39 euros
Pack Xiaomi 17T
Le Xiaomi 17T est un smartphone milieu de gamme qui propose des performances convenables pour la vie quotidienne et une autonomie qui frôle les deux jours. Pendant le Black Friday, il est proposé à moins de 600 euros, avec une coque, des écouteurs sans fil et une balise bluetooth.
Les points forts du Xiaomi 17T
- Téléobjectif périscopique x5, identique au modèle Pro
- Batterie 6 500 mAh, autonomie proche de deux jours
- Écran AMOLED 6,59 pouces bien calibré et très lumineux
Pendant le Black Friday, Darty propose le Pack Xiaomi 17T – smartphone, coque, écouteurs sans fil et balise Bluetooth inclus – à 599 euros au lieu de 803 euros, soit 204 euros d’économie.
Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G
Le Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G mise tout sur l’endurance avec sa batterie silicium-carbone de 8 340 mAh, un écran de 3 500 nits et une certification d’étanchéité complète – noté 7/10 dans notre test, c’est la version 8 Go + 512 Go qui est en promotion aujourd’hui.
Les points forts du Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G
- Batterie silicium-carbone de 8 340 mAh, autonomie de deux jours
- Écran AMOLED 120 Hz, luminosité de pointe à 3 500 nits
- Étanchéité certifiée IP66, IP68 et IP69K
Sur Amazon, le Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G (8 Go + 512 Go) passe à 399 euros au lieu de 553 euros, soit 154 euros de remise.
Xiaomi Poco C81 Pro
Le Black Friday casse les prix d’une multitude de smartphones, y compris sur les références d’entrée de gamme. Si vous cherchez un appareil efficace sans exploser votre tirelire, le Xiaomi Poco C81 Pro est le candidat idéal : sur Amazon, son prix chute à seulement 109 euros au lieu de 139 euros au départ.
Les points forts du Xiaomi Poco C81 Pro
- Un grand écran IPS LCD de 6,9 pouces avec rafraîchissement adaptatif
- Une très grosse batterie de 6 000 mAh pour deux jours d’autonomie

De base, le Poco C81 Pro est un smartphone abordable, puisqu’il coûte 139 euros. Mais avec la promo actuelle sur Amazon, il passe à 109 euros jusqu’au 30 novembre.
Xiaomi Electric Scooter Elite
Sécurisante, endurante, puissante, résistante… Et surtout abordable : voici la Xiaomi Electric Scooter Elite, une trottinette électrique que la marque a dévoilée cette année. Un modèle qui va à l’essentiel, mais qui le fait bien. Elle sera idéale pour les riders citadins qui recherchent une trottinette compacte et bien conçue, sans payer le prix fort.
Les points forts de la Xiaomi Electric Scooter Elite
- Suspension avant à double ressort, absorption jusqu’à 30 mm
- Autonomie annoncée de 45 km, moteur 400 W
- Pentes jusqu’à 20 %, frein tambour avant + E-ABS arrière
Chez Mi, la Xiaomi Electric Scooter Elite est proposée à 329 euros au lieu de 349 euros, soit 20 euros de remise.
Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Active
Petit prix, grande liste de capteurs : c’est le positionnement habituel des bracelets connectés Xiaomi, et le Smart Band 11 Active ne déroge pas à la règle. Son boîtier embarque un suivi de la fréquence cardiaque, de l’oxygène sanguin et du stress, ainsi que le suivi du sommeil. Son principal atout reste son tarif : lancé à un prix déjà agressif, il chute encore davantage pour le Black Friday.

articles.title: Route, gravel, VTT : pour le 11.11, le Garmin Edge 540 tombe à 241,80€ chez AliExpress
articles.text:
Sur une longue sortie en forêt ou en montagne, un compteur doit garder le signal sous les arbres et tenir jusqu’au retour. Le Garmin Edge 540 descend à 241,80 € chez AliExpress avec le code CLU40, sous son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, mais reste plus cher qu’en juin, quand nous le relayions sous les 181 €.
Lancé en avril 2023 à 399,99 €, le Garmin Edge 540 est le frère à boutons de l’Edge 840, doté lui d’un écran tactile. Il en reprend l’essentiel : GNSS multi-bandes, cartographie intégrée, ClimbPro et entraînement adaptatif. AliExpress le propose à 241,80 € avec le code CLU40, contre 305,71 € pour son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, soit 63,91 € d’écart.
Il s’agit de la version standard, sans recharge solaire. Elle vise les cyclistes réguliers, sur route, en gravel ou en VTT, qui veulent naviguer et suivre leur forme sans payer un modèle tactile.
Le Garmin Edge 540 en version standard est à 241,80 € au lieu de 305,71 € chez AliExpress, avec le code CLU40.
Pourquoi choisir le Garmin Edge 540 ?
- Un positionnement qui tient sous les arbres : Le GNSS multi-bandes améliore la précision de la position, y compris en forêt dense ou le long d’une falaise.
- ClimbPro sans parcours préparé : Pendant une montée, le compteur affiche le dénivelé et la pente des sections restantes, même sans itinéraire chargé au préalable. De quoi doser son effort sur une côte inconnue.
- Une autonomie taillée pour les longues journées : Garmin annonce 26 heures en utilisation intensive et 42 heures en mode économie d’énergie, assez pour une cyclosportive ou plusieurs sorties sans recharge.
De la cyclosportive au single VTT, ce que ce compteur sait faire
Sur route, l’Edge 540 sert d’abord de copilote d’entraînement : il suggère des séances quotidiennes selon votre charge d’entraînement, votre récupération et vos objectifs, dehors comme sur home trainer Tacx. Le niveau d’énergie en temps réel (Stamina) et le guide de puissance aident à ne pas exploser avant le sommet d’un col. En VTT, la cartographie intégrée s’appuie sur Trailforks et le compteur mesure les sauts, leur distance, la difficulté (Grit) et la constance (Flow) d’une descente. Ses boutons se manipulent avec des gants, sous la pluie comme dans la boue.
Il convient au cycliste qui roule plusieurs fois par semaine et veut structurer sa progression, ou au vttiste qui explore de nouveaux secteurs. Côté sécurité, LiveTrack, la messagerie de groupe et la détection d’incident couvrent toutes les activités, VTT compris, et le compteur se couple aux radars Varia. Il est moins pertinent pour un usage de loisir occasionnel : Stamina, le guide de puissance et le coaching adaptatif réclament des capteurs compatibles vendus à part, capteur de puissance ou ceinture cardio. Sans eux, une partie du compteur reste inexploitée.
Edge 540 ou Edge 840 : l’écran tactile justifie-t-il l’écart ?
Face à l’Edge 840, lancé à 499,99 €, le 540 partage le même écran de 2,6 pouces, la même autonomie et l’essentiel des fonctions : la différence tient surtout au tactile du 840. Celui-ci rend plus directe la navigation sur la carte, quand le 540 oblige à passer par ses boutons ou par l’application Garmin Connect pour préparer un parcours. Les versions Solar, 100 € plus chères au lancement, ajoutent la recharge solaire et portent l’autonomie jusqu’à 60 heures en mode économie. Si vous préparez vos itinéraires sur smartphone avant de partir, le 540 couvre l’essentiel sans le surcoût.
✅ Les points forts
- GNSS multi-bandes pour une trace fiable en forêt ou en montagne
- Jusqu’à 26 heures d’autonomie, 42 heures en mode économie
- ClimbPro actif sur n’importe quelle montée, sans parcours chargé
- Métriques VTT dédiées et pistes Trailforks intégrées
- Boutons utilisables avec des gants, certification IPX7
❌ Les limites
- Pas d’écran tactile, menus et carte pilotés aux seuls boutons
- Aucun capteur fourni, alors que le coaching avancé en dépend
- Plus cher qu’en juin, où il était passé sous les 181 € chez AliExpress
- Définition de 246 x 322 pixels, modeste pour sa diagonale
Le code CLU40 ramène le Garmin Edge 540 à 241,80 € chez AliExpress : pensez à le saisir avant de valider votre commande.
À 241,80 €, le Garmin Edge 540 passe nettement sous son prix de lancement de 399,99 € et sous son plus bas des 30 derniers jours, une offre solide pour un compteur aussi complet. Ce n’est pas pour autant son meilleur prix : nous l’avions relayé à 180,78 € en juin, chez le même marchand. Rien ne garantit qu’un tel prix revienne, mais qui n’est pas pressé peut patienter.
L’offre s’adresse aux cyclistes réguliers qui attendent d’un compteur qu’il les guide, les entraîne et les suive sur plusieurs heures, sur route comme en tout-terrain. Les amateurs d’écran tactile regarderont plutôt l’Edge 840, plus cher. Ceux qui roulent peu et sans capteur se contenteront d’un modèle plus simple. Pour les autres, c’est un outil complet à un prix bien plus raisonnable qu’à sa sortie.

articles.title: Binance says fake job interview led to $6.3 billion crypto heist
articles.text:
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says North Korean hackers used a fake job interview to trick an employee into installing malware that ultimately let them compromise the company's wallet infrastructure and steal about $6.34 billion in digital assets.
This new information was shared in an incident report published today, which details how the attackers used social engineering, malicious software, and compromised internal systems to carry out the October 29 crypto theft.
As previously reported by BleepingComputer, the FBI attributed the attack to North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor, also tracked as Lazarus Group, Jade Sleet, and APT38.
Binance says the attack began in September when a software engineer was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform by someone impersonating a Project Director at a fictitious company.
The employee's profile referenced his experience at Binance, making him a valuable target for attackers looking to breach the cryptocurrency exchange.
The fake recruiter scheduled two interviews for the employee, first with someone posing as a human resources representative, then with another individual claiming to be the company's CEO.
During the first interview, the fake HR representative held a live video call and shared a social media account with personal photos and videos to build trust.
The second interview took place through a popular social chat application where the employee was instructed to download a coding assignment from an online code repository.
According to Binance, the repository contained malicious code that, when executed, compromised the employee's device with previously unseen custom malware that antivirus software did not detect.
"The malware employed sophisticated obfuscation and evasion techniques, including replacing a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version to execute commands and establish communication with an attacker-controlled external server," explained Binance.
"The 0-day malware was not detected by the endpoint security protection tools at the time. The attacker also took steps to conceal the malicious activity and remove traces of the compromise, making detection and subsequent investigation more challenging."
Binance explained that the malicious script created a replacement executable named pyenv_ in the macOS Homebrew installation directory.
The script then deleted the legitimate pyenv executable, renamed the malicious file to pyenv, modified its symbolic link, and used it to spawn a Z shell (zsh) process.
The malicious replacement allowed the attackers to execute commands received from an attacker-controlled server.
By October 20, the attackers had used the compromised engineer's computer and an internal AI tool to compromise two additional employees working on Binance's wallet infrastructure, obtaining credentials and a container deployment token.
On October 29, the hackers used the stolen credentials to deploy a malicious script and gain unauthorized access to Binance's wallet signing service, allowing them to transfer billions of dollars in cryptocurrency across multiple blockchains.
The attackers also abused Ethereum's EIP-7702 authorization mechanism, allowing them to continue stealing cryptocurrency even after the exchange suspended withdrawals.
Binance says it has since rebuilt affected systems, replaced compromised devices, and revoked stolen credentials.
As of November 3, approximately $2.85 billion in stolen assets had been frozen or intercepted, while 98% of impacted token assets had been replenished as of October 31.
Binance says it is continuing to investigate the breach and has brought in independent security firms to review its findings.
Malicious job interviews
Fake job interviews that lead to malware installs are a common tactic in North Korean hacking campaigns known as Contagious Interview and Operation Dream Job. These campaigns use fake job offers and interviews to trick developers and cryptocurrency employees into installing malware.
In June 2025, cybersecurity firm Socket reported that a Contagious Interview campaign impersonated recruiters on LinkedIn and sent developers coding assignments containing malicious npm packages.
As part of these attacks, the hackers distributed 35 malicious npm packages that installed malware, allowing them to steal browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallet data, and other information from infected computers.
North Korean Lazarus hackers have also used similar tactics in Operation Dream Job, distributing malware disguised as employment documents to people working in software development and DeFi companies.
While Binance has not linked the employee compromise to either specific campaign, the use of a fake recruiter, multiple interviews, and a malicious coding assignment closely mirrors these previously documented North Korean tactics.

articles.title: Sergio Ramos compró una finca de 44 hectáreas, donde cría caballos y desarrolla un proyecto de 12.000 metros cuadrados: “Una de las jornadas más especiales del año; tradición, familia y raíces”
articles.text:
Sergio Ramos pasa buena parte de su día a día en La Alegría, la finca que tiene en Bollullos de la Mitación, cerca de Sevilla. El campeón del mundo de 2010 ha enseñado en Instagram el día de herradero de su ganadería, que para él es “una de las jornadas más especiales del año”, y ha explicado de paso cómo marca a sus caballos.
Frío en lugar de fuego. Ramos acompañó las imágenes con un escueto “Tradiciones, familia y raíces”, pero lo que más preguntas generó entre sus seguidores fue el marcado de los animales. Y es que, según su respuesta recogida por 101TV, en la Yeguada SR4 “desde hace años” lo hacen “en frío con nitrógeno líquido”, una técnica “avalada por veterinarios” que, siempre en palabras del futbolista, “elimina las quemaduras térmicas del hierro tradicional y minimiza el estrés del animal”.
Eso sí, el aval veterinario es una afirmación suya, y el propio medio andaluz matiza que el método evita la quemadura del hierro caliente pero no deja al caballo libre de dolor o molestias.
Una finca con plaza de toros. La Alegría es además la casa familiar. La propiedad tiene unas 44 hectáreas y allí vive con Pilar Rubio y sus cuatro hijos, detrás de un muro perimetral de gran altura, entre una piscina, un lago artificial, un campo de fútbol siete, una pista de pádel, una plaza de toros privada, una sala de proyecciones y piezas de arte contemporáneo. La vivienda principal es de estilo cortijo de más de 12.000 metros cuadrados.
Del ladrillo a las apps. Pero los caballos no son el único negocio de Ramos, que controla la práctica totalidad de sus inversiones a través de la sociedad matriz Sermos 32. En el terreno tecnológico, en 2014 participó junto a Alejandro Sanz en una ronda de financiación de Fever, la app para descubrir planes de ocio.
Su apuesta inmobiliaria más conocida es Desarrollos Inmobiliarios Los Berrocales, la sociedad con la que entró en 2011 en ese nuevo barrio del sureste de Madrid, junto a la A-3 y la M-45, y que tardó más de una década en dar beneficios por culpa de la crisis inmobiliaria, los trámites administrativos y varios conflictos judiciales. De hecho, según las cuentas del Registro Mercantil, la sociedad ganó 4,1 millones de euros en el ejercicio cerrado en enero de 2026, frente a los 281.000 euros del anterior, gracias a la venta de parcelas.
El Sevilla que no fue. El otro gran movimiento de Ramos lejos del césped pasaba por el Sevilla FC, el club de su cantera. En enero de 2026, el grupo inversor que encabezaba alcanzó un principio de acuerdo verbal para hacerse con el club por unos 400 millones de euros, deuda incluida.
Pero, según elDiario.es, que cifra lo pactado después en 450 millones menos la deuda neta, los principales accionistas dieron por rotas las negociaciones a finales de mayo de 2026 por lo que consideraron una rebaja sustancial de la oferta, y su vuelta al club, esta vez como propietario, se quedó en nada.
La Alegría tampoco se ha librado de sobresaltos, como el robo que sufrió en 2023 y que recuerda el mismo artículo de Infobae. Pese a ello, el defensor que pasó por el Real Madrid, el Paris Saint-Germain y el Sevilla sigue teniendo en esta finca su centro de operaciones, repartido entre esas inversiones y la tradición ecuestre que lo acompaña desde hace años.

articles.title: Crypto : la Corée du Nord dément avoir piraté Binance et dénonce une « provocation » américaine
articles.text:
La semaine dernière, des pirates ont siphonné les portefeuilles de Binance, la plus grande plateforme d’échange de cryptomonnaies au monde. En moins de 20 minutes, les cybercriminels se sont emparés de plus de 6 milliards de dollars d’actifs numériques. C’est le plus gros braquage de l’histoire des cryptos, devant le casse de Bybit un an plus tôt.
Tous les soupçons se sont rapidement tournés vers la Corée du Nord. Deux jours après la cyberattaque, le FBI a officiellement attribué l’attaque à TraderTraitor, un gang de pirates au service du régime nord-coréen. Membre du célèbre collectif Lazarus, ce gang opère à la demande des services de renseignement de la Corée du Nord. Pour le FBI, il ne fait aucun doute que le pays est « responsable » du vol. Ces dernières années, les pirates nord-coréens ont multiplié les attaques contre les plateformes d’échange et les protocoles de cryptomonnaies. L’an dernier, ils ont dérobé plus de 2 milliards de dollars de cryptodevises, estime Chainalysis. Coupé des circuits financiers par les sanctions internationales, Pyongyang considère les vols de cryptomonnaies comme une importante source de financement. L’argent amassé servirait notamment à financer le programme nucléaire et militaire du pays.
À lire aussi : 351 millions de dollars de cryptos dérobées – la plateforme Bitget a été piratée par des hackers nord-coréens
« Une provocation éculée »
Sans grande surprise, la république populaire démocratique de Corée (RPDC) dément toute implication dans le piratage de Binance. Quelques jours après la cyberattaque, Kim Yo-jong, la sœur du dirigeant Kim Jong-un, a balayé les accusations du FBI lors d’une prise de parole officielle. Elle dénonce « une rhétorique absurde » et « une provocation éculée » de la part des États-Unis.
« Ce n’est pas la première fois que les États-Unis tentent de répandre une image déformée de la RPDC au sein de la communauté internationale, en associant aveuglément la RPDC aux incidents de “cybercriminalité” chaque fois qu’ils surviennent à l’échelle internationale », affirme Kim Yo-jong.
Selon elle, le FBI cherche à faire passer la Corée du Nord pour un « État cybercriminel ». Kim Yo-jong ajoute que la « position constante » du gouvernement nord-coréen est de « s’opposer résolument à toutes sortes d’actes malveillants dans le cyberespace ». Ce démenti n’a rien d’une surprise. Pyongyang a toujours nié être à l’origine des cyberattaques attribuées à des gangs criminels nord-coréens.
Des milliards de dollars retirés de Binance
En parallèle, Binance tente de tourner la page de la cyberattaque. Ce week-end, la plateforme a commencé à rouvrir les retraits de cryptos, suspendus dans le sillage du hack. Comme il fallait s’y attendre, de nombreux clients, échaudés par le piratage, en ont profité pour retirer leurs actifs numériques. Le jour de la réouverture, Binance a traité 4,6 milliards de dollars de retraits, pour seulement 1 milliard de dépôts. Plus de 5 milliards de dollars ont été retirés de la plateforme. Binance assure que les retraits se sont désormais stabilisés. La plateforme ne fait pas face à une vaste fuite de capitaux.

articles.title: Un ejecutivo de una firma admitió que gasta hasta USD 200.000 al año en una IA que lee todo su correo
articles.text:
Garry Tan, director ejecutivo de Y Combinator, la aceleradora de startups de Silicon Valley, afirmó que gasta entre USD 100.000 y USD 200.000 al año en tokens, las unidades de texto que procesan y cobran los modelos de IA. Lo dijo en el podcast The Builders, de Walter Isaacson, según TechCrunch.
Tan usa agentes de IA, asistentes que ejecutan tareas por su cuenta, para proyectos de trabajo y tareas de programación. También los usó para preparar la propia entrevista con Isaacson e investigar las preguntas que podían hacerle.
Según TechCrunch, Tan bromeó antes con sufrir una “psicosis cibernética” y con dormir poco por el entusiasmo que le generan sus agentes. Ahora puso un precio a esa dedicación.
Cuál es el trabajo del asistente de Garry Tan
El agente de Tan va más allá del trabajo. “Ha leído todo mi correo y todo mi Dropbox. Ha leído todas mis notas de Apple, incluso mis notas de terapia de hace 20 años”, afirmó el ejecutivo.
Tan describe esa herramienta como una ayuda para “casi cualquier cosa” del día a día, con más autonomía que un programa tradicional. La comparó con un “Pepito Grillo” (el grillo consejero del cuento de Pinocho) sobre el hombro, que “se adelanta” con preguntas y ayuda a “ver detrás de las esquinas”.
Según el ejecutivo, quien usa estos agentes debe dejar de tratarlos como software convencional. Dijo que algunas personas se preocupan tanto por la repetibilidad y la seguridad que renuncian a lo mejor de trabajar con la herramienta, que puede parecerse mucho a un humano.
Un asistente interno con el contexto de cada fundador
Tan contó que Y Combinator también usa un agente interno llamado Stray Light, que tiene personalidad y un “cerebro de la empresa”. Según el director, ese agente conoce a cada fundador que la aceleradora respaldó, a cualquiera que le haya escrito y todas las solicitudes recibidas.
Tan se describe como un usuario temprano de OpenClaw, una herramienta de agentes de IA. En marzo, TechCrunch informó que había publicado en GitHub, con licencia de código abierto, su configuración de Claude Code, el asistente de programación de Anthropic. La llamó gstack.
Esa configuración reúne hoy 23 “habilidades”, instrucciones reutilizables que asignan al asistente roles como revisor de código o responsable de seguridad. Según el repositorio, es gratuita y funciona con licencia MIT. Tan dijo que la comparte para enseñar lo que pueden hacer los agentes.
La inteligencia artificial también concentra una parte relevante de las inversiones de la aceleradora. De las 196 startups que participaron en el Demo Day de Y Combinator, 149 fueron clasificadas como proyectos de aprendizaje automático e inteligencia artificial, según CNBC.
El propio Tan reconoció el límite de esa apuesta. “Es demasiado caro ahora mismo”, dijo, y admitió que su gasto es “un privilegio enorme que no todos pueden tener”. Para él, los agentes personales se volverán masivos solo si el costo baja.
Tampoco ve como solución a los agentes gratuitos que ofrecen las grandes tecnológicas. Sobre Meta, mencionó que es una empresa enorme que controla el algoritmo y que “todos desearíamos que no” lo hiciera. Imaginó una IA personal que cada usuario controle y programe.

articles.title: Si acabas de empezar en el gimnasio, esta es la respuesta que buscas: cuánto tarda el músculo en crecer
articles.text:
Cuando comenzamos a ir al gimnasio, buscamos tener resultados cuanto antes, llegando al punto de que se han generado muchos memes alrededor de este fenómeno. Y para resolver este misterio, son varios los estudios que han ido surgiendo sobre cuánto tiempo tenemos que dedicar a nuestro entrenamiento para ver finalmente un poco más de músculo en los brazos o en las piernas.
La ganancia inicial. En redes sociales es bastante frecuente ver cómo se promete que en las primeras semanas es cuando hay una gran ganancia muscular. Esto es algo que puede crear cualquiera, puesto que en el momento de acabar un ejercicio y en las horas posteriores es frecuente ver el músculo 'hinchado'.
Es un espejismo. Aquí un estudio clásico publicado en 2016 analizó a 10 jóvenes no entrenados para entender qué ocurría en las primeras semanas de entrenamiento. Lo que vieron fue que en la semana 3, el área de sus cuádriceps había aumentado un 2,7% y a las 10 semanas un 10,4%. El problema es que este aumento tan prematuro estaba acompañado de edema inducido por el daño muscular, por lo que este cambio en el volumen no debe etiquetarse como hipertrofia pura sin descontar la inflamación.
Esto mismo se vio también en un estudio hecho en 2011, donde tras medir semanalmente a 25 hombres sedentarios se concluyó que la hipertrofia estructural y real no empieza a consolidarse hasta las semanas 3 o 4, alcanzando un +9,6% a las 8 semanas. Pero ese "crecimiento" es en gran medida debido a la reparación del daño que se ha hecho sobre el músculo.
Un gran trabajo. Este mismo año se ha publicado un metaanálisis que se encuentra en proceso de revisión y que está firmado por referentes de la investigación deportiva. En este se analizan 2.237 observaciones extraídas de 480 estudios diferentes, filtrando solo aquellos que midieron el crecimiento muscular mediante resonancia o ecografía, dejando fuera las mediciones más subjetivas con básculas de bioimpedancia.
En este modelo se confirma que el músculo crece con el tiempo, pero arroja una curva de rendimientos decrecientes. Se dice esto porque el aumento medio muscular es de un 8,9% a las 20 semanas, un 9,4% a las 24, un 10,5% a las 36 y un 12,6% al año y medio. Como vemos, no sigue un crecimiento lineal, sino que conforme vamos avanzando en las sesiones de entrenamiento, nos encontramos con un músculo que cuesta más que crezca, lo que puede terminar desmotivando a seguir entrenando.
Interviene la genética. Con estos porcentajes es fácil marcarse unos objetivos claros y decir que si entreno durante 20 semanas, voy a tener casi un 10% más de músculo en el cuerpo, pero la realidad es que cada persona es completamente diferente. Aquí, un estudio publicado en 2005 sometió a 585 personas a 12 semanas de entrenamiento y determinó que el tamaño muscular varió entre una pérdida del 2% y una ganancia del 59%.
Esto hace que debamos concienciarnos de que cada persona va a un ritmo diferente a la hora de hacer un cambio físico que pase por una ganancia muscular y que no hablamos de una ciencia exacta. De esta manera, si dos personas van a entrenar juntas y hacen la misma cantidad de ejercicios, es posible que una de ellas vea antes los resultados esperados.

articles.title: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50-Series Scheduled for up to $500 Price Hike This Week
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 3rd 2026
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50-Series Scheduled for up to $500 Price Hike This Week
NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 50-Series "Blackwell" gaming graphics cards are expected to see significant price adjustments this week. According to Chinese ChannelGate, add-in card (AIC) partners have confirmed that price hikes are scheduled due to the ongoing demand for these GPUs outstripping supply. Some major AIC partners, like Colorful and Galax, have reportedly already started sharing information about these price increases. The most significant example is expected to be for SKUs based on NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 5090 DV2, which will see an increase of up to 3,300 RMB, translating to nearly $500. Even entry-level GPUs are not exempt, as the GeForce RTX 5060 is expected to see around a $30 price increase on existing models. These changes are anticipated to be implemented this week for retail partners, meaning that consumer prices might take a week or two to reflect the new listing prices.Below is the list of price hikes in China, expected to be the norm.
- RTX 5090 DV2: 2200-3300 RMB ($329-$494);
- RTX 5080: 2500-2800 RMB ($374-$419);
- RTX 5070 Ti: 1000 RMB ($150);
- RTX 5070: 600-900 RMB ($90-$135);
- RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB: 250-400 RMB ($37-$60);
- RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB: 100-150 RMB ($15-$22);
- RTX 5060: 150-200 RMB ($22-$30).
Other series from NVIDIA, as well as AMD and Intel GPUs, are not affected by this immediate price hike. However, AMD's Radeon graphics cards are expected to see another price increase this month. The main factors behind these price hikes are the tight memory supply and the significant rise in the cost of raw materials, such as copper, used in production.

articles.title: LinkedIn Uses OpenTelemetry to Trace the Member Journey from Tap to Backend
articles.text:
LinkedIn has built an OpenTelemetry-based telemetry platform that connects what members do in its iOS, Android, and web applications with the backend services processing those interactions.
The goal is to close a common observability gap. Client analytics can show that a member tapped a button or encountered an error, while backend tracing explains what happened inside the services handling the request. Historically, connecting these views required engineers to correlate separate systems. LinkedIn's approach allows a member interaction to be followed from the client through frontend and backend services to the underlying data stores.
A single page can generate numerous requests, each potentially passing through multiple services. LinkedIn introduced a pageForestId to provide context above individual distributed traces.
Each request retains its OpenTelemetry traceId, while related requests from the same page context can be associated through the pageForestId. Engineers can therefore investigate both an individual request and the wider activity that contributed to a member's experience.
This is important because conventional distributed tracing generally follows one request, whereas a member journey can involve many related requests.
LinkedIn operates a diverse technology stack spanning mobile and web clients alongside backend services written in Java, Python, Go, and Rust. OpenTelemetry provides a common model for instrumentation, trace context, and semantic conventions across those environments.
LinkedIn has built its own wrappers and extensions around the standard OpenTelemetry SDKs, allowing product teams to use consistent instrumentation while the platform handles concerns such as mobile lifecycle, export, and LinkedIn-specific metadata.
Client and backend applications generate OpenTelemetry spans, with trace context propagated as requests move through the system. Shared HTTP and gRPC frameworks automatically instrument common request paths, while teams can add explicit spans around important business operations.
Telemetry is transported through Apache Kafka and stored in ClickHouse, with pageForestId, traceId, and timestamps providing the keys for correlation. This allows engineers to begin with a member-facing interaction and drill into the backend execution responsible for it.
Capturing every span would generate an enormous amount of telemetry, making sampling fundamental to the architecture.
LinkedIn uses coordinated head sampling so related client and server activity receives a consistent sampling decision. A pseudonymised member identifier helps maintain that consistency across the journey, preventing the client from being sampled while the corresponding backend trace is discarded, or vice versa.
The company also distinguishes valuable quality-of-experience telemetry from lower-value debugging information. LinkedIn estimates that up to 90% of some backend tracing volume could potentially be treated as debug-level data.
Client-side observability introduces additional constraints. Mobile applications can be suspended or terminated before telemetry is transmitted, so LinkedIn batches spans but can flush telemetry when an application moves into the background.
The platform also applies controls around what data can enter traces, including attribute allowlists, denylists, and redaction. This is important because distributed traces can otherwise become an unintended channel for sensitive application or member information.
Traditional distributed tracing tools such as Jaeger and Grafana Tempo are primarily focused on following requests across backend services. Commercial platforms such as Datadog and New Relic also combine distributed tracing with real-user and application monitoring.
LinkedIn's approach is less about introducing a capability that these platforms cannot provide and more about making OpenTelemetry the common foundation connecting its client and backend telemetry. Its own pageForestId model adds a higher-level grouping around standard traces, while Kafka and ClickHouse provide a customised ingestion and storage architecture.
This also gives LinkedIn greater control over its observability stack and avoids making application instrumentation dependent on a particular commercial backend.
A member does not experience a traceId; they experience a page that loads slowly, an action that fails, or a feature that behaves unexpectedly. Connecting those experiences to the distributed systems behind them gives engineers a much more direct path from user impact to technical cause.

articles.title: “Les gens méritent d’avoir leur RAM” : Elon Musk se moque de Sam Altman qui regrette que nos PC utilisent de la RAM
articles.text:
Pénurie de mémoire : Elon Musk recadre Sam Altman, qui préférerait voir la RAM de nos PC dans ses serveurs
En pleine crise mondiale de mémoire vive, Sam Altman juge “tout à fait terrible” que les ordinateurs personnels mobilisent de la RAM, s’attirant illico les moqueries d’Elon Musk.
La pénurie mondiale de mémoire vive continue de faire flamber les prix des produits tech et de créer quelques tensions entre multimilliardaires. Alors que les fabricants réorientent leurs usines vers l’intelligence artificielle au détriment du grand public, le patron d’OpenAI, Sam Altman, a remis de l’huile sur le feu en critiquant la présence même de RAM dans nos ordinateurs. Une sortie très mal accueillie sur le web, qu’Elon Musk s’est empressé de tourner en dérision.
La RAM des PC au service du cloud : Elon Musk se moque de Sam Altman
Invité sur la chaîne YouTube Cheeky Pint, le dirigeant d’OpenAI a affirmé que, du point de vue de l’allocation mondiale des ressources, il serait “tout à fait terrible que tout le monde ait une part de l’offre mondiale limitée de DRAM assise dans son propre ordinateur et utilisée 5 % du temps”. Face à la pénurie actuelle, il estime qu’il serait bien plus logique de regrouper toute cette mémoire dans les serveurs du cloud pour la faire tourner à plein régime, tout en déplorant que le grand public pense exactement l’inverse.
Il n’en fallait pas plus pour faire réagir le patron de Tesla et SpaceX sur son réseau social X. Affirmant que “les gens méritent aussi d’avoir leur RAM”, Elon Musk a publié un mème détournant le film Inglourious Basterds avec un officier allemand de la Seconde Guerre mondiale traquant des personnes cachant des barrettes de DRAM au détriment du cloud.
Derrière la position de Sam Altman se dessine surtout l’intérêt financier d’OpenAI. Si l’entreprise propose quelques modèles open source, elle tire ses revenus des modèles hébergés dans ses centres de données et facturés aux utilisateurs. Des ordinateurs domestiques capables de faire tourner des modèles en local viennent ainsi réduire mécaniquement le besoin de passer par ses serveurs payants.
Pénurie de RAM et IA : une flambée des prix partie pour durer au-delà de 2027
Cette déclaration passe d’autant plus mal que les consommateurs subissent une hausse généralisée du prix des composants et produits tech, liée justement au développement à vitesse grand V de l’infrastructure IA. Samsung, SK Hynix et Micron, leaders de ce marché, prévoient des pénuries de mémoire vive jusqu’en 2027 et au-delà.
Alors que Lenovo prévenait dès le mois de juin que les tarifs ne reviendraient pas de sitôt (voire jamais) à leurs niveaux d’avant 2026, Apple a annoncé hier lors de la présentation de ses résultats trimestriels que cette flambée “sans précédent” rogne ses marges et restreint les stocks de Mac et d’iPad pour décembre. Cela laisse au passage planer la menace d’une nouvelle hausse de prix chez la firme à la pomme après celles de juin et septembre, bien que rien n’ait été confirmé pour le moment.
