articles.title: Así cotizan las principales criptomonedas del mundo digital este martes 3 de noviembre
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 76.532,24 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de -0,189% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de 0,129% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 2.251,78 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de -0,03%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 691,29 dólares, con un cambio de -2,89%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 53.65 dólares, tras una variación de -3.4159956.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,07 dólares tras presentar un cambio de -2,4% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Su avance en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: Attendue depuis des mois, cette nouveauté d’Android sauvegarde toute seule vos photos sur Windows
articles.text:
Transférer automatiquement des photos et vidéos d’Android vers un PC Windows, c’est maintenant possible
Google déploie enfin la sauvegarde automatique des photos et vidéos d’un smartphone Android vers un PC Windows grâce à Quick Share. Une fonction gratuite et totalement indépendante du cloud.
Face à des stockages saturés sur smartphone par des milliers de photos et vidéos, le cloud est souvent la solution de la simplicité. Bien que Google propose ses propres abonnements avec Google One, la firme américaine a finalement décidé d’enrichir les liens entre Android et Windows pour transférer ces fichiers vers un PC de façon automatique. Une solution locale et gratuite, qui évite aussi bien les branchements par câble que le stockage en ligne payant.
Un transfert automatique vers Windows, le rêve devient enfin réalité
L’information figure désormais noir sur blanc dans les notes de version des services système de Google pour novembre 2026. Intégrée à la mise à jour v26.43 des services Google Play sous la rubrique dédiée à la connectivité des appareils, une courte ligne destinée aux téléphones comme aux PC confirme l’arrivée de la sauvegarde automatique des photos et vidéos d’Android vers Windows via Quick Share.
C’est la première fois que Google reconnaît officiellement cette fonctionnalité suivie depuis des mois par le média Android Authority. Dès le mois d’avril, une option baptisée “Automatic backup” avait en effet été repérée dans les paramètres de Quick Share (l’outil de partage de fichiers de proximité d’Android, équivalent d’AirDrop chez Apple), où elle promettait de copier photos, vidéos et fichiers audio du téléphone vers un PC via le réseau domestique, c’est-à-dire votre connexion Wi-Fi.
L’analyse des lignes de code des services Google Play réalisée en octobre avait également dévoilé le fonctionnement de la configuration. L’utilisateur devra lancer la procédure depuis l’application Quick Share pour Windows, en gardant son téléphone à proximité et en connectant les deux appareils au même compte Google. Une fois l’opération terminée, l’outil enregistrera de lui-même les clichés et vidéos sur l’ordinateur, sans nécessiter de câble ni d’abonnement cloud. La synchronisation se fera ainsi quotidiennement en arrière-plan, dès lors que le smartphone et le PC sont allumés, proches l’un de l’autre et connectés au même réseau Wi-Fi.
Un doute subsiste toutefois concernant Samsung : le code analysé ces derniers mois semblait exclure les smartphones Galaxy et PC Galaxy Book de la marque, sans que les notes officielles de Google ne le confirment. Une mise à l’écart qui s’expliquerait par la volonté du constructeur coréen de privilégier ses propres outils (Smart Switch et sa version dédiée de Quick Share sur Windows), malgré la fusion de Nearby Share et Quick Share début 2024.
Le déploiement étant progressif, la nouveauté mettra du temps à arriver sur tous les smartphones, et nécessitera une mise à jour de l’application Quick Share sur Windows et des services Google Play sur Android.

articles.title: Sachin Tendulkar backs Hitwicket maker Metasports Interactive
articles.text:
Sachin Tendulkar backs Hitwicket maker Metasports Interactive
Sachin Tendulkar joins Hitwicket maker Metasports Interactive as a strategic investor, backing its ambition to reach 100 million downloads amid growing competition in India's gaming industry.
Metasports Interactive, the Hyderabad-based maker of cricket strategy game Hitwicket, has brought cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar on board as a strategic investor. He will also serve as the game’s brand ambassador.
Financial terms and valuation remain undisclosed.
Existing backers include venture-capital firms Prime Venture Partners and Singapore’s Horizon Ventures, as well as cricket commentator Harsha Bhogle.
This development is separate from the $20 million in user-acquisition funding it secured from London-based Metica in April. That earlier, non-dilutive facility was intended to fund marketing and international expansion without giving up equity.
Metasports has not specified how Tendulkar’s investment will be deployed. It aims to reach 100 million downloads within three years. The company claims Hitwicket has more than 20 million users across 120 countries, revenue doubled in the six months before the announcement, and players spend an average of 51 minutes daily on the game.
According to the company, more than 97% of its revenue comes from in-app purchases, or optional items bought within the game. Its wider ambition is to build mobile sports gaming franchises beyond cricket.
Hitwicket is a multiplayer strategy title that puts tactical decisions ahead of reflexes. Players manage a virtual side and choose how to approach each ball.
Tendulkar said it captures cricket’s strategic thinking, explaining that “Cricket has always involved reading the bowler, assessing the field and deciding the right approach for every ball.” He will also feature in the game and related content.
Reddy said Tendulkar’s cricketing knowledge would help the team understand elite players’ decisions and refine gameplay.
India’s gaming market offers a substantial audience, although converting it into globally competitive businesses and original intellectual property remains a challenge. The Game Developer Association of India estimates that the country had 511 million players and $1.04 billion in video-game revenue in 2025.
Recent funding deals demonstrate investor interest across genres. Bengaluru-based Spill Games raised $10.5 million in October, led by Elevation Capital, while social gaming platform Matiks raised $10 million led by General Catalyst. Cricket-focused LightFury Games also secured $11 million from investors including Blume Ventures, V3 Ventures, MIXI and Times Internet.
Policy is shifting too. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, and its rules, effective from May 1, 2026, prohibit online money games while establishing a framework for e-sports and online social games, with user-safety and grievance-redressal requirements. Classification considers factors such as stakes, expected cash winnings and whether rewards can be converted outside a game.

articles.title: EPA throws in the towel on policing air pollution from factory farms
articles.text:
The Environmental Protection Agency late last week announced it would end a 20-plus-year effort to develop methods to monitor air pollution from factory farms, effectively shuttering the agency’s stop-and-start attempts to regulate the potentially pollutant-spewing facilities under the Clean Air Act.
The announcement came just days before the midterm elections and was characterized by the agency as a long-awaited reprieve for farmers, a historically important constituency for Trump and the Republican Party.
When tens of thousands of animals are packed into one place, pollution from their waste is blown from ventilation fans or emanates from giant lagoons of liquid effluent. Livestock facilities emit fine particulate matter, ammonia, nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide, and volatile organic compounds, all contributing to a toxic mix. Research has shown that emissions from these operations are a major cause of air pollution, causing nearly 12,700 deaths in the United States a year.
Strictly speaking, concentrated animal feeding operations, or CAFOs, are required to get permits under the Clean Air Act and report emissions of these pollutants under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability and Act and the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act. But through a deal crafted in tandem with the EPA and the livestock industry, they’ve been given amnesty from doing so for more than 20 years.
The arrangement goes back to the early 2000s when the agency attempted to prosecute CAFOs for exceeding limits on some of these pollutants. The industry pushed back, arguing there was no adequate way of measuring them. So the agency worked with industry groups to develop what was dubbed the Air Consent Agreement, through which the EPA granted thousands of CAFOs safe harbor from legal action in exchange for their participation in a study that was funded by the industry.

articles.title: 'We set out to illustrate what happens when Razer’s engineering and design capabilities are pushed to their absolute limits' — The limited release Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition is Razer's 'most ambitious' officially licensed PS5 controller to date, and you can get yours now
articles.text:
The Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition is Razer's 'most ambitious' PS5 controller to date, featuring materials 'chosen for strength, durability, and finish' — here's where you can get the limited release gamepad
The controller will have a limited release supply of 1,337 units
- The Razer Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition launches November 10 for $349.99 / €368.99
- The licensed PS5 controller features a magnesium alloy exoskeleton and an open polygonal top and back plate design with chamfered edges
- The controller is also optimized for PC and boasts "reliable precision, exceptional control, and blazing-fast speed"
Razer has announced the Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition, a new version of its officially licensed PlayStation 5 controller built on a decade of experience for "the highest level of performance and craftsmanship."
Launching exclusively at Razer on November 10 for $349.99 / €368.99 in an initial limited release supply of 1,337 serialized units, the Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition is Razer's "most ambitious" PS5 controller to date and combines materials chosen for "strength, durability, and finish."
The jet-black controller features a strong magnesium alloy exoskeleton, and the handles are wrapped in matte black textured TPU grip that resists oils and abrasion for a pristine finish for extended play sessions.
Layered over the touchpad, the Razer logo is laser-etched on a semi-transparent, tinted glass panel, which offers a subtle view of the open-air polygonal design underneath.
The Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition also has an open polygonal top and back plate design with chamfered edges, and its nano coating leaves the internal elements exposed beneath the shell, keeping them safe from debris.

Built for PS5 consoles and optimized for PC with a 2,000Hz polling rate thanks to Razer HyperPolling Wireless for sharper movement and tracking, the controller also offers six mappable multi-function buttons, two claw-grip bumpers, and four mouse-click back buttons.

articles.title: Le retour du manga Dragon Ball Super se complique de plus en plus
articles.text:
Lancé en juin 2015 dans le magazine japonais V Jump, Dragon Ball Super est la suite officielle du manga d’Akira Toriyama. Dessinée par Toyotaro, la série a longtemps bénéficié de la participation de l’auteur original au scénario. Le manga compte aujourd’hui 24 tomes. Sa publication mensuelle s’est arrêtée au chapitre 103, paru quelques semaines après la mort d’Akira Toriyama, le 1er mars 2024. Depuis, un seul chapitre est sorti, le 104, une histoire courte publiée en février 2025.
Après plus de deux ans de pause et plusieurs indices laissant espérer une reprise, la série est absente de la programmation de la Jump Festa 2027, ce grand rendez-vous annuel de l’éditeur autour de ses mangas, qui se tiendra les 19 et 20 décembre au Makuhari Messe, près de Tokyo. La série ne figure ni sur l’affiche promotionnelle ni parmi les 34 œuvres qui auront droit à un programme sur l’une des trois scènes de l’événement.
Ce lundi 2 novembre, elle a aussi été retirée du Jump Original Art World, l’exposition d’illustrations originales présentée pendant l’événement. Le site de la Jump Festa indique désormais qu’elle y est remplacée par Metaphor: ReFantazio, l’adaptation en manga du jeu vidéo d’Atlus publiée depuis janvier 2025 dans le même magazine, le V Jump. Aucune raison n’est donnée.
Shueisha rompt ainsi avec une habitude. Selon CBR, c’est la première fois en onze ans que Goku ne figure pas sur le visuel officiel de la Jump Festa. Pour les fans, l’espoir d’une annonce sur le manga avant la fin de l’année s’amenuise.
La reprise de Dragon Ball Super s’éloigne encore
Pourtant, les espoirs d’une reprise de la série avaient été ravivés le 21 mars 2026, lorsque Toyotaro a modifié sa biographie sur X avec une formule pour le moins évocatrice : « Tout pour la reprise de la série ». En août, le mangaka avait également répondu à un jeune fan qui lui demandait de dessiner davantage de Dragon Ball Super. Sa réponse, « Merci. J’ai bien compris », avait été relayée par le compte officiel de V Jump, alimentant les spéculations sur une reprise de la série.
La licence n’est pour autant pas au point mort : Dragon Ball Super: Beerus, la version retravaillée des débuts de l’anime, est diffusé depuis le 11 octobre au Japon. Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol, encore sans date, adaptera ensuite la saga du Prisonnier de la Patrouille Galactique. Le retour du manga, lui, se fait toujours attendre.
La principale difficulté reste évidemment l’absence d’Akira Toriyama. Pendant près de neuf ans, Toyotaro a travaillé à ses côtés. Akira Toriyama lui fournissait les grandes lignes du scénario et lui faisait ses retours, comme le dessinateur le racontait régulièrement dans les pages du V Jump et dans les tomes. Continuer sans celui qui a imaginé cet univers et qui le chapeautait dans l’ombre représente forcément un défi, aussi bien sur le plan créatif qu’éditorial.
Toyotaro a pourtant déjà fait l’exercice. Le chapitre 104, une histoire courte centrée sur Goten et Trunks, est le premier qu’il a mené seul. Dans une interview accordée mi-2025, il jugeait une reprise sans Akira Toriyama « pas impossible » et reconnaissait avoir déjà écrit lui-même une bonne partie des derniers chapitres, comme le rapporte Complex en août.
Les messages de Toyotaro entretiennent l’espoir de revoir Dragon Ball Super un jour, mais Shueisha a écarté le manga de son plus grand événement de l’année. Ni l’éditeur ni le V Jump, qui paraît chaque mois autour du 21, n’ont annoncé de date de reprise. Les fans n’ont plus qu’à patienter.

Une immersion 3D puissante et des choix techniques singuliers
La Marshall Heston 120 est une barre de son qui ne cherche pas à disparaître sous votre téléviseur : c’est un objet de décoration assumé qui reprend les codes esthétiques de la marque, avec sa grille en nylon tressé, ses finitions en similicuir et son logo doré frontal. Sous ce châssis généreux de 110 cm de large pour 7 kg, le constructeur a intégré une architecture 5.1.2 ambitieuse pour un coup d’essai. Sous son capot, la barre déploie une puissance crête de 150 watts et parvient à s’affranchir d’un caisson de basses externe grâce à l’intégration d’un mini-caisson interne. Il s’appuie sur deux transducteurs dédiés orientés vers l’arrière et quatre radiateurs passifs, ce qui permet à la barre de son de descendre jusqu’à 40 Hz.
La scène sonore est élargie par onze transducteurs actifs, avec des haut-parleurs latéraux et deux unités verticales qui projettent le son vers le plafond pour le côté Dolby Atmos et DTS:X. Les voix sont claires et la sensation d’enveloppement est réussie, même si l’ensemble n’atteint pas la précision chirurgicale de la Sennheiser Ambeo Soundbar Plus. Du côté de la connectique filaire, la Heston 120 intègre deux ports HDMI, dont une prise eARC capable d’assurer un pass-through 4K à 120 Hz. Ce qui est plus étonnant, c’est que la protection HDCP se limite à la norme 1.4, ce qui peut bloquer la lecture de certains contenus 4K HDR si la barre sert de relais vidéo direct. Pour compenser, la marque ajoute une entrée RCA stéréo rare sur ce format.
L’alliance du streaming et de l’analogique
Là où l’interface d’un home cinéma contemporain se résume à une simple application smartphone, la Heston 120 invite plutôt au contact physique. Son panneau de contrôle supérieur arbore trois potentiomètres en laiton cerclés de chemins lumineux rouges qui permettent d’ajuster le volume, régler les graves et les aigus ou sélectionner la source d’un simple clic. Ce retour assumé au tactile offre une expérience d’utilisation organique satisfaisante et un peu oubliée à l’heure du tout-numérique. Mais ça ne l’empêche pas d’avoir une app mobile quand même, avec une fonction d’auto-calibration acoustique, qui exploite les deux micros embarqués.
Pour ce qui est de la restitution musicale, la signature sonore Marshall est bien là, avec un fort dynamisme, là où la concurrence préfère parfois lisser les fréquences pour plaire au plus grand nombre. Ici, si vous êtes fan de rock ou de performances en live, vous allez pouvoir vous faire plaisir. Et vous pouvez utiliser sans problème AirPlay 2, Google Cast, Spotify Connect et Tidal Connect. Par contre, il faudra composer avec l’absence de télécommande physique, un choix moderne qui peut diviser et qui oblige à s’en remettre au contrôle CEC du TV ou votre smartphone.

articles.title: OpenAI built itself a new Git backend, too
articles.text:
OpenAI built itself a new Git backend, too
OpenAI on Monday detailed how it built a new Git backend for its monorepo to power the ever-increasing number of commits its developers and their agents now create.
Pando, as the team calls the new backend, cut push latency by nearly 5x, the company says, and it currently serves close to a petabyte of Git data per day at OpenAI.
OpenAI is obviously an early adopter of agentic coding tools. Compared to the first quarter of 2024, the quarterly commits to its monorepo will have increased by over 2,400% by the end of this year, the company says. But the issues it is facing are similar to what many other enterprises and Git forges like GitHub are now seeing.
With the pace of development increasing, Git itself is becoming a bottleneck. GitHub, for example, spent much of its recent Universe keynote on how it is improving its infrastructure to become faster and more reliable, all while serving billions of pull requests every month.
That has given rise to startups like Entire (from former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke) and projects like Origin from Cursor. Like OpenAI’s work, those are based on Git, but others, like Anthropic, basically start from scratch with a new client and architecture.
Why OpenAI stayed with Git
The OpenAI team explicitly notes that it wanted to retain compatibility with Git. The team was seeing the reliability of its Git backend fall below 90%, with slow fetches and failed merges, but decided to stay within the Git ecosystem.
As OpenAI’s Aaron Friel, Taylor Blau, and Ted Nyman ask in the announcement, the question the team asked itself was if it had “reached a limit of Git itself, or of the way we served our monorepo?” The answer for OpenAI was that the Git client and protocol weren’t really the problem (though the team is also making some tweaks there), but the way conventional Git servers are built.
“For more than two decades, developers have adapted their tools around Git as the way they build software has changed,” they write. “When we started to feel friction in our own monorepo, it mattered to us that we could keep building on that work.”
How Pando works
Pando drops two things most Git servers treat as requirements. The first is keeping every branch in the repository in a consistent state at once. The second is building a custom packfile, Git’s format for bundling compressed objects, for every client that fetches code.
In Git, a branch is simply a pointer to that latest commit. Moving that pointer is the only part of a push that requires coordination. Conventional Git servers order those updates across the entire repository, so when there are many developers working in parallel, a push to one agent’s branch can end up waiting on another’s.
Pando, on the other hands, doesn’t coordinate every write across the whole repository. Instead, it handles each branch on its own. Because of this, pushes to unrelated branches then don’t have to wait on each other.
There’s a tradeoff here, the team acknowledges. When a client is looking at several branches at once, it may see them at slightly different points in time. In practice, however, users and agents only care about the order of updates to a single branch, OpenAI argues.
When a client pushes, Pando validates the incoming packfile as it streams it into blob storage, without unpacking it into a local repository. It records the new branch tip, the packfile’s location, and its dependencies in a metadata store. By default, Pando advertises only the trunk branch as a base for feature-branch pushes. That makes each pack reusable by other clients that already have the advertised trunk history.
Then, when another client fetches the branch, Pando selects the stored packs it needs based on the history it already has. It then returns download links through packfile-uri, a Git protocol feature that lets clients download packs separately.
A caching service called Express then serves those packs from regional caches, with a hit rate above 99%, the company says. On standard cloud VMs, clones and fetches can max out a 10 Gbps network link.
A busy monorepo would otherwise leave clients downloading tens of thousands of small packs a day, so background workers merge them into larger ones over time, much like a log-structured database compacts its data. That also lets Pando work out which packs a client needs in logarithmic time.
Pando vs. standard Git servers
On a standard Git server, every fetch means working out which objects the client is missing and compressing a fresh packfile just for that client. Those packs are expensive to generate and hard to cache, OpenAI says. Pando mostly hands out bytes it already has.
Before a push, a regular Git server also lists every branch it holds so the client can skip objects the server already has. With millions of branches, that list alone can grow past 100 MiB, according to OpenAI. Advertising only trunk keeps it small, but it means repeat pushes to the same branch resend everything that isn’t on trunk. The team says that’s a fair trade, since the median pack in its monorepo is still under 20 KiB.
Regular Git servers also have to repack and garbage-collect repositories to keep them fast, which eats up compute and disk I/O. Pando never throws a pack away. It keeps packs at every compaction level and serves from all of them.
For developers, little of this is visible. They keep using standard Git commands, though OpenAI now ships its own Git build to developer machines and inside the ChatGPT desktop app.
OpenAI built Pando in Rust in 10 weeks, with one engineer designing the core and teams of Codex agents implementing it. It went into production in April.
What goes back into open source Git?
Building on Git also meant running into some of Git’s own rough edges, and OpenAI says it’s sending many of its fixes back to the project. Because Pando leans so heavily on packfile-uri, which a Google engineer first proposed in 2019, the team had to fix how the Git client handles concurrent pack downloads, cleans up after interrupted transfers, and resumes downloads that had already finished. It also added tracing for those downloads, which makes it easier to tell whether a slow fetch is spending its time generating packs or transferring them.
Not all of that work has landed in Git yet. OpenAI says several of its changes are already upstream, while many others for now only live in the company’s public Git repository. Those include support for downloading and indexing packs in parallel and a new “explicit haves” feature, which lets a server tell a pushing client where a branch currently points without letting the client leave that history out of its pack. The company is tracking all of this in a public patch tracker.
Pando itself isn’t part of that, though. OpenAI isn’t open sourcing the backend, and as of now, it only says that it’s looking into ways to share the underlying technology with its users. Anthropic, too, has said it has no plans to release Scion, either.
Learning Path

articles.title: Bethesda confirms Elder Scrolls VI title is 'Sentinel' -- 8 years after reveal
articles.text:
Bethesda has announced that the next Elder Scrolls game will officially be called The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. The company unveiled the full title, which had recently been leaked, in a larger video celebrating its 40th anniversary.
However, that’s all the quick trailer shows us outside of a dune and a quote from a character called Yazar the Moth Priest. Otherwise, we still know nothing about the game itself. For context, The Elder Scrolls VI was first announced way back at E3 2018 alongside the sci-fi RPG Starfield. But while that latter game launched in 2023, Bethesda went dark on the sixth Elder Scrolls.
To be clear, it undoubtedly takes a long time to make the kind of sprawling RPGs that are Bethesda’s bread and butter. But it also begs the question of why you’d announce the game way back in 2018 when it was still in pre-production and clearly many years away, especially since Starfield was the focus at the time. For what it’s worth, Bloomberg‘s Jason Schreier said the announcement was made to placate fans who were upset over Fallout 76, a multiplayer game. (We still don’t even have a release window for Sentinel, although Schreier speculated it’s at least two years away still.)
It certainly hasn’t helped Bethesda in recent months that parent company Xbox has been an absolute mess, laying off thousands of people and having big corporate shake-ups throughout. These reductions have included at least 50 people at Bethesda Game Studios, which, understandably, has also left those who remain with reduced talent and diminishing morale. (All of this comes, mind you, as Microsoft continues to report soaring profits.)
But hey, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma took some time in the summer in between axing everyone to say that the game is great, so we can all rest easy.
Image credit: Bethesda

articles.title: Introducing India-based inference for Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Introducing India-based inference for Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock
Kimi K3 is a multi-modal, open-weight foundation model (FM) that provider Moonshot AI reported achieved frontier-level coding and general agentic intelligence at release.
In addition to global and US-based inference, Amazon Bedrock now supports in-country inference in India for Kimi K3: unblocking local workloads with strict data residency requirements. Customers like Ultrahuman are already seeing the benefits in production:
        “Jade, an AI Health and Wellness assistant in the Ultrahuman app, answers questions in plain language using each person’s own Ring and glucose data, across more than 14,000 conversations a day. Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock let us add a leading open-weight model through the API we already use, with health data staying inside AWS and Mumbai as a fallback Region. With prompt caching, we’ve cut LLM costs by 80 percent and made multi-turn chats 85 percent faster.”
— Aditya Patawari, VP Engineering, Ultrahuman
In this post, we explain the different global and geographic inference options available, and share code for an example use case: optical character recognition (OCR) and understanding of Indic-language documents, with follow-up question answering in code-mixed Hinglish.
Choose where inference can run
Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock is offered through cross-Region inference profiles. You can invoke the model from any of a wide range of AWS Regions (the “source”). Amazon Bedrock then securely processes your request in one of multiple possible “destination” Regions.
Cross-Region inference is fully managed by AWS: Data is encrypted in transit between Regions and remains on the AWS network, never traversing the public internet or requiring you to set up any multi-Region virtual private cloud (VPC) infrastructure.
The inference profile ID you invoke controls which destination Regions are eligible:
| Profile | Model ID | When to choose it | 
| Global | global.moonshotai.kimi-k3 | Recommended for most use cases: lowest cost and most broadly available | 
| India geographic | in.moonshotai.kimi-k3 | Inference processing must stay within Mumbai and Hyderabad Regions | 
See the Amazon Bedrock Kimi K3 model card for up-to-date information on available inference profiles, which AWS Regions they can be called from, and what destination Regions they can use for inference.
Example walkthrough: Indic-language document understanding
Let’s consider an example use case: reading a scanned Hindi document, extracting structured data, and answering follow-up questions in mixed Hindi and English (Hinglish).
This need is common in Indian financial services and public sector workflows where know your customer (KYC) forms, utility bills, and similar documents must often be digitized. Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock can directly read and reason about images, including those containing multilingual text. It offers a potential solution with no separate OCR or translation service required.
Prerequisites
The full source code for this example is available on GitHub.
To follow along, you need:
- An AWS account.
- Python 3.11 or later installed, with internet access to install the required PyPI packages.
- The AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) installed, with credentials configured with sufficient AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions to invoke the Kimi K3 model through the India inference profile.
For example, to use Kimi K3 through the ap-south-1 Mumbai Region with India geographic inference, the following IAM policy grants sufficient access. Replace the {ACCOUNT_ID} placeholders with your AWS account ID:
For more information about permissions, see Prerequisites for running model inference in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. If your organization restricts AWS Regions, ask your administrator to review the geographic cross-Region inference IAM and SCP guidance. Keep the source Region permitted and allow routing to both India destinations, using a profile-scoped exception where appropriate. The Responses API guide also describes required default-project access.
Get started with the inference APIs
As detailed on the model card, Amazon Bedrock supports multiple APIs for invoking Kimi K3, all under the Bedrock Runtime endpoint:
| API | Request and response format | 
| Chat Completions | OpenAI-compatible messages input and assistant-message output. | 
| Responses | OpenAI-compatible input and structured output items. | 
| Converse | Standardized messages, content blocks, and inference parameters across supported models. | 
| InvokeModel | Model-specific JSON request and response bodies. | 
Because the OpenAI-compatible APIs are recommended for this model, we use those in this example and connect through the openai Python Library.
Amazon Bedrock supports generating API keys for integrations that require them. However, AWS recommends using short-lived credentials instead where possible. The AWS token generator Python library derives a short-term API key-like token from the standard AWS CLI credential chain.
If you use a named profile for your AWS CLI, you might need to set the AWS_PROFILE environment variable first. After CLI credentials are set up, you can invoke the model with the following code:
Here, region (ap-south-1 Mumbai) specifies the source Region to which the request is made. The inference profile in.moonshotai.kimi-k3 ensures that inference is processed in Indian Regions only.
A broad range of features like streaming, tool calling, and structured outputs are supported across both the Chat Completions and Responses APIs. See the OpenAI Python API Reference for more examples.
Analyze images
Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock supports images as well as PDFs and a range of other file types. You can send input files to the model directly by base64-encoding. For OCR or other use cases where small details are important, consider setting the image detail parameter to high. This improves accuracy, at the cost of more input tokens consumed per image.
In some cases, we’ve seen higher output quality for Kimi K3 when images are provided before text inputs. We suggest experimenting with request ordering. Consider the following example code:
To demonstrate, we generated an image of a synthetic electricity bill in Hindi.
Given this image input, the model can answer questions by pulling data directly from the document with no separate digitization step required. For example:
Q: Bill kitne ka hai aur last date kab hai? Late hua toh kitna dena padega?
A: Bill ka total ₹2,217.20 hai, aur last date 20/10/2026 hai. Late hua toh ₹2,261.54 dena padega.
Build a structured extraction pipeline
Beyond general question-answering, you can create structured document processing workflows by using static prompts to extract a consistent set of expected fields across many documents.
To apply firm constraints on output structure (rather than best-effort prompt-guided generation), Kimi K3 supports structured output on Amazon Bedrock either through function calling or by providing a JSON Schema output format. These options are described in more detail in the OpenAI documentation (for OpenAI-compatible APIs) and the Amazon Bedrock User Guide (for native Converse/InvokeModel APIs).
In the full sample code repository, we’ve provided an end-to-end pipeline that:
- Transcribes the document in its original script (OCR).
- Extracts key fields as JSON using a configurable schema, with dates normalized to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD), Devanagari digits (for example २८८) converted to Western digits (288), and names transliterated into English.
- Writes a short English summary.
- Answers multi-turn follow-up questions in Hinglish (Hindi written in Latin script, mixed with English) about the same document.
For the same synthetic Hindi electricity bill in the preceding figure, the pipeline returns structured fields such as the following (abbreviated):
We’ve also included a KYC form example and an open-ended schema-free mode, where the model selects the most useful fields itself for any other document type. All provided sample documents are synthetic, with fictional names and addresses and masked identity numbers.
Download the sample code from GitHub to explore further and try it out on your own images.
As with any automated extraction, you should verify the outputs are reliable for your specific use case before relying on them for important decisions. Consider adding post-validation logic or a human review step for critical workflows.
Optimize price-performance, service tiers and caching
Tune your system prompts and schemas against example documents for reliable extractions. Amazon Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization (AdvPO) provides a fully managed option to optimize prompt templates based on reference examples.
Amazon Bedrock service tiers give you control over price-performance on a per-request basis. For less latency-sensitive cases, you can select the flex tier to enjoy a 50 percent discount on default standard pricing. For latency-critical scenarios, you can select “priority” to request higher queue priority at a higher price. See the pricing page for details.
Use cases with long, seldom-changing content in their input prompts can also benefit from prompt caching on Amazon Bedrock. Make sure the static content (system prompt, tool descriptions, and so on) appears at the beginning of the input, before dynamic sections like the current image and question.
Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock supports both discounted pricing for cache hits, as well as an explicit caching mode. In the default implicit caching mode, the service attempts to automatically cache and reuse repeated prompt prefixes between requests with no user action required. However, you can improve performance by selecting the explicit mode and specifying ‘breakpoints’ of cacheable content in your input, boosting cache hit rate, response speed, and cost savings.
The following example shows explicit prompt caching with the Responses API. For more information, see prompt caching in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide:
Monitor usage
Amazon CloudWatch metrics are automatically generated for Kimi K3 under the AWS/Bedrock namespace, giving visibility of the invocation rate, token counts, cache usage, latency, errors, and throttling.
Model invocation logging is opt-in and can optionally contain prompts and outputs. Review access, retention, and storage location settings before enabling it.
Logs and metrics are stored in the source Region where you submitted your request, regardless of which destination Region might have processed it in cross-Region inference. You can optionally enable AWS CloudTrail data event logging to log model invocations in CloudTrail, which records requests’ destination Region as an additionalEventData.inferenceRegion field.
Clean up
Kimi K3 is billed on a per-token basis, so these code samples don’t provision any persistent AWS resources to clean up. If you created a new IAM Role or User to explore with, or added extra permissions to your existing User/Role, remember to delete them when you’re finished.
Conclusion and next steps
In this post, we explored how Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock provides on-demand intelligence capable of understanding mixed Indic and English languages. It now supports fully in-country data processing in India (AWS Mumbai and Hyderabad Regions) through the in.moonshotai.kimi-k3 inference profile.
Try it today in the Amazon Bedrock console or through the inference APIs. Check out the model card for more information, and visit AWS re:Post to find answers or ask the community about Amazon Bedrock.

articles.title: Avant son entrée en Bourse, le créateur de Claude lance une mise en garde troublante sur l'IA
articles.text:
En aidant les chercheurs à développer de nouveaux modèles, l’IA pourrait accélérer sa propre évolution. Anthropic avertit ses futurs investisseurs que cette boucle risque de progresser plus vite que les méthodes utilisées pour en garder le contrôle.
Anthropic juge désormais proche le seuil où l’IA permettrait aux modèles de progresser deux fois plus vite. Dans son dossier d’introduction en Bourse amendé le 2 novembre, le créateur de Claude prévient qu’il pourrait n’en prendre la mesure qu’après coup. Aucun modèle actuel n’a toutefois été déclaré au-delà de ce seuil d’alerte.
Une génération d’IA qui prépare la suivante
Dans une boucle d’auto-amélioration récursive, ou RSI (recursive self-improvement), une IA aide à créer une version plus performante, qui participe à son tour au développement de la suivante. Pour fonctionner de façon autonome, cette boucle doit couvrir toute la chaîne de recherche, du choix des expériences à leur analyse, en passant par l’écriture du code et l’entraînement.
Des méthodes d’entraînement plus efficaces pourraient ainsi accélérer l’arrivée d’IA utiles à la recherche scientifique ou médicale. Mais une étape résiste encore à l’automatisation. Selon Anthropic, Claude se montre plus à l’aise pour exécuter une expérience bien définie que pour choisir les pistes qui méritent d’être explorées. Le jugement des chercheurs reste donc déterminant.
Un doublement des progrès comme signal d’alerte
Pour repérer cette accélération, Anthropic s’appuie sur sa Responsible Scaling Policy, son cadre de sécurité interne. L’un des critères retenus est un doublement du rythme des progrès des modèles, largement attribuable à l’automatisation de la recherche et de l’ingénierie. Un an suffirait alors à obtenir les avancées qui en auraient demandé deux sans cette contribution.
Le critère porte sur les capacités acquises par les modèles. Doubler la quantité de code produite ne suffit donc pas à démontrer que ce seuil a été franchi.
Des modèles plus rapides à développer qu’à sécuriser
Anthropic redoute que ses prochaines IA gagnent de nouvelles capacités avant que les équipes aient pu en évaluer les risques et adapter leurs protections. L’entreprise admet d’ailleurs n’avoir repéré certaines accélérations qu’après coup. Elle souligne aussi qu’une erreur ou un biais présent dans un modèle pourrait se transmettre aux générations suivantes et s’amplifier, rendant sa détection et sa correction plus difficiles.
Son cadre de sécurité envisage également qu’une IA puisse manipuler l’entraînement de ses successeurs ou les éléments utilisés pour les juger sûrs. Mais les équipes humaines de sécurité pourront-elles suivre le rythme ?
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace

articles.title: Digital fraud slows African banks’ cross-border expansion
articles.text:
A surge in cybercrime across African banks and fintechs is forcing financial institutions to retreat to domestic markets, stalling cross-border integration and leaving continental initiatives like PAPSS and AfCFTA underutilised.
An escalating wave of digital fraud has emerged as the primary operational deterrent to cross-border financial integration in Africa, with 88% of commercial banks and fintech companies reporting increased electronic financial crimes.
The finding, detailed in the sixth edition of the African Financial Industry Barometer presented at the Africa Financial Summit (AFIS) in Luanda, highlights a growing security crisis that is prompting lenders to abandon cross-border ambitions in favour of domestic retrenchment.
Published jointly by Deloitte and Jeune Afrique Media Group, the survey gathered responses from financial leaders across 20 African nations.
Although overall industry confidence remained steady at 8 out of 10, matching the previous year’s rating, operational caution has intensified significantly as institutions struggle to secure digital channels against cross-border fraud.
Africa is confident in its financial future. So why is integration stalling?
Financial institutions rate the industry’s outlook highly, yet many are consolidating at home, regional initiatives are struggling to deliver, and digital fraud is rising. Explore the contradiction in the 2026 African Financial Industry Barometer.
Confidence is high. Expansion is another matter.
African financial leaders remain broadly optimistic. But confidence varies significantly between institutions already operating across borders and those focused on domestic markets.
Confidence depends on where you operate
Scores are out of 10. The categories include both institution types and business segments; they are not mutually exclusive groups.
Where do institutions want to grow?
Select a strategy to see what the survey says about expansion priorities.
Domestic consolidation was the most commonly identified growth strategy, particularly among banks and insurance companies.
Some local institutions favour regional alliances instead of establishing wholly owned operations abroad.
Fintech operators are the group most inclined towards organic regional expansion, despite their exposure to digital fraud.
Multi-market financial groups continue to consider acquisitions to strengthen existing regional footprints.
These percentages represent reported strategy preferences and are not parts of a single whole. Separately, 25% reported no regional expansion plans.
Three integration projects. Limited tangible progress.
AfCFTA, PAPSS and the African Exchanges Linkage Project are intended to make cross-border commerce, payments and investment easier. Survey respondents see slow implementation. Select a project to compare the findings.
AfCFTA
African Continental Free Trade Area — designed to deepen intra-African trade and regional economic integration.
HOW RESPONDENTS ASSESS IMPLEMENTATION
What stands out: Only 7% report tangible progress, despite the agreement’s continent-wide ambition.
PAPSS
Pan-African Payment and Settlement System — designed to support intra-African cross-border payments in local currencies.
HOW RESPONDENTS ASSESS IMPLEMENTATION
What stands out: PAPSS has the highest reported tangible progress of these three projects, but institutional participation remains limited.
The PAPSS participation problem
Beyond perceptions of progress, the survey asked institutions about their connection plans.
These are selected response categories, not a complete breakdown of all respondents.
AELP
African Exchanges Linkage Project — intended to connect participating African stock exchanges and facilitate cross-border investment.
HOW RESPONDENTS ASSESS IMPLEMENTATION
What stands out: AELP records the weakest progress assessment. Separately, 56% of respondents report no concrete benefits from the project.
The risks behind the retreat
Digital fraud is rising, cybersecurity remains a major concern, and the infrastructure needed to deploy defensive AI tools is uneven. Select a risk category to explore the findings.
Digital fraud is increasing
Share of surveyed institutions reporting an increase in digital fraud.
The tension: Fintechs are among the institutions pursuing regional expansion, yet banks and fintechs also report particularly widespread increases in digital fraud.
Cybersecurity tops the risk agenda
Share identifying cybersecurity as a major operational concern. This is distinct from reporting an increase in digital fraud.
Why this matters: Cross-border activity introduces additional operational and counterparty complexities, making security capacity especially important.
AI could help detect fraud. Deployment is harder.
85% recognise the impact of AI for fraud detection, but institutions report significant barriers to implementation.
The contradiction: Institutions recognise AI’s potential, but data, security and talent constraints complicate its practical deployment.
Confidence in Africa’s financial future is not the same as confidence in operating across its borders. The survey reveals a gap between industry optimism, actual integration progress and the operational capacity needed to connect African markets.
How to read this data
Source: Sixth African Financial Industry Barometer, presented at AFIS 2026 by Deloitte and Jeune Afrique Media Group. The survey gathered responses from financial leaders across 20 African countries.
Confidence: Scores use a 0–10 scale. Institution categories and business segments can overlap.
Growth strategies: Respondents could identify different approaches. Percentages should not be added together.
Integration: AfCFTA, PAPSS and AELP percentages reflect surveyed institutions’ assessments of progress. They are not independent measurements of actual transaction volumes, trade flows or market connectivity.
PAPSS participation: The connected, onboarding and no-plans figures are selected categories, not a complete distribution.
Risks: Increased digital fraud, cybersecurity concerns and AI adoption barriers are different survey measures. They should not be interpreted as equivalent or as proof that fraud alone caused institutions to avoid regional expansion.
Domestic consolidation over cross-border expansion
Rather than deploying capital into regional corridors, financial institutions are prioritising their domestic bases.
When asked about growth strategies, 49% of respondents identified consolidating their existing national markets as their primary objective.
Regional partnerships and alliances followed at 42%, while only 37% favoured organic expansion into other African jurisdictions. Formal cross-border mergers and acquisitions registered 32%, and a quarter of all surveyed institutions stated they have no plans for regional expansion.
Strategic postures reflect distinct operational priorities across sectors. Commercial banks and insurance companies are focusing almost exclusively on domestic consolidation, seeking to avoid unfamiliar legal and counterpart risks abroad.
Fintech operators represent the primary group pursuing organic regional expansion, even as they face the highest incidence of digital fraud. Pan-African banking conglomerates continue to pursue selective acquisitions to defend their established multi-market footprints, while purely local institutions favour bilateral partnerships as a low-capital route beyond their domestic borders.
This divergence in strategy is mirrored in institutional sentiment. Multi-country institutions reported confidence scores of 8.53 out of 10, and regional banking groups gained 0.75 points to reach 8.00.
Capital markets registered the sharpest rise in optimism, increasing from 6.50 to 8.57. Conversely, purely domestic institutions saw their confidence drop to 7.33, while the insurance sector declined by 0.90 points to 7.45.
José Barata, Managing Partner and Banking Sector Lead at Deloitte Angola, noted during the presentation that institutional scale heavily dictates market sentiment.
Barata explained that while confidence remains high among multinational and regional groups with established structures, purely local and national players report lower confidence, indicating that capital allocation decisions require a closer assessment of specific institutions and their operating environments.
Flagship integration projects face an adoption stall
The inward turn of the financial sector is taking a visible toll on continental integration initiatives, including the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), and the African Exchanges Linkage Project (AELP).
Only 7% of respondents reported tangible commercial progress resulting from AfCFTA, with 69% stating that implementation is moving too slowly, and another 24% viewing the agreement as stalled.
The AELP, designed to interconnect stock exchanges across the continent to unlock regional portfolio investments, recorded even weaker sentiment.
Just 4% of respondents reported tangible progress from the linkage project, while 53% described its pace as too slow and 43% considered it at a complete standstill. Fifty-six per cent of respondents reported experiencing no concrete benefits from the platform.
Adoption metrics for PAPSS, the African Union-backed payment network developed to clear intra-African trade in domestic currencies, indicate severe structural friction.
Although 19% of institutions acknowledged tangible operational progress, 57% stated that rollout has been too slow, and 24% considered it stalled.
More critically, 45% of surveyed institutions reported having no plans to connect to PAPSS. Only 11% are actively connected, with an additional 12% currently working through onboarding.
Across the wider survey, 41% of respondents reported deriving no commercial benefits from either AfCFTA or PAPSS.
Lenders attribute this hesitation to unmitigated counterparty liabilities, clearing uncertainties, and an absence of harmonised dispute-resolution systems.
In the absence of regulatory alignment across jurisdictions, cross-border operations must comply with competing anti-money-laundering, customer verification, and capital repatriation rules, thereby driving up administrative costs.
Barata stressed that software and infrastructure cannot bridge this gap without systemic alignment, observing that regional integration requires more than a stated intention to operate across borders.
He emphasised the necessity of interconnected payment networks, practical settlement protocols, stronger regulatory cooperation, and the foundational financial mechanisms required to process cross-border transactions safely.
The $775 billion capital mobilisation gap
The operational retreat is compounding the continent’s internal capital mobilisation shortfall. Citing OECD figures from the African Financial Markets Initiative, the report highlights that African pension funds and insurance firms hold an estimated $775 billion in institutional assets. However, this pool of domestic savings remains largely disconnected from long-term real-economy requirements.
While 64% of respondents are actively engaged in financing small and medium-sized enterprises, 41% reported no involvement in funding affordable housing developments.
Africa has $775 billion in institutional assets. Why isn’t more reaching the real economy?
Africa’s pension funds and insurers hold an estimated $775 billion in assets. But financing for businesses, housing and infrastructure remains constrained. Explore the gap between available institutional capital and its deployment.
This is an estimated stock of institutional assets — not cash sitting idle, and not an amount that could immediately be redirected into new projects.
How can more long-term African savings support productive investment without undermining pension obligations, insurance liabilities or investment risk standards?
The money exists. But it isn’t a single pot.
The $775 billion estimate brings together long-term assets managed by pension and insurance institutions. These investors have different obligations, liquidity needs and investment mandates. Select a category to understand why that matters.
What does $775 billion actually mean?
It describes an estimated asset pool managed by institutions across Africa. The survey does not provide a verified allocation of this total between pensions, insurers, infrastructure, SMEs and housing.
Pension funds invest to meet future retirement obligations. Infrastructure and other long-duration assets may fit some portfolios, but investments must satisfy rules on risk, diversification, liquidity and expected returns.
Insurance portfolios must support claims-paying capacity and regulatory capital requirements. Their investment choices depend on the duration and predictability of liabilities, as well as the risk and liquidity of available assets.
The $775 billion estimate demonstrates the scale of institutional assets. It does not tell us how much is uncommitted, how much is invested outside Africa, or what proportion could safely finance additional domestic and regional projects.
Financial institutions are not equally engaged.
The survey reveals a difference between financial institutions’ participation in SME financing and affordable housing. These figures measure institutional engagement, not the share of the $775 billion allocated to either sector.
Indicates reported institutional engagement, not the volume of SME credit.
Measures non-participation, not the size of the housing finance deficit.
Explore the two financing markets
Select a sector to see why institutional participation does not automatically translate into sufficient financing.
That indicates substantial institutional activity, but it does not reveal how much finance SMEs receive, the terms on which it is offered, or how much unmet demand remains. Lending risk, information gaps and the availability of suitable financing instruments can constrain access.
Housing finance can require long-duration funding and reliable repayment structures. Land administration, project preparation, affordability and credit risk can affect investment viability. The survey’s non-participation figure does not quantify the funding shortfall.
Three ways to make long-term capital more investable
Mobilising institutional assets is not simply a matter of directing funds towards new sectors. Investors need suitable instruments, manageable risks and confidence in how projects are governed. Explore three possible approaches.
Give institutions more suitable assets to buy
Deeper bond markets, investment funds, securitisation structures and infrastructure securities could create more investable opportunities for pension funds and insurers.
The goal is not to force capital into particular projects, but to develop instruments whose risk, maturity, liquidity and returns are compatible with institutional mandates.
Make viable projects less risky to finance
Credit guarantees, first-loss capital, blended-finance structures and development-finance participation can sometimes reduce the risks borne by private investors.
Such mechanisms still have costs and require careful design. They cannot turn fundamentally unviable projects into sustainable investments.
Strengthen the foundations of investment
Reliable financial reporting, transparent procurement, enforceable contracts and credible project governance can improve investors’ ability to assess and manage long-term risks.
Better project preparation and regulatory clarity may help expand the pipeline of opportunities that meet institutional investment standards.
These are potential policy and market mechanisms, not quantified forecasts of how much of the $775 billion they could mobilise.
Having a large pool of institutional assets does not mean having an equally large pool of capital available for new investment. Mobilising more of Africa’s long-term savings requires bankable projects, suitable financial instruments and credible safeguards for investors.
About the data and what it does not show
Source: Sixth African Financial Industry Barometer, AFIS–Deloitte 2026. The survey includes financial institutions across 20 African countries.
Institutional assets: The $775 billion figure is an estimated combined stock of pension and insurance assets. It is not a measure of idle funds or immediately investable capital.
SME financing: The 64% figure represents institutions reporting significant engagement in SME financing. It is not the percentage of institutional assets allocated to SMEs.
Affordable housing: The 41% figure represents institutions reporting no engagement in affordable-housing financing. It is not the proportion of unmet housing-finance demand.
Limitations: The available findings do not quantify how the $775 billion is divided among asset classes, how much is invested abroad, or how much could be redirected into new projects.
Policy options: The final panel describes possible mechanisms for mobilising investment. These are explanatory approaches, not measured outcomes from the survey.
An executive quoted in the barometer observed that Africa does not lack savings but rather lacks sufficient mechanisms to channel them into productive investments at scale.
Barata reinforced this assessment, stating that the primary challenge is not a shortage of capital, but the absence of functional channels through which funds can be directed toward productive enterprise.
He noted that policymakers and institutions must address investment risk, deepen local markets, and build the confidence required to deploy domestic capital into the productive economy.
To unlock this capital, executives surveyed by Deloitte and AFIS recommended three interventions: opening national markets to reciprocal capital flows, mitigating investment risk through guarantees and blended-finance vehicles, and enhancing corporate governance alongside transparent financial reporting.
The report notes that these measures are interdependent and argues that opening markets without mitigating underlying financial risks will fail to attract institutional investors.
Escalating fraud and an acute talent deficit
The worsening operational risk profile presents an immediate obstacle to these reforms. Cybersecurity now ranks as the primary operational threat for 51% of surveyed institutions, rising to 79% among commercial banks and 63% among fintech firms.
Digital fraud was reported to have increased across 66% of the general industry, escalating to 88% among banks and fintech operators.
Barata pointed out a contradiction in how institutions perceive this operational environment. He explained that while approximately two-thirds of institutions surveyed previously identified digital fraud as a substantial risk, many continue to perceive their individual exposure as relatively low.
He warned that as digital service delivery expands, exposure to fraud and cyberattacks increases concurrently.
This security exposure is intensified by a widening skills deficit, with 41% of institutions identifying technical talent shortages as a critical risk, an 11-percentage-point increase year-on-year.
External variables have added to the pressure, with 48% of leaders citing geopolitical instability as an operational risk, up six percentage points, and 41% reporting sustained margin compression due to domestic inflation and currency depreciation.
AI ambitions constrained by infrastructure deficits
To counter rising fraud volumes and streamline verification tasks, financial institutions are turning to artificial intelligence.
Practical interest is concentrated heavily in defensive applications, led by fraud detection at 85% impact recognition, process optimisation at 84%, predictive analytics and business intelligence at 74%, and product personalisation at 69%.
Overall, six of the seven AI use cases evaluated in the survey registered impact recognition above 60%, with only 15% of executives citing the lack of a clear commercial case as an adoption barrier.
The challenge instead lies in institutional infrastructure. Deficiencies in data quality were cited by 56% of respondents as a barrier to AI deployment, matching the 56% who cited cybersecurity and data privacy concerns.
Technical skill deficits were identified by 44%, and regulatory uncertainty was noted by 33%. Barata remarked that the sector has shifted from experimental applications to execution, with executives focused on deploying automated tools in practice to improve credit underwriting, secure operations, and demonstrate operational returns.
The complete AFIS-Deloitte African Financial Industry Barometer is scheduled for full publication between late January and February.
The preliminary findings suggest that waiting for universal regulatory alignment across all 54 African nations is impractical.
The report recommends pursuing practical gains through bilateral regulatory corridors, institutional capacity enhancements, and sector-targeted frameworks, highlighting the insurance industry as an accessible starting point for cross-border alignment.
The underlying requirement for meaningful integration remains operational security. Until national regulators, central banks, and financial institutions build the technical frameworks necessary to curb the surge in cross-border fraud, the continent’s $775 billion in institutional capital reserves will remain confined within domestic borders.

articles.title: FreightTech startup Conlio secures €6.4 million to expand AI-powered financial automation across Europe | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Conlio, a German AI-powered financial operations platform for road freight forwarders, today announces a €6.4 million fundraise to expand across Europe – accelerating the automation of financial systems across freight.
The fundraise was led by Piton Capital, with participation from Haufe Group Ventures and the backing of two logistics groups: WaVe-X (WALTER GROUP), and F-LOG Ventures, the venture investment fund of FIEGE. Existing investors System.One, Puzzle Ventures, Booom Ventures and Yellow also participated in the round. Conlio has raised €6.4 million to date.
Dr. Claudio Consul, Founder and CEO of Conlio, says: “Freight is one of the world’s largest industries, and digitalisation has transformed large parts of it. But the industry is full of edge cases and decisions that depend on context, which has made true end-to-end automation difficult with traditional software. AI changes that.
“At sennder, I saw first-hand how much operational complexity still sits behind freight documentation, settlement and payments. With Conlio, we turn that complexity into verified data and automated financial workflows. Our long-term ambition is to change how money moves across supply chains, and verified freight documents are where this begins.”
Conlio’s fundraise follows a series of European investments in freight software and AI-enabled financial operations during 2026.
In Germany, Hamburg-based Procuros raised €20 million to automate supply-chain data exchange and invoicing, while Berlin-based cargo.one secured nearly €17 million for its multimodal freight platform.
Elsewhere, Ukraine-based Cargofy raised €5.2 million in primary capital for AI-powered freight operations, Belgium’s Vectrix secured €1.15 million for transport-order automation, and Denmark’s Plinto and the UK’s Zalos raised €2.9 million and €3.1 million respectively for AI-enabled financial workflows.
Together, these rounds represent approximately €49.4 million in newly raised funding, excluding Conlio’s investment.
EU-Startups has also previously covered Conlio investor F-LOG Ventures’ participation in Germany’s FRYTE Mobility, which raised €3.5 million in September to expand its electric truck charging coordination platform.
Michael Macklin, Investor at Piton Capital, adds:”Road freight forwarding handles huge volumes of transactions dependent on manual checks, and many people have been stumped on how to fix this. What we liked most about Conlio and Claudio was that they know the problem inside out, from the perspective of their customers, while also having the technologist’s insight on how it can be done differently.
“The product is already embedded in customers’ daily operations and we believe that can build a platform with powerful network effects as more participants join and more transactions flow through it.”
Founded in Berlin in 2023 by Dr Claudio Consul, Conlio uses AI to turn complex freight documents into verified data and automate the financial workflows that follow.
The company explains that European road freight is a roughly €430 billion market, yet freight forwarders operate on thin margins. Conlio can reportedly automate more than 90% of freight document checks, reducing manual processing costs, catching overpayments and accelerating invoicing.
Conlio’s platform can increase a forwarders’ EBIT by up to 30% – more than €1 million in annual EBIT impact for a forwarder with €100 million in revenue.
Every road freight transport generates a trail of documents, from CMRs and proofs of delivery to carrier invoices. Before paying carriers or invoicing customers, forwarders need to check that those documents are complete and correct. But documents arrive in different formats and languages, often contain handwritten notes, and need to be checked against rules that vary by customer, route and geography.
This complexity has historically made the process difficult to automate with traditional software.
Conlio uses AI to read, interpret and verify freight documents at scale, applying context that traditional rules-based software struggles to understand. A single CMR, for example, can carry up to four dates, recording when it was issued, when the goods were collected, when they were delivered and other events during the transport.
The challenge is not reading the date but knowing which event it refers to, and Conlio checks each one against the requirements for that shipment.
Thomas Muscher, Managing Director at WaVe-X, says: “AI is moving from pilot projects into the core processes of freight forwarding, and the finance back office is one of the areas where the impact is most immediate. Conlio turns unstructured freight documents into verified transaction data, which is the foundation for genuinely automated, increasingly agentic workflows. With WALTER GROUP’s decades of experience in European road transport, WaVe-X can support Conlio not only with capital but with real industry insight as it scales across Europe.”

articles.title: Windows 11 Geheimtipp: Rechtsklickmenü in wenigen Minuten aufräumen
articles.text:
Windows 11 Update: So kürzt du endlich dein überladenes Rechtsklickmenü
Da Microsoft die Funktion schrittweise ausrollt, ist sie nach der Installation des optionalen Updates KB5127936 vom Oktober möglicherweise nicht sofort sichtbar. Sie lässt sich mithilfe des kostenlosen Open-Source-Werkzeugs „ViVeTool“ aber in wenigen Minuten aktivieren – und zwar so.
So bekommt ihr das kostenlose Open-Source-Werkzeug „ViVeTool“
Als erstes müsst ihr „Einstellungen“ > „Windows Update“ öffnen und auf „Nach Updates suchen“ klicken. Falls das Update KB5127936 nicht angezeigt wird, aktiviert die Option „Die neuesten Updates erhalten, sobald sie verfügbar sind“ und sucht erneut. Sobald ihr das Update KB5127936 installiert habt, startet ihr den PC neu. Führt auch den Befehl „winver“ aus, um sicherzustellen, dass ihr Build 26200.9818 oder 26300.9818 verwendet.
Dann klickt ihr im Datei-Explorer mit der rechten Maustaste auf eine beliebige Datei. Wenn ihr unten den Eintrag „Menü anpassen“ seht, habt ihr laut windowslatest.com Glück – in diesem Fall benötigt ihr ViVeTool nicht. Falls die Funktion bei euch, wie wohl bei den meisten Nutzer:innen, noch nicht vorhanden ist, müsst ihr ViVeTool von der offiziellen Github-Seite herunterladen. Entpackt die ZIP-Datei dabei so, dass sich die Datei „ViVeTool.exe“ unter „C:\ViVeTool“ befindet.
Zwei Befehle müssen ausgeführt werden
Klickt dann mit der rechten Maustaste auf die Start-Schaltfläche, öffnet das Terminal als Administrator:in und führt nacheinander die folgenden beiden Befehle aus:
cd C:\ViVeTool
vivetool /enable /id:60813048
Wenn die Meldung „Successfully set feature configuration(s)“ erscheint, könnt ihr den PC neu starten und erneut mit der rechten Maustaste auf eine Datei klicken.
Software-Nostalgie: Kennt ihr diese Programme noch?
Statt 25 Einträgen nur noch acht
Das neue Menü enthält am unteren Rand die Schaltfläche „Menü anpassen“, die direkt zu den Einstellungen unter „Personalisierung > Kontextmenü“ führt. Laut Microsoft ist für die Nutzung der Standardkonfiguration kein weiteres Handeln erforderlich. Wer dennoch das alte Menü im Stil von Windows 10 bevorzugt, kann dies weiterhin aufrufen, indem er beim Rechtsklick auf den Desktop oder eine Datei die Umschalttaste gedrückt hält.
Vor dem Update erschienen laut windowslatest.com bei einem Rechtsklick auf eine Bilddatei unterhalb der Symbole für „Ausschneiden“, „Kopieren“, „Umbenennen“, „Freigeben“ und „Löschen“ 20 weitere Einträge. Diese überladen wirkende Systematik könnt ihr dann beispielsweise so anpassen, dass das neue Standardmenü für eine solche Bilddatei nur noch acht Einträge enthält.

articles.title: NATO’s Crossed Swords Exercise Brings AI Agents Into Cyber Operations Training
articles.text:
The NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence (CCDCOE) kicked off Crossed Swords 2026 in Tallinn, Estonia, on Monday, with the exercise’s execution phase set to run through Friday.
More than 250 people from over 40 countries, both NATO members and non-members, are practicing how to plan cyber operations and time them with kinetic military action.
Participants come from national cyber forces and the units supporting them, including military cyber operators, threat hunters, and digital forensics experts. At the command level, the drill sharpens how staff direct both offensive and defensive cyber assets, while hands-on specialists hone their tactical skills. The cyber exercise is also tied into a training event for special operations forces.
“The core operational challenge we are testing is synchronisation. Cyber effects must hit at the right moment to support a kinetic or special operations action – not in parallel, but in sequence, with timing measured in minutes, not hours. This year, that gets harder, because AI is now in the loop on both sides,” said Crossed Swords 2026 Exercise Director Jozef Kostelansky.
New this year is a dedicated track on AI agents, in which participants build, deploy and assess agents and operate side by side with them. The exercise environment runs on locally hosted AI and, in a first for Crossed Swords, also uses OpenAI’s Daybreak cyber defense offering.
“By introducing AI agents into the operational workflow, Crossed Swords 2026 is directly addressing one of the most significant shifts in the modern cyber threat landscape. We are training our participants to harness the power of AI while maintaining the critical human oversight required for complex, multi-domain mission success,” Kostelansky said.
The drill also pairs national cyber forces with civilian partners so that critical infrastructure protection is built into their plans. Over 20 organizations from industry, academia and the NGO sector support the event with know-how, systems to target and specialized tooling. Among them are Bitdefender, ESET, Elastic, Mandiant, OpenAI, Stamus Networks, TryHackMe, and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
Crossed Swords traces its roots to a 2014 red teaming workshop and has since expanded to include command-level training and combined cyber and kinetic operations. Participation has roughly doubled since 2022, when around 120 people from 24 countries took part, and last year’s edition had 240 participants from about 40 nations.
The CCDCOE’s larger Locked Shields exercise involved more than 4,000 participants from 41 nations in 2026.
