articles.title: MediaMarkt adelanta su Black Friday con las nuevas Semanas Black, y estas son sus mejores ofertas en tecnología
articles.text:
Pese a que todavía quedan unas cuantas semanas, y como venimos viendo en los últimos años, algunas tiendas no han querido esperar a la llegada del Black Friday y ya han comenzado a lanzar sus respectivas campañas. MediaMarkt, por ejemplo, ha iniciado las Semanas Black, por lo que en este artículo vamos a repasar cuáles son los chollos de la campaña que finalizará el próximo 10 de noviembre.
- Google Pixel 11 por 854,05 euros al iniciar sesión en la tienda, un móvil pequeño y con buenas cámaras.
- Marshall Stanmore IV por 288 euros, un potente altavoz Bluetooth con diseño retro.
- Samsung TU65M73HAUXXC por 499 euros, un televisor Mini LED con diagonal de 65 pulgadas.
- TP-Link Tapo P100 Mini por 7,99 euros, un enchufe inteligente que se puede controlar desde el móvil.
- Western Digital WD Easystore Desktop por 479 euros, un disco duro de escritorio con capacidad de 18 TB.
TP-Link Tapo P100 Mini
Google Pixel 11
Si queremos comprar un buen móvil, ahora podemos tener en MediaMarkt el Google Pixel 11 por 854,05 euros, precio que sale únicamente al iniciar sesión en la tienda. No obstante, El Corte Inglés lo tiene más barato, ya que la tienda lo ha dejado por un precio de 799,90 euros.
Se trata de un móvil pequeño con pantalla de 6,3 pulgadas, sus cámaras fotográficas están a un buen nivel y además viene con una configuración de 12 GB de RAM y 256 GB de almacenamiento interno. Además, en El Corte Inglés se encuentra al mismo precio en todos sus colores.
Google Pixel 11 (256 GB)
Marshall Stanmore IV
Si de cara a la Navidad queremos amenizar las reuniones con familiares o amigos y buscamos un buen altavoz, MediaMarkt tiene rebajado el Marshall Stanmore IV por 288 euros. Se trata de un altavoz Bluetooth que ofrece una potencia de 60W, tiene un diseño retro muy llamativo y botonera en la parte superior.
Marshall Stanmore IV
Samsung TU65M73HAUXXC
La época del Black Friday también es interesante de cara a renovar el televisor, y MediaMarkt tiene ahora mismo por 499 euros el modelo Samsung TU65M73HAUXXC. Esta tele Mini LED incorpora una pantalla de 65 pulgadas, es compatible con el formato de imagen HDR10+, cuenta con modo Filmmaker y funciona con Alexa.
Samsung TU65M73HAUXXC (65 pulgadas)
TP-Link Tapo P100 Mini
La tienda también tiene de oferta el TP-Link Tapo P100 Mini por 7,99 euros, uno de los mejores precios que hemos visto hasta la fecha. Se trata de un enchufe inteligente que se puede apagar, encender o programar con horarios a través del móvil, estemos o no conectados a la misma red WiFi. Yo personalmente tengo varios conectados a regletas para que no estén encendidos durante la noche.
TP-Link Tapo P100 Mini
Western Digital WD Easystore Desktop
Por último, MediaMarkt también tiene de oferta el Western Digital WD Easystore Desktop por un precio de 479 euros. Se trata de un disco duro de escritorio que destaca tanto por su diseño compacto como por la enorme capacidad de 18 TB, ideal para realizar copias de seguridad con mucha frecuencia o para almacenar muchas fotos, vídeos y archivos.
También está de oferta el mismo modelo, pero con capacidad de 12 TB, por un precio de 349 euros.
Western Digital WD Easystore Desktop (18 TB)

articles.title: Un grupo anónimo anunció que publicará más de 150 direcciones de multimillonarios, empezando por Elon Musk
articles.text:
Un grupo activista clandestino que se hace llamar Capytistas anunció que publicará, en una campaña por etapas contra lo que llama la “oligarquía estadounidense”, más de 150 direcciones de domicilios de multimillonarios. La primera entrega, prevista para este mes, se centrará en Elon Musk, su hermano Kimbal y el directorio de Tesla, según Wired.
Dos integrantes hablaron con la revista bajo condición de anonimato. Dijeron que dedicaron el último año a armar expedientes sobre multimillonarios, un billonario en dólares y sus principales colaboradores, con métodos propios de un investigador privado y, según admitieron, algunos que no lo son.
En un comunicado difundido el lunes 2 de noviembre de 2026, el grupo afirma que sus próximas entregas incluirán más de 150 direcciones, la mayoría no divulgadas antes, y más de 3.500 registros sobre personas con una fortuna conjunta de unos USD 1,4 billones. Promete material sobre presuntos “delitos y fallas de seguridad”.
Los Capytistas aseguran haber recaudado más de USD 1,2 millones de donantes ricos a quienes llaman “traidores de clase”, según su comunicado.
Qué contiene el expediente
El expediente contiene 32 direcciones vinculadas con el empresario Elon Musk y sus ejecutivos, que figura como “objetivo primario”. La presidenta del directorio de Tesla, Robyn Denholm, y Kimbal Musk aparecen entre los “secundarios”. Cada perfil combina una biografía crítica, basada en fallos judiciales y registros públicos, con una dirección.
Los inversores, entre ellos Vanguard y BlackRock y cerca de 40 proveedores integran el tercer nivel. De ellos solo se listan oficinas, fábricas o minas, no domicilios. La oficina de prensa y el área de relaciones con inversores de Tesla no respondieron a las consultas de la revista.
Los activistas explicaron que obtienen los datos sobre todo de registros de propiedad, expedientes judiciales y de las sociedades y fideicomisos que usan los ricos para comprar inmuebles. Recurren con menos frecuencia, dijeron, a vigilancia física, infiltración y datos de ubicación que se compran y venden en el mercado publicitario en línea.
Admiten que lo suyo es doxing, es decir, difundir datos privados de una persona para exponerla.
Musk fue elegido primero, según los voceros, porque ningún otro personaje concentra tanto enojo público. Dijeron que su expediente es de los más breves y que lo consideran uno de los objetivos “menos importantes”. Lo usarán como puerta de entrada para dirigir ese malestar hacia otros magnates.
Protestas frente a las casas y antecedentes de violencia
El grupo busca que los afectados sientan que alguien los vigila y espera que el público proteste frente a sus viviendas y en campos de golf. Según su comunicado, la exposición pública servirá como “salida” para evitar “resultados violentos y trágicos”. Un integrante citó el asesinato del director ejecutivo de UnitedHealthcare, Brian Thompson, en diciembre de 2024.
La ira contra Musk ya tuvo consecuencias materiales. Un boletín conjunto del FBI y el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional, obtenido por ley de acceso a la información, registró ataques contra vehículos y concesionarias de Tesla en al menos nueve estados de Estados Unidos en 2025.
En abril de 2026, la policía de San Francisco arrestó a un hombre de 20 años acusado de lanzar un artefacto incendiario contra la casa del director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman. Nadie resultó herido.
El mismo reportaje menciona otros casos de difusión de datos. Hace una semana, hackers publicaron nombres y contactos laborales de más de 40.000 empleados y contratistas del Departamento de Seguridad Nacional. Los Capytistas dicen que quieren dar a los magnates “una muestra de las invasiones de privacidad” que, afirman, estos cometen y rentabilizan.
El grupo no precisó la fecha exacta de la primera publicación. El medio dijo que será este mes de noviembre.

articles.title: Police seizes over 100 servers in investment scam crackdown
articles.text:
European law enforcement authorities arrested seven suspects and seized more than 100 servers in a joint action targeting an unnamed company suspected of providing fraudulent trading websites to criminal gangs.
Supported by Europol and Eurojust, this coordinated international action involved authorities from Albania, Cyprus, Finland, Germany, Kosovo, and North Macedonia and followed four years of investigation and earlier interventions in 2022 and 2025.
The investigation began in 2022 after a German couple reported they couldn't withdraw money invested through an online trading platform, leading investigators to link multiple call center operators behind investment scams to potential victims in at least 50 countries.
"The action follows four years of investigation and earlier interventions in 2022 and 2025. Evidence gathered during those operations led to the company allegedly operating the 'crime-as-a-service' model from Cyprus and Israel. Investigators also identified suspected clients operating fraudulent call centres in Albania, Kosovo* and North Macedonia," Europol said.
The scheme promised potential victims substantial, quick returns from trading in foreign currencies, stocks, or cryptocurrency, using deceptive advertisements to direct them to fraudulent investment platforms and steal their personal data. They later sold this stolen data to criminal groups running call centers, whose operators reached out with supposed investment opportunities.
They encouraged victims to transfer a small amount and showed them fake online accounts with fictitious profits, making the platforms seem credible. These gains were used to sustain psychological pressure to push the victims into larger transfers. However, when they asked to withdraw the money, the scammers used delaying tactics and eventually stopped contact, leaving victims with no way to recover their funds.
"A first international action day that year resulted in two arrests and the seizure of evidence. Europol-supported analysis helped investigators develop the case, which identified seven additional suspects, including suspected call centre managers," Europol added.
This is the latest in a series of similar criminal rings dismantled by European law enforcement in recent years, including the March 2022 shutdown of a massive call-center investment fraud network that used 200 "traders" to steal at least €3 million each month.
Police also took down multiple call centers across Europe in 2023, linked to millions of euros in losses and run by a criminal gang behind online investment fraud (also known as 'pig butchering' or romance baiting scams). European police also shut down 12 fraud call centers in May 2024 that were linked to thousands of daily scam calls.
In July 2025, Spanish police dismantled another massive crypto investment fraud ring that laundered over €460 million($540 million) stolen from over 5,000 victims worldwide, one week after taking apart a large-scale investment scam operation behind cumulative damages exceeding €10 million ($11.8 million).
More recently, in April, Austrian and Albanian authorities also took down a criminal organization that ran a large-scale cryptocurrency investment fraud operation linked to estimated losses of over €50 million ($58.5 million).

articles.title: Why South Africa's AGOA fallout threatens its startups
articles.text:
South Africa’s planned removal from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) won’t only affect exporters, but also raise questions about how the country’s worsening relations with the United States (US) might affect investment into its technology sector.
While AGOA is a trade preference programme covering goods exports, the fallout from the decision could reach businesses that have little direct exposure to the programme. For South African startups, one concern is whether deteriorating diplomatic and trade relations could influence the appetite of American venture capital investors.
US venture capital firms are among the international investors backing African startups, with the United States remaining the continent’s largest source of foreign venture investors in 2024, according to the African Private Capital Association (AVCA), a trade body for African investors.
In 2022, South African gaming startup Carry1st raised a $20 million Series A extension led by US venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz.
Jeff Miller, chief executive (CEO) of Grovest Investment Holdings, a South African investment and venture capital firm, warned that the diplomatic fallout could make US investors more cautious about backing South African startups, even without any direct restrictions on technology investment.
“My assessment is that the first effect would likely be greater selectivity and slower decisions, as a result of negative sentiment that the withdrawal of AGOA brings with it,” he told TechCabal in an interview on Tuesday.
Miller said foreign investors weigh a country’s political landscape, capital flows, rule of law, red tape and tax implications. He believes Black Economic Empowerment (B-BBEE) requirements can also present challenges.
“Uncertainty about these pathways can make an otherwise attractive investment harder to approve,” he said.
He cautioned that worsening relations with Washington could add to the risks American investors associate with South Africa. Negative sentiment in the US could also affect international investor confidence, potentially influencing investors from other markets.
The warning comes after US President Donald Trump notified Congress and the governments of South Africa and Rwanda of his intention to terminate their AGOA eligibility from January 1, 2027. The notification, announced on November 2, gives the countries 60 days’ advance notice of the planned withdrawal.
In a statement, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the Trump administration was concerned about “barriers to U.S. trade and investment, corruption, and threats to US national security and foreign policy interests.”
The statement said an annual interagency review had found practices by South Africa and Rwanda inconsistent with AGOA’s eligibility criteria. It did not announce restrictions on venture capital, technology partnerships, or digital services.
AGOA provides eligible sub-Saharan African countries with preferential access to the US market for thousands of products. Its withdrawal directly affects trade in goods, not the flow of venture capital into technology companies. Any effect on startup funding would be indirect, through the broader investment climate and how investors interpret the diplomatic fallout.
South Africa’s automotive industry is among the sectors most exposed to the loss of AGOA benefits. TechCabal reported in February that vehicles and automotive components accounted for more than half of the country’s $4 billion in AGOA-qualifying exports to the US in 2024, generating about $1.6 billion in export revenue.
The sector was already under pressure from US tariffs, with the uncertainty around AGOA threatening export competitiveness and long-term investment planning. South Africa’s Department of Trade, Industry and Competition says the country’s wider economic relationship with the US remains significant.
According to the Department, 89% of South African exports to the US entered under ordinary World Trade Organization most-favoured-nation terms in 2025, while about 10% entered under AGOA. The value of AGOA exports fell from $4 billion in 2024 to $1.7 billion in 2025, representing about 1% of South Africa’s total global exports.
Bilateral trade reached $28.8 billion in 2025, while more than 600 American companies operate in South Africa, supporting approximately 134,600 jobs.
Parks Tau, South Africa’s Trade, Industry and Competition Minister, sought to separate the AGOA decision from the wider economic and diplomatic ties between the two countries.
“This decision does not define the broader relationship between South Africa and the United States, however a solution depends on the willingness of both Parties to find solutions,” he said in the same statement on Tuesday.
The government said it will continue pursuing US trade and investment while diversifying export markets through the African Continental Free Trade Area, the European Union, the United Kingdom and Asia.
For South African startups, however, finding alternative sources of capital may be more difficult than diversifying export destinations. Miller said the US venture capital market has substantial capital and a greater appetite for risk than other markets, making it an important source of funding for companies seeking to scale.
“Whilst a good business should always find funding, the US market is a low-hanging fruit,” he stated.

articles.title: “Je veux leur offrir une meilleure fin” : Johnny Depp prêt à revenir dans Pirates des Caraïbes 6
articles.text:
“Je veux leur offrir une meilleure fin” : Johnny Depp prêt à revenir dans Pirates des Caraïbes 6
L'acteur a confirmé qu'il serait partant pour remettre le tricorne de Jack Sparrow dans la franchise Pirates des Caraïbes, mais à une seule et unique condition.
Près d'une décennie après la sortie de son dernier volet en date, Pirates des Caraïbes n'a jamais été aussi proche de revenir sur grand écran... et peut-être bien avec Jack Sparrow à la barre. C'est en tous cas ce qu'a laissé entendre l'acteur Johnny Depp, confirmant les plans de reboot de la franchise dans les tuyaux de Disney depuis des années.
Le retour du capitaine Jack Sparrow ?
En pleine promotion de son prochain film Scrooge (en salles le 11 novembre), Depp en a profité pour répondre à la question de nos confrères américains d'Entertainment Tonight sur la possibilité d'un retour de Jack Sparrow dans un Pirates des Caraïbes 6 :
"Je suis prêt à travailler avec Jerry Bruckheimer (producteur de la franchise Pirates des Caraïbes, ndlr) dès demain. Peu importe ce que c'est, s'il s'agit de Jerry, je lui fais confinace. Nous avons une amitié profonde".
Il poursuit : "Si tout est parfaitement en place pour conclure en beauté la franchise Pirates des Caraïbes... La seule chose que je souhaite vraiment, au fond, c'est de leur offrir une meilleure fin".
- Regardez l'interview d'Entertainment Tonight :
On peut comprendre la volonté de Johnny Depp de revenir pour corriger le tir tant le cinquième film - Pirates des Caraïbes : La Vengeance de Salazar - avait reçu un très mauvais accueil critique à sa sortie en 2017, et est souvent considéré par le public comme l'opus le plus faible de la saga.
En 2024, Jerry Bruckheimer confirmait que le scénariste Jeff Nathanson (Le Roi Lion version 2019, Arrête-moi si tu peux) était en train de terminer le script de ce Pirates des Caraïbes 6, et se montrait particulièrement enthousiaste : "nous avons encore besoin de peaufiner les première et seconde parties, mais il a écrit un troisième acte vraiment génial."
Si rien n'a encore été officialisé, ces différentes déclarations laissent donc penser que ce n'est qu'une question de temps avant que la franchise de pirates repartent en mer. Et ce n'est pas étonnant : avec 4,5 milliards de dollars générés au box-office mondial en cinq longs-métrages, c'est l'un des joyaux de la couronne de Disney, qui compte bien en faire quelque chose.
Outre ce potentiel Pirates des Caraïbes 6 avec Jack Sparrow, un autre reboot a longtemps été en développement avec Margot Robbie en tête d'affiche. Mais le projet a été mis en pause, sans aucun signe de vie depuis plusieurs années.
L'intégralité de la franchise Pirates des Caraïbes est disponible en streaming sur la plateforme Disney+.

articles.title: OPINION: Healthcare’s pilot culture is holding back HealthTech innovation | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Across Europe, HealthTech companies are developing new technologies that can improve patient care, ease pressure on clinicians and help health services make better use of limited resources. But while these technologies are often successful in getting into hospitals in the pilot phase, many struggle to move beyond that and secure long term adoption.
This is not a new problem. Companies working with large public healthcare organisations, like the UK’s National Health Service (NHS) or Ireland’s Health Service Executive (HSE), are familiar with the issues surrounding new technology implementation. These organisations work at a considerable scale with complex responsibilities and obligations around patient safety and public spending. In short, widespread implementation of new technology, no matter how innovative, can often be met with hesitancy.
And while the caution is understandable, with so many companies unable to get out of the pilot phase, it raises the question of whether processes are designed to welcome innovation or whether they are designed to keep healthcare stuck in its ways.
The problem with pilot culture
Pilots play an important role in healthcare innovation. They allow clinicians to assess whether a technology works in practice, from how patients respond to identifying changes needed before wider implementation. They are the first step to mass adoption of new technologies, but far too frequently, they are also the last step.
Wider adoption of successful pilots can run into issues on many fronts: Who owns the budget needed to buy the technology? Which team is responsible for implementation? How will the technology work with existing systems? Who provides training and support?
These are all questions that should be obvious but are often addressed far too late and end up stopping adoption in its tracks.
Another issue is the fact that the clinicians who champion pilots are often the people most willing to experiment; some can even be evangelistic about new technologies. However, their colleagues may not have the same priorities or passions and so a technology that works well in one department can struggle to get buy-in from the key stakeholders across other departments.
Procurement can favour the familiar
Procurement is another point where promising HealthTech companies can encounter difficulties.
Healthcare procurement carries the huge responsibility of spending public money, meaning they need to find suppliers that are financially sound with products that must meet the appropriate clinical, technical, and regulatory requirements. They need to have complete confidence in what they’re choosing.
A young, unestablished HealthTech company may not garner that confidence, no matter how effective the solution they have developed is. Young companies are also up against it when it comes to meeting the requirements set out by procurement, which are often designed around suppliers with years of experience securing public-sector contracts.
This creates a difficult cycle where a company needs a contract to build its track record, but needs a track record to secure the contract.
Not to mention the fact that procurement’s decisions can often focus mainly on price, so a technology that carries a high immediate cost may struggle to secure approval.
The result of these issues can be an unintended preference for established suppliers, even when a smaller company has a better approach to a clinical problem.
When caution becomes culture
Similar to the case with procurement, healthcare providers have to make sure that what they are offering the public is backed by an incredibly high standard of evidence and accountability. This can create a culture that puts caution ahead of good clinical outcomes and this can actually create risks of its own, as delaying the adoption of useful technology as a result of being overly cautious can have negative consequences for patients, clinicians and public finances not to mention the commercial consequence for Europe.
HealthTech startups need to generate revenue, build a sustainable business and invest in further development. If the route from pilot to procurement remains unpredictable, companies may struggle to plan their growth or attract the investment required to expand.
For many it may push them to look to markets where purchasing decisions are more straightforward, meaning healthcare organisations risk losing access to innovations developed close to home, while European companies lose opportunities to build global businesses from their early clinical successes.
Build the route to scale from day one
There are practical steps healthcare systems can take to improve the path from pilot to adoption.
First, the people responsible for implementation and procurement should be involved early. An enthusiastic clinician on-side is valuable, but a pilot also needs buy-in from finance, IT, operations, procurement and those who will support the technology after launch. They can’t be overlooked.
Second, pilots should be designed with scale in mind. Before a trial begins, the organisation and supplier should agree what success looks like, which outcomes will be measured and what evidence would justify wider deployment. They should also consider training, integration, support costs and the effect on existing workflows.
Third, procurement requirements should better balance risk, costs and the long-term benefits of proposed technology. And the evidence new healthcare companies are required to give should be proportionate to the contract and the potential consequences of failure. The size and the experience of the company should not determine the outcome if the solution they are offering is genuinely helpful to clinicians and/or patients.
Finally, healthcare organisations should learn from their own pilots. Sharing results, including unsuccessful projects and the reasons behind them, can reduce duplication and help other teams make better decisions when it comes to their own pilots. Working in silos doesn’t help anyone.
Innovation needs a destination
The NHS has previously recognised the importance of tackling the problems with pilot culture through innovation guidelines, which help innovators navigate the routes towards wider use.
In Ireland, the HSE’s Framework for Health Innovation was also introduced this year with the explicit aim of creating a more consistent pathway from local ideas and pilots to lasting impact across the health system.
These initiatives point towards the same underlying need: successful experiments must have a realistic route into everyday healthcare.
Europe has the talent and entrepreneurial ambition to build world-class HealthTech companies. Giving those companies a credible route from evidence to adoption will help ensure their innovations have the opportunity to make a meaningful difference.

articles.title: Ein Stück Mars in der Sahara: Was uns dieser 4,1 Milliarden Jahre alte Stein verrät
articles.text:
In der Sahara gefunden: Was ein 4,1 Milliarden Jahre alter Mars-Meteorit über den roten Planeten verrät
Meteoritenbruchstücke, die irgendwo auf der Erde landen, können beeindruckende Zeugen der Vergangenheit unseres Sonnensystems sein – das zeigt sich jetzt gerade wieder an „Teghaza 001“. Verschiedene Analysen ergaben, dass der unscheinbare Stein vom Mars stammt und mindestens 4,1 Milliarden Jahre alt ist. Und: Der Meteorit enthält Hinweise auf ein Wasservorkommen auf dem Mars.
Die Ergebnisse der gemeinsamen Untersuchung des Meteoriten durch die University of New Mexico, das Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), das Caltech und die UCLA wurden jetzt in der Fachzeitschrift Science veröffentlicht.
Ähnlichkeit mit „Black Beauty“: Warum der Meteorit Forscher überraschte
Zunächst war es der Wissenschaftler Carl Agee vom Institut für Meteoritenkunde der University of New Mexico, der auf die Besonderheiten des Meteoriten aufmerksam wurde. In seiner Analyse von Proben des Marsmeteoriten entdeckte Agee „ungewöhnliche Merkmale in Textur, Mineralogie und Zusammensetzung, die bei Marsmeteoriten unüblich sind.“
Unüblich, aber nicht unbekannt. Stattdessen erinnerte Agee die Zusammensetzung an „Black Beauty“, den ersten Meteoriten, der der Kruste des Mars zugeschrieben werden konnte.
„Mir fiel auf, dass dieser Meteorit Black Beauty ein wenig ähnelte, nicht genau, aber die Sauerstoffisotopenwerte wiesen Ähnlichkeiten auf“, so Agee gegenüber phys.org. „Ich untersuchte ihn mikroskopisch und fand Bereiche mit hohen Konzentrationen an Manganoxid, einer Verbindung, nach der die Rover auf dem Mars suchen, da sie als Indikator für lebensfreundliche Umgebungen gilt.“
Manganoxid-Funde: Hinweise auf Wasser und mögliches Leben auf dem Mars
Manganoxid gilt für viele Wissenschaftler:innen als ein häufiges Nebenprodukt mikrobiellen Lebens. Auch die ungewöhnliche Sauerstoffisotopen-Zusammensetzung und veränderte Mineralien fielen den Wissenschaftler:innen als bemerkenswert auf. Laut Agee zeichnen sie ein ganz anderes Bild vom Mars als das, das wir heute kennen.
„Diese Probe stammt wahrscheinlich aus einer Umgebung auf dem Mars, die der Erde ähnlicher war“, sagt der Wissenschaftler. Dabei spricht er von Oberflächenwasser, einer dichteren Atmosphäre und möglicherweise sogar einem schützenden Magnetfeld, das vor Strahlung aus dem All schützte. Das ist zwar alles noch kein Beweis für einstiges Leben auf dem Mars, hilft aber, die Geschichte unseres Nachbarplaneten besser zu verstehen.
4,1 Milliarden Jahre alt: So wurde Teghaza 001 datiert
Aufgrund der besonderen Beschaffenheit des Meteoriten holten Agee und sein Team schließlich weitere Wissenschaftler:innen und Institute ins Boot. Dabei wurden Zirkonkristalle in dem Meteoritengestein entdeckt, die per Uran-Blei-Methode zur Altersbestimmung genutzt werden konnten. Und das Ergebnis beeindruckt: Teghaza 001 ist rund 4,1 Milliarden Jahre alt. Laut Agee ist er damit der älteste bekannte Mars-Meteorit aus Lava-Gestein überhaupt.
Doch nicht nur die Superlative beeindruckt, auch die Bedeutung dahinter: Der Meteorit stammt aus der Frühphase des Mars, dem sogenannten Prä-Noachium. „Wenn primitives Leben auf dem Mars weit verbreitet war, dann ist dies der wahrscheinlichste Zeitpunkt dafür“, ordnet Agee ein. Und die Analysen stützten diese frühere Einschätzung.
Anders als andere Mars-Meteoriten: Aus welcher Region stammt Teghaza 001?
Weil sich Teghaza 001 chemisch und mineralogisch deutlich von anderen Mars-Meteoriten unterscheidet, dürfte er aus einer Region stammen, die bisher kein Rover erreicht hat. Mit Fernerkundungsdaten konnte das Team die Suche immerhin eingrenzen: Die Mineralogie passt zu den südlichen Hochländern des Mars, möglicherweise Richtung Hellas-Becken, sagt Yang Liu vom JPL der Nasa.
Künftige Marsmissionen könnten also diese Region ins Auge fassen, um weitere, ähnlich aufschlussreiche Proben zu finden.

articles.title: Over 100 European Stores Hit as Supermarket Fridge Attacks Return
articles.text:
More than 100 stores in several European countries saw their fridges and freezers heat up overnight from Sunday to Monday, and several retailers have blamed a cyberattack. The incidents closely resemble the attacks that disrupted European supermarkets three weeks ago.
The affected businesses, ranging from major chains to small butcher shops, are in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden. Some units were set as high as 50°C (122°F), and problems have also been reported in Finland, Italy and Portugal.
Nobody has taken responsibility for the attacks. Investigators have not established whether the two waves are connected.
The first wave hit France overnight from October 11 to 12. Around 700 supermarkets had their refrigeration units forced into defrost mode, including Intermarché, Carrefour, Coopérative U and Monoprix stores. Food was spoiled, and the attacks reportedly caused fires.
CERT-FR, the incident response team of France’s cybersecurity agency ANSSI, initially linked the compromises to Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC series controllers. A day later, it expanded its alert to cover Copeland and Dixell XWEB systems. Danfoss said most of the hacked units were legacy products it no longer updated.
Exposed Danfoss, Copeland controllers hijacked in new attacks
The technique appears to be the same. Stephan Moelans, CEO of Belgian refrigeration firm Sabcobel, told the Belga news agency that the attackers forced the units’ evaporators into defrost mode, as happened in France.
According to Moelans, a software update is not enough to fully resolve the weakness, and the affected equipment also needs to be physically modified.
Dutch broadcaster NOS reported that, as far as is known, the targeted devices were made by Danfoss and Copeland. An Estonian refrigeration supplier said the units attacked there were older Danfoss models.
Danfoss said that on October 13 it had told its customers to cut their systems’ internet connections and to reconnect only through a secure network. “Most stores took action at that time, but a small number did not,” a company spokesperson told NOS.
Security researcher Kevin Beaumont said people he spoke with had confirmed that every freezer hit on Monday had a management interface reachable from the internet. According to Beaumont, many of the devices are end-of-life and have no available patch.
Officials have not publicly explained how the attackers got in.
Deception security firm Lupovis told SecurityWeek that, between October 20 and 30, it saw suspicious activity aimed at its Danfoss AK-SM refrigeration controller sensors, including sensors in some of the affected regions. Most of the login attempts relied on factory-default credentials that Danfoss documents publicly, while others appeared to be trying to fingerprint specific Danfoss controller components.
“The activity peaked on 26 October, and importantly, we had not observed this behaviour on these sensors before 20 October. All authentication attempts were rejected by our sensors,” said Lupovis CEO Xavier Bellekens, adding that the timing is noteworthy.
Censys has found just over 1,000 Danfoss StoreView interfaces reachable online worldwide. “France continues to lead Danfoss StoreView exposures globally, followed by Belgium and the US,” the internet intelligence firm said.
The number of exposed StoreView instances in France has fallen sharply, from 1,825 before the October attacks to 220 at the time of Censys’ latest analysis.
By matching firmware build dates, Censys estimates that 41% of the French instances still online run a patched version. It counted 138 exposed instances in Belgium, 51 in the Netherlands and 50 in Sweden, of which 68%, 37% and 58%, respectively, appear to be patched.
Only a handful of exposed instances were seen in Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia. Censys did not indicate whether any patched devices were among those compromised on Monday.
Belgium among hardest hit
Belgium appears to have taken the biggest hit. Delhaize said an IT incident disrupted refrigeration at several dozen of its stores, Carrefour counted 15 affected locations out of more than 700, and Colruyt said five franchised Spar shops were attacked.
An IKEA store in Mons was hit as well, and the Belgian federal prosecutor’s office has opened an investigation.
In Luxembourg, four Delhaize outlets were affected. In Ireland, SuperValu pulled chilled and frozen products from 13 stores where one specific refrigeration model was impacted.
Swedish grocer ICA confirmed that a limited number of its stores were impacted, while Coop reported problems at a handful of locations. An ICA store manager said they had to throw out significant amounts of food.
In the Netherlands, Danfoss said the systems of at least 17 businesses were hit, mainly butcher shops and small grocers.
Finnish retailer Kesko said a few of its smaller stores had temperature disruptions. In Italy, the operator of several Coop-branded supermarkets in Sicily alerted the national cybersecurity agency, and in Portugal, the Mosqueteiros group confirmed incidents at seven Intermarché stores.
EU agriculture commissioner Christophe Hansen called the attacks a deliberate bid to disrupt the food supply chain and erode consumer trust. “The repeated occurrence of these cyberattacks is deeply concerning,” he said.
Hansen said the bloc’s food security is not under threat for now, but he acknowledged the food that had to be thrown away and the harm to businesses.

articles.title: Here’s what it’s like to use Audio Intelligence on the Apple Watch
articles.text:
It’s impossible to paint a full picture of what Audio Intelligence on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 will be right now. The watchOS 27.3 developer beta just dropped earlier this afternoon, and these features are meant to be lived with in day-to-day life. We’re definitely going to do that over the next few weeks at The Verge. That said, here are some initial impressions.
Here’s what it’s like to use Audio Intelligence on the Apple Watch
The watchOS 27.3 beta adds Live Rewind and Siri Recap to the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
What’s newly available today is Live Rewind and Siri Recap. The former lets you see a transcript of the last 15 seconds, while the latter provides high-level summaries of your conversations. (The other two Audio Intelligence features have been available for the last few weeks. I wrote about those in my Series 12 review.) And as always, this is the developer beta. These features could still change quite a bit before a final version arrives for the public.
The first thing I noticed is that these features are not turned on by default. I wasn’t expecting anything different, but it’s worth remembering that these features don’t automatically turn every Apple Watch into a surveillance device. Audio Intelligence requires the latest Apple Watch hardware, a compatible version of iOS (so in this case, the iOS 27.3 developer beta), and someone has to actively choose to enable these features. You can download the beta and double-press the crown to initiate a Live Rewind. It won’t do anything. You must opt in via your iPhone’s Watch app. Same goes for Siri Recap. Enabling Live Rewind also requires an initial microphone calibration with your phone.
Privacy-wise, Apple has publicly available support documentation about its approach to these features. I’m not weighing in on how well it executes them in this hands-on. But Apple has pretty clear messaging in the onboarding process. There are quite a few customization options for when Siri Recap is active. You can get pretty granular. For example, you can have Siri Recap on only at the office during weekdays from 1PM to 4PM if that’s when you have meetings. This is hard to convey to bystanders, and I think ethical use should come with an in-person heads-up to the people you frequently interact with. (Hello, fellow Verge writers and editors.)
Live Rewind, so far, has worked as described — with the heavy caveat that I’ve only tested it in my quiet home office with my spouse. Even so, it takes a hot second to learn the timing of a double press. My spouse noticed the audible chime signaling the feature is in use, though they didn’t notice the animation. I’ll have to see how this fares in louder environments. Siri accurately captured our attempts to get my cat to roll over, though in subsequent tests, it misheard a word or two.
I’m more hesitant to comment on Siri Recap. It’s not just because I haven’t had many organic, lengthy spoken conversations yet since downloading the beta. (Siri did not deem my brief conversation with my spouse as worthy enough for recapping.) But I won’t really get a sense for how this feature feels until I’ve tested it in a wide variety of scenarios. Will it work if I talk to myself aloud? How well does it filter out gossip? How will this change how people speak to me? That’ll be the true test of this feature and Apple’s bystander privacy claims.
My first Siri Recap was for an editorial planning meeting for a story I’m working on. It was decent at identifying different topics discussed, and I was impressed that it stripped out some sensitive information. Any outsider looking at these notes would be terribly confused. Ironically, it meant that this summary wasn’t the most useful for my job.
What I will say is that I’ve been testing the Amazon Bee Frontier for the past few weeks. In the little time I’ve spent with the watchOS 27.3 beta, the differences between Audio Intelligence and the Bee are very clear. The latter has more of what I’d call an AI-forward presence. Bee, for example, offers insights about the emotional tone of a conversation. I’ve also found that the AI can be a bit judgy about insights and takeaways. Live Rewind is just a straight transcript. Apple’s said publicly that Siri Recap is meant to be highly factual notes to jog a person’s memory. That rings true based on my first one. And, as far as I can tell, there is no commerce angle for Siri Recaps, whereas Bee has an Amazon integration that surfaces buying suggestions based on conversations.
In any case, I’ll be diving deep into these features in the days to come. Let us know in the comments what you’re most curious about.

articles.title: New York City's Mamdani criticizes Madison Square Garden owner over surveillance tech | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Mayor of New York City Zohran Mamdani has criticized the owner of Madison Square Garden, one of the city’s largest entertainment venues, arguing that the company’s surveillance technology should not be allowed.
Mamdani told Wired in an interview on Tuesday that surveillance technologies are “indicative of much that is wrong in our country today.” He added that City Council member Shahana Hanif introduced two pieces of local legislation aimed at banning the collection of biometric data, such as using facial recognition, in public places across the city. Mamdani said that the draft legislation is “an important response to this kind of an issue.”
The comments come after a stream of reporting from Wired detailing how Madison Square Garden’s owner James Dolan relies on surveillance cameras and face-scanning technology to track people across and outside of its venues.
In one report, Wired revealed that Dolan’s company keeps a database that, among other things, marks some visitors, including celebrity performers, as “LGBTQIA,” for reasons that are unclear. Dolan subsequently sued Wired over its reporting.
In 2021, MSG made headlines after a woman was banned from Radio City, another Dolan-owned venue, after being recognized by facial recognition systems as an attorney at a law firm who was suing Dolan’s company but was not involved in the litigation.
When reached by TechCrunch, Madison Square Garden spokesperson Mikyl Cordova said: “Wired’s reporting is inaccurate and false. MSG is pursuing legal remedies,” without providing evidence for its claim.
Since 2021, New York City has required businesses to disclose when they are collecting biometric data from visitors.
Updated with comment from MSG.

articles.title: Shopify posts $462-million USD net income, but stock falls on narrow Q3 revenue miss | BetaKit
articles.text:
Shopify’s third-quarter revenue numbers didn’t satisfy all analysts this morning as the e-commerce company’s stock fell by roughly nine percent, before rebounding slightly.
The Ottawa-based e-commerce giant posted revenue growth of 32 percent year-over-year on Tuesday, in line with internal estimates, as it accelerated its embrace of agentic online shopping tools. But its revenue of $3.74 billion USD ($5.23 billion CAD) for the quarter missed analyst expectations, which ranged from $3.75 billion to $3.77 billion. According to Bloomberg, it was Shopify’s first revenue miss in four years.
Shopify’s online merchants brought in $119 billion USD in gross merchandise volume this quarter, a 29-percent increase from last year but slightly less than what analysts were expecting.
Shopify’s online merchants brought in $119 billion USD in gross merchandise volume (GMV) this quarter, a 29-percent increase from last year but slightly less than what analysts were expecting, Barron’s reported.
Shopify’s TSX close on Monday was at $220 CAD, roughly flat on the year; by 11:30 a.m. ET on Tuesday, it was trading around $200 CAD. After this morning’s earnings kicked off a rough pre-trading session, Shopify shares on both the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX) and the Nasdaq fell by nine percent when markets opened, but they have since ticked back up to an intraday loss of four percent (about the same on the year). This came amid a broader tech selloff fuelled by concerns around AI trading that began in late October and pushed tech-heavy indexes like the Nasdaq down by more than two percent last week.
On an earnings call Tuesday morning, Shopify president Harley Finkelstein emphasized the company’s reliable growth. “We delivered exactly what we said we would,” he said. “Consistent, durable growth yet again.”
Shopify fared better on profitability metrics. It posted earnings per share of $0.49 USD, exceeding analyst projections, and $462 million in net income in the three months before Sept. 30 (75 percent higher than last year), including a $122-million paper loss on its equity investments.
The company also reported a free cash flow margin of 22 percent this quarter, which CFO Jeff Hoffmeister attributed to “multiple growth drivers” and an “expanding addressable market.”
Thanos Moschopoulos, an analyst at BMO Capital Markets, said Shopify has sustained a very strong growth rate. Markets were likely responding to the softer GMV and slight revenue miss, which is “unusual” for the e-commerce company.
“If we look at the quarter and guide in an absolute sense, the business is showing sustained momentum across their key growth vectors,” Moschopoulos wrote to BetaKit in an email, “with some early indication that agentic commerce is driving incremental, high-conversion traffic to their merchants, and that [AI assistant] Sidekick is helping their merchants become more successful.”
Agentic firsts
Canada’s largest tech company has embraced AI, both mandating its use internally and building features for agentic commerce, where chatbot and agent interfaces function as “storefronts” for customer purchases.
Finkelstein said this quarter was the “first time we saw shoppers experimenting with delegated purchasing through personal agents” that can make purchases on users’ behalf. Since Meta released its consumer AI agent, Muse, in September, interest in consumer AI agents has risen, and Shopify has leaned in to connect them to its shopping infrastructure.
Beyond allowing Muse and other agents to connect to Shop Pay, Shopify also connected Muse to its vendor side so the AI agent could create or manage a Shopify store.
While the volume of agentic payments is still small, Finkelstein said, there are “early signals” showing that AI-driven shopping could become a “powerful surface area.” He noted that this quarter, AI traffic more than doubled year-over-year, while AI-driven orders tripled. AI channels (like a chatbot conversation) also sent shoppers to product pages at three times the rate of typical search.
Agentic updates were a highlight of Shopify’s Fall 2026 Editions, released last week. Other product updates included expanded AI capabilities for Sidekick, Shopify’s AI chatbot, and a number of other tools to make online store management easier through natural-language chat conversations. The company also officially bought the website domain shop.com, which now hosts a website version of its Shop app.
RELATED: Shopify stock surges on revenue beat in big quarter for merchants
Shipping new AI features hasn’t been without its hurdles. The digital retail giant had a security issue with one of its agentic tools, which the company said has now been resolved. Shopify’s “knowledge base” tool, which allows merchants to review information AI agents get about their store, like return policies and contact details, automatically included the phone numbers and email addresses of merchants entered in store contact settings. In an email to BetaKit, a Shopify spokesperson said emails and phone numbers are no longer automatically published to the knowledge base tool.
Shopify also saw a high-profile staff departure this month. BetaKit reported on Oct. 19 that CTO Mikhail Parakhin was stepping down after two years in the role and would stay on as an advisor; it’s currently unclear who will take on the executive position. According to social media posts by former employees, the company also cut staff this quarter, though it is unclear how many roles were impacted. Shopify wouldn’t confirm specific layoffs but told BetaKit it is always looking at the “size and shape” of the team to deliver services for merchants, and that it’s actively hiring.
As Shopify heads into the holiday season—typically its busiest quarter—it expects revenue growth in the low thirties year over year.
Disclosure: BetaKit majority owner Good Future is the family office of two former Shopify leaders, Arati Sharma and Satish Kanwar.
Feature image courtesy Shopify.

articles.title: Waymo cars already appearing on Toronto streets despite worries
articles.text:
Self-driving taxi service Waymo has officially hit Toronto streets just weeks after the company’s Oct. 16 announcement that it would begin testing its autonomous vehicles on local streets.
It’s a potential major step forward in the way people move around Toronto, but Waymo’s Canadian launch still has a tough road ahead to navigate, between regulatory hurdles and serious concerns from officials at City Hall and the taxi industry.
On the eve of Waymo’s big announcement, lobbyist Aidan Grove-White, of StrategyCorp, logged a call to Adam Chaleff, the mayor’s Director of Legislative Affairs & Issues Management. Another StrategyCorp lobbyist, Alex Bernst, attended an Oct. 22 meeting with City staff from the Strategic Policy & Initiatives and Policy & Innovation units of the Transportation Services department.
Matt Elliott first reported on these lobbying files in his City Hall Watcher newsletter, though no further details about the phone call and meeting are publicly available.
And while talks are ongoing behind closed doors, resistance to the new technology has been a bit more public.
Mayor Chow is wary about the new technology, and in an interview with the Toronto Star, her press secretary, Braman Thillainathan, said that “Any move toward autonomous vehicles must not put people out of work or undermine workers’ livelihoods.”
“The mayor will not support Waymo if it costs jobs, drives down wages for other workers, or contributes to precarious work in our city,” added Thillainathan.
Kristine Hubbard, Managing Director at Beck Taxi and an outspoken critic of the rideshare industry, raised concerns over a video that surfaced on Monday showing a Waymo vehicle (albeit with a human driver) turning through a pedestrian crossing.
Love how the pedestrian walk sign was lit but you go ahead WHAT ARE WE DOING
— Kristine Hubbard (@KristineHubbard) November 2, 2026
Hubbard tells blogTO that Waymo’s arrival “is a very timely issue as we discuss the traffic crisis that faces our city.”
“Simply put: there are too many cars on our roads,” says Hubbard, adding that the U.S. tech company’s expansion north of the border comes at a time when “we attempt to protect Canadian sovereignty, we have yet another billion-dollar American company ready to take ownership of our roads.”
“The false promises of fewer cars on the streets are the echo of all of the lies told by companies like Uber when they entered the market. We have more cars, higher emissions, and the largest poverty-paid workforce in history as a result of inaction from the provincial and municipal governments.”
Though data suggests Waymo’s robotaxis are less prone to accidents than human drivers, Hubbard argues that, based on social media evidence shared on Monday, “Roads are less safe.”
“As we saw from social media posts, Waymo is not even trying to be a safer option as they gather data through surveillance of our City.”
Hubbard noted that Waymo vehicles were spotted on the eve of news that food bank visits are on the increase, and argues that “Taking jobs from Ontarians is certainly not a safe option.”
Waymo has argued that its technology is safer than human drivers, and the company has stressed that vehicles will not even operate autonomously until local roads have been fully mapped.
Waymo explained in October that it will be “taking a rigorous, phased, safety-first approach starting with high-definition mapping of local street networks and testing with trained autonomous specialists behind the wheel” before the cars can go driverless.
Other locals welcome the new technology, noting that autonomous vehicles have lower collision rates than human-driven cars.
So excited to ride Waymos in Toronto. Even more excited to have drivers who are safer than humans on the roads!
— Alex Glista 🇨🇦🇪🇺 (@AlexanderGlista) November 2, 2026
Would you drive in a Waymo? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: El calendario completo de 'La edad dorada' temporada 4: número de episodios y fechas de estreno
articles.text:
La edad dorada ha regresado por fin a HBO Max con el estreno de su primer episodio de la temporada 4. El querido drama de época vuelve a estar en emisión para que sus fans disfruten de una entrega que promete más que nunca. Porque, ambientada en el siglo XIX, es uno de los grandes títulos modernos de este género. No en vano su creador es Julian Fellowes responsable también de Downton Abbey.
Bertha Russell cambió la alta sociedad, pero a un alto precio. Ahora, en la temporada 4 de La edad dorada, su familia debe afrontar las consecuencias mientras Agnes van Rhijnaprovecha la oportunidad para recuperar su posición. Mientras tanto, Marian se abre un nuevo camino y Peggy se esfuerza por ganarse la aceptación de sus futuros suegros. En esta nueva era, hay que tener cuidado con lo que se desea.
El primer capítulo de la temporada 4 de La edad dorada ya ha llegado a HBO Max en lo que sin lugar a dudas era uno de los estrenos más importantes de la plataforma en este final de año. A partir de ahora, la compañía seguirá con la serie una estrategia de estreno semanal al uso. Es decir, el servicio de streaming lanzará sus nuevos capítulos durante las próximas semanas cada domingo por la noche en EE. UU y Latinoamérica, las madrugadas de los lunes en España. Así hasta el octavo y último de ellos, que será el final de temporada.
Calendario de estreno de La edad dorada temporada 4
Con esta estrategia de estreno cada semana, el calendario completo de La edad dorada temporada 4 es el siguiente.
- Episodio 1: domingo 1 de noviembre.
- Episodio 2: domingo 8 de noviembre.
- Episodio 3: domingo 15 de noviembre.
- Episodio 4: domingo 22 de noviembre.
- Episodio 5: domingo 29 de noviembre.
- Episodio 6: domingo 6 de diciembre.
- Episodio 7: domingo 13 de diciembre.
- Episodio 8: domingo 20 de diciembre.
*IMPORTANTE: En España los capítulos se estrenan en la madrugada del lunes debido a la diferencia horaria.
Date de alta en HBO MAX y tendrás acceso a las mejores series y películas exclusivas como The Wire, Los Soprano o Casa del Dragón. Incluye todo el catálogo de Warner, los clásicos de Cartoon Network, los grandes estrenos y el mejor deporte.
De esta forma, La edad dorada contará con un calendario de estreno que mantendrá a su temporada 4 en emisión durante bastante más de un mes. Será un aperitivo perfecto para la época navideña, y en definitiva un cierre perfecto para este otoño televisivo. A partir de su final, tendremos que esperar novedades sobre una hipotética temporada 5.

articles.title: Google adds new $250,000 Cloud VRP reward for Root-in-Cloud bugs
articles.text:
Google has expanded its Cloud Vulnerability Reward Program (VRP) with a new top-tier reward for high-impact architectural security flaws.
Starting this month, researchers can earn $250,000 for Root-in-Cloud bugs, including tenant-isolation bypasses and complex cross-service logic flaws that let attackers gain full administrative control over arbitrary Google Cloud organizations.
"To earn this premier reward, you must demonstrate full administrative control, the equivalent of 'roles/owner' or complete IAM control, over arbitrary Google Cloud organizations or projects with no prior access or special project setup," said Chris Betz, Google Cloud's Chief Information Security Officer (CISO).
"Additionally, valid vulnerability reports demonstrating remote code execution (RCE) in underlying Google production infrastructure (Borg) or achieving root-in-prod will automatically be evaluated by the Google Cloud VRP panel for root-in-cloud eligibility."
However, to qualify for this reward, the exploits cannot depend on prior access to the victim project, compromised credentials, social engineering, or user interaction.
Additionally, security researchers who achieve execution on Google's production infrastructure must stop probing since escalating, obtaining production credentials, or lateral movement are not allowed and will result in disqualification.
"High incentives require clear, safe rules of engagement. We never want researchers testing exploits against real customer projects," added Cloud VRP Lead Michael Cote.
"Instead, we created a deterministic proof-of-root mechanism using a designated service account. Researchers can cryptographically prove unauthorized access against that identity."
More details on the Google Cloud VRP, including endpoint specifications, JSON payloads, and CLI examples, are available on the rules page.
This follows Google's suspension of submissions to its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program (OSS VRP) in October after a flood of AI-generated reports.
Google has rewarded thousands of security researchers worldwide with more than $81.6 million since launching its first Vulnerability Reward Program in 2010.
In 2025, Google awarded a record-breaking $17.1 million to over 700 security researchers, a 40% increase from 2024, when it awarded $12 million in total.

articles.title: Affinity arrive enfin sur iPad, et Canva ne s’est pas contenté d’un simple portage
articles.text:
Canva réunit la retouche photo, le dessin vectoriel et la mise en page dans une nouvelle application Affinity pour iPad. Gratuite pour les particuliers, elle accueille aussi un espace de dessin pensé pour l’Apple Pencil.
Il aura fallu patienter un peu plus longtemps que sur ordinateur. Un an après la fusion de ses trois logiciels dans une application gratuite, Affinity adopte enfin la même formule sur iPad. Nous vous avions annoncé son arrivée pour novembre : Canva a lancé l’application le 2 novembre, avec une interface adaptée à la tablette et quelques nouveautés qui donnent davantage de travail au stylet.
Du premier croquis à la maquette, sans changer d’application
Dans son annonce, Canva met notamment en avant Sketch Studio, un nouvel espace consacré au dessin à main levée. L’utilisateur peut y esquisser une illustration au doigt ou à l’Apple Pencil, jouer avec les pinceaux, les textures et les calques, puis passer dans Vector Studio pour retravailler les courbes et les points de son dessin. Le tout reste dans le même fichier, sans export intermédiaire.
L’intérêt dépasse donc le simple regroupement de boutons dans une nouvelle interface. On peut préparer un croquis, construire son illustration, retoucher la photo qui l’accompagne et assembler les différents éléments dans une brochure. Les espaces Sketch, Vector, Pixel et Layout se partagent le travail, sans obliger à jongler entre plusieurs applications.
La partie photo comprend le développement des fichiers RAW, les masques, les sélections et les retouches non destructives, qui permettent de revenir sur ses réglages. Côté mise en page, Affinity propose notamment des pages maîtres et des outils typographiques pour préparer des documents destinés à l’impression.
Pour reprendre ses projets existants, Canva annonce la prise en charge des fichiers PSD de Photoshop, AI d’Illustrator, INDD et IDML d’InDesign, mais aussi des PDF et SVG. De quoi retrouver ses créations sur la tablette et poursuivre les modifications sans repartir de zéro.
Canva promet également une utilisation fluide sur les fichiers complexes, y compris hors ligne. Une ambition bienvenue, même s’il faudra vérifier ce que deviennent ces belles promesses avec un document bien chargé et un iPad moins récent.
Les outils gratuits d’un côté, l’IA sur abonnement de l’autre
Le modèle économique reprend celui de la version pour ordinateur : les outils principaux de dessin, de retouche, de création vectorielle et de mise en page sont gratuits pour les particuliers. Il faut toutefois se connecter avec un compte Canva, lui aussi gratuit, pour utiliser l’application.
Canva AI Studio reste, lui, réservé aux comptes premium. Cet espace rassemble notamment des fonctions de réduction du bruit, de correction du flou et de suppression d’arrière-plan. La gratuité couvre donc bien les outils de création, mais pas l’ensemble des fonctions mises en avant par l’éditeur.
L’application est proposée sur l’App Store français, avec une interface en français, et nécessite iPadOS 18 ou une version ultérieure. Prévoyez également 1,9 Go pour le téléchargement. La boutique affiche Canva Pro à 12 euros par mois ou 109,99 euros par an pour ceux qui souhaitent accéder aux fonctions premium. Pour commencer son premier dessin ou retoucher ses photos, la carte bancaire peut rester dans le portefeuille.

articles.title: Wann der Führerschein aufs Smartphone kommen soll – und was du damit machen kannst
articles.text:
Einführung des digitalen Führerscheins: Das müssen Autofahrer jetzt wissen
Der digitale Führerschein soll noch in diesem Jahr auf Smartphones verfügbar sein. Das bedeutet, dass Autofahrer:innen in Deutschland ihren Kartenführerschein künftig nicht mehr mitführen müssen, wenn sie den digitalen Nachweis gespeichert haben. Wie das Bundesverkehrsministerium der Frankfurter Allgemeinen Sonntagszeitung mitteilte, ist die Einführung bis Ende November geplant.
So funktioniert der digitale Führerschein
Bei der Digitalisierung hinkt Deutschland im internationalen Vergleich oft hinterher. Das soll sich jetzt sukzessive ändern – und der digitale Führerschein ist der nächste Schritt. Für das Abspeichern des Dokuments ist die i-Kfz-App vorgesehen, die das Kraftfahrtbundesamt zusammen mit der Bundesdruckerei entwickelt hat. Sie steht für Android- und iOS-Geräte schon jetzt kostenlos zur Verfügung. Um Fahrzeugscheine zu hinterlegen, benötigen Nutzer:innen die aktivierte Online-Ausweisfunktion, eine PIN und ein NFC-fähiges Smartphone. Laut Angaben des Kraftfahrtbundesamtes war die App im August 2026 auf mehr als zwei Millionen Mobiltelefonen installiert.
Schon heute können Nutzer:innen ihren Fahrzeugschein in der App digital speichern und bei Verkehrskontrollen vorzeigen. Mit dem digitalen Führerschein kommt ein zweites wichtiges Fahrzeugdokument hinzu. Wer ihn in der App hinterlegt hat, muss die Plastikkarte bei Fahrten innerhalb Deutschlands künftig nicht mehr zwingend mitführen. Auch bei Mietwagen und Carsharing soll der digitale Führerschein den Alltag von Autofahrer:innen erleichtern. Er dient als Ergänzung – ersetzen soll er die klassische Plastikkarte aber nicht. Diese wird unter anderem für Fahrten ins Ausland weiterhin erforderlich sein.
Polizeigewerkschaft begrüßt digitalen Nachweis
Die Gewerkschaft der Polizei (GdP) hatte sich im vergangenen Jahr für die Digitalisierung von Fahrzeug- und Fahrerlaubnisdokumenten ausgesprochen. „Moderne, digitale Nachweise können Verwaltungsprozesse vereinfachen, Ressourcen sparen und den Bürgerinnen und Bürgern den Alltag erleichtern”, erklärte Michael Mertens, stellvertretender Bundesvorsitzender der GdP, in einer Mitteilung der Gewerkschaft.
Kritisch sieht die GdP allerdings die mangelnde Vorbereitung der Polizeibehörden. „Bislang gibt es keine bundeseinheitlichen Schulungen, wie digitale Dokumente geprüft oder rechtssicher dokumentiert werden sollen“, sagte er Ende 2025. „Außerdem müssen digitale Nachweise in Echtzeit gegen offizielle Datenbanken abgeglichen werden können – sonst bleibt die Kontrolle lückenhaft.“ Ob sich diese Lücken inzwischen schließen ließen, bleibt abzuwarten.
Konkretes Datum steht bisher nicht fest
Ein offizielles Datum für die Einführung des digitalen Führerscheins wurde noch nicht genannt. Wer den Nachweis auf seinem Smartphone nutzen möchte, kann sich aber schon jetzt vorbereiten, die App herunterladen und sich online identifizieren. Laut Bundesverkehrsministerium soll der digitale Führerschein Anfang 2027 zusätzlich in der deutschen EUDI-Wallet verfügbar werden. Eine europäische Umsetzung ist ebenfalls geplant, könnte allerdings noch bis 2030 dauern.

articles.title: Following Austria's first commercial satellite launch, Tumbleweed raises €6.9 million to accelerate space missions | EU-Startups
articles.text:
SpaceTech company Tumbleweed has raised €6.9 million, allegedly the largest SpaceTech Seed round ever raised in Austria, four months after the startup put the country’s first commercial satellite in orbit.
The round was led by PactVC, with participation from Vanagon Ventures, early backer Prototype Capital, and EWOR. Notably, over one-third of Tumbleweed’s 25-person team also invested personal funds.
“This funding will allow us to scale what we’ve proven on our first mission, Oasis Alpha: that microgravity can be a widely accessible industrial resource. We’re so excited to be able to bring this transformative capability to even more customers, and ultimately build a future where microgravity is used to make 10x better cures for cancer, 10x better semiconductors and 10x faster developed pharmaceuticals,” says Julian Rothenbuchner, Tumbleweed CEO and co-founder.
Tumbleweed’s funding follows a series of European SpaceTech financing announcements in 2026.
In Germany, ATMOS Space Cargo raised €25.7 million to develop orbital transport and re-entry services, while deltaVision secured €10.2 million to expand spacecraft component production.
Elsewhere, UK-based NewOrbit raised €16 million for its very-low-Earth-orbit satellite technology, and Switzerland’s Stellar Alpina secured €3.8 million for in-space propulsion systems.
In Austria, Vienna-based ENPULSION secured €22.5 million in March to expand its spacecraft propulsion business.
Together with Tumbleweed’s newly announced round, these financings amount to approximately €85.1 million.
“The fact that Austrian space technology is mobilising international private capital and is
already being used commercially in space sends an important signal about the strength of our research and business location. Companies like these strengthen domestic value creation, create skilled jobs, and demonstrate that Austria is internationally competitive in demanding future technologies,” adds Peter Hanke, Austrian Federal Minister for Innovation, Mobility and Infrastructure.
Founded in 2024, Tumbleweed sells modular payload containers (aka Pods) to labs, manufacturers and R&D teams. Pod is a modular payload container that handles power, data and certification.
The Pods are fault-isolated payload containers that arrive pre-certified and keep customer experiments powered and connected in orbit. Research groups, manufacturers and R&D teams send their payload directly to Tumbleweed, and receive data during flight. Pods come in different sizes, and mission costs start at €15k.
Oasis, their spacecraft, takes the Pods up, operates them, and brings them back to earth.
Compared to equivalent experiments conducted via the International Space Station, Tumbleweed customers reportedly ship 5x faster and 10x cheaper.
“Tumbleweed put Austria’s first commercial satellite in orbit in less time than it usually takes to certify a single experiment. Julian has done exactly what he told us he would do when we first met him, only faster. Now every lab and manufacturer can use space without becoming a space company first,” says Daniel Dippold, CEO of EWOR.
Oasis Alpha was built in nine months, five times faster than industry standard, and launched on 7 July 2026 aboard SpaceX Transporter-17 as Austria’s first commercial satellite, carrying four customers. The mission was sold out a year before launch and paid for upfront.
Today’s funding will fund three missions in 2027, carrying more than 10 customers. The capital will also accelerate development of Oasis Beta, Tumbleweed’s next-generation orbital platform scheduled for 2028, which will support larger payloads and feature re-entry capability to safely bring experimental samples back to Earth.

articles.title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple is adjusting its App Store policies to make it more difficult for minors to use online dating apps or AI companions that engage in “sexual or romantic content,” the tech giant shared in an announcement to developers on Monday.
The new rules follow other changes the company has made to better protect minors, which include the rollout of its age assurance technology globally and more parental controls and child safety features.
While most major dating services typically restrict their platform to adults, Apple’s new policy will require all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features to carry an 18+ rating. Starting November 16, developers will be required to include new content descriptors to ensure their app’s age ratings reflect its features, the company said.
It’s perhaps more interesting how this rule could impact AI companion apps, or those where such functionality is one of many features. Often targeted at younger people, Character.AI, Replika, and other AI apps let people create AI companions, including friends, lovers, boyfriends and girlfriends, and other fantasy characters.
xAI last year also launched 3D animated AI companions that allowed users to unlock NSFW capabilities. As of last summer, top AI companion apps across the Apple App Store and Google Play had been downloaded 220 million times globally.
In addition to “dating and relationships,” apps will also need to indicate if they are sharing the real-world locations of a user with another person or group as part of their functionality. Any app doing so raises obvious privacy concerns, especially if the user wasn’t aware that their location was being shared.
The company noted that in Brazil, apps that provide location-sharing features for families can request an official rating from the government’s Ministry of Justice and Public Security (MJSP/Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública), instead of being required to list them with the A16 rating, as the local law requires.
